Job.CustomJobTypeName: Loss Control Consultant, Risk Management / Loss Control
Job.JobDescription:
NJM Insurance Group, is a leading mid-sized U.S. property and casualty insurance company with 90 consecutive years of A+ financial strength ratings by AM BEST. Due to exceptional employee experience, NJM has been included on the latest Forbes List of Best Employers in New Jersey for the fourth year in a row. The NJM reputation for being a top provider of outstanding customer service was reaffirmed by the most recent J.D. Power Auto Insurance Claims Survey.


NJM has focused on a strategic plan that calls for it to become a regional property & casualty insurer and has transitioned away from its affinity-based membership model. To that end, the Company has added an independent agency model for new lines of middle and large commercial and has more than doubled its product offerings. NJM now offers its various products to businesses across New Jersey, Pennsylvania, New York, Maryland, Delaware, and Connecticut.

NJM’s Commercial Lines department conducts business for policyholders and preferred agencies within the Mid-Atlantic region, specifically NJ, PA, NY, MD, DE, CT. Products include Commercial Auto, G/L, Workers Comp, BOP, Excess/Umbrella, and Package. The Commercial Lines function encompasses Underwriting, Sales, Operations, Premium Audit, Product Management, Product Development, Loss Prevention and Business Process Unit.

The Commercial Lines Loss Prevention team is searching for a Senior Loss Prevention Representative. The goal of the Sr. Loss Prevention Representative is to assist our policyholders in the process of identifying, quantifying, eliminating, or reducing the risk of loss.  This is a senior level position that will entail training and mentoring of staff.

** This position does not provide a company vehicle but NJM does reimburse for mileage and tolls.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Essential functions of this job are listed below in order of priority. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals to perform the essential duties. Regular and predictable onsite attendance is an essential function of the job.

  • Conduct on-site loss control surveys and underwriting evaluations to assess potential hazards for our policyholders and agency partners

  • Conduct accident investigations

  • Prepares loss control reports and sends recommendations to policyholders to help them improve potential risk factors

  • A knowledge of workplace safety

  • An understanding of nationally recognized standards and codes

  • Develop, enhance and present training programs in the area of loss prevention

  • Communicate loss prevention services available to policyholders and agency partners

  • Will be responsible for mentoring loss prevention representatives in the department

  • May act on behalf of the loss prevention supervisor in their absence

  • May train other loss prevention representatives on conducting site evaluations, training, or other loss control services

Required Qualifications and Experience: Knowledge, skills & abilities, experience, minimum & desired education, certification and/or license requirements.

  • 6+ years of experience in loss control including Industrial Hygiene

  • Air sampling and noise monitoring experience

  • High School Diploma/GED Required

  • Excellent communication, interpersonal and presentation skills

  • Ability to work in a team environment or independently

  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to multi-task and be detail-oriented

  • Excellent analytical and decision making skills

  • Experience with laptop computers as well as Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook

  • Safety experience is required 

  • Loss Control and Safety Experience in the Insurance Industry (Workers’ Comp, Commercial Auto, Property and/or General Liability)

  • This position is the field and requires regular travel throughout the Central NJ area.

  • Certified Safety Professional (CSP) preferred

  • OHST (Occupational Health and Safety) Certification Preferred

  • ARM (Associate in Risk Management) preferred

  • ASC (Advanced Safety Certification)

Job.JobDescription:
NJM’s WC Claims Department is seeking an experienced Claims Specialist, Sr. who lives in Western or Central PA to provide on-site service to our policyholders and agents in that area.  This is a 100% remote position which includes virtual claims handling for customers in any area of PA and possibly MD, DE or CT as needed.  

At NJM, our WC Claims Department empowers our employees to focus on delivering guidance and empathy to our customers.  As a department driven by service and customer advocacy, we are committed to providing transparent, empathetic support and collaborative engagement during the life of a claim. The WC Claims Department takes pride in being a key component in the growth and success of our policyholders’ business operations.

To meet these expectations, WC Claims Specialists are supported by a dedicated call center who can field calls for them and other specialized units who are responsible for setting reserves, making permanency payments, and following through on subrogation so they can dedicate the time needed to manage claims. Many of our staff are long-tenured with a focus on building relationships, not only with our customers, but with each other providing a positive and nurturing work environment.

Hours:

Monday to Friday 8:00AM- 4:15PM (Hours can vary depending on start time).

Training is required at the NJM- West Trenton office.

Responsibilities:

  • Ensure quality management of claims in accordance with claims best practices and company guidelines, and timely, accurate documentation of claim activity

  • Provide a high level of customer service that promotes injured worker advocacy-based principles to improve outcomes for all parties 

  • Determine compensability and coverage issues by gathering medical and factual evidence

  • Administer the delivery of timely, appropriate, and accurate benefits

  • Evaluate the claim for potential fraud indicators and escalate the claim to SIU, as appropriate

  • Recognize and investigate subrogation opportunity and refer to NJM subrogation staff for recovery of third-party funds

  • Initiate and provide excellent communication with all stakeholders (injured workers, medical providers, attorneys, policyholders, agents, etc.) professionally and proactively with a customer-centric approach

  • Apply critical thinking skills to evaluate and mitigate exposures, and establish and implement a proactive strategic plan of action

  • Assign and refer claim petitions to Counsel, and work to resolve the claim within given authority

  • Build rapport with policyholders and agents, conduct on-site investigations when necessary, and educate policyholders and agents on NJM procedures, policies, and claim practices

  • Prepare and attend Claim Reviews at policyholder or agent locations in Western and/or Central PA or virtually for further locations.

  • Serve as a liaison between policyholders/agents and various departments in NJM.

  • Represent WC Claim in on-site capabilities meetings to onboard new policyholders in Western and/or Central PA. 

  • Participate in training programs to keep current on relevant issues/topics

  • Recommend process improvement where applicable to best improve the department efficiency, work product, and service commitment to interested parties

  • Demonstrate a commitment to NJM’s Code of Business Conduct and Ethics, and apply knowledge of compliance policies and procedures, standards, and laws applicable to job responsibilities in the performance of work

Required Qualifications and Experience:

  • 5+ years’ experience as a Workers' Comp Claim Representative, or comparable knowledge and experience with various aspects of claims handling and/or process including advanced knowledge of medical terminology and WC regulations for PA, MD and/or DE claims.

  • Knowledge of and/or experience working with liens and Medicare Set-Asides to secure full and final settlements

  • Customer service oriented with strong written and oral communication skills

  • Strong interpersonal skills with ability to work both in a team and independently

  • Demonstrated organizational skills, and use of sound decision-making capabilities

  • Working knowledge utilizing an automated claim processing system and Microsoft Office tools including Word and Outlook

  • Licensed in DE and/or CT to adjust WC claims or have the ability to obtain these licenses within 90 days.

  • Ability to travel for business purposes, approximately 2 – 3 days a week meeting with policyholders and/or agents

Preferred:

  • Associate or bachelor’s degree

  • AIC/CPCU or other applicable insurance designations

  • Experience using Guidewire Claim Center, OnBase and additional Microsoft Office tools including Teams, Excel and PowerPoint

  • Knowledge and experience in claims handling for other commercial line products in various states including PA, MD and/or DE.

Salary:

  • Sr Level starting rate is $79,129.05+ annually based on experience and credentials

We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Sourcing Manager, Professional Services to join our team. The ideal candidate will have a proven track record in strategic sourcing, category management, supplier relationship management, and indirect procurement. This role requires a strategic thinker with excellent analytical abilities, strong stakeholder management skills, and a deep understanding of market dynamics. The successful candidate will be responsible for developing sourcing strategies, managing supplier relationships, and delivering measurable value across assigned categories, including professional services and other indirect spend areas.


This role requires 4 days per week in our Atlanta office.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement comprehensive category strategies to optimize cost, quality, service levels, and business value.
  • Manage assigned indirect spend categories, identifying opportunities for cost savings, supplier consolidation, process improvements, and risk mitigation.
  • Conduct market analyses to identify trends, opportunities, innovation, and risks within assigned categories.
  • Lead strategic sourcing initiatives, including RFPs, RFQs, and RFIs, from strategy development through supplier selection and contract execution.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams and business stakeholders to align sourcing strategies with organizational objectives.
  • Negotiate, execute, and manage supplier contracts, ensuring compliance with company policies and applicable regulations.
  • Source and negotiate complex Professional Services agreements, including consulting, contingent labor, managed services, and other knowledge-based service categories.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance sourcing processes, supplier performance, and overall procurement effectiveness.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with key suppliers and internal stakeholders.
  • Monitor supplier performance and key performance indicators (KPIs) to ensure accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Identify and mitigate supply, commercial, operational, and financial risks within assigned categories.

Qualifications:

  • Professional Services sourcing experience required.
  • 5+ years of strategic sourcing, category management, or procurement experience, including ownership of indirect spend categories within a complex corporate environment.
  • Demonstrated experience sourcing and managing Professional Services categories, including consulting, contingent workforce, managed services, and other indirect services.
  • Proven track record developing and executing category strategies that deliver cost savings, supplier innovation, risk mitigation, and business value.
  • Experience leading competitive sourcing events (RFPs, RFQs, and RFIs) and managing supplier evaluation and selection processes.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities with experience leveraging spend analysis, market intelligence, and data-driven decision-making.
  • Excellent negotiation, contract management, and supplier relationship management skills.
  • In-depth knowledge of market dynamics, industry trends, and strategic sourcing best practices across indirect procurement categories.
  • Ability to influence and collaborate effectively with stakeholders.
  • Strong communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills.
  • Proficiency with sourcing, procurement, contract lifecycle management, and spend analysis tools.

Job.JobTitle: Assistant General Counsel, Bad Faith Litigation
Job.JobDescription:
Who we are:

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. Building on 100 years of experience, today AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance and other financial services to customers in more than 80 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets, manage risks and provide financial security.

Get to know the business:

AIG’s Global Legal, Compliance, Regulatory and Government Affairs (GLCR) department is comprised of attorneys and other professionals providing high-quality advisory and transactional support with integrity and objectivity across all parts of the organization. The team ensures an operating environment that minimizes legal, regulatory and reputational risks, complies with all laws and regulations, and enforces AIG policies and procedures. 

This is a global, diverse and award-winning team that has been recognized for its leadership and innovative solutions. You will also be eligible to participate in AIG’s award-winning pro bono program.

AIG’s GLCR department is looking for an experienced attorney to serve as an Assistant General Counsel managing bad faith litigation and providing advice to AIG’s claims organization in the New York office.  

Specific Responsibilities Include:

The primary purpose of the position is to manage an active litigation docket consisting of bad faith and extra-contractual matters arising from the handling of claims under casualty, financial lines, property and specialty policies issued to commercial and personal lines insureds.  The attorney will also be responsible for providing timely advice to claim handlers in order to avoid and/or mitigate extra-contractual exposures. 

  • Manage an active litigation docket consisting of bad faith and extra contractual matters;
  • Develop resolution strategies and make recommendations to senior management;
  • Direct and supervise outside counsel with respect to the implementation of litigation strategies;
  • Ensure that high-quality written work product is filed on behalf of the AIG member insurance companies;
  • Collaborate with business partners in the claims organization on strategic decisions and provide timely advice to claim handlers to avoid and/or mitigate bad faith exposure;
  • Prepare and conduct regularly scheduled training presentations to claim handlers.
  • On occasion and as necessary, travel for mediations, trials;

Education / Experience:

  • Attorney with at least 7+ years of law firm litigation experience strongly preferred;
  • J.D. from an accredited law school and strong academic credentials;
  • Admitted to practice in at least one state;
  • Litigation experience should include preparing witnesses for, taking, and defending depositions, as well as drafting and arguing dispositive motions;
  • Trial experience very useful but not required
  • In-house experience with another insurer is also useful but not required.

 

To succeed in this position, the successful candidate must possess the following skills:

  • Strong initiative and work ethic; 
  • Focused attention to detail and honed analytical skills; 
  • Superior oral and written communication skills; 
  • Strong interpersonal skills; 
  • Ability to be a self-starter and work independently; 
  • Flexibility and a willingness to adapt to changing needs of the organization and/or business clients; 
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills, including the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment; 
  • Ability to deliver creative and well-reasoned plans to resolve challenges and to execute on such plans; 
  • Ability to thrive in an environment where coordination and teamwork is a priority while also being committed to individual accountability and results; 
  • Willingness to be mentored and trained to meet the needs of the organization; and 
  • Sound legal and business judgment.

Job.JobTitle: Lead Specialist, Workers' Compensation Oversight Claims
Job.JobDescription:
At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Lead Specialist, Workers' Compensation Oversight Claims to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Claims 


Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency.   


How you will create an impact 


  • Focused on Workers' Compensation, this role is an ideal opportunity to develop your expertise in handling and investigating complex claims. The aim is deal with genuine claims through a proactive, best practice approach, in line with AIGs quality standards – you will actively promote and demonstrate the principles of ‘Treating Customers Fairly’ in claims handling.   
  • You will also proactively identify and review suspect/fraudulent claims on a consistent basis – dealing with such claims in line with our clear guidelines. 
  • Your work will involve regular contact with internal stakeholders and brokers, (medical) experts, clients’ lawyers, victims or their legal representatives. We want you to build effective relationships with internal and external customers, while acting as a point of referral.   
  • You will have the opportunity to grow your experience by providing support to Team Managers and deputizing in their absence. For example, you will assist with monitoring market/industry practices in claims handling. 
  • In addition, you can use the claims experience you gain to help improve our products in collaboration with colleagues in underwriting. 

 

What you’ll need to succeed 


  • At least 5-10 years' experience of Workers' Compensation, with knowledge of legal / regulatory and litigation / procedural requirements
  • Specialist knowledge of Workers' Compensation technical claims topics is preferred.  
  • Ideally some experience in negotiation, mediation, and arbitration.  
  • Policy language skills enabling accurate and consistent policy wording interpretation.  
  • Lateral thinking and the ability to problem solve and develop new ideas to improve working practices. 
  • Strong communication, time management, administrative and report-writing skills. 

Ready to take your career to the next level? We would love to hear from you!

Compensation for this position includes base salary and eligibility for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan.  In addition, we’re proud to offer a range of competitive benefits, a summary of which can be viewed here: US Benefits Overview

Major Job Responsibilities:

  • Lead complex cyber incident investigations and coordinate the investigation, containment, remediation, recovery, and closure of security events.
  • Own investigative workstreams end to end, establishing root cause, scope, lateral movement, potential data exposure, organizational impact, and required response actions.
  • Assess incident severity and risk, develop investigation strategies, facilitate incident scoping discussions, and prioritize response activities as circumstances evolve.
  • Drive risk-based containment and remediation decisions, including endpoint isolation, account restriction, and blocking of malicious infrastructure, while balancing cyber risk against business impact.
  • Conduct investigations using EDR, SIEM, identity, email, network, web, application, cloud, and other available telemetry; preserve relevant evidence and reconstruct incident timelines.
  • Perform and guide digital evidence collection, forensic artefact analysis, and appropriate static or dynamic malware analysis to identify adversary behavior and indicators of compromise.
  • Lead hypothesis-driven threat hunting and use emerging threat intelligence to identify opportunities for stronger detection logic and monitoring coverage.
  • Develop and improve SIEM, SOAR, detection, monitoring, and security automation use cases, collaborating with Detection Engineering and other technical teams to implement improvements.
  • Advance AI and agentic security capabilities that improve investigation quality, operational efficiency, and analyst decision support within Security Operations.
  • Build, maintain, and exercise incident response runbooks, playbooks, and operating procedures to strengthen readiness across a global, cloud-based environment.
  • Coordinate response activity across technology, business, security, and third-party teams; present findings, containment recommendations, and response options to technical, management, and executive stakeholders.
  • Maintain clear, accurate, and timely incident records, investigation plans, decisions, findings, actions, and handovers within the relevant case-management and workflow systems.
  • Review proposed security exclusions and exceptions to confirm appropriate supporting evidence and identify potential blind spots before implementation.
  • Provide technical leadership, coaching, and practical support to analysts; lead effective shift handovers and strengthen team capability through mentoring, training, and knowledge sharing.
  • Perform basic oversight of security tooling and telemetry health, escalating material gaps that could affect detection or investigation capability.
  • Lead or contribute to Security Operations improvement initiatives, using metrics, process optimization, automation, and lessons learned to improve incident response effectiveness and operational resilience.

Requirements:

  • At least 7+ years of overall experience in Cyber or Information Security, consisting of a minimum of 5+ years’ recent experience in Cyber Security Operations or Cyber Incident Response
  • Experience working in complex enterprises and global organizations.  Insurance and financial services experience strongly encouraged.
  • Strong Information Technology technical skills, with experience in coordination of technical teams and individual resources

Job.JobDescription:
Get to know the business:

AIG’s Global Legal, Compliance, Regulatory and Government Affairs (GLCR) department is comprised of attorneys and other professionals providing high-quality advisory and transactional support with integrity and objectivity across all parts of the organization. The team ensures an operating environment that minimizes legal, regulatory and reputational risks, complies with all laws and regulations, and enforces AIG policies and procedures. 


Key Responsibilities:

The Senior Manager & Counsel, Insurance, Reinsurance & Underwriting, is responsible for providing day-to-day legal advice and support to AIG Risk Management, commercial insurance executives, underwriters and other personnel regarding transactional, legal, regulatory and compliance matters.  AIG Risk Management provides customized workers’ compensation, auto liability, and general liability/products liability program structures for sophisticated organizations that retain portions of their risk.  The position reports to the lead lawyer for AIG Risk Management. 


Specific duties include:

  • Providing legal support with regard to complex insurance programs, structured loss sensitive programs, and credit arrangements. 
  • Negotiating, drafting and/or reviewing insurance policies, endorsements, credit and collateral agreements, as well as marketing material, and other ancillary documents related to complex insurance programs.

 Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of legal experience at a law firm or corporation preferred - with a focus on insurance, credit agreements, restructuring/bankruptcy, reinsurance, etc.
  • Knowledge of and experience providing legal and regulatory support with loss sensitive accounts, credit and bankruptcy issues, collateral arrangements, group insurance, group captives, insurance regulatory issues, and worker’s compensation, general liability and automobile coverages is preferred. 
  • 3+ years of experience with loss sensitive business or other commercial insurance preferred.
  • JD is required, with admission to at least 1 state bar.
  • Excellent drafting, negotiating and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong initiative and work ethic.
  • Focused attention to detail.
  • Additionally, the position requires the ability to interact with clients and brokers, all levels of underwriting business partners, from senior executives to more junior underwriters, and other legal and service teams within the company.


For positions based in NYC, the base salary range is $159,000 - $195,000 and the position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. Job.CustomJobTypeName: Excess & Surplus Lines Underwriter, Underwriting, Insurance Underwriter
Job.JobDescription:
Join us as a Senior Executive  Underwriter, Excess Casualty to step up to a key team leadership role that will drive business growth.


Make your mark in Underwriting


AIG underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, Multinational Clients, and High Net Worth individuals. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model, and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.


How you will create an impact


We are seeking a Senior Executive Underwriter to contribute to their industry leading Excess Casualty underwriting team.  AIG’s strong foundation as the market leader in this area has evolved through its long-term commitment to the marketplace, investment in technology, commitment to industry knowledge sharing, underwriting creativity and emphasis on data and analytics.  AIG prides itself as staying ahead of the curve and looking for forward thinking and inventive underwriters to navigate a constantly changing global, economic and geopolitical landscape. 


In this role you will:


  • Perform highly technical and complex assignments within area of expertise.
  • Provide technical direction to management, less senior specialists, producers, and claims adjusting personnel.
  • Be responsible for underwriting NA Excess Casualty products.
  • Accept, decline, or modify new and renewal submissions submitted by brokers. Identify exposures and analysis required to underwrite an account, as well as the coverage policies, and determine the exposure to loss assumed and restricted by the insuring agreements and the exclusions.
  • Manage a book of business and may participate in the formulation of the budget relative to regional budget/goals.
  • Establish new business production goals and submission flow relative to the book of business.
  • Collaborate with Distribution, Territory Managers, and other line(s) of business underwriters to target desirable accounts and cross selling opportunities from brokers while soliciting customer/producer input for improving and enhancing service.
  • Develop and implement pricing and negotiation strategy, terms & conditions, and deal structures with brokers and clients while maintaining the quality of the risk and NA Excess Casualty strategy.
  • May review, evaluate and recommend modifications to underwriting guidelines.
  • Participate in special underwriting projects as needed.
  • Develop strong, long-term relationships with brokers and clients to profitably grow a book of business.
  • Provide superior customer service to brokers and clients.
  • May draft manuscript endorsements that are particular to an underwriting exposure(s) for approval by legal.
  • May be responsible for assigning and managing the work of a team of underwriters while providing guidance.

What you’ll need to succeed:


  • Commercial Insurance Company, Agency or Brokerage experience.
  • Bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university.
  • Proven ability to build and maintain strong professional relationships.
  • Advanced working knowledge of lines of business NA Excess Casualty products including product features, forms, regulatory environments and risks, etc.
  • Demonstrated sales, marketing, and relationship building experience.
  • Very strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Highly motivated and results-oriented.
  • Ability to work in dynamic, rapidly changing environment, adapting to changing requirements and collaborating with a wide range of colleagues to quickly deliver solutions.
  • Willingness to be flexible, learn on the job, and maintain a can-do attitude.
  • Comfort with analytical tools and technology.

For positions based in New York the base salary range for this position is $150,000 - $185,000, Chicago the base salary range for this position is $145,000-$175,000 and the position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan.  Your actual compensation will be dependent on your skills, experience, and qualifications. At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Senior Specialist, Casualty Claims to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

Make your mark in Claims

Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency.

How you will create an impact

The Senior Specialist will handle auto and general liability claims under general supervision and moderate exposure claims involving litigation. The position also ensures ongoing adjudication of claims within the Company standards, industry best practices and specific client service requirements.

Key Responsibilities:

·       Maintains high standards of customer service. This includes prompt contact and follow up to complete timely and accurate investigation, damage evaluation and claim resolution in accordance with regulatory and company standards.

·       Conducts a thorough investigation of coverage, liability and damages.  Must document facts and maintain evidence to support claim resolution.

·       Complies with all statutory and regulatory requirements in all applicable jurisdictions.

·       Establishes appropriate loss and expense reserves with documented rationale; ongoing review of reserves required through life of file.

·       Demonstrates technical efficiency through timely, consistent execution of best claim handling practices and claim handling guidelines.

·       Communicates effectively with internal and external customers on claims and account issues.

·       Maintains and manages a diary system to efficiently manage and resolve assigned claim inventory.

·       Effectively manages litigation process and defense counsel to ensure timely and cost-effective outcomes.

·       Property and Casualty licenses required.  Must be obtained within 6 months of hire. 

What you’ll need to succeed

 

·       2+ years of Auto and General Liability claim experience with a carrier

·       Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent work experience.

·       Must possess excellent interpersonal and organizational skills and be able to handle multiple tasks while managing competing priorities.

·       Ability to work independently, handle multiple tasks simultaneously and exercise good judgment.

·       Ability to collaborate and successfully manage work when working at home or in office.

·       Effective decision-making skills including the ability to recognize, analyze, and improve claims performance against standards and goals.

·       Knowledge of claim handling procedures and best practices.

·       Experience handling self- insured retentions, surplus lines coverages, and partnering with MGAs is a plus.

·       Multi-state adjuster licenses a plus; ability to obtain required licenses within 90 days.

Ready to take your career to the next level? We would love to hear from you!

Make your mark in Product Development


Senior Product Development Manager, Programs position is a product and process leadership role requiring strong expertise and extensive internal and external client interaction and support. This role is responsible for managing the tasks and processes associated with the product development, filing submission/approval, and implementation of new or revised products (rates/rules/forms) for use within the Programs Division.  


The role requires extensive ISO, AAIS, AIB MA Auto and proprietary product knowledge spanning admitted and non-admitted commercial property and casualty lines of business, including but not limited to Property, Inland Marine, General Liability, Auto, Umbrella, Excess, Cyber, and Professional Liability (including Claims Made and Defense Within Limits products). Product knowledge must include strong expertise in complex form, rate, rule development, along with knowledge of underwriting guidelines and procedures, admitted filings, filing strategies, issuance systems and product implementation, and regulatory and compliance requirements. This role will own, direct and supervise the end-to-end product development processes starting with due diligence through completion and implementation. This role requires a customer centric and solutions-oriented approach, strong multi-tasking skills, superior organizational and project management skills, and the ability to work independently and collaborate extensively.


How you will make an impact


  • Maintain extensive and current product and filings knowledge, and ownership of assigned products/programs. 
  • Own the development and implementation of product and filings strategy. Conduct product project planning, inclusive of establishing deliverables and due dates, resolve conflicts, identify solutions, and ensure stakeholder accountability and project completion within established parameters. Lead cross functional product development initiatives with Glatfelter product development associates.
  • Train junior and new associates in product development tasks and processes. Share knowledge. Provide technical guidance, mentorship and peer review for forms drafting, filings, implementation, and other processes.
  • Vendor product development oversight – Provide training and guidance, manage workflow and deliverables, review developed product for accuracy.
  • Provide complex forms drafting expertise - Collaborate with Program Managers, Product Line Officers, and Program Administrators to fully understand underwriting intent, and ensure such underwriting intent is reflected by developing clear and unambiguous policy and endorsement wording.
  • Provide expertise to Program Managers, Program Administrators, and other stakeholders in the analysis, development and documentation of products (rates/rules/forms) with a focused responsibility for rate/rule page manuals development and complex forms drafting. 
  • Act as a liaison, coordinating and driving policy and endorsement wording drafting, product review and discussions with various stakeholders (Program Managers, Product Line Officers, Actuarial, Claims, Compliance, Systems, Program Administrator, etc.), and drive to conclusion the Legal review and approval process for forms/endorsements. 
  • Drive remediation of existing policies and endorsements, identifying those that should be retired, updated, or replaced.
  • Co-ordinate and prepare product for filing submissions. Handle all coordination aspects of the state filings submission process serving as a liaison between AIG Programs staff and the AIG State Filings Department. Be responsible for the accurate completion of all required filing related transmission documentation. 
  • Coordinate and prepare the response and product revisions to State Insurance Department objections on state filings with input from Program Managers, Product Line Officers, Program Administrator, Actuarial and Legal. Direct AIG State Filings Department personnel on responding. 
  • Provide product support for market conduct inquiries. 
  • Monitor filings for timely approvals and conduct filing reviews and reconciliation for accuracy and completeness (AIG and vendor filings).
  • Communicate state filing product approvals and approved products to Program Administrators, Underwriting and AIG Systems/Operations for implementation.  Provide related system programming specifications to align with product/filing intent. 

What you'll need to succeed


  • Ability to conduct research on competitor products and filings and periodically monitor market changes. Analyze and compare product offerings and provide related guidance on Program development and expansion opportunities. Provide advice and insights with respect to policies and endorsements used by competitors.
  • Experience providing support, and continuing to implement and maintain  organizational controls to the manuscript endorsement request/development process. In addition to any product drafting/review efforts required, provide regulatory guidance on acceptability and maintain manuscript forms library and inventory/tracking sheet in shared environment. 
  • Participate in coordination meetings with other business units and support areas of AIG to ensure that the administration, state filing and system implementation activities of AIG Programs are in alignment with the rest of the organization. 
  • Ability to maintain a library of finalized products for reference. 
  • Drive the development and maintenance of SOPs, Checklists, Status Sheets and other tools to reflect various aspects of the product filing and implementation processes. 
  • Lead product development and management initiatives as assigned by the VP of Product Development.

Ready to take your career to the next level?  We would love to hear from you.

Job.JobTitle: Senior Manager, Sourcing Category Management, IT Professional Services
Job.JobDescription:
This role requires 4 days per week in our Atlanta office location.


About the role

This position is responsible for sourcing and category management for IT Professional Services. The role will work with senior business partners and suppliers to manage spend, improve commercial terms and deliver GSPS cost-reduction goals. Depending on the scope, the position may also lead a small team of sourcing professionals.


The role will lead sourcing and supplier initiatives across consulting, advisory and technology services. Key activities include category planning, negotiations, demand review, rate analysis, contract strategy and supplier performance.


The individual will advise stakeholders across AIG, use market and spend data to support decisions, and identify practical ways to reduce cost, manage demand and improve value.

This role requires someone who can independently manage complex priorities, influence senior stakeholders and drive work through completion. The individual should be comfortable leading negotiations, reviewing financial and commercial data, and resolving supplier or engagement issues. Success will depend on sound judgment, clear communication and strong execution.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute category plans for consulting, advisory, technology services and other Professional Services spend.
  • Partner with senior stakeholders to understand demand, shape requirements and identify savings opportunities.
  • Lead sourcing events and supplier negotiations for complex engagements.
  • Review rates, roles, locations and commercial models to improve overall value.
  • Guide statement-of-work reviews, including scope, deliverables, pricing, milestones and change controls.
  • Manage supplier performance and resolve service, commercial and contractual issues.
  • Maintain spend, savings, pipeline and supplier reporting, and present recommendations to leadership.
  • Partner with Legal, Finance, Risk and other teams to support sourcing decisions and contract outcomes.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
  • 10+ years of experience in sourcing, procurement, category management or a related field.
  • Experience sourcing IT Professional Services and negotiating complex contracts.
  • Experience managing large, complex supplier relationships, including governance, performance, vendor risk, contracts, negotiations, and issue and dispute resolution.
  • Ability to analyze spend, rates, supplier proposals, commercial models and contract terms.
  • Strong business judgment and the ability to work across a matrixed organization, influence stakeholders and negotiate effectively.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, including experience working with senior leaders.
  • Experience leading a small team or guiding the work of others.
  • Experience with sourcing tools, procurement processes and spend reporting.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree (MBA or MS) preferred.
  • Experience in strategic sourcing or building a vendor management program, preferably at a Fortune 100 company.
  • Knowledge of Professional Services pricing models, including time and materials, fixed price and milestone-based engagements.
  • Experience working in a global organization with teams and stakeholders in different locations.

CS - Corporate ServicesAIG Employee Services, Inc.

Who we are

AIG, Inc. is a leading provider of insurance products and services for commercial and personal insurance customers.  It includes one of the world’s most far-reaching property casualty networks.  AIG, Inc. (“AIG”) offers a broad range of products to customers through a diversified, multichannel distribution network.  Customers value AIG’s strong capital position, extensive risk management and claims experience and its ability to be a market leader in critical lines of the insurance business.


Corporate Finance - Investment Accounting

The Investment Accounting group at AIG is responsible for the accounting and reporting for AIG's Invested Assets of over $95 billion a comprised primarily of fixed maturity securities and includes private equity, hedge funds, commercial/residential loans and equity securities.  In addition, AIG’s derivative portfolio consists primarily of foreign exchange derivatives but also includes interest rate and other derivative instruments. 


The Investment Accounting group’s specific responsibilities include reconciliation of transactional data from various sub-ledgers to the general ledger and ultimately AIG's financial statements as well as all related external reporting for investments (10Q/K, Financial Supplement, STAT Audited Financials, Investment NAIC reporting and various government regulatory reports).  AIG has multiple legal entities around the globe.


The team is also responsible for establishing the accounting for new transactions or new investment products, implementation of new GAAP and STAT accounting standards as it relates to invested assets, the implementation of new accounting systems as it relates to invested assets, and management of the risks, controls and AIG audit as it relates to investments and supporting Investment FP&A.


Responsibilities

  • Execute and manage accounting processes related to the monthly and quarterly accounting close to ensure accuracy of AIG’s invested assets data of certain international entities
  • Support the preparation of certain Investment disclosures for AIG 10Q/K and Financial Supplement, including as appropriate the Investment, Lending, Fair Value, VIE Footnotes and Investment MD&A
  • Assist with the implementation of process improvements and new systems, in coordination with other areas of the department/organization
  • Point of contact and support for the various business unit and corporate controllers
  • Coordinate with various areas in the organization to develop an understanding of new investment transactions and to provide guidance/support that ensures the accounting results from these investments are accurately recorded in the AIG ledgers
  • Perform ad-hoc analytical requests

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting or finance
  • At least 3 years’ experience in accounting and reporting for investment products
  • Understanding of investment products and accounting treatment for fixed maturity, equity, cash equivalent and alternative investments
  • Working knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principle (GAAP) and the recording of investments-related journal entries
  • Experience with foreign currency remeasurement and translation
  • Strong analytical skills, including experience performing investment data analysis including commentary
  • High level of competency using Microsoft Excel including pivot tables and formulas to create/manage investment data and perform analysis
  • Ability to work collaboratively with teams in multiple locations
  • Ability to balance multiple projects at once, to prioritize appropriately, and to approach the work with a sense of urgency and strong attention to detail to produce high quality results in a time sensitive environment
  • Team-player mindset geared towards process improvements and the implementation of accounting controls to ensure consistency and data quality of the team’s financial output
  • High level of motivation and initiative, ability to work independently, including strong organizational skills
  • Comfort level working within a dynamic and complex organizational structure
  • Excellent interpersonal skills with ability to maintain relationships at all levels within the organization
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to communicate effectively with staff, peers, and other external and internal audiences
  • Computer proficiency with a strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office, database experience a plus

For positions based in New York, the base salary range is $87,000-$109,000. For positions based in Connecticut, the base salary range is $87,000-$109,000. For positions based in New Jersey, the base salary range is $88,000-$110,000. The position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. Underwriter - Property


Join us as an Underwriter to make a greater impact through your technical expertise and people skills. This could be the ideal chance to step up into your first Senior level role.


Make your mark in Underwriting


AIG underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, Multinational Clients, and High Net Worth individuals. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model, and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.


At AIG, we empower our underwriters to put their exceptional analytical skills to use every day to assess and measure risk. Their decisions are critical to driving the company’s success and profitability.  Our underwriters embody AIG’s tradition of innovation, developing insurance solutions to minimize the risk exposures of corporate and individual clients. They delve into a wide range of areas, including aviation, catastrophic events and high-net-worth individuals.


How you will create an impact:

  • Evaluate risks, quote and issue Property policies in order to increase production on a profitable business.
  • Analyze, prepare, define structure, place and negotiate facultative reinsurance either directly or through reinsurance brokers, adhering to reinsurance and underwriting policies and procedures.
  • Negotiate externally and internally the underwriting of the accounts and analyze engineering information (survey reports), valuation reports, catastrophe modelling results and other documents of underwriting. Request additional information to the insurance brokers to analyze the risk, if it was deemed relevant.
  • Drive underwriting excellence across the business determining acceptability of the risk by establishing and ensuring adherence to risk appetite, line setting, standards and guidelines, and ensure rating and pricing adequacy.
  • Collaborate with Distribution, Executive, and other line(s) of business underwriters to target desirable accounts and cross selling opportunities from brokers and ceding companies.
  • Provide superior customer service to brokers and clients.
  • Increase policy retention on the line of businesses.
  • Contribute to operational efficiencies.

What you’ll need to succeed:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Actuarial, Business Administration (Finance or Accounting preferred), or related areas.
  • Demonstrated business savvy, analytical and quantitative skills with strong problem-solving abilities.
  • Experience in facultative reinsurance is desirable.
  • Experience in Property underwriting accounts for at least one year.
  • Proficient in the use of MS Office suite products specially Excel (a must) and Word.
  • Excellent communication skills in English and Spanish including verbal, written and negotiation.
  • A proven track record of excellent customer service skills and Interpersonal skills.
  • Fast learner and has decision making criteria. 
  • Excellent organizational and prioritization skills.
  • A good level of experience in writing reports and business correspondence.

Director, Technology Analytics & Automation


Who we are

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. Building on 100 years of experience, today AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance and other financial services to customers in more than 80 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets, manage risks and provide for retirement security.


Purpose of the Role

The Director, Technology, Analytics, and Automation will design and deliver technology and automation-driven solutions to enable the optimal delivery of legal, compliance, and regulatory services within AIG across all regions in which the company operates. 

Key Accountabilities and Responsibilities

In this Legal Operations role you will be leading a global high performing team across Ireland, the US, and Japan driving technology and process innovation, including the adoption of AI capabilities, across legal, compliance and regulatory functions. As a subject matter expert in the systems, workflows and data, you will ensure alignment with their standards. You will put the Global Legal, Compliance and Regulatory Technology Roadmap into practice to support organizational transformation, improve efficiency and deliver operational excellence across the application environment.

You are a process-driven, strategic thinker with a proven track record of managing high-performing teams with an operational excellence mindset and evidence of having delivered significant organizational results. 

Complementing your core responsibilities, you will elicit, analyze, and document business, functional, and system requirements and translate those into clear system specifications, user stories, and process flows for technology teams will round out your profile.


Qualifications

  • 10+ years of relevant technology, operations, and analytics experience.  Insurance industry and/or legal, compliance, and regulatory knowledge is preferred.
  • Experience leading high-performing teams with strong track records of flawless project execution and driving a culture of operational excellence.
  • Experience in leading the development and execution of automation strategies.
  • Experience developing applications utilizing desktop and web-enabled reporting, database, and analytics tools.
  • Experience collaborating with the IT organization and business partners on a project.
  • Strong project management skills, including effective attention to detail.
  • Strong interpersonal skills to establish effective working relationships with and provide constructive feedback to stakeholders, colleagues, and reviewers.
  • Effective time management skills; coordinate and prioritize competing initiatives while meeting deadlines.
  • Ability to educate team members in using automation.
  • Ability to identify process improvements and suggest efficiencies.
  • Ability to document processes, and transfer knowledge to team members.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including ability to create and deliver effective presentations.
  • BA or equivalent experience; Masters degree is a plus.  Preferred areas of study include, Computer Science, Finance, Business Administration, Technology, and other related disciplines.

Make your mark in Fast Track Claims

Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency.


How you will create an impact

The role of a Specialist, Casualty Claims is to investigate, evaluate and resolve first and third-party auto liability claims, and occasionally minor injury claims and low complexity general liability losses.  We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Auto Physical Damage Claims Adjuster to investigate, evaluate, negotiate, and resolve claims. This role is ideal for someone with prior insurance, automotive, or claims experience who is looking to grow a career in claims handling. The adjuster will work directly with policyholders, claimants, repair facilities, and vendors to provide timely and fair claim resolution while delivering strong customer service.


  • Investigate and manage auto physical damage claims from first notice of loss through final resolution.
  • Review coverage, determine liability as applicable, and evaluate vehicle damages.
  • Coordinate inspections with repair facilities, appraisers, rental vendors, and customers.
  • Communicate clearly and professionally with insureds, claimants, attorneys, and internal partners.
  • Review estimates, photographs, repair documentation, and total loss evaluations.
  • Negotiate settlements within authority limits and document claim activity accurately.
  • Monitor claim progress to ensure timely handling and compliance with company standards and state regulations.
  • Identify potential fraud indicators and escalate concerns when appropriate.
  • Maintain productivity, quality, and customer service expectations in a fast-paced environment.
  • Assist customers through what can often be a stressful experience with empathy and professionalism.

What you will need to succeed:


  • Bachelor’s degree preferred.
  • 2+ years of experience in insurance claims, customer service, collision estimating, or related field preferred.
  • Basic understanding of automobile repair processes and vehicle damage evaluation preferred.
  • Strong communication, negotiation, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently.
  • Comfortable using claims management systems and standard business software.
  • Ability to make sound decisions and apply problem-solving skills.
  • Property and casualty licenses required. Must be obtained within 6 months of hire.

Job.JobTitle: Manager, Sourcing Category Management, AI & Data
Job.JobDescription:
This role requires 4 days per week in our Atlanta office.


About the role

We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Sourcing Category Manager, AI & Data to join our team. The ideal candidate will have a proven track record in strategic sourcing, category management, supplier relationship management, and indirect procurement, with experience sourcing technology, data, software, cloud, or AI solutions.


This role requires a strategic thinker with strong analytical and stakeholder management skills and an understanding of the rapidly evolving commercial, licensing, and risk considerations associated with AI and data. The ideal candidate will also have practical knowledge of enterprise AI and emerging commercial and delivery models, including generative and agentic AI, AI-enabled SaaS, foundation models, APIs, and consumption-based services.


The successful candidate will develop and execute sourcing strategies across AI and Data, manage strategic supplier relationships, and deliver measurable value. The role will also partner with other sourcing category teams where AI capabilities intersect with enterprise software, cloud, professional services, and other areas of third-party spend.


Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute comprehensive AI and Market Data category strategies to optimize cost, quality, service, innovation, risk, and business value.
  • Manage assigned AI and Data spend, identifying opportunities for savings, demand management, supplier optimization, and commercial improvement.
  • Conduct market analysis to identify emerging AI technologies, suppliers, commercial models, pricing trends, regulatory developments, and sourcing opportunities and risks.
  • Lead strategic sourcing initiatives, including RFPs, RFQs, and RFIs, from strategy development through supplier evaluation, selection, negotiation, and contract execution.
  • Partner with sourcing category teams and cross-functional stakeholders across Technology, Data, Legal, Privacy, Cybersecurity, Finance, Risk, Compliance, and business functions where AI intersects with enterprise software, cloud, professional services, data, and other categories.
  • Source and negotiate complex AI, technology, and data agreements, including enterprise SaaS, foundation models and LLMs, agentic AI, AI-enabled SaaS, AI platforms and agents, cloud solutions, data and model licensing, and consumption-based services.
  • Evaluate AI commercial and consumption models, including token, API, GPU/compute, subscription, usage-based pricing, volume tiers, committed consumption, and usage forecasting, to understand key cost drivers and support sourcing decisions.
  • Understand evolving AI delivery and commercial models, including agentic AI, AI-enabled SaaS, and Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) models, and their implications for sourcing, pricing, contracting, and supplier management.
  • Address sourcing considerations for emerging AI models, including usage and consumption controls for agentic AI; feature bundling, licensing, and incremental charges for AI-enabled SaaS; and resource models, deliverables, knowledge transfer, intellectual property, scalability, and supplier dependency for FDE models.
  • Negotiate and manage supplier contracts and strategic relationships, balancing commercial objectives with licensing, data usage, intellectual property, privacy, security, third-party risk, AI governance, supplier performance, and innovation.
  • Develop market intelligence, benchmarks, and supplier insights to support negotiations, business decisions, and identification of commercial, licensing, operational, financial, data, technology, and third-party risks.
  • Leverage AI tools practically within sourcing, including market intelligence, supplier research, spend and commercial analysis, negotiation preparation, and category strategy development, while contributing to AI sourcing frameworks, playbooks, standards, and best practices.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of strategic sourcing, category management, or procurement experience, including ownership of indirect spend categories in a complex corporate environment.
  • Experience sourcing technology, enterprise software, cloud, data/Market Data, AI, or other complex technology-enabled solutions, including exposure to SaaS, AI platforms, model or data licensing, and consumption-based agreements.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and executing category strategies that deliver cost savings, supplier innovation, risk mitigation, and measurable business value.
  • Experience leading competitive sourcing events, including RFPs, RFQs, and RFIs, and managing supplier evaluation and selection.
  • Working knowledge of AI commercial and unit economics, including token, API, compute/GPU, subscription, consumption, model tiers, volume commitments, and usage-based pricing.
  • Practical understanding of generative and agentic AI and how AI is delivered in an enterprise environment, including foundation models, LLMs, AI agents, AI-enabled SaaS, APIs, RAG, and FDE models. The candidate does not need to be an AI engineer but should be able to engage credibly with technical teams and translate requirements into sourcing and commercial decisions.
  • Demonstrated practical use of AI tools to improve productivity, research, analytics, sourcing, negotiation preparation, or decision-making is strongly preferred.
  • Strong analytical, negotiation, and problem-solving skills with experience in commercial modeling, benchmarking, market intelligence, contract management, and supplier relationship management.
  • Understanding of sourcing considerations related to data privacy, cybersecurity, intellectual property, data and model licensing, AI governance, and third-party risk, with the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Strong written, presentation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to translate complex technical and commercial topics into clear recommendations and continuously adapt as AI technologies, suppliers, and commercial models evolve.

Job.JobDescription:
Property and Specialty Complex Adjuster

In AIG we are always looking for talent!


At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk.  Join us as a Property and Specialty Adjuster in the Claims Department to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.


Make your mark in Claims

Our Claims teams are the proven problem solvers of choice for clients, delivering consistent technical excellence and showcasing our service differentiation to create an unparalleled global claims handling experience. Through a robust stakeholder feedback loop and supported by consistent processes and leadership, we take pride in delivering responsive, fair and professional service with empathy and efficiency. 


How you will create an impact

The candidate will actively support the department in providing a customer focused, cost-efficient claims handling service by a pro-active approach to claims handling that puts customer service as the core value whilst operating within a regulatory framework.

The role will be client facing and in addition to coverage, legal liability and quantum analysis, will require interaction with brokers, insureds, external providers and internal stakeholders.


Key Responsibilities


  • Managing key claims handling enquiry; coverage determination, and quantum assessment, where appropriate within authority limits and providing a consistently strong standard of customer service
  • Ensuring effective vendor and litigation management on Complex claims
  • Broadening internal / external stakeholder communication where required
  • Striving for continuous improvement on claim file handling with feedback and support to stakeholders
  • Contributing to maintenance of best practice procedures for Property and Specialty intermediate to high value Complex claims, consistent with global best practice.
  • Demonstrate a high standard of technical claims competence.
  • Demonstrate a strong standard of competence in handling intermediate to advanced complex claims in Property and Specialty Lines of Business.
  • Timely, accurate and customer focused claim resolution, minimizing indemnity exposure and mitigating vendor and legal expense for claims of medium to high complexity
  • Consistent proactive claims handling on an ongoing basis (i.e. initial file review, investigations and coverage, negotiations and settlement, and litigation management)
  • Effective communication of key medium to high Complexity claims and messages to internal stakeholders and external stakeholders
  • Financial control through consistent reserve and other financial transaction discipline
  • Accurate and consistent policy interpretation against claims of intermediate to high complexity
  • Any other related tasks / responsibilities required by AIG.

What you’ll need to succeed

The ideal candidate should enjoy working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment with constant change and possess the following skills: 

Qualifications


  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Adminstration or the equivalent of a combination of studies and experience.
  • This position is suitable for seasoned candidates with experience in the commercial insurance industry.
  • Demonstrate strong communication skills, both written & verbal
  • Time management – ability to manage & prioritize workload and diary management
  • Ability to contribute effectively within a team environment
  • Ability to work with claims stakeholders to effectively direct claims strategy
  • Good specialist knowledge in Property and Specialty technical claims
  • Policy language skills enabling accurate and consistent policy wording interpretation
  • A strong knowledge of legal / regulatory and litigation / procedural  requirements for the lines of business
  • Strong experience in negotiating on intermediate to high complex claims and knowledge and experience in mediation, arbitration and Alternative Dispute Resolution
  • Experience in effectively following up on recommendations from technical claims audits and continuous claim handling improvement
  • Licensing — Insurance Commissioner Adjuster License required or must be obtained within 6 months of hire.

Ready to prove your potential? We would love to hear from you.

At AIG, our business spans the globe. To achieve our objectives, we must be able to navigate complex and rapidly changing landscapes with confidence. Reporting into the Chief Security Officer, this role is designed to help deliver that confidence, enabling the business to operate free from distraction. Delivering real-time exposure analysis and highly relevant proactive risk intelligence is our formula to making informed, security-based decisions. Making that work and delivering results requires the right people, structure, processes, partnerships, and evolving technology enablers.  At the core of this team is AIGs Global Security Operations Center (GSOC), responsible for asset monitoring, strategic threat detection & reporting, travel risk management, and incident response. This team acts as our around-the-clock eyes and ears; when a risk or crises event emerges, the GSOC provides real time intelligence and enhances our ability to proactively understand and mitigate risks, while always maintaining a network of partners and qualified response solutions when needed. The ideal candidate will have extensive program management and process development experience, strong international experience, and be highly collaborative. We are also seeking candidates who embrace change and innovation as a constant means to improve and evolve.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Lead AIG's global monitoring, intelligence, and response program, establishing strategic priorities, operational objectives, and long-term capabilities that protect employees, facilities, operations, and corporate reputation worldwide.
  • Serve as a principal security advisor to Global Security leadership and key business stakeholders, providing strategic counsel regarding geopolitical developments, emerging threats, security incidents, and organizational risk and exposure.
  • Define and monitor key performance indicators, operational metrics, and program maturity measures to evaluate effectiveness, identify improvement opportunities, and drive continuous enhancement of global security capabilities.
  • Constant evaluation and calibration of existing org design, process, and supporting technology stacks to best achieve the team’s core objectives.
  • Set the strategic direction and governance model for security platforms supporting executive protection, emergency notification, global incidents, travel risk, etc. 
  • Develop and maintain strategic relationships with internal stakeholders, including Human Resources, Legal, Corporate Real Estate, Facilities, Communications, Technology, Resiliency, and business leadership to ensure alignment on security priorities and response activities.
  • Manage the team’s budget, ensuring the effective allocation of resources and delivery of measurable value.
  • Lead, develop, and mentor a team of security managers, including the GSOC Operations Manager, Protective Intelligence Manager, and Travel Risk Manager, fostering a culture of operational excellence, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
  • Represent Global Security in enterprise initiatives, cross-functional projects, and external industry engagements, strengthening organizational awareness of risk and advancing security best practices across the company.
  • Maintain strong ties to Global Security, Intelligence, Diplomatic Corps, and Law Enforcement experts around the world, with access to vital benchmarks at a moment's notice.

Proactive Intelligence

  • Oversee the Protective Intelligence function, including threat monitoring, threat assessment, executive-focused intelligence support, and risk mitigation strategies designed to enhance the protection of senior leaders and other at-risk personnel.
  • Develop a repeatable and actionable threat intelligence program/suite of products designed to identify key risks to the organization, communicate potential impact to personnel and business operations, and communicate mitigation and response measures for consideration and/or operationalization.
  • Develop an effective daily horizon scanning program designed to detect and report on incidents that may impact AIG operations, employees, and/or facilities around the world.
  • Govern data repositories (travelers, meetings & events, expats, offices, etc.) to assess global exposure and support rapid, informed decision-making.

Travel Risk Management

  • Refine and maintain an effective Travel Risk Management program designed to help AIG employees conduct business anywhere in the world, free from distraction. This includes maintaining global risk rating systems, understanding and integrating with various travel management systems, development and execution of emergency communications and response plans during crises incidents, and development of concise and impactful reporting to field teams on a regular and proactive basis.

Crises Response

  • Establish and maintain enterprise response frameworks, playbooks, and operational procedures that strengthen organizational preparedness, resilience, and security response effectiveness. Train and drill the GSOC and security partners to ensure optimal readiness.
  • Deliver products and services to empower local security staff to make informed security decisions and to more effectively act as our operational lead during crises incidents large and small.
  • Manage a global network of emergency response vendors to ensure we have access to the right response capabilities, information sharing networks, advice, and equipment anywhere in the world.

 

Enhanced Monitoring & Asset Protection

  • Direct the Enhanced Facilities Monitoring program, leveraging technology and operational processes to improve situational awareness and proactively identify threats affecting critical facilities, employees, and business operations.
  • Work in partnership with Security Operations to build out site-specific procedures and escalation pathways incorporating guard services, landlord security teams, receptionists, and other key partners to maintain the security integrity of AIG office space.

 

 

 

Knowledge and Experience

  • Bachelor's or higher degree required.
  • 10+ years of experience managing a team of analysts and preferably with military, major law enforcement, intelligence, public or private sector security experience.
  • Strong drive and desire to develop and motivate teams.
  • Results oriented – positive attitude – problem solver – team oriented.
  • Experience dealing across a variety of markets - language capabilities is a plus.
  • Ability to build a strong network of intelligence resources is a must.
  • Extensive knowledge and understanding of current global geopolitical activity, threat conditions, and government structures.
  • Strong familiarity with security hardware- door technology, access control systems, security video, sensor technology stacks, and other key components.
  • Strong understanding of security intelligence capture, processing, lifecycle management, and dissemination.
  • Advanced awareness of the digital landscape and emerging threat trends across the ecosystem.
  • Business acumen and ability to drive value in a for-profit organization.

·         Well-developed communication, interpersonal and presentation skills – team building/relationship management is a key attribute and required for success.

Key Relationships

  • Internal Interactions (Within the Organization)
  • Corporate Functions - HR, Enterprise Resiliency, Real Estate, Facilities, Legal, Communications, Global Sourcing/Procurement
  • Security Operations, Security Technology, Security Investigations, Executive Protection
  • External Interactions
  • Security Industry Community (ACGS, ASIS, OSAC, DSAC, etc.)
  • Industry Peer GSOC leaders
  • Security/Crisis response vendors

 

Job Challenges

·         Ability to work both operationally and strategically.

·         To work effectively in a matrix organization and influence people not directly under job holders control.

·         Flexibility – fostering an atmosphere of trust and success in an environment where competing priorities and different strategic mindsets exist.

·         Must be able to work with and understand cultural complexities.

·         Work across multiple time zones.

 

Other dimensions

·         The job holder may be required to undertake travel.  

·         In addition to normal office hours, the job holder will need to be flexible to work outside of core office hours e.g. during operational support activities, conference calls with people in countries on other time zones or run with major security events as they develop.
