PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Quality Engineer II is an established, technical professional who serves as the Quality Engineering lead for their assigned delivery team. This role takes complete ownership of the test strategy, planning, and quality outcomes for the team, ensuring that quality is engineered into every stage of the software delivery lifecycle. Working independently with limited supervision, the QE II drives shift-left practices within the team, builds and maintains automated test solutions, and sets quality objectives that directly impact department results. The role requires practical depth in test engineering, the ability to solve difficult and moderately complex problems by drawing from prior experience, and the capacity to coordinate quality activities, delegate tasks, and coach junior team members.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the complete test strategy and test planning for the assigned Projects – defining scope, approach, risk assessment, entry/exit criteria, and test coverage targets for each release and sprint.
  • Act as the QE lead within the team and drive quality discussions during grooming, sprint planning, and design reviews; set quality objectives; and ensure the team delivers against them.
  • Develop, execute, and maintain comprehensive test plans, test cases, and test scripts for functional, regression, integration, API, and exploratory testing.
  • Build, maintain, and extend automated test suites using frameworks such as Playwright for UI, Postman/Newman for API, following clean code practice.
  • Execute API-level testing including payload validation, error handling, and contract verification for in-house and third-party service integrations.
  • Contribute automated tests to CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions), supporting continuous testing across regression, smoke, and feature validation stages.
  • Validate data integrity across integrated systems including ETL pipelines, data transformations, and end-to-end data reconciliation.
  • Identify, record, and thoroughly document defects; perform root cause analysis by reviewing logs, stack traces, and database states to diagnose systemic issues.
  • Participate in code reviews to provide quality-focused feedback on testability, error handling, and edge-case coverage.
  • Recommend enhancements to testing processes, tools, and standards to improve efficiency and effectiveness within the POD and broader team.
  • Own test data management, mock services, and QA environment configurations for reliable, repeatable test execution.
  • Leverage AI tools to assist in test case generation, coverage analysis, and failure triage.
  • Track and report quality metrics including defect density, escape rate, test coverage, and automation progress. Uses data to influence quality decisions.
  • Coordinate quality activities with distributed teams and offshore/nearshore vendor partners on test assignments, status calls, and triage.
  • Coach, guide, and review the work of junior team members; provide training on quality engineering practices and tools.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct reports but may mentor and/or train less experienced members.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, or related field (or equivalent experience); 3+ years in quality engineering or software testing with 2+ years in test automation.


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

N/A


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Practical, hands-on proficiency in at least one programming language (Java, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript) with the ability to read, understand, and debug production code.
  • Demonstrated experience designing test strategies and owning end-to-end test planning for a product, team, or release.
  • Hands-on experience building and maintaining automated tests using Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, REST Assured, or Postman/Newman.
  • Solid understanding of API testing concepts: request/response validation, status codes, error handling, and RESTful service patterns.
  • Working knowledge of SQL and database concepts – ability to write queries for data validation, verify data transformations, and support ETL testing.
  • Experience contributing automated tests to CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions) and understanding of continuous testing principles.
  • Familiarity with version control (Git), branching strategies, and pull request workflows.
  • Understanding of the test automation pyramid and strategic allocation of coverage across unit, API, UI, and data layers.
  • Exposure to performance testing concepts and tools (JMeter, k6, or equivalent).
  • Awareness of AI-assisted testing tools and willingness to adopt AI workflows for test generation and defect analysis.
  • Solid understanding of Agile/Scrum practices, shift-left testing, and the software development lifecycle.
  • Ability to work independently on moderately complex assignments with limited supervision; strong problem-solving skills drawing from prior experience and analysis.
  • Good communication skills; able to influence within the team and communicate with contacts within and occasionally outside the department.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate quality tasks, delegate work, and review the output of junior team members.
  • Preferred skills include strong Insurance domain background, specifically in Claims Management and/or Insurance Billing business workflows.


PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.  Employees are required to reach with hands and arms; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.  Employees must occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 pounds.  Employees are required to have visual acuity and be capable of operating and viewing computers and other electronic devices for extended periods of time.

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The SDET II is an established technical professional who serves as the automation platform builder within ICW Group’s Quality Engineering organization. The SDET II builds the automation infrastructure, frameworks, developer tools, and CI/CD pipeline integrations that Quality Engineers and development teams depend on. This is a code-first, engineering-heavy role – the SDET II writes production-grade software to solve quality problems at scale, enabling teams to test faster, more reliably, and with less manual overhead. Working independently, the SDET II exerts technical influence across multiple teams by delivering reusable tooling that raises the automation capability of the entire engineering organization.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Architect, develop, and maintain scalable test automation frameworks and shared libraries (Playwright, Selenium, REST Assured, TestNG) that serve as the foundation for all QE test automation across teams.

  • Write production-grade code (Java, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript) to build internal test tools, utilities, harnesses, and CLI-based test runners that abstract complexity and accelerate test authoring for QEs.

  • Design and implement self-healing test mechanisms, dynamic locator strategies, and data-driven test patterns that reduce framework maintenance burden and improve test suite resilience.

  • Develop synthetic test data generators, service virtualizers, and mock service layers that decouple test execution from external dependencies and environment availability.

  • Design, build, and own the automated test stages within CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, AWS CodePipeline, GitHub Actions) including pipeline configuration, trigger logic, parallel execution, and quality gate enforcement.

  • Build and maintain QA environment provisioning scripts, container-based test environments (Docker), and infrastructure-as-code solutions that ensure consistent, on-demand test environments.

  • Develop automated performance, load, and stress testing solutions (JMeter, k6, Locust) building reusable test harnesses that teams can configure for their specific service endpoints.

  • Partner with Software Engineers and Architects to improve application testability, advocating for testability hooks, contract interfaces, logging standards, and observable service designs during architecture discussions.

  • Build and publish internal developer documentation, framework onboarding guides, and reusable code samples that enable QEs and developers to self-serve on the automation platform.

  • Instrument test frameworks with telemetry and reporting integrations that surface automation health, execution trends, flaky test detection, and coverage metrics to engineering dashboards.

The Claims Examiner position handles a variety of claims with a focus on providing the highest level of service for policyholders and ICW Group to bring claims to an equitable conclusion within Company standards and best practice guidelines. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Manages all aspects of a moderately complex claims inventory

  • Effectively communicates with policyholders, agents, attorneys, and witnesses to gather information and provide the highest possible level of customer service.

Bachelor's degree (or equivalent combination of education and experience) required along with a minimum 1- 4+ years’ related claims or claims handling experience.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The AI Architect II is a senior technical leadership role working to modernizing the company’s technology platform. This position will provide both thought and technical leadership, influencing cloud and AI strategy while working hands-on to deliver solutions that matter. This role will make architectural decisions that have real business impact and utilize expertise to help shape the direction of a rapidly evolving organization.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Establish architectural standards, patterns, and reference architectures for AI solutions — covering RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, model serving, and AI gateway design.

  • Lead the evaluation, selection, and integration of AI/ML services and frameworks including LLMs, AI agents, and multi-agent systems using protocols such as MCP and A2A.

  • Design and implement scalable cloud architectures on AWS, leveraging serverless technologies and design patterns.

  • Define and enforce cloud architecture standards, patterns, and guardrails across development teams to ensure consistency, security, and cost optimization.

  • Collaborate with business and technology stakeholders to translate business requirements into technical architecture solutions aligned with enterprise strategy.

  • Lead systems design efforts including microservices architecture, API design, event-driven systems, and integration patterns across cloud-native and hybrid environments.

  • Evaluate emerging AI technologies and provide recommendations on adoption strategies, including generative AI, agentic workflows, and intelligent automation.

  • Develop and maintain architecture documentation, reference architectures, and technology roadmaps guiding the organization's cloud and AI transformation.

  • Provide technical mentorship and guidance to engineering teams on cloud best practices, AI implementation patterns, and modern software design principles.

  • Conduct architecture reviews, risk assessments, and proof-of-concept initiatives to validate technology decisions and drive innovation.

  • Lead application rationalization initiatives to assess, consolidate, and modernize the application portfolio, reducing technical debt and aligning technology investments with business priorities.

This position has no supervisory responsibility.

PREFERRED CERTIFICATIONS

  • TOGAF, Zachman Framework, FEAF

  • Solutions Architect Associate, Solutions Architect Professional, Machine Learning – Specialty, Data Engineer

  • SnowPro Core, SnowPro Advanced Architect

  • AI/ML, Data Engineering, DevOps, Security

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Strong understanding of AI concepts including LLMs, AI agents, agentic frameworks, Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication, and prompt engineering.

  • Hands-on experience with AWS AI/ML services: Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, Kendra, and Amazon Q Business for building and deploying intelligent applications.

  • Knowledge of LLM function calling, structured output patterns, and tool integration techniques for reliable agentic systems.

  • Familiarity with multimodal AI use cases including document understanding, image analysis, and audio processing.

  • Understanding of AI cost and performance optimization: token management, prompt caching, model quantization, and right-sizing for inference workloads.

  • Deep knowledge of AWS cloud services with emphasis on serverless architectures and design patterns.

  • Proficiency in Linux and Windows system administration including networking, storage, security, and scripting.

  • Proficiency in Python for scripting, automation, and cloud-native application development.

  • Hands-on experience with Snowflake, AWS Aurora (PostgreSQL), DynamoDB, Glue, Redshift, Athena, S3-based data lakes, and data pipeline design.

  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code tools: AWS CDK, CloudFormation, or Terraform for automated, repeatable cloud deployments.

  • Knowledge of enterprise integration patterns, RESTful API design, event-driven architecture, and microservices design principles.

  • Familiarity with DevSecOps practices including CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, container orchestration (ECS, EKS), and security-by-design.

ABOUT ICW GROUP 

ICW Group is a national, multi-line insurance carrier with an AM Best rating of 'A', approximately 1,300 employees, and headquarters in San Diego, California. ICW Group is executing an enterprise AI strategy that treats AI as core infrastructure: built on a single enterprise platform, governed by a single framework, and deployed under regulatory oversight from day one. As AI moves into underwriting, claims, and operational decisions, disciplined governance is what allows ICW to adopt AI quickly and defensibly. 

ABOUT THE AI GOVERNANCE OFFICE 

The AI Governance Management Office is ICW's standing execution and coordination function for artificial intelligence, sponsored by the SVP and Chief Digital and AI Officer. It serves the AI Governance Executive Committee (AIGEC) as its operational arm, turning AIGEC's policy, risk, and approval decisions into coordinated, well-governed delivery. The Office is the single operational home for AI intake, prioritization, coordination, enablement, and transparency.  

The Office is also ICW's single coordination point for NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool response preparation. California, ICW's domiciliary state, is participating in the 2026 NAIC pilot, which creates an active compliance window for the organization's higher-risk AI systems in underwriting and claims. 

PURPOSE OF THE JOB   

The AI Governance Manager is an advanced professional individual contributor within the AI Governance Management Office, reporting to the Director of Cloud, AI, ML, and Enablement Platforms. This dedicated position works independently with limited oversight to administer, facilitate, and execute AI governance day to day: coordinating the governance committees, operating the intake-to-decision workflow, owning the AI Hub, and maintaining the governance artifacts and evidence that keep ICW audit-ready and regulator-ready.  

Working closely with leadership and management at all levels, control functions, business owners, and external stakeholders, the AI Governance Manager makes governance practical and efficient so that teams move through it rather than around it. AIGEC and its subcommittees set policy, risk tolerance, and approvals; this role translates those decisions into consistent, well-documented execution, leads governance projects and processes, and provides guidance, coaching, and review of work products contributed by lower-level professionals and cross-functional partners. 

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 

Governance Operations and Lifecycle Management 

  • Coordinate and administer AIGEC and its AI Risk & Compliance and Third-Party AI Governance subcommittees: run the cadence (intake triage, risk review, forums), prepare review packs, and document decisions and action items to closure. 

  • Operate the intake-to-decision workflow -- apply the risk taxonomy (Tier 0 through Tier 4), move each use case through the lifecycle gates with required signoffs and triggered control-function reviews, resolve intake or escalation issues, and maintain the decision log, exception register, and escalation paths. 
     

Policy, Standards, Controls, and Inventory 

  • Maintain the AI policy, standard, procedure, and control library with clear owners and review cadence, coordinate rollout of the policy suite (including the prohibited-use list), keep governance templates current, support control sufficiency testing for Tier 1 and Tier 2 systems, and recommend process and control enhancements that improve governance performance across the function. 

  • Administer the AI Systems Registry as the single audit-ready inventory of AI use cases, models, agents, and vendor AI, enforce the registry gate before build or deploy, guide business and technical owners through registry requirements, and coordinate model and system cards with lineage and classification for higher-risk systems. 

AI Hub Ownership 

  • Own and operate the AI Hub on SharePoint as the enterprise's single front door for AI serving approximately 1,300 employees -- intake, approved tools, responsible-use guidance, governance materials, learning, and metrics -- managing the content lifecycle and running it as the interface between AIGEC and the workforce. 

NAIC Regulatory Compliance Coordination 

  • Serve as the NAIC Response Coordinator, or lead significant portions of the response, for California DOI AI Systems Evaluation Tool inquiries, coordinate cross-functional evidence collection, maintain the artifacts serving Exhibits A through D (AI Systems Registry, model cards, AI Data Element Registry with Data Services, and the risk classification methodology), and track readiness and related policy updates as the pilot evolves. 

Monitoring, Audit Readiness, and Reporting 

  • Operate the governance KPI and KRI dashboard and produce reporting for AIGEC and executive leadership, assemble audit-ready evidence packs for Tier 1 systems, run regulatory scanning (NIST AI RMF, NAIC, ISO/IEC 42001, state AI laws), and route material changes into policy and control updates with operational recommendations. 

Training, Awareness, and Change Management 

  • Coordinate role-based AI governance training, attestation, and change-triggered learning, support the governance champion network and cultural-change activities, and provide guidance, coaching, and review of governance work products to reinforce clear ownership and consistent governance behavior. 
     

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES 

This role does not have direct supervisory responsibilities. 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Information Technology, Risk Management, or related field, or equivalent experience.  

  • Minimum of ten years of experience in program or project management, governance, risk, or compliance operations within a technology, IT, or regulated environment. 

  • Demonstrated experience independently operating a governance, risk, or compliance program, including committee coordination, decision logging, evidence management, escalation management, and cross-functional process improvement. 

  • Experience with AI/ML programs, digital transformation, or technology transformation initiatives, or a strong record of ramping quickly on new governance domains. 

  • Advanced facilitation, stakeholder-management, and influencing skills, with the ability to navigate technical and business audiences at all levels of the organization, and influence practices, procedures, and policies at an operational level 

  • Proficiency with collaboration and tracking tools such as Jira, Confluence, Smartsheet, or equivalent, and experience with SharePoint content management. 

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to produce executive-level packs, dashboards, regulatory response materials, and reporting. 

  • Extensive working understanding of governance frameworks and compliance requirements in regulated industries, including the impact of governance decisions on business, technology, risk, and control functions 

  • Experience in the insurance or financial services industry preferred. 

  • Familiarity with AI governance frameworks: NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, the NAIC AI Model Bulletin, and the NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool (Exhibits A through D) preferred. 

  • Experience with NAIC regulatory requirements or Department of Insurance examination processes preferred. 

  • Familiarity with the AI and ML platforms in use at ICW (AWS Bedrock, Snowflake Cortex) and enterprise AI tools (Claude Enterprise, Microsoft 365 Copilot) preferred. 

  • Experience with SharePoint site design and enterprise portal management. 

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS  

  • Risk, audit, or governance certification such as CRISC or CGEIT, or a project and program management certification such as PMP or PgMP, or SAFe / Lean Portfolio Management preferred. 

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS 

  • Governance Discipline: Advanced ability to operate and improve governance processes, cadence, controls, and evidence, so decisions are defensible, repeatable, and scalable across the enterprise. 

  • Facilitation: Ability to run committees, reviews, and cross-functional decisions across diverse technical and business teams, and to influence operational practices, procedures, and policies within and outside the immediate job function. 

  • Detail Orientation: Meticulous attention to governance artifacts, compliance documentation, and registry data integrity. 

  • Communication: Ability to synthesize technical, business, and regulatory information into clear, actionable materials for business owners, control functions, vendors, and executive leadership. 

  • Ownership and Project Leadership: Self-directed execution across multiple concurrent governance workstreams in a fast-paced environment. 

  • Adaptability: Comfort with ambiguity and the ability to establish structure and process where none exists. 

  • Regulatory Awareness: Genuine interest in AI regulation and responsible AI, and in keeping ICW's posture current as expectations evolve. 

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS   

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk and hear.  

WORK ENVIRONMENT   

This position is based at ICW Group's Innovation Point campus in San Diego, CA. Occasional collaboration with remote team members and external partners via Microsoft Teams may be required. This position observes standard business hours with flexibility to support cross-time-zone engagements as needed.

The Scrum Master III facilitates and guides the agile practice within the product development teams. This position plays a crucial role in ensuring that the Scrum framework is effectively implemented, fostering collaboration, removing obstacles, and promoting continuous improvement between cross-functional teams. This position will be instrumental in shaping our Agile transformation journey and ensuring the successful delivery of our products in the Claims domain.


WHAT YOU WILL DO

Manages the development projects and drives sprint execution to ensure quality and timeliness. 

  • Facilitates Scrum ceremonies, including daily stand-up, sprint and release planning, sprint review, and retrospectives for two or more product teams to ensure alignment, accountability, and progress tracking.
  • Collaborates with Product Owners, Product Managers, and stakeholders to define product vision, roadmap, and priorities, and ensure alignment with business objectives.
  • Guides team in time estimating practices utilizing techniques like Planning Poker and facilitates team estimates and conversations around any differences that may crop up.
  • Manages sprint execution through effective management of Scrum board and ensures that Jiras are up to date with acceptance criteria, estimates etc.
  • Removes impediments and obstacles that hinder the team's progress, proactively identifies and addresses risks, and escalates issues as needed to ensure timely delivery of high-quality products.
  • Performs regular analysis of burndown charts and other portfolio planning tools to track velocity, team capacity, scope changes, escaped defects etc.

Manages program level risks and challenges to foster transparency and collaboration.

  • Facilitates internal communication and keeps project stakeholders up to date on progress of projects and works collaboratively to resolve people problems and project roadblocks.
  • Represents the team at broader planning and coordination sessions (e.g., Scrum of Scrums), and protects the team from uncontrolled injection of work.
  • Presents high level Sprint and Program Increment execution report for product managers. Supports product owner(s) with intra-team dynamics with respect to priorities and scope.
  • Identifies organizational impediments and systemic issues that hinder Agile adoption and team performance, and leverages influence and leadership skills to drive resolutions. Escalates to management, as necessary.
  • Works with multiple development vendor partners to build scalable products and development lifecycle processes. 

Mentors and supports scrum teams to adopt and follow agile values, principles, and practices. 

  • Serves as a change agent and advocates for Agile values, principles, and practices within the organization.
  • Stays updated on industry trends, emerging Agile practices, and Scrum frameworks to continuously enhance self and contribute to the maturity and evolution of Agile practices within the organization.
  • Facilitates Agile training, workshops, and communities of practice to enhance Agile capabilities and knowledge across the organization.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB 

The purpose of this job is to provide full-service enterprise strategic sourcing and vendor management services as well as drive operational efficiency with the strategic sourcing process by implementing tools and procedures to streamline the strategic sourcing process and support strategic enterprise initiatives. This position will manage relationships with team members and ensure the best value is achieved through the strategic sourcing process.  


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Executes on organizational goals and strategic plans for the PVMS Department.

  • Leads the execution of initiatives for the PVMS department that support the strategic sourcing goals of the organization.
  • Manages the ongoing planning and monitoring of department projects focused on efficiency, innovation, risk reduction and cost savings.
  • Plans and executes strategic sourcing, contract negotiations and vendor management activities and operations in compliance with corporate policies, applicable law, and effective cost management principles.
  • Fosters collaborative relationships with internal stakeholders involved in procurement programs.

Fosters effective procurement infrastructure and leads continuous improvement to ensure alignment with company initiatives.

  • Develops an understanding of the needs of assigned business stakeholders to generate creative solutions and persuasive arguments that deliver effective and timely procurement results.
  • Assists in the development and maintenance of policies, procedures, tools, and guidelines for the company.
  • Trains and conveys value of RFx sourcing, and contract negotiation to team members and stakeholders to ensure standards for purchasing are met.
  • Understands developing trends in the market through analysis and recommends continuous improvement processes/tools based to achieve targeted metrics for strategic sourcing, contract negotiation and vendor management success.

Leverages data to engage and educate vendors and internal customers in the policies, tools, processes, and benefits of effective procurement partnerships.

  • Prepares market analysis or data related to procurement, contracts, and vendor management as necessary. Designs and manages complex data sets and contract negotiation strategies.
  • Performs complex procurement efforts and research necessary to implement cost savings initiatives for assigned commodities via development of category strategies reflecting market conditions.
  • Uses logic and considerable independent judgment to analyze information and evaluate solutions, conclusions or approaches to execute negotiation strategies and tactics that will enhance company’s negotiation position and outcomes.
  • Develops reporting metrics tracking and management, creates presentations of information and statistics on procurement operations.

Manages procurement vendor communications and relationships.

  • Manages relationships with current and prospective vendors, and other external constituencies involved in strategic sourcing efforts.
  • Performs outreach to identify and foster potential relationships with diversity vendors.
  • Demonstrates versatility in a constantly evolving environment.
  • Serves as trusted advisor; uses influence to generate favorable positions and strategies for contract negotiations.
  • Provides recommendations to leaders on vendors, best practices, negotiations, and other aspects of procurement based on assigned categories.
  • Facilitates alignment and effective communication with internal and external stakeholders to drive optimal outcomes for the company.

Mentors new team members within the PVMS Department.

  • Provides strategic sourcing and contract negotiation mentorship and guidance to team members. 
  • Contributes to the performance management of the team directing discrete tasks.
  • Acts as a resource for team members to answer questions and provide guidance related to complex problems.
  • Ensures data quality, adherence to IT and compliance policies, and other risk-related metrics for self and guides other members of the team on these items.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES 

This role does not have supervisory responsibilities but may mentor and train junior team members.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 

Bachelor's degree from four-year college or university required in Business, Economics, or related field. Minimum 7 years of related experience in procurement, contracting and strategic sourcing processes for several commodity areas required. Minimum 3 years of experience in a role with complex vendor contract negotiations required. Experience managing the full life cycle of commodity procurement with sophisticated negotiating techniques. Experience in contracts negotiation across a variety of commodity categories. Insurance industry experience preferred. Experience in complex SaaS technology or cloud procurement preferred.


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS 

Certifications in procurement and supply management preferred, i.e., Senior Professional in Supply Management (SPSM), Certified Professional in Supply Management (CPSM), Certified Procurement Professional (CPP), Certified Supply Chain Professional (CSCP), Certified Professional Purchasing Manager (CPPM).


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

Experience effectively consulting with others, facilitating, and presenting technical information and demonstrated ability to influence others. Strong knowledge of strategic sourcing and procurement principles and techniques. Contracts negotiation experience. Experience with negotiating techniques and developing solutions to issues in a timely manner. Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications must. Must be able to effectively facilitate meetings and create presentations. Excellent interpersonal and communication. Ability to accept new ideas and embrace change. Demonstrated organizational and time management skills. Must be capable of coordinating and organizing input from various channels, perform negotiation, resolve conflicts, and build consensus at all levels of the organization. Experience working with cross-functional teams and presenting to various audiences. Ability to read, analyze, and interpret common procurement related technical journals, financial reports, and/or legal documents.  Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as probability and statistical inference. Ability to apply principles of logical or scientific thinking to a wide range of intellectual and practical problems.  Ability to combine disparate skills and thinking to craft solutions and solve operational problems.  Ability to hypothesize on root cause of inefficiencies and then test out probable solutions against those hypotheses.

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.

JOB SUMMARY

The Licensing Coordinator provides operational and administrative support for agency licensing, appointments, contracting, onboarding, and related activities. Working under established procedures and with guidance from senior staff, this role tracks documentation, updates records, responds to routine inquiries, and helps ensure assigned activities are completed accurately and on time. The position supports the onboarding of agents for current and new insurance lines of business (LOBs) nationwide.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Licensing, Appointments, and Compliance

·    Processes routine producer licensing and appointments, including assigned renewal tasks, using established procedures.

·    Verifies licensing and appointment information and assists with confirming that producers are appropriately appointed with applicable state Departments of Insurance.

·    Tracks required documentation, follows up on routine outstanding items, and maintains complete and accurate licensing and appointment records.

Agency Contracting and Onboarding

·    Supports the onboarding of new agents and agencies by collecting required information, reviewing submissions for completeness, and entering approved information into applicable systems.

·    Maintains agency and contract records, including agreements, contract terminations, and agency profile updates, in accordance with established procedures.

·    Provides administrative licensing and onboarding support for new and existing lines of business nationwide.

Agency and Cross-Functional Support

·    Responds to common questions from current and prospective agencies and business partners regarding licensing, contracting, documentation, and onboarding status.

·    Researches routine inquiries using approved resources and routes legal, interpretive, or complex questions to Underwriting, Accounting, Legal, or senior licensing staff.

·    Notifies appropriate internal departments of agency, contract, appointment, and licensing changes so that related system records can be updated.

Systems, Reporting, and Process Support

·    Enters and updates information in business systems to maintain records, process routine transactions, and support licensing operations.

·    Compiles information for weekly and monthly reports on outstanding onboarding items, licensing activity, operational metrics, and other assigned indicators.

·    Assists with special projects, process-improvement initiatives, and new lines of business by completing assigned data-entry, documentation, testing, and follow-up tasks.

·    Performs routine quality checks and promptly addresses missing, inconsistent, or potentially inaccurate information.

Administrative and Document Support

·    Processes incoming correspondence by responding to routine matters, routing items, scanning documents, and retaining records in accordance with established procedures.

·    Prepares licensing- and appointment-related payment requests and supporting documentation for approval, processing, and allocation.

·    Maintains organized electronic records and follows applicable document retention and confidentiality requirements.

 

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibilities

 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

High school diploma or general education degree (GED) required. Associate’s degree preferred. Minimum 2 years’ related experience.

 

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

None required

 

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

•         Working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite and the ability to learn database and workflow systems, including Majesco or similar platforms.

•         Good communications skills (verbal and written) with ability to provide courteous, accurate customer service to internal and external contacts.

•         Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and the ability to manage assigned priorities and deadlines.

•         Ability to follow documented procedures, maintain accurate records, protect confidential information, and escalate questions appropriately.

•         Effective interpersonal and collaboration skills, with the ability to work constructively across teams and with external partners.

 

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

This role is performed in an office environment. Employees are regularly required to sit, stand, walk, talk, and hear. No unusual physical or environmental demands are associated with the position.

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB 

The purpose of this job is to oversee the complete lifecycle recruitment process, including candidate sourcing and assessment, onboarding, and maintaining good hiring practices. This position exists to attract and place high-quality talent across the enterprise while providing exceptional candidate experiences to promote the brand and generate engagement to support Human Resources (HR) initiatives.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Participates in the execution of Corporate Talent Attraction strategies.

  • Coordinates the placement of ads utilizing online job boards, internal job postings, and school postings.
  • Recommends and participates in proactive recruitment strategies, such as college relations, job fairs, and military recruiting as warranted.
  • Creates and maintains contacts within the insurance and related industries.
  • Participates in networking groups and other business and community programs to increase skill and market knowledge.
  • Assists in the creation and execution of social media and relationship-building strategies to secure pre-employment interest and loyalty to the organization.
  • Places and maintains internal and external job postings for all positions, including technical roles, through schools, professional organizations, technical communities, and other sources in alignment with the Recruiting Plan.

Manages the candidate selection and onboarding process.

  • Sources qualified candidates for assigned and other positions using the most effective means, including internal and external job boards such as LinkedIn, Indeed, communities, professional associations, schools, or other target sources to minimize the use of agencies and provide high-caliber candidates.
  • Uses the most efficient and effective method of recruiting based on the position's requirements.
  • Works closely with Hiring Managers and HR Business Partners to determine staffing needs, role requirements, and timeliness of the recruitment process.
  • Maintains regular contact with possible future candidates and develops pipelines for recurring and hard-to-fill roles.
  • Pre-screens and recommends candidates to hiring managers, assessing relevant technical experience and competencies.
  • Works with the Talent Coordinator to schedule interviews and arrange travel as needed.
  • Notifies leadership of any concerns related to candidate experience, hiring practices, or the recruitment process.
  • Closes candidates and negotiates salary and hiring terms. Prepares offer letters and secures acceptance.
  • Participates in New Hire Orientations as needed in partnership with Learning and Development.
  • Creates and documents technical talent leads within a centralized tracking system and follows up with leads to convert them into active candidates.

Engages in Team Member Process Management and Talent Acquisition programs.

  • Works with the Sr HR Administrator on the visa process for new employees.
  • Partners with the Talent Coordinator on all aspects of temporary employee placement.
  • Supports HR and Recruiting projects as necessary.
  • Promotes the Employee Referral Program, including outreach for hard-to-find technical talent.
  • Supports relationships with academic institutions, technology programs, and community partners to build future talent pipelines.
  • Engages ICW Group Team Members to promote insurance technology careers and Company opportunities.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES 

This role does not have supervisory responsibilities.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 

Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university required, with a major or emphasis in Human Resources, Business, or a related field. An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered in lieu of a degree. Minimum 2 years of related talent acquisition/recruiting experience required, including experience supporting or recruiting for corporate roles.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

Working knowledge of professional HR recruiting in a fast-paced environment; corporate and technical recruiting experience preferred. Exposure and desire to engage in social networking strategies to engage potential talent. Sourcing experience using Indeed, LinkedIn Recruiter, GitHub, Stack Overflow, technical communities, or other job boards, Boolean searches, and networking groups. Ability to understand technical job requirements and evaluate candidate experience across software engineering, infrastructure, cybersecurity, data, cloud, and related disciplines. Creative thinker who can develop new ideas and build them into successful actions. Demonstrated skills in negotiating, multitasking, organization, and execution; current knowledge of recruiting best practices and California, federal, and local labor laws relative to staffing; sophisticated interpersonal skills that project optimism, a “can-do” spirit, and fun, with the ability to adapt style depending on the situation. Strong verbal communication skills; demonstrated good judgment; solid project management skills; competence in technology and Microsoft Office applications. Familiarity with Applicant Tracking Systems.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS  

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear. 


WORK ENVIRONMENT  

This position is based on-site, on a hybrid schedule, at our San Diego headquarters. This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Claims Specialist position is responsible for handling complex claims with a focus on providing exceptional service for stakeholders in order to drive claims to an equitable resolution within Company standards.  The Claims Specialist works with a sense of urgency, understands insurance coverage concepts, and navigates the legal system with the support of counsel to drive strategic outcomes.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Manages complex claims inventories requiring advanced technical expertise and strategic claim handling  

  • Effectively communicates with policyholders, agents, attorneys, and witnesses to gather information and provide the highest possible level of customer service.
  • Promptly investigates claims to determine exposure, works with appropriate experts and makes strategic recommendations.
  • Utilizes appropriate resolution tactics (e.g., mediation, negotiation, denial, litigation or offer) to proactively drive outstanding results.
  • Operates within the requirements of related state and/or the governing entity rules and regulations as well as internal claims handling policies and procedures. 
  • Directs defense counsel throughout the litigation process in line with ICW litigation guidelines while monitoring legal fees and costs.

 All Claims Specialists:

  • Consistently provides exceptional customer service
  • Effectively collaborates with cross-functional Team Members for project and process discussions
  • Makes recommendations for streamlining processes and adopting the industry’s best practices
  • Ensures accuracy of data in claims system for compliance with applicable regulatory reporting
  • Provides knowledge transfer across the organization
  • Continuously seeks to improve technical skills by attending job related training and tracking current case law. 
  • As a SME (subject matter expert), serves as a technical resource and mentors/trains less experienced Team Members

Workers’ Compensation Claims (Specific Responsibilities):

  • Prepares and presents claims status reports for internal and external stakeholders.
  • Administers timely and appropriate benefits to injured workers; manages and approves payment of benefits within designated authority level.  Works within applicable state rules, regulations as well as ICW Group’s internal claims handling policies and procedures.
  • Creates and adjusts reserves in a timely manner to ensure reserving activities are consistent with company policies.
  • Resolves claims fairly and equitably, acting in the best interest of the insured while providing timely benefits to injured workers as required by law.
  • Supports specialty claim handling programs and strategic initiatives involving complex litigation, medical exposure, catastrophic injuries, fatality, PTD, or long-duration claims
  • Provides technical guidance and collaborates with leadership on complex claim resolution strategies and specialty handling initiative
  • Identifies and drives resolution opportunities on complex or long-duration claims through proactive settlement, reserving, and medical management strategies.


SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibility


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree (or equivalent combination of education and experience) required along with a minimum of 8 – 10+ years’ related claims handling experience involving complex litigation, reserving, settlement strategy, and high exposure claims. 


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Workers’ Compensation: Certification that meets the minimum standards of training, experience, and skill required. WCCA and WCCP preferred. State Workers Compensation License is required in some branches.



KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

  • Excellent understanding of laws and jurisdictional restraints to manage claims
  • Excellent verbal communication skills, time management, attention to detail and organizational skills
  • Must be adept at learning new technology
  • Flexibility to adapt to changes in a fast-paced environment

Must have the ability to:

  • Read, analyze, and interpret technical and legal documents
  • Write reports and business correspondence
  • Respond to common inquiries or complaints from customers (insured), claimants and regulatory agencies
  • Present information at meetings, to management and clients
  • Solve practical problems and deal with a variety of variables in situations where limited standardization exists

Workers’ Compensation: Advanced knowledge of workers’ compensation claims handling, reserving, litigation management, and resolution strategies



PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear. 

WORK ENVIRONMENT 

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB 

The purpose of this job is to prepare and analyze financial information to provide accurate and useful information to management for review and provide insight to management to help in overall decision making. This position exists to ensure accounting processes and financial statements are completed thoroughly and accurately, while aligning with Company standards. 


The Reinsurance Accountant supports the accurate and timely accounting for the Company’s assumed reinsurance portfolio. This role processes and reviews broker bordereaux and statements, records premium, loss, commission and cash activity in accordance with the underlying treaties, prepares and reconciles reinsurance general ledger accounts, and supports month-end, quarter-end and year-end close. This position combines accounting skills with an operational mindset: it manages a steady flow of high-volume, deadline-driven work, tracks items from receipt through to resolution, and keeps handoffs between teams clean. The Reinsurance Accountant works closely with brokers, Operations, Underwriting, Actuarial and Internal Audit, and contributes to the controls and process improvements that keep reinsurance financial information accurate, complete and aligned with Company standards.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Reinsurance Process and Analysis

  • Enters and reviews broker bordereaux (BDX) and statements, including premium, losses, commission and brokerage, and completes the review checklist for each item. 
  • Records initial premium booking with allocation of premiums to annual statement lines (ASL), along with premium adjustments and endorsements; calculates premium earnings. 
  • Records claims and loss activity reported on bordereaux and statements, including allocation of losses to ASL, and confirms that cash is cleared only after the related claim is recorded. 
  • Ensures all recorded transactions are in line with the reinsurance contract. 
  • Monitors contractual reporting timing and payment terms and applies and settles cash to and from various brokers. 
  • Follows up with broker accounting departments on delayed or large payments, exception payments and complex premium or claim bordereaux; sets up trust accounts and collateral as required; and flags reporting or accounting anomalies. 
  • Monitors the shared intake folder and mailbox for incoming broker bordereaux, statements and correspondence daily, and logs and tracks each item from receipt through to completion. 
  • Manages a workload of high-volume transactions against processing deadlines and service targets, prioritizing items by due date, size, and complexity. 
  • Coordinates handoffs with Operations and Underwriting (for example, claims and cash calls) so that no item is left unentered or unowned between teams. 
  • Builds and maintains relationships with the accounting departments of brokers and clients as needed. 

 

Accounting Operations and Reconciliations 

  • Prepares income statement, balance sheet, consolidated and other accounting statements and reports. 
  • Reviews general ledger accounts, prepares journal entries, and reconciles reinsurance accounts between the reinsurance administration system and the general ledger. 
  • Identifies, researches, resolves and follows up on reconciling items, including any inefficiency in department policies and procedures. 
  • Analyzes financial reports and records, and makes recommendations relative to the accounting of reserves, assets, and expenditures. 
  • Maintains and manages an assigned section of the statutory financial statements. 

Process Improvement and Governance 

  • Follows internal controls, including segregation of duties, and does not review or approve their own entries. 
  • Reviews and verifies the accuracy of journal entries, bordereaux entries and accounting classifications entered by others, and documents and escalates errors or omissions found. 
  • Assembles, creates and reconciles month-end accounting entries, resolving discrepancies. 
  • Prepares asset, liability and capital account entries by compiling and analyzing account information. 
  • Maintains desk procedures, checklists and tracking logs, and follows up on aged or outstanding items (such as unreconciled cash or outstanding premium) until they are resolved. 
  • Supports internal and external audits by preparing documentation and responding to requests. 
  • Demonstrates effective communication and problem-solving skills, and contributes ideas and tools that improve department processes, including checklists, automation and review procedures. 
  • Accurately passes internal information to state agencies and works with them to make sure requirements are completed. 

Financial Reporting & Analysis 

  • Prepares ad-hoc reinsurance reports and memos as required by management. 
  • Assists in the preparation of the Quarterly and Annual Statement Schedule F. 
  • Updates and reconciles all reinsurance-related general ledger accounts. 
  • Calculates and records quarterly adjustments, such as commuted treaty reserve adjustments and reinsurance reserves, and uploads changes in ceded reinsurance reserves to the general ledger. 

 

 SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES  

This role does not have supervisory responsibilities. 

 

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE  

  • Bachelor's degree from four-year college or university preferred, with a major or emphasis in Accounting, Finance, or related field.  
  • Minimum 2 years of related experience in Accounting; or equivalent combination of education and experience required.  
  • Experience in insurance or reinsurance accounting or operations preferred. 

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS  

None required.  

 

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS 

  • Working knowledge of General Accounting, Accounts Payable (A/P), Accounts Receivable (A/R) and/or in an entry-level accountant role, required.   
  • Understanding of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) regulations.  
  • Operational orientation, with experience in process-driven, high-volume, or workflow-based work and comfort managing queues, deadlines and handoffs between teams. 
  • Strong attention to detail, with the ability to review work for accuracy and identify errors and omissions. 
  • Proficiency in Excel for tracking, reconciling and analyzing data. 
  • Proven ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, and to interact effectively with management, employees, brokers and auditors. 
  • Ability to work independently and meet stringent deadlines. 
  • Willingness to adopt new tools and automation to improve review and reconciliation processes.  
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite applications. 

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS   

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.   

 

WORK ENVIRONMENT   

This position operates in an office environment and requires the frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, and other standard office equipment.

The purpose of this job is to create deliverables that help develop target-state guidance (standards, guidelines, reference implementations) for evolving the data infrastructure across the enterprise in order to enable business strategy, knowledge worker productivity, improve customer experience and business decision-making, and deliver targeted business outcomes. This position exists to provide the leadership, facilitation, analysis and design tasks required for the development of an enterprise's data architecture.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 

Leads efforts to develop and maintain the architectural assets for the data domain including current and target state data architectures.

  • Sets an architecture direction for the data domain that is aligned with business goals. Leads presentations for the organization.
  • Maintains a holistic view of data assets by creating and maintaining blueprints that illustrate how data is stored, processed, and accessed.
  • Ensures data solutions are in alignment with data architecture principles and target state.
  • Oversees end-to-end data asset lifecycle management activities. Drives collaboration efforts and capitalizes on the talents of others to achieve established goals.
  • Facilitates and orchestrates the delivery of targeted business outcomes through architectural decisions. Leads the creation of models, architecture design work products, and new technology innovation initiatives within area(s) of responsibility and for the enterprise.
  • Leads the design, documentation, and analysis of the business architecture in their area and provides recommendations to ensure the delivery of an integrated, holistic solution.   

Collaborates with enterprise, solution, and domain architects to understand the implications of respective architectures on data architecture and maximize the value of information across the organization.

  • Works with senior stakeholders and subject matter experts in driving effective data management standards and policies across the organization.
  • Provides recommendations on business information that will need to be available and shared consistently across the organization through the identification, definition, and analysis of how information assets aid strategies and business outcomes.
  • Assists data and analytics leaders, and business and IT leadership in developing data strategy, and governance processes and structures.
  • Leads the creation of models, technical standards, and architecture design work products within area(s) of responsibility. Leads technology portfolio prioritization efforts and owns the management of technology portfolio within area(s) of responsibility.
  • Expands the use and successful delivery of information across the enterprise, resulting in improved decision making. 

Provides strategic recommendations to maximize the value of enterprise data assets, including the external data ecosystem through data exploitation, envisioning data-enabled strategies and enabling business outcomes through analytics, data and analytics governance, and enterprise information policy.

  • Evaluates and recommends emerging technologies for data management, storage, and analytics.
  • Provides insight into the relationship of data to business objectives, applications, technology, principles, and standards.
  • Represents enterprise architecture by advocating and sharing knowledge. Builds credibility for an initiative by presenting evidence and ensuring that individuals affected are included in the process at the outset.
  • Participates as a member of one or more architectural review boards (ARB) that ensure architecture quality and compliance.
  • Leads short and long-term initiatives and road mapping efforts that drive change and gains support for proposed solutions. Sets goals, strategic vision, and leads others work. Questions current assumptions and seeks out-of-the-box solutions to challenges.  

Contributes to the design, documentation, and analysis of the data architecture in area(s) of responsibility to ensure the data portfolio operates more simply and reliably.

  • Works with Head of Architecture and acts as a leader to influence enterprise direction/approach and the strategic planning process. Coaches and mentors others and assists with problem resolution.
  • Acts as an expert and sets the current and future state information architecture(s). Seeks out a wide range of views on the topic to refine options, which they communicate to key stakeholders.
  • Educates business and IT partners on information architecture. Contributes ideas and makes recommendations to improve the process followed for work product by making it more efficient and effective.
  • Researches, proposes, and champions new technology innovation initiatives in the organization. Creates and advances the data architecture vision and strategy.
  • Leads the design, documentation, and analysis of the technical and integration architecture practice to ensure the infrastructure runs efficiently and effectively.
  • Leads project-level architectural reviews and ensures alignment with architectural deliverables, principles, strategies, and standards.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Security Architect II is a senior individual contributor within the Enterprise Architecture team who develops and influences enterprise security architecture direction and establishes frameworks and reusable guidance within assigned areas of responsibility to support the operationalization of security across the enterprise. The role translates business objectives, risk priorities, and regulatory obligations into practical security capabilities, standards, reference architectures, and implementation patterns. Working across business, technology, security, infrastructure, data, and delivery teams, the Security Architect II promotes consistent risk-based decisions and ensures security is designed into enterprise platforms, cloud environments, applications, integrations, data solutions, and emerging AI capabilities.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


Develops and influences enterprise security architecture and strategic direction.

·   Develops, maintains, and communicates enterprise security architecture frameworks, principles, target-state architectures, reference architectures, roadmaps, and reusable security patterns.

·   Maps business goals, risk appetite, regulatory obligations, and enterprise strategy to security capabilities and technical implementation direction.

·   Partners with enterprise, solution, cloud, data, integration, infrastructure, and AI architects to embed security into technology strategies and solution designs.

·   Defines current-state and target-state security capabilities, identifies gaps and dependencies, and recommends sequenced initiatives to improve enterprise security maturity.

·   Provides architecture guidance for identity and access management, zero trust, network and cloud security, application security, data protection, cryptography, secrets management, logging and monitoring, resilience, vulnerability management, and third-party technology risk.

·   Creates decision records and clearly documents security trade-offs, assumptions, risks, compensating controls, and required follow-up actions.


Defines and maintains security standards, guidelines, and procedures.

·   Develops and maintains enterprise security standards, guidelines, control patterns, and procedures within assigned areas of responsibility and contributes to broader enterprise security direction, ensuring the resulting guidance is actionable, internally consistent, and aligned with enterprise policy.

·   Uses recognized frameworks and principles such as NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST SP 800-53, NIST Zero Trust Architecture, ISO/IEC 27001 and 27002, CIS Controls, and secure-by-design practices as appropriate to the organization.

·   Develops and maintains minimum security requirements and approved patterns within assigned areas of responsibility for AWS services, cloud accounts, networking, identity, encryption, key management, secrets, workload protection, observability, and incident readiness.

·   Contributes to exception and risk-acceptance criteria and partners with Security, Risk, Compliance, and technology owners to ensure deviations are explicit, time-bound, and appropriately approved.

·   Maintains traceability among business objectives, security risks, policies, standards, architecture decisions, technical controls, and implementation evidence.


Provides security architecture governance and solution guidance.

·   Performs and documents security architecture reviews for strategic initiatives, platforms, products, vendor solutions, integrations, and material technology changes.

·   Presents security-significant decisions and recommendations to the Architecture Review Board and other governance forums.

·   Engages early in initiative planning and solution design to identify threats, misuse cases, trust boundaries, attack paths, security requirements, and control responsibilities.

·   Advises teams on secure architecture patterns without displacing accountable engineering, cybersecurity operations, risk, privacy, legal, or business owners.

·   Evaluates vendor products and services, including security capabilities, architectural fit, data handling, integration requirements, operational dependencies, and concentration risk.

·   Mentors architects and technical teams, builds security architecture competency, and serves as a trusted advisor on complex or high-impact decisions.


Advances AI security architecture.

·   Defines security architecture guidance for AI and generative AI solutions, including data protection, identity and authorization, model and supply-chain risk, prompt injection, tool misuse, and unintended data disclosure.

·   Develops risk-based security patterns for AI applications and agentic workflows within assigned areas of responsibility, including adversarial testing, monitoring, human oversight, and controls that constrain autonomous actions.

·   Collaborates with data, privacy, legal, risk, and AI governance stakeholders to align AI security controls with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, the NIST Generative AI Profile, OWASP guidance, business impact, and acceptable risk.


SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct supervisory responsibilities. The role provides technical leadership, architecture mentorship, and influence across teams and initiatives.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

·   Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field required. Equivalent relevant experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.

·   Minimum 8 years of progressively responsible IT or cybersecurity experience required.

·   Minimum 4 years of experience in security architecture, cloud security architecture, enterprise architecture, or solution architecture with substantial security responsibility required.

·   Demonstrated experience defining security standards, reference architectures, technical controls, and architecture roadmaps in a complex enterprise environment required.

·   Hands-on or architecture-level experience with AWS security services, identity and access management, network security, application security, data protection, security monitoring, and secure cloud adoption required.

·   Experience supporting regulated industries, financial services, or property and casualty insurance is preferred.

·   Experience with AI, machine learning, generative AI, or agentic-system security and governance is preferred.


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, AND REGISTRATIONS


One senior-level security or security architecture certification is required. CISSP is preferred as the baseline credential. Relevant alternatives or advanced credentials may include:

·   ISC2 Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Information Systems Security Architecture Professional (ISSAP), or Certified Cloud Security Professional (CCSP).

·   AWS Certified Security - Specialty or AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional.

·   GIAC Defensible Security Architecture (GDSA), GIAC Cloud Security Architecture and Design (GCSA), or another relevant GIAC certification aligned to the role.

·   ISACA Certified Information Security Manager (CISM) or Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC).

·   AI security training or certification, such as GIAC AI Security Automation Engineer (GASAE), is desirable when supported by relevant practical experience.


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

·   Advanced knowledge of security architecture principles, threat modeling, zero trust, defense in depth, least privilege, secure-by-design, privacy-by-design, and risk-based control selection.

·   Strong working knowledge of NIST, ISO, CIS, cloud security, and enterprise architecture practices; ability to tailor frameworks rather than apply them mechanically.

·   Advanced knowledge of AWS security architecture and cloud-native control patterns.

·   Knowledge of application and API security, identity federation, privileged access, network segmentation, encryption, key management, secrets management, logging, monitoring, incident readiness, vulnerability management, and software supply-chain security.

·   Working knowledge of AI security risks and controls across data, models, prompts, retrieval, tools, agents, infrastructure, monitoring, and human oversight.

·   Ability to translate business goals, regulatory obligations, and risk scenarios into clear architecture requirements, technical standards, roadmaps, and solution options.

·   Ability to communicate strategic and tactical perspectives and explain complex security topics to executives, business leaders, architects, engineers, and control functions.

·   Strong facilitation, negotiation, written communication, presentation, and stakeholder-management skills.

·   Ability to operate as a self-directed senior individual contributor while collaborating effectively across architecture, cybersecurity, engineering, operations, risk, compliance, legal, privacy, and audit teams.

·   Ability to balance risk reduction, delivery speed, user experience, cost, resilience, and operational supportability.

The AWS Cloud Engineer IV will collaborate closely with various teams, including development, operations, and security, to create and implement automation processes and standards for AWS cloud services. This position will ensure that all infrastructure components meet performance and security standards, conduct systems tests, develop and maintain design and troubleshooting documentation. This role will participate in the creation of new policies and procedures for cloud service use and compliance. The AWS Cloud Engineer IV will provide technical support for the AWS platform, working to improve capabilities and ensure the optimal operability of the AWS infrastructure.

The Legal Operations & Analytics Manager is responsible for the strategic management of ICW Group's outside (panel) counsel network across all lines of business. This role monitors the annual defense spend on Workers' Compensation, General Liability, Auto Liability, Coverage, and Bad Faith litigation. This position oversees the outside counsel panel, manages a data-driven performance framework to monitor law firm effectiveness and outcomes, governs e-billing and invoice compliance, and identifies opportunities to leverage artificial intelligence and legal technology to improve claim outcomes, enhance operational efficiency, and optimize litigation spend while maintaining defense quality.


Outside Counsel Panel Management & Governance 

  • Provides strategic oversight of ICW Group’s outside counsel panel across insurance offerings encompassing Workers' Compensation, General Liability, Auto Liability, Coverage, and Bad Faith, including panel selection standards, performance expectations, tiering, geographic coverage and specialty expertise.  
  • Leads the Request for Proposal (RFP) process as well as firm onboarding/offboarding. Negotiates rates  including alternative fee arrangements (flat fee, blended rate, success-based structures) where appropriate based on claim severity and complexity. 
  • Serves as the primary relationship owner for panel firms, balancing cost discipline with the need to maintain strong defense relationships and good litigation quality. 

Legal Spend & Budget Management 

  • Manages the Workers' Compensation defense budget and builds out comparable spend visibility and budget ownership for GL, Auto, Coverage, and Bad Faith as programs are onboarded. 
  • Partners with Finance / Claims leadership for quarterly and annual forecasting of outside counsel spend by line of business and severity band. 
  • Identifies and executes cost-reduction opportunities without compromising claim outcomes.  

Performance Analytics & Objective Scorecards 

  • Leads the design, administration, and ongoing refinement of ICW Group's Defense Attorney Scorecard, leveraging objective, weighted KPIs to assess law firm performance, outcomes, efficiency, and cost effectiveness across severity bands. 
  • Translates law firm performance results into actionable panel management recommendations, including counsel assignment, referral, and In-House Counsel utilization strategies. 
  • Partners with Data Science and Analytics to enhance performance measurement frameworks, validating and incorporating emerging indicators of legal outcomes, efficiency, service quality, and litigation effectiveness. 
  • Delivers executive-level reporting and trend analyses on law firm performance, litigation spend, and panel effectiveness, providing strategic insights to Claims leadership and key stakeholders. 

Billing Governance, E-Billing & Compliance 

  • Establishes and oversees outside counsel billing policies and standards, promoting cost discipline, transparency, and compliance across all lines of business. 
  • Conducts billing analytics and invoice audits to identify cost-saving opportunities, improve billing efficiency, and ensure legal services are aligned with agreed-upon engagement standards. 
  • Manages the e-billing program, ensuring efficient invoice processing, effective controls, and clear communication of billing requirements to both internal stakeholders and outside counsel. 

AI & Legal Technology Enablement 

  • Partners with Claim Strategy & Operations and IT to assess, pilot, and deploy AI-driven solutions that improve legal operations, spend management, and litigation efficiency. 
  • Establishes the strategic roadmap for AI adoption within legal operations, prioritizing opportunities to streamline workflows, enhance productivity, and improve organizational outcomes. 
  • Evaluates outside counsel adoption of AI and related legal technologies, incorporating their impact on efficiency, value, and pricing into panel management and engagement strategies. 

Coverage & Bad Faith Program Build-Out 

  • Develops the governance and vendor management framework required to extend ICW Group’s data-driven legal operations model to Coverage and Bad Faith litigation.  
  • Works closely with stakeholders to manage counsel selection, bad faith escalation protocols, and performance monitoring tailed to the unique risk profile of these matters.  

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Reporting 

  • Acts as a strategic connector across Claims, Legal, Finance, and Analytics functions, facilitating data-driven decisions related to outside counsel performance, legal operations, and spend management. 
  • Produces and delivers executive-quality analytics, scorecards, dashboards, and presentation materials that communicate litigation performance, legal spend, and key business trends. 
  • Evaluates evolving litigation trends and market developments across Workers' Compensation, General Liability, Auto Liability, Coverage, and Bad Faith matters, incorporating insights into panel oversight and long-term legal operations strategy.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have supervisory responsibilities.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field required (or equivalent combination of education and experience).  J.D., paralegal certification, or equivalent legal operations credential preferred.
  • Minimum of 7 years’ experience in legal operations, outside counsel management, or claims litigation management, preferably within a P&C or workers' compensation insurance carrier.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

None required.
