Do you enjoy managing relationships and employing your critical thinking skills? Underwriters perform the critical function of evaluating the acceptability of risk and determining appropriate pricing for insurance products. The Business Insurance (BI) Underwriting Professional Development Internship Program provides students with an amazing opportunity to gain exposure to this critical function at Travelers. The 10-week program (running from early June to mid-August) provides qualified interns with an excellent opportunity to gain first-hand commercial insurance underwriting experience, receive valuable on-the-job training, and learn more about the property and casualty insurance industry from industry professionals. Given that, we are seeking interns that are serious about entering the insurance industry and who are excited about the prospect of making underwriting their future career choice. This role is a potential pathway to our full-time Underwriting Professional Development Program (UPDP). Housing assistance is not provided.

What Will You Do?

  • Complete challenging and meaningful project work over the course of this program at the discretion of your manager. You may work independently or with other interns and will be asked to present your findings to local leadership. Sample projects include a territorial risk assessment to determine profitability and underwriting opportunities as well as a business process analysis to determine underwriting gaps.
  • Learn to leverage modern analytical and artificial intelligence (AI) tools/platforms with the ability to apply critical thinking to evaluate limitations related to quality and accuracy of AI-assisted outputs.
  • Learn about other areas at Travelers such as Risk Control, Claims, and related corporate functions. Interns may also engage in agency visits with Account Executives.

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Job.JobDescription:
Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$136,100.00 - $224,500.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

The Sourcing and Supplier Management (S&SM) team drives enterprise-wide sourcing strategy, supplier governance, and supplier risk management across Travelers' technology and operations supplier portfolio. This multi-disciplinary team manages Travelers' global sourcing and supplier relationships, and is accountable for implementing strategic sourcing models that optimize supplier relationships and deliver measurable business outcomes.

This Senior Director leads S&SM's Sourcing Risk & Operations function, managing a team responsible for supplier risk reviews, business continuity and disaster recovery (BC/DR) planning, offshore development center (ODC) management, site audits, and various other supplier operations and governance functions. The Risk & Operations team is shifting from a reactive, process-facilitation model to a proactive, portfolio-based approach to supplier risk management - this role is accountable for leading that transition and for building the frameworks, cadence, and team capability needed to deliver a holistic, enterprise view and approach to risk management for these suppliers.

Additionally, this role will play a key role in expanding Sourcing and Supplier Management's strategic partnership role with Tech & Ops platform and product partners, enhancing governance frameworks and relationship management protocols. Additionally, the role encompasses developing and maintaining executive briefing materials that provide leadership visibility into strategic vendor partnerships and performance outcomes.

This senior director role is also a key member of the extended S&SM leadership team, which is responsible for developing and executing Tech & Ops sourcing strategies that align supplier selection, relationship management, and strategic sourcing models with enterprise objectives. The position partners closely with Line of Business Technology & Operations leadership and cross-functional stakeholders - including SLT/ELT, Procurement, Legal, and Workforce Management. Leveraging Travelers' scale and strategic positioning, this role partners with technology and business leaders on managed services models, sourcing strategies, and supplier selection aligned to workforce planning initiatives.

This position manages a team.

What Will You Do?

  • Supplier Risk Program Leadership & Proactive Risk Monitoring: Own end-to-end supplier risk management for the Tech&Ops strategic supplier portfolio - including risk reviews, due diligence, and ongoing monitoring. Lead the team's transition from reactive, case-by-case process facilitation to proactive, portfolio-based oversight that gives S&SM and Tech & Ops leadership a holistic, enterprise view of supplier risk exposure. Drive continuous improvement to how the work is completed, emphasizing value-add activities and approaches while reducing reactive, manual work wherever possible.
  • Portfolio Design and Management: Develop a portfolio-based approach to Tech&Ops strategic supplier population, including a framework for determining which suppliers are in-scope, how suppliers align to portfolios, what level of governance/operational support are required for each supplier, and how to align portfolios to team members. Lead the growth of the team's role in ongoing supplier governance - identifying opportunities to add value, deepen the team's knowledge of the supplier's footprint, and partner to help business stakeholders drive the most value from each supplier relationship. Leverage S&SM's mature professional services sourcing (GSO) program to drive the development of a strategic, substantive approach to Tech&Ops non-GSO strategic providers.
  • Executive Briefings: Lead the development, maintenance and continued improvement of briefing materials for senior executives within Tech&Ops, in partnership with stakeholders across the organization, ranging from the supplier's executive sponsor to leaders responsible for day-to-day operations with the supplier, to procurement, finance and legal. Ensure materials are comprehensive, provide a holistic view of the total supplier footprint, and include timely, actionable information; additionally, prepare distilled talking points as required to summarize key aspects of each supplier relationship to support senior executive meetings.
  • BC/DR and Incident Management: Manage business continuity and disaster recovery planning and readiness across S&SM's strategic suppliers, including partnering with BC/DR stakeholders to plan and facilitate annual tabletop testing, drafting/disseminating communications to strategic suppliers in connection with incident management/DR events, and identify opportunities to improve BC/DR preparedness.
  • ODC Management, Site Audits & Other Operational Controls: Oversee oversight of Travelers' offshore development center footprint, evaluating site changes - capacity shifts, technology updates, operational control changes - for risk and operational impact, and directing site audits toward the areas of greatest control exposure. Own SOC review outcomes for strategic professional services partners, assessing findings for substantive risk and driving suppliers to remediate gaps rather than simply tracking review completion.
  • Team Leadership: Lead and manage the Sourcing Risk & Operations team, setting direction, priorities, and performance expectations. Build team capability - through coaching, role clarity, and tooling - to support the shift to portfolio-based risk management.
  • Maintain substantive, current knowledge of strategic suppliers' delivery capabilities, fit within our priorities and roadmaps and competitive positioning.
  • Serve as a credible, technically substantive counterpart to supplier leadership and delivery teams - able to engage directly rather than operating solely through account managers or relationship cadence.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Procurement, Legal, Workforce Management, and Tech & Ops leadership to align supplier risk and governance frameworks to enterprise objectives.
  • Participate in the Enterprise Supplier Management Steering Committee and represent Risk & Operations in enterprise governance forums.
  • Define and consult on risk measurement strategies, scorecards, and reporting cadence across the organization.
  • Maintain awareness of supplier risk indicators and emerging industry/regulatory trends, surfacing anomalies and risks proactively to senior leadership rather than waiting for escalation.
  • Support ad hoc analytical requests and special projects aligned to S&SM's strategic priorities.
  • Serve as the point of resolution for supplier risk issues, audit findings, or governance gaps prior to leadership review.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Typically 9+ years of Finance, Audit, Procurement or Sales/Servicing related experience.
  • Master's or other advanced degree.
  • Thorough knowledge of project management processes.
  • Thorough knowledge of business law, legal contracts and various financial issues including cash flow and working capital.
  • Intermediate to advanced proficiency of eSourcing and Ariba procurement applications.
  • Intermediate to advanced proficiency of MS Access, Excel, PowerPoint and Word.

What is a Must Have?

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience.
  • 8 years of supplier management or related experience.
  • Advanced communication skills, advanced computer literacy and ability to analyze and resolve complex issues.
  • Ability to successfully operate in a team and in a fast-paced environment.
  • Requires a demonstrated record of initiative, problem solving, and change management.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences.

What Is the Opportunity?

As an Auto Salvage Coordinator, you will play a critical role in managing the end-to-end salvage process, ensuring timely and compliant disposal of total loss vehicles while maximizing asset recovery value. In this role, you will collaborate closely with salvage vendors, appraisers, and claim handlers to coordinate title work, manage vendor expenses, and uphold state titling laws and regulations. Your attention to detail and organizational expertise will directly contribute to accurate claim file management and outstanding customer outcomes.

What Will You Do?

  • Prepare and process title documentation and required paperwork for timely submission to the appropriate salvage vendor.
  • Evaluate and determine the most appropriate disposal method for salvage assets in accordance with applicable state titling laws and regulations. Establish follow-up activities to ensure prompt and efficient sale of the asset.
  • Review and audit vendor invoices to ensure accurate and appropriate expense management. Proactively review invoices for billing discrepancies, and engage the salvage vendor, Appraiser or Claim Handler to assist in negotiation to achieve fair and reasonable outcomes.
  • Review credit and debit transactions posted to the claim file to ensure accuracy.
  • Verify proper execution of inbound titling documents, and appropriately process payments for customers. Resolve improperly executed title documents and proactively contact relevant parties to obtain missing or incomplete transferable ownership documentation, including keys, to successfully resolve the salvage.
  • Establish minimum bids utilizing the salvage vendor pricing system, entering accurate data to ensure reliable pricing results. Provide counter bids as appropriate and re-list vehicles in accordance with established office guidelines to maximize recovery value.
  • Review auto sale listings to verify accuracy of sale data including loss type, area of damage, vehicle year, make, model, and percentage of damages. Evaluate vehicle photos for image quality, OEM or aftermarket parts, missing equipment, inconsistencies with accident facts or auto appraisal, and odometer readings where applicable.
  • Perform sale price audits by monitoring internet auto auctions to validate sale prices against gross proceeds and ensure competitive asset returns.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date salvage capture screens throughout the claims process and document all claim file activity not captured within the system, ensuring current and precise data integrity at all times.
  • Manage left-with-owner (LWO) vehicle dispositions and resolve associated title issues in accordance with local office workflows and procedures.

What Is the Opportunity?

Member of the Sourcing and Supplier Management team within Tech & Ops Finance responsible for enterprise-wide sourcing and supplier strategies, governance, performance management, risk and operational processes for Travelers' global sourcing and supplier relationships.

As a Manager, Sourcing Strategy, Management and Governance, you will play a critical role in executing work order processes across assigned business lines and area-specific strategic sourcing strategies, including sourcing model design, supplier selection, and alignment of suppliers to business needs across our professional services and outsourcing partner portfolio. You will serve as a key point of contact on execution of sourcing strategy, workforce demand, and supplier performance across assigned lines, partnering closely with business stakeholders to track activity, resolve issues, and identify opportunities to improve how the team operates. This position does not manage others.

What Will You Do?

  • Work Order/Vendor Management and Sourcing Strategy: Manage a defined set of supplier work orders or portfolio activities across multiple assigned lines, including intake, modifications, closures, data-driven analysis, and process and tool optimization. Serve as a proactive sourcing advisor to LOB stakeholders, providing counsel on sourcing model selection, supplier performance, and workforce demand planning. Apply enterprise sourcing models and rate card structures to work being requested, advising stakeholders on right model, right supplier, right rate.
  • Onboarding and Team Support: Oversee resource onboarding and monitor engaged resources for quality, progress, and team dynamics. Own resource onboarding end-to-end, including understanding the skills required for the work being engaged, validating skill requirements with LOB stakeholders, and driving Technical Assessments. Cultivate ongoing, trusted relationships with the owners of the work, including engagement managers and LOB stakeholders, staying close enough to the business to anticipate needs, flag risks early, and bring forward solutions before issues escalate. Partner with Circle Leads on resource and team alignment needs.
  • Proactivity and Risk Management: Monitor assigned vendor performance data and flag early indicators of risk or control gaps, addressing delivery issues as they arise and escalating when appropriate. Analyze work order data, supplier capability changes, and sourcing market conditions to identify business continuity risks, surface insights, and deliver proactive recommendations to leadership. Maintain deep understanding of assigned business lines to anticipate workforce needs, monitor internal demands, and inform sourcing strategy.
  • Internal and External Stakeholder Engagement: Build and sustain trusted relationships with business stakeholders, finance partners, and assigned supplier contacts to surface risks, resolve delivery concerns and budget variances, and support governance interactions, performance discussions, and sourcing process coordination. Provide data and updates supporting ELT visibility for assigned lines on execution of sourcing strategy, workforce demand, and supplier performance.
  • Work Transition and Migration: Own the operational execution of work transitions when sourcing decisions result in a change of supplier, sourcing model, or workforce composition. This includes coordinating the migration of work from internal resources to external suppliers, managing supplier transitions, supporting onboarding of new supplier teams, and ensuring continuity of delivery throughout the transition period. Partner closely with LOB stakeholders, DFRs, and the S&SM Strategy team to sequence and execute transitions in alignment with enterprise sourcing strategy and workforce plans.
  • Process Optimization: Identify and implement process improvements and automation opportunities, including AI-enabled workflow enhancements. Optimize like work across assigned lines, standardizing repeatable processes, eliminating redundancy, and driving consistency across the Sourcing Delivery and Execution team. Champion the use of Travelers' AI tooling to streamline reporting, automate recurring workflows, and improve the quality and speed of work.
  • Rate Card Adherence: Ensure compliance with established enterprise sourcing models and rate card structures. Partner with the S&SM Strategy team to validate that work being requested aligns to the appropriate rate card, role designation, and sourcing model, and assist stakeholders in understanding and adhering to rate card guidelines.
  • Track and report on sourcing footprint, role utilization, team composition, and premium role usage across assigned lines.
  • Manage sourcing activity across multiple assigned lines or areas. Bring cross-line perspective to sourcing decisions, identify patterns and efficiencies across the portfolio, and ensure consistent application of enterprise sourcing strategy regardless of line-specific variation.
  • Monitor work order alignment to budget; proactively flag variances and partner with DFRs to resolve.
  • Contribute to the preparation of Business Review materials and Monthly Operating Review (MOR) data for assigned lines, supporting leadership visibility into supplier performance, workforce trends, and sourcing activity across the portfolio.
  • Partner cross-functionally with LOB stakeholders, DFRs, and Procurement to support sourcing and contracting activity, ensure alignment on budget and resource plans, and facilitate resolution of issues that span organizational boundaries.
  • Engage with and learn Travelers' AI tooling, applying these capabilities to improve the speed and quality of recurring work such as reporting, data analysis, and workflow management.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience required.   
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in sourcing, workforce strategy, supplier management, or a related field.
  • Experience with Fieldglass, ACS, and workforce planning tools strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting or managing work transitions, supplier migrations, or sourcing model changes preferred.
  • Familiarity with rate card structures, role modernization concepts, and supplier performance principles.
  • Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with senior LOB or technology leaders.
  • Experience identifying and implementing process improvements or automation opportunities.
  • Familiarity with AI-powered tools and large language models (e.g., Claude); demonstrated ability or willingness to integrate AI capabilities into day-to-day work processes preferred.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite, including Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Strong working knowledge of sourcing models: managed services, staff augmentation, GSO, POD/catalog models, and rate card structures.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage complex, ambiguous situations and drive to resolution with senior stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to evaluate sourcing data, identify trends, and translate findings into actionable recommendations for business partners.
  • Process improvement and automation orientation, with experience identifying and implementing operational efficiencies.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills, comfortable engaging with senior LOB leaders and building trusted advisor relationships.
  • Demonstrated initiative in identifying and adopting tools, technology, and process improvements that increase team efficiency and output quality, including AI-enabled solutions.
  • Demonstrated proficiency or willingness to actively develop proficiency with AI-powered tools, including large language models such as Claude; ability to apply these tools to sourcing workflows, reporting, and operational tasks to improve efficiency and output quality.
  • Ability to operate effectively through change and ambiguity, adapting approaches as the function evolves.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present information clearly to stakeholders at all levels.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and in a team environment.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, multiple workstreams, and deadlines simultaneously in a fast-moving environment.

What is a Must Have?

  • Three years of experience Supplier Management, Finance, Audit, Procurement, or a related field.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

You will deliver optimal results for Travelers' insured customers and will mentor less experienced attorneys.

Venues for this role typical cover Southwest & Central Georgia including but not limited to Macon, Columbus, and Warner Robbins.

What Will You Do?

  • In the independent handling of a caseload of higher exposure cases and most complex litigation matters, including Major Case and Complex Claim depending on line of business, your responsibilities will include:
  • Leverage trial experience to apply effective use of litigation skills and techniques to try cases to verdict or negotiate resolution.
  • Conduct advanced legal research and demonstrate strong and persuasive legal writing and presentation skills.
  • Draft substantive pleadings, motions, briefs, discovery and other legal documents.
  • Attend court events, depositions, and other appointments independently.
  • Provide in-depth, substantive case analysis and recommendations to insured clients and Claim partners on file handling strategies.

  • Provide internal and external training, seminars and legal updates to insured clients and Claim partners.

  • Travel as required to meet business needs.

  • Strong aptitude for trying cases to a jury; proven track record of litigating jury trials, with a history of successful courtroom outcomes
  • Demonstrates strong technical knowledge in the practice area(s) and the ability to effectively communicate complex information on litigated matters to diverse audiences.
  • Advanced oral and written advocacy skills, with a demonstrated track record of summary judgment and/or appellate successs.
  • Possesses in-depth knowledge of the bench, bar, local jurisdictional practices, adversaries.

  • Demonstrates strong leadership through mentoring and influencing skills.

What Is the Opportunity?

In this role, you will serve as a trusted resource and will deliver exceptional customer service by providing clear explanations of policies and coverage options while investigating and evaluating claims to ensure accurate payments.

What Will You Do?

  • Manage auto physical damage claims from first notice of loss through resolution and settlement, handling low to moderate complexity cases, including total loss evaluations and vehicle repair oversight. Types of claims are typically multi-vehicle (2 or more cars) auto damage with unclear liability and no injuries.
  • Evaluate and analyze policy terms, conditions, and exclusions to determine coverage, liability, and damage; negotiate equitable settlements within your authority.
  • Coordinate and partner with appraisal team(s) and repair facilities to obtain necessary information and ensure thorough accurate damage assessments and timely claim resolution.
  • Leverage all internal and external resources to conduct thorough investigations to gather all relevant facts accurately document findings in the claim management system and maintain accurate records of claim activity in claim management systems.
  • Determine settlement amounts based upon appraisal estimate, negotiate and convey claim settlements within authority limits to insureds and claimants. As appropriate, write denial letters, Reservation of Rights and other necessary correspondence to insureds and claimants.
  • Provide timely and professional communication to customers, representatives, and internal stakeholders.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts, particularly in the areas of AI while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • Acquire and maintain relevant Insurance License(s) to comply with state and Travelers' requirements within three months of starting the job.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

  • Ability to exercise sound judgement and make effective decisions.

  • Demonstrated conflict resolution skills; ability to facilitate productive discussions and reach equitable outcomes.
  • Ability to manage stress, navigate difficult situations, and maintain composure and professionalism under pressure while always taking accountability for decisions.
  • Basic understanding of insurance principles and terminology, state insurance regulations and claim handling requirements.
  • Ability to quickly learn from experience and apply it to new situations with speed and flexibility.

  • One year auto claim handling experience or comparable claim experience, or successful completion of Travelers Auto Claim Representative training program.

Are you curious by nature? Do you enjoy managing relationships and employing your critical thinking skills? Underwriters perform the critical function of evaluating the acceptability of risk and determining appropriate pricing for insurance products. The Business Insurance (BI) Underwriting Professional Development Internship Program provides students with an amazing opportunity to gain exposure to this critical function at Travelers. The 10-week program (running from early June to mid-August) provides qualified interns with an excellent opportunity to gain first-hand commercial insurance underwriting experience, receive valuable on-the-job training, and learn more about the property and casualty insurance industry from industry professionals. Given that, we are seeking interns that are serious about entering the insurance industry and who are excited about the prospect of making underwriting their future career choice. This role is a potential pathway to our full-time Underwriting Professional Development Program (UPDP).
Housing assistance is not provided.

What Will You Do?

  • Within your assigned business unit, each intern will be given a designated coach and be expected to:
  • Complete core assignments and training modules geared toward insurance and underwriting principles.
  • Participate and complete self-paced professional development courses in time management, presentation skills, and other key areas.
  • Complete challenging and meaningful project work over the course of this program at the discretion of your manager. You may work independently or with other interns and will be asked to present your findings to local leadership. Sample projects include a territorial risk assessment to determine profitability and underwriting opportunities as well as a business process analysis to determine underwriting gaps.
  • Learn to leverage modern analytical and artificial intelligence (AI) tools/platforms with the ability to apply critical thinking to evaluate limitations related to quality and accuracy of AI-assisted outputs.
  • Learn about other areas at Travelers such as Risk Control, Claims, and related corporate functions. Interns may also engage in agency visits with Account Executives.
  • Participate in the Enterprise Internship experience which includes Executive Speaker Series, Networking events, and Rising Senior Intern Symposium.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

  • Preferred cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above.
  • Obtained or pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Economics, Finance, Liberal Arts (with business focus preferred), Management, Marketing, Risk Management and Insurance.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office.

What Is the Opportunity?

National Property provides tailored property protection solutions for high value, complex risks across a wide array of industries. The Account Executive Officer (AEO), National Property will partner with agents and brokers to provide coverage for new and renewal business based on customers' needs. This role is seen as a technical resource. As an AEO, you are decisive, detail-oriented, and know how to build relationships internally and externally to drive results. Your ability to independently assess complex risk and sell our products in challenging markets will contribute to the profitability and success of Travelers.

What Will You Do?

  • Manage the profitability, growth, and retention of an assigned book of business.
  • Underwrite and skillfully negotiate complex customer accounts to minimize risk and maximize profitability. Additionally, occasionally negotiate and procure reinsurance to underwrite complex accounts.
  • May facilitate the placement of foreign admitted policies, serve as a resource to field Account Executives on global underwriting capabilities, as well as assist in the business development activities for such global underwriting services.
  • Cultivate and maintain relationships with internal partners within the business unit and across the enterprise to create sales plans and identify cross-selling opportunities.
  • Foster and maintain relationships with external partners by regularly meeting in person with agents and brokers to market and sell Travelers products with a goal of writing and retaining accounts consistent with our risk appetite. Must be able to travel to such meetings.
  • Identify and capture new business opportunities using consultative marketing and sales skills.
  • Independently develop and execute agency sales plans and frequently partner with your Managing Director (MD) to develop region/group sales plans.
  • May assist in the training and mentoring of less experienced Account Executives.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's degree.
  • Six to eight years of relevant underwriting experience with experience in National Property.
  • Deep knowledge of property-related products, the regulatory environment, and the local insurance market.
  • Deep financial acumen.
  • Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to proactively identify underwriting, marketing, or financial challenges and analyze available information to make timely decisions in alignment with our risk appetite.

1

What Is the Opportunity?

Applications for this posting will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. now and in the future. The company does not sponsor/support H-1B petitions, TN, or Forms I-983/STEM OPT, for this role. Applications for this posting will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Are you curious by nature? Do you enjoy managing relationships and employing your critical thinking skills? Underwriters perform the critical function of evaluating the acceptability of risk and determining appropriate pricing for insurance products. The Business Insurance (BI) Underwriting Professional Development Internship Program provides students with an amazing opportunity to gain exposure to this critical function at Travelers. The 10-week program (running from early June to mid-August) provides qualified interns with an excellent opportunity to gain first-hand commercial insurance underwriting experience, receive valuable on-the-job training, and learn more about the property and casualty insurance industry from industry professionals. Given that, we are seeking interns that are serious about entering the insurance industry and who are excited about the prospect of making underwriting their future career choice. This role is a potential pathway to our full-time Underwriting Professional Development Program (UPDP). Housing assistance is not provided.

What Will You Do?

  • Within your assigned business unit, each intern will be given a designated coach and be expected to:
  • Complete core assignments and training modules geared toward insurance and underwriting principles.
  • Participate and complete self-paced professional development courses in time management, presentation skills, and other key areas.
  • Complete challenging and meaningful project work over the course of this program at the discretion of your manager. You may work independently or with other interns and will be asked to present your findings to local leadership. Sample projects include a territorial risk assessment to determine profitability and underwriting opportunities as well as a business process analysis to determine underwriting gaps.
  • Learn to leverage modern analytical and artificial intelligence (AI) tools/platforms with the ability to apply critical thinking to evaluate limitations related to quality and accuracy of AI-assisted outputs.
  • Learn about other areas at Travelers such as Risk Control, Claims, and related corporate functions. Interns may also engage in agency visits with Account Executives.
  • Participate in the Enterprise Internship experience which includes Executive Speaker Series, Networking events, and Rising Senior Intern Symposium.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

  • Preferred cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above.
  • Obtained or pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Economics, Finance, Liberal Arts (with business focus preferred), Management, Marketing, Risk Management and Insurance.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office.

Job.JobDescription:
Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$0.00 - $22.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. now and in the future. The company does not sponsor/support H-1B petitions, TN, or Forms I-983/STEM OPT, for this role.

Applications for this posting will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

The Bond & Specialty Insurance (BSI) Underwriting Internship Program provides qualified interns with an excellent opportunity to gain first-hand experience, receive valuable on-the-job training and learn more about the property & casualty insurance industry.

What exactly is an Underwriter? Insurance is the contractual transfer of financial risk from one party to another. Underwriters (Account Executives) are the heart of the insurance process, gathering and researching pertinent information and then using finely tuned analytical skills to evaluate the acceptability of business and institutional risk. However, underwriters are more than just analysts - they are the core relationship builders with our agents and clients. They are responsible for managing a profitable portfolio of business through our distributing agents and brokers. An underwriting career includes a dynamic blend of analytical and marketing skills - it's challenging, stimulating and a superb career choice.

BSI provides management liability, professional liability and surety to businesses of all sizes. It also provides traditional property casualty coverages to financial institutions, and is organized into six separate and distinct business units which include:
-Commercial Surety (protects a third party from the failure of an insured to perform or fulfill an obligation)
-Construction Services (insuring the bond between contractors and clients)
-Financial Institutions (insurance for community banks, credit unions, insurance companies, investment advisors and large depository & non-depository institutions)
-Private/Non Profit Liability (insurance products for private companies and non-profit institutions)
-Professional Liability (coverage protects against liability claims for negligence, errors and omissions in the performance of professional services)
-Public Company Liability (insurance products crafted to address the diverse management liability exposures faced by today's public companies.)

Positions last approximately 10-12 weeks beginning in late May/early June and ending in mid-August.
Housing assistance is not provided.

What Will You Do?

The Bond & Specialty Insurance (BSI) Underwriting Internship Program provides qualified interns with an excellent opportunity to gain first-hand experience, receive valuable on-the-job training and learn more about the property & casualty insurance industry.

What exactly is an Underwriter? Insurance is the contractual transfer of financial risk from one party to another. Underwriters (Account Executives) are the heart of the insurance process, gathering and researching pertinent information and then using finely tuned analytical skills to evaluate the acceptability of business and institutional risk. However, underwriters are more than just analysts - they are the core relationship builders with our agents and clients. They are responsible for managing a profitable portfolio of business through our distributing agents and brokers. An underwriting career includes a dynamic blend of analytical and marketing skills - it's challenging, stimulating and a superb career choice.

BSI provides management liability, professional liability and surety to businesses of all sizes. It also provides traditional property casualty coverages to financial institutions, and is organized into six separate and distinct business units which include:
-Commercial Surety (protects a third party from the failure of an insured to perform or fulfill an obligation);
-Construction Services (insuring the bond between contractors and clients);
-Financial Institutions (insurance for community banks, credit unions, insurance companies, investment advisors and large depository & non-depository institutions);
-Private/Non Profit Liability (insurance products for private companies and non-profit institutions);
-Professional Liability (coverage protects against liability claims for negligence, errors and omissions in the performance of professional services);
-Public Company Liability (insurance products crafted to address the diverse management liability exposures faced by today's public companies.) Positions last approximately 10-12 weeks beginning in late May/early June and ending in mid-August.
Housing assistance is not provided.

What Will You Do?

  • Each intern will be expected to complete challenging and meaningful project work over the course of this program. In addition, there are core assignments and a designated coach to further develop interns' knowledge of insurance underwriting, sales and marketing.

What Is the Opportunity?

The Sales Executive Team is dedicated to navigating and managing a high performing sales culture in person and/or virtually which contributes to the overall success of the Select business. The team executes on industry-leading sales strategies aligned with business objectives, builds effective relationships with customers, distribution partners and fellow employees, and creates tactical sales plans for profitable growth through extensive product knowledge and state of the art sales and influencing tactics. The team also uses digitally advanced strategies to move the business forward, leads the relationships with our aggregator/networking groups, and partners with the agent to imbed into higher producing revenue streams. As a Sales Executive, Select, you will manage and develop a moderately complex group of Travelers agency assignments/territories, optimize growth within defined new business, retention and profitability goals and deliver success within Travelers' framework of Corporate values. You will act as a brand ambassador to sell the Travelers value proposition to distribution partners. This position is an outside sales position where assigned distribution relationships within the geographic territory tend to be best served through an in-person sales strategy.

What Will You Do?

  • Develop and implement comprehensive sales strategies to expand and manage a portfolio of business, with the objective of driving profitable growth.
  • Own assigned territory, including business development, leveraging performance metrics to create annual plans and manage territorial performance.
  • Conduct in-depth agency diagnostics to assess performance and identify growth opportunities.
  • Facilitate agency appointments and build long-term relationships through office visits (both in person and virtual).
  • Prospect, onboard and set performance goals for new agencies, while providing training and support.
  • May pre-qualify accounts as needed.
  • Influence agency partners through effective communication and negotiation skills.
  • Collaborate with internal teams, such as, Product and Underwriting to ensure alignment of sales strategies with business objectives.
  • Understand Travelers Enterprise focus and seize opportunities to cross-sell Travelers products by discussing with business partners in other lines. May identify book transfer opportunities.
  • Develop knowledge of competitor products and capabilities and local market trends.
  • Utilize advanced data and analytics for sales decisions and performance measurement, leveraging extensive knowledge of Travelers' systems and platforms to support the sales process.
  • Leverage AI technologies to optimize industry processes, enhance decision-making, and drive innovation, while continuously learning and adapting to emerging AI trends and tools.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's degree in sales, marketing, business or related field.
  • Four or more years of insurance sales or related experience managing a book of business, driving significant sales growth, achieving sales targets, conducting agency diagnostics and utilizing digital sales tools.
  • Certified Insurance Counselor (CIC) (or willingness to pursue).
  • Strong knowledge of Travelers products and general Property & Casualty marketplace.
  • Strong influencing and negotiation skills to encourage agency partners to adopt Travelers products and services.
  • Proven ability to collaboratively build and maintain relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders both internally and externally.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to define goals and priorities and meet these goals in a timely manner.
  • Exceptional organizational skills to manage complex tasks and priorities to meet sales goals and deadlines effectively.

What is a Must Have?

  • Three years of professional experience in sales, sales support or relevant insurance field.
  • Must live in the territory that they manage and have the ability to travel up to 75% of the time.

When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.

What Is the Opportunity?

Travelers is seeking a Senior Software Engineer, Guidewire BillingCenter, to join our organization as we grow and transform our billing technology landscape. We are looking for a Guidewire BillingCenter engineer with strong integration development and configuration experience. The individual will complete advanced, end-to-end engineering tasks within Guidewire BillingCenter and related integrations, including designing, developing, configuring, analyzing, testing, debugging, troubleshooting, documenting, health monitoring/alerting, and implementing solutions based on user or system specifications. The individual will also consult with users and partners to define functional and technical specifications for Guidewire BillingCenter, manage the effective use of resources, act as a subject matter expert for BillingCenter and associated services, leverage deep Guidewire and business knowledge to drive the planning and execution of complex billing modernization initiatives, actively participate in the design and development process, and provide technical leadership to the broader Guidewire delivery team. The role also includes working with business and technical teams to clarify requirements, investigate defects, and deliver reliable solutions, and it requires the ability to work in a fast-paced, high-demand, visible environment across multiple teams.

What Will You Do?

  • Perform complex analysis, advanced level design and configuration, and develop functionality within Guidewire BillingCenter for high visibility, high impact initiatives.
  • Configure, troubleshoot, and support multiple BillingCenter functional areas.
  • Take the lead on designing and implementing solutions for moderately complex, loosely scoped billing and payments problems aligned with team and business goals.
  • Serve as a Technical Lead on key initiatives, delivering efforts both independently and by leading other team members.
  • Play a key role in a large 2027 transformation program, migrating from an in-house, mainframe-based billing platform to Guidewire BillingCenter.
  • Lead investigation, diagnosis, and resolution efforts for critical, high impact problems, defects, and incidents within BillingCenter and related integrations, while working with business and technical teams to clarify requirements.
  • Act as a technology advocate, identifying opportunities to leverage Guidewire capabilities, cloud technologies, and, where applicable, AI to improve billing processes and business outcomes.
  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship on Guidewire BillingCenter and modern engineering practices while fostering a collaborative, Agile team environment.
  • Apply knowledge of Guidewire events, batch processing, and integration patterns, as well as current industry and cloud trends, to design and deliver effective solutions.
  • Seek opportunities to continuously expand your technical knowledge of Guidewire, AWS, and Agile delivery practices.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • 5+ years of hands-on programming/development experience.
  • 5+ years of experience with Guidewire BillingCenter, including configuration and integration.
  • Technical Skills & Domain Expertise
    • Deep experience with Guidewire BillingCenter configuration, integrations, and extension.
    • Hands-on experience developing and supporting integrations with Guidewire BillingCenter.
    • Experience with commission calculation configuration and troubleshooting, invoice logic and document mapping, and payment management, including configuration and issue resolution.
    • Strong knowledge of Guidewire events and batch processing.
    • Experience acting as a Technical Lead on complex initiatives, ideally in billing, payments, or policy administration domains.
    • Experience working in Agile environments (e.g., Scrum/Kanban) and using modern DevOps practices (CI/CD, automated testing).
    • Experience with AWS (or another major cloud provider), including designing, deploying, or supporting cloud-hosted applications and integrations.
    • Experience with Java and/or GOSU for Guidewire development.
    • Exposure to or hands-on experience with AI/ML capabilities and how they can be applied to billing or financial operations.
    • Prior experience with or understanding of mainframe-based systems, especially in modernization or migration to Guidewire.
  • DeliveryAdvanced delivery skills, including the ability to:
    • Determine the software design strategy and methodology for Guidewire BillingCenter efforts.
    • Use automated tests, analysis, and informed feedback loops to ensure quality and production readiness before release.
    • Monitor the health of BillingCenter components and adjacent systems, addressing issues proactively.
  • Problem SolvingStrong problem solving skills, including the ability to:
    • Use data, experimentation, and proofs of concept to find creative solutions to complex billing and integration challenges.
    • Reflect on implemented solutions, measure their impact, and use those insights to iterate and optimize.
    • Make sound decisions that involve multiple complex factors and broad business/technical implications.
  • CommunicationExcellent communication skills, including the ability to:
    • Translate Guidewire and cloud technical concepts into language that is clear and meaningful to business partners.
    • Document initiatives in a concise, clear, and structured manner.
    • Collaborate effectively with engineers, product owners, architects, and business stakeholders across multiple teams.
    • Quickly identify and articulate core issues in discussions and meetings.
    • Give and receive constructive feedback, raise issues and challenges constructively, offer support when asked, and ensure all voices are heard; listen attentively and with empathy.
  • LeadershipAdvanced leadership skills, including the ability to:
    • Take ownership and drive work forward even when there is no clearly defined owner.
    • Lead and mentor engineers in Guidewire BillingCenter and modern engineering practices.
    • Inspire, motivate, and align team members around common goals, particularly during large transformation efforts.

What Is the Opportunity?

As an Outside Auto Appraiser, you are responsible for physically inspecting damaged vehicles, estimating repair costs, working closely with repair facilities, and determining and settling the actual cash value of total loss vehicles to ensure accurate and timely claim settlements. In this customer-facing role, you will need to have a high level of technical expertise in vehicle damage assessment, strong customer service skills, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment. This position will serve as a technical resource for auto claim staff and will provide advice and direction to claim professionals on claim damages to achieve optimal outcomes. This position is based remotely with work at residential and/or commercial locations with a combination of mobile work, work from your primary residence, or the nearest Travelers office.

What Will You Do?

  • Inspect and assess vehicle damage resulting from accidents, weather events, or other covered losses by conducting thorough virtual or on-site inspections at body shops or customer locations.
  • Perform estimate review work, conduct virtual inspections, and collaborate with repair facilities to ensure accuracy, consistency, and quality across claims.
  • Prepare accurate repair estimates using industry-standard estimating software to determine the cost of parts, labor, and materials required to restore vehicles to pre-loss condition.
  • Evaluate and settle vehicle total losses by determining actual cash value (ACV) through market research, comparable vehicle analysis, and application of appropriate valuation tools and methodologies.
  • Negotiate repair costs and settlements with body shops, customers, and third-party claimants to reach fair and timely resolutions while maintaining quality repair standards.
  • Identify and document pre-existing damage, prior repairs, and potential fraud indicators to ensure accurate claim evaluation and protect company interests.
  • Collaborate with claim representatives, body shops, and vendors to coordinate repairs, authorize supplements, and resolve coverage or repair-related issues.
  • Provide exceptional customer service by explaining the appraisal process, answering questions, assisting in moving claims towards timely resolution, and keeping vehicle owners informed throughout the claim lifecycle.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts, particularly in the areas of AI while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Active adjuster license, where applicable.
  • Two years of auto physical damage appraisal experience.
  • Proficient in claims management and estimating software, with advanced skills in Microsoft Office and enterprise technology systems and platforms.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to convey information clearly and professionally.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgement and make effective decisions.
  • Exceptional customer service skills and commitment to providing a positive experience for customers throughout the claim process.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills; ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated conflict resolution skills; ability to facilitate productive discussions and reach equitable outcomes.
  • Ability to manage stress, navigate difficult situations, and maintain composure and professionalism under pressure while always taking accountability for decisions.
  • Basic understanding of insurance principles and terminology, state insurance regulations and claim handling requirements.
  • Ability to quickly learn from experience and apply it to new situations with speed and flexibility.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED required.
  • One year of auto physical damage appraisal or comparable claim related experience or successful completion of required Travelers Claim Representative training program.
  • Valid driver's license.

What Is the Opportunity?

This position is responsible for representing the interests of the clients in the litigation of disputed Workers Compensation claims. Provides client services as part of a legal team. Independently provides aggressive case handling with a resolution focus. Remains current on related legal and regulatory governances and changes.

What Will You Do?

  • Independently handles a full to moderate caseload with low to moderate level of severity and complexity from case inception through trial/resolution with limited support.
  • Handles hearings, court events, and other appointments independently as jurisdictionally appropriate.
  • Conducts legal research as necessary.
  • Independently drafts pleadings, motions, briefs, discovery and other file documents.
  • Interprets and analyzes medical reports or bills/invoices and provides disability ratings and/or other Official Medical Fee Schedules where jurisdictionally applicable.
  • Provides recommendations and case analysis to business partners and clients on appropriate file handling strategy.
  • Builds and maintains superior internal and external client relationships.
  • Completes all required administrative tasks including time reporting, closed cases, and other reports appropriate to performance of job duties.
  • Effectively utilizes and adapts to available technology, case management system and automation in the practice of law.
  • Meets annual billable hour expectations.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree or law degree.
  • 7+ years of workers compensation claim or legal experience
  • 5+ years hearing rep experience with strong litigation focus
  • Strong understanding of jurisdiction's Workers Compensation law and litigation procedures.
  • High proficiency in using legal research software (e.g Westlaw, Pacer) and Microsoft Office.
  • Strong and persuasive legal writing and oral advocacy skills.
  • Strong organizational skills.
  • Strong evaluation and negotiation skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and also effectively with others in a team environment.
  • Ability to analyze legal issues with minimal supervision.

Applications for this posting will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Are you curious by nature? Do you enjoy managing relationships and employing your critical thinking skills? Underwriters perform the critical function of evaluating the acceptability of risk and determining appropriate pricing for insurance products. The Business Insurance (BI) Underwriting Professional Development Internship Program provides students with an amazing opportunity to gain exposure to this critical function at Travelers. The 10-week program (running from early June to mid-August) provides qualified interns with an excellent opportunity to gain first-hand commercial insurance underwriting experience, receive valuable on-the-job training, and learn more about the property and casualty insurance industry from industry professionals. Given that, we are seeking interns that are serious about entering the insurance industry and who are excited about the prospect of making underwriting their future career choice. This role is a potential pathway to our full-time Underwriting Professional Development Program (UPDP). Housing assistance is not provided.

What Will You Do?

  • Within your assigned business unit, each intern will be given a designated coach and be expected to:
  • Complete core assignments and training modules geared toward insurance and underwriting principles.
  • Participate and complete self-paced professional development courses in time management, presentation skills, and other key areas.
  • Complete challenging and meaningful project work over the course of this program at the discretion of your manager. You may work independently or with other interns and will be asked to present your findings to local leadership. Sample projects include a territorial risk assessment to determine profitability and underwriting opportunities as well as a business process analysis to determine underwriting gaps.
  • Learn to leverage modern analytical and artificial intelligence (AI) tools/platforms with the ability to apply critical thinking to evaluate limitations related to quality and accuracy of AI-assisted outputs.
  • Learn about other areas at Travelers such as Risk Control, Claims, and related corporate functions. Interns may also engage in agency visits with Account Executives.
  • Participate in the Enterprise Internship experience which includes Executive Speaker Series, Networking events, and Rising Senior Intern Symposium.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

  • Preferred cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above.
  • Obtained or pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Economics, Finance, Liberal Arts (with business focus preferred), Management, Marketing, Risk Management and Insurance.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office.

In that capacity, you are accountable for EXO's engagement model, emerging demand pipeline, vendor and contract strategy, operational metrics our leadership team makes decisions from, and a team of Delivery Leads embedded across the portfolio. You will also help define how the team builds, bringing AI-native practices into product discovery, delivery and the full analytic development lifecycle.
At Travelers, we're focused on expanding the application of data and analytics beyond managing risk, helping businesses increase their productivity and efficiency and enabling great experiences for our customers and agents. As the Director, Business Insights Delivery, you will lead the strategic direction to ensure technical capabilities fit long-term business partner roadmaps. You will build highly complex data stories and present to management to enable sound decision making. You will leverage your negotiation skills to come to optimal solutions with business partners that align capabilities within the portfolio to business value. What Is the Opportunity?

Are you curious by nature? Do you enjoy managing relationships and employing your critical thinking skills? Underwriters perform a critical function of evaluating the acceptability of risk and determining appropriate pricing of insurance products. The Underwriting Apprenticeship Program provides students with the amazing opportunity to gain exposure to this critical function at Travelers.

The semester long program provides qualified students with an excellent opportunity to gain first-hand insurance underwriting experience, receive valuable on-the-job training and learn more about the property & casualty insurance industry from industry professionals.

It is a potential pathway to our 12 month Underwriting Professional Development Program. The intent of this position is to provide students the ability to apply to our 2024 Underwriting Apprenticeship opportunities which start in January. Applications outside of this audience will not be considered at this time. However, for summer internship opportunities, we encourage anyone to apply to our current 2024 Underwriting Professional Development Program Internship roles in various locations.

What Will You Do?

  • Within your assigned business unit, each apprentice will be given a designated coach and be expected to:
  • Complete core assignments and training modules geared toward insurance and underwriting principles.
  • Participate and complete self-paced professional development courses in time management, presentation skills and other key areas.
  • Complete challenging and meaningful project work over the course of this program at the discretion of your manager. You may work independently or with other interns and will be asked to present your findings to local leadership. Sample projects include a territorial risk assessment to determine profitability and underwriting opportunities as well as a business process analysis to determine underwriting gaps.
  • Learn about other areas at Travelers such as Risk Control, Claims, and related Corporate functions. Interns may also engage in Agency visits with Account Executives.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Because the Underwriting Apprenticeship Program is itself complex and dynamic, we welcome applicants that have a variety of majors, backgrounds, and experiences. We are most interested in students who are serious about entering the insurance industry and who are excited about the prospect of making underwriting their future career choice.
  • Preferred cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong analytical skills.
  • Legal eligibility to work in the United States.
  • Targeted Majors:
  • Business Administration
  • Economics
  • Finance
  • Liberal Arts (with business focus preferred)
  • Management
  • Marketing
  • Risk Management and Insurance

What is a Must Have?

  • Candidate must be pursuing an undergraduate degree.
  • Approximate work availability from January through May required.

By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$85,600.00 - $141,200.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

As a Northland Claim Litigation Specialist, you will be responsible for managing and investigating moderate complexity injury and/or property damage claims including customer contact, determining coverage, evaluating liability, assessing damages, establishing timely reserves, and issue timely and accurate payments within appropriate authority and oversight.

In this technical role, you will leverage your expertise in claims management, investigative techniques, coverage evaluation, and settlement negotiation to ensure timely and fair resolution.

You will foster positive, professional relationships with customers and stakeholders on claims that may involve significant litigation or span extended periods.

You will provide guidance and mentorship to Claim Reps and Associate Claim Reps, sharing knowledge and best practices to support their development.

What Will You Do?

  • Independently manage an active caseload of injury and/or property damage claims and litigation from first notice of loss through resolution within level of authority. Typically, handles personal and/or business insurance high complexity liability claims which may include coverage disputes and contractual indemnity issues.
  • Gather and thoroughly investigate information by contacting all relevant parties to determine coverage, evaluate liability exposure, assess bodily injury and/or property damage, and establish appropriate reserves in accordance with policy terms and management guidance.
  • Provide timely and professional communication to customers, representatives, opposing counsel, third-party vendors, and internal stakeholders.
  • Leverage resolution strategies and coordinate internal and external resources to conduct comprehensive claim investigations and evaluations.
  • Actively negotiate with multiple constituents (e.g., claimants, attorneys, contractors, representatives) and convey claim settlements within authority and issue payments timely and accurately.
  • Assist in coordinating with Counsel to support litigation management strategies.
  • Maintain accurate records of claim activity in claim management systems.
  • Identify areas in which we can improve or enhance current best practices and offer creative solutions.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts, particularly in the areas of AI while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • Acquire and maintain relevant Insurance License(s) to comply with state and Travelers' requirements within three months of starting the job.
  • May require travel, including overnight stays, to attend mediations, trials, arbitration, etc.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Three years of liability, bodily injury or comparable claim experience.
  • Two years of litigation claim experience.
  • Active adjuster license, where required by state law.
  • Experience with claims management systems, with advanced skills in Microsoft Office and enterprise technology systems and platforms.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to comprehend, synthesize, and clearly articulate complex information to multiple stakeholders.
  • Ability to analyze complex situations, exercise sound judgement, and make effective decisions independently.
  • Exceptional customer service skills and commitment to providing a positive experience for customers; ability to manage difficult conversations with empathy and professionalism.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills with the ability to manage a high-volume workload and prioritize effectively.
  • Proven conflict resolution and negotiation skills; ability to handle complex or disputed claims, negotiate settlements, and manage litigation.
  • Ability to manage stress, navigate difficult situations, and maintain composure and professionalism under pressure while always taking accountability for decisions.
  • Thorough understanding of insurance principles and terminology, state insurance regulations, fair claims practices, and legal requirements applicable to claim handling.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret, apply, and clearly articulate complex policy language, endorsements, exclusions to assess coverage and claim eligibility.
  • Ability to quickly learn from experience and apply it to new situations with speed and flexibility.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Two years of bodily injury liability, property damage liability, or comparable claim related experience.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.
