Job Summary

This role supports and maintains a sustainable, landscaping, snow removal and outdoor maintenance program. Performs day-to-day landscaping and maintenance activities at one or all of three or more separate locations or a campus environment.

Shift Hours & Location

  • This role is an essential onsite role in Caledonia, MI.
  • Shift hours generally will be 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM; Monday - Friday. 
  • Pls note: shift hours will have to adjust during the Winter season, depending on when snow accumulations takes place.
    • This could include working weekends and the opportunity for overtime. 

To apply: https://jobs.farmersinsurance.com/job-invite/36435/

Essential Job Functions

  • Performs tasks common to the care of grounds and landscapes by seeding, watering, mulching, fertilizing, and applying chemicals to outside plantings, lawns and turf, transplanting; inspecting plant materials for insects, disease, physical and mechanical damage to irrigation systems and identifying replacements; transplanting, pruning, trimming, and cultivating trees, shrubs, ground cover, and flowers; pest management; storing and caring for bulbs and cuttings in the winter season.
  • Performs regular and directed grounds and landscape maintenance by mowing lawns with riding or push mowers; trimming and edging around trees, shrubs, ground cover, flowers, sidewalks and buildings; weeding, thinning, and cleaning flower beds and other grounds by hand or utilizing proper tools and equipment; and setting up, adjusting, repairing, and cleaning irrigation systems.
  • Operates light and medium equipment in the winter months to clear snow from parking lots, sidewalks, and other traversed areas. As part of the snow removal program, candidate must be available to work differing shifts depending on when snow accumulations take place.
  • Applies chemicals used in grounds keeping (horticulture, turf management, and floriculture) properly and safely by wearing prescribed protective clothing, masks, and/or rubber gloves and boots, following either written or verbal directions for mixing chemical compounds according to specifications, applying the chemicals properly on grounds and landscapes designated for their use, and disposing of residual chemical products as directed or storing and labeling them for future use.
  • Documents a record of grounds and landscape watering and chemical spraying by keeping daily logs of areas watered and duration of watering and the application of chemicals, including areas sprayed, amount and type of chemicals used, substances sprayed and reason, and the wind speed and direction at time of spraying.
  • Safely operates light and medium duty vehicles such as pick-up trucks, tractors, loaders, skid steers, street sweepers or riding mowers.
  • Operates portable power tools and equipment such as saws, grass trimmers, snow/leaf blowers, sprayers, paint machines and other grounds keeping equipment.
  • Obeys applicable traffic laws, follows operator instructions, and wears appropriate safety items such as goggles, gloves, or other appropriate protective clothing.
  • Ensures grounds maintenance equipment and building maintenance equipment are operational by performing routine and preventative maintenance and cleaning of tools, equipment and machines within reasonable capabilities.
  • Maintains record of mechanical equipment operations, building/landscape maintenance, and vendor service visits.
  • Initiates or advises needs for purchases requisitions, verifies receipt of services or product or service.
  • Responsible for the inspection, maintenance, and repair of the campus grounds and out buildings.
  • Responsible for recommending modifications of the grounds systems including electrical, lighting, plumbing, painting and remodeling and irrigation systems, pumps, ponds, drainage and grading of terrain.
  • As needed, consults and reports any security related matters to leadership as well as Corporate Security.

Education & Career Experience Requirements

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Licensed by state Department of Agriculture as a certified applicator or handler of insecticides, herbicides, and fungicides where required or a willingness to obtain such certifications within the first year. 
  • 1-3 years experience in the landscaping or irrigation industry preferred.
  • Medium/heavy equipment operation will be preferred.  This will involve operating a large tractor for snow removal in the wintertime, skid steers, mowers, etc, throughout the rest of the year.   
  • A valid Drivers License is required. 

Additional Qualifications

  • Strong verbal communication and listening skills including written communication skills.
  • Demonstrated customer service skills.
  • Excellent collaboration and team building skills.
  • Friendly and service-oriented; maintains professionalism at all times.
  • Possesses strong technical aptitude; proficient in Microsoft applications.
  • Strong mechanical skills; knowledgeable and skilled in the safe use and maintenance of hand tools, power tools, user-moved aids, mechanical equipment and measuring devices.

Physical Actions

Requires ability to perform physical actions, primarily outdoors, such as frequent walking and standing on feet for long periods of time, maneuvering different terrain, bending, stooping, pushing, pulling, climbing, and using a ladder. Ability to lift up to 50lbs.

Physical Environment

Exposure to noise and extreme temperatures, exposure to hazards such as chemicals and paint.

  • Farmers offers a competitive salary commensurate with experience, qualifications and location.

Workplace: Remote ( #LI-Remote )

Job Summary

  • Develops assigned agent portfolio to full sales potential as described in the production plan, prioritized by agent segment and readiness. Achieves top and bottom-line results for assigned territory through effective Agency and District Performance Management, using segment-based playbooks, KPI scorecards, and defined operating cadence.
  • Works in conjunction with the Sales Director, and members of the product and underwriting team to develop an effective business plan that incorporates sufficient marketing, sales, retention and pricing initiatives to accomplish the assigned territory’s financial plan, with actions and support tailored by agent segment. 
  • Engages with specific segments of agents to meet sales goals, which may include using one-on-one appointments, sales builder meetings, and effective training, leveraging segment Journey to Success playbooks and KPI gates to progress agents (step-up/step-down support based on results. Coordinate with agents, Sales Director, Territory Office and to set goals, define marketing/sales objectives, achieve profitability, influence business processes, and follow through to defined goals, including clear handoffs to virtual execution/referral support where applicable.
  • Support levels and engagement cadence are adjusted based on agent activity and results, with resources prioritized to agents demonstrating sustained commitment and measurable outcomes. Work with assigned agents to influence sales and marketing behaviors and drive top-line business results.

Essential Job Functions

  • Achievement of top line and bottom-line sales results within assigned segment. Accomplishes rotating territory field travel schedule as outlined in the plan for meeting one-on-one with agents or in groups to present methods, ideas and support aligned to segment playbooks and operating cadence for the specific purpose of increasing sales in the assigned segment.
  • Develop business plans for defined segment agents to focus activity on achieving all sales goals, including specific marketing and sales activities, as well as presentations and sales training tailored by agent segment and readiness, that will be used within the assigned segment to drive sales results to the specified goals.
  • Reviews segment performance and prepares estimated run rates and reports of operations that include corrective actions where necessary. Assist agencies in the identification of prospective customers through recommendations of effective lead developing methods, including segment-appropriate activation (example, referral-first for lower engagement segments and pipeline discipline for growth segments).
  • Follows through on identified quotes with underwriting to assure achievement of desired hit ratios, yield, and conversion, evaluating results monthly, recommending actions to either correct deficiencies or to exploit a developing market opportunity. Establish methods to gain knowledge and understanding of market conditions, product innovations and competitor’s products, prices and sales, as well as new regulatory and statutory requirements that may affect marketplace and distribution system. Performs other duties as assigned.

Physical Actions

Job is performed in-person at a Farmers office or virtually at an approved alternative work location. Job may include work performed at field locations. The physical work environment is indoors and climate-controlled with adequate lighting and ventilation. Normal and customary distractions include background noise produced by office equipment and chatter among people, as well as interruptions. Field work performed outdoors may include exposure to weather elements. Frequently sits or stands for prolonged periods of time, up to a full shift. Occasionally moves about the workplace including navigating stairs, ramps, and level or uneven surfaces. Occasionally moves, pushes, pulls, lifts, carries, and places objects or materials weighing up to 50 pounds without assistance. Frequently uses shoulders, arms, hands, and fingers to manipulate equipment, tools, and objects necessary to perform job duties. Frequently performs fine motor tasks such as typing, mousing, or writing, up to a full shift. Occasionally performs movements such as bending, stooping, crouching, kneeling, twisting, and reaching overhead or below the knees. Possesses clear vision, with or without correction, to visually read and verify information. Relies on depth perception and peripheral vision to navigate the work environment visually by identifying barriers, changes in terrain and locating objects. Possesses adequate hearing, with or without correction, to communicate with co-workers, respond promptly to auditory signals or alarms, and discern sounds essential for maintaining safety and productivity in the workplace. Jobs in this category may require regular travel between Farmers offices, alternative work locations, and/or field locations.

Physical Environment

  • Required job duties are normally performed in a climate- controlled office environment, with some exposure to uncontrolled outside environmental conditions and travel via automobile and/or commercial transportation.

Education Requirements

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
  • Bachelors degree and attainment of, or actively pursuing, CPCU or CIC designations preferred.

Experience Requirements

  • Five years property & casualty insurance marketing or sales experience or five years commercial underwriting experience.
  • P&C license will be required if hired.

Additional Qualification

  • Knowledge of Farmers commercial products and appetite, as well as demonstrated general property & casualty and workers compensation insurance knowledge.
  • Strong selling skills and creative sales approach. Ability to coach to standardized playbooks and operating cadences by agent segment. 
  • Strong ability to analyze and interpret information, including KPI/scorecard interpretation and managing to leading indicators and corrective actions.
  • Strong organizational skills.
  • Demonstrate above average oral and written communication skills.
  • Able to share information in a clear, concise, and well-organized manner.
  • Proficient with computer using Word, Excel, Power Point.

Benefits

Workplace: Field-based role - must reside in S. Minn or N. Iowa

Job Summary

  • This position manages an assigned territory of core Foremost Independent Agencies, including responsibilities to prospect and appoint new agencies, drive profitable premium growth, and achieve financial and operational goals. This role develops and manages agency partnerships and serves as the primary relationship between the agency and the company.
  • The position develops and successfully promotes and supports the available suite of Foremost products and services, including a portfolio of complex accounts, within an assigned territory. This role is at the forefront of building premium growth through relationships with agents to ensure market share is built successfully. This position is an individual contributor who works independently with minimal guidance and direction from management and field distribution partners while performing work with business unit and enterprise impacts.
  • It may mentor or coach less experienced team members to support peer learning but has no supervisory responsibilities. The position is remote with required weekly field travel.

Essential Job Functions

  • Owns and manages assigned territory driving profitable growth to achieve financial and operational targets. Leads, develops, and executes territory tactical plan and agency management processes (example business planning, training, compensation) to support financial and operational targets, measure results, and pivot as necessary. Independently builds and cultivates mutually beneficial agency partnerships in person with agency ownership, management, and frontline staff using a consultative sales framework. Acts as a trusted advisor while delivering product, underwriting philosophy, appetite, and system training to support retention and new business development to increase depth and maximize agency revenue.
  • Creates, maintains, and executes high quality agency strategies and plans, including holding agents accountable, to achieve written premium, profit, and new business goals. Collaborates with field distribution partners to plan and align strategic and tactical components with key business strategies such as carrier consolidation (agency book consolidation), agency storefront expansion, and new product or program rollout support. Drives and ensures quality of new business flow, appropriate mix of business, and overall risk management of both individual agency books and overall assigned territory.
  • Provides appetite and target market clarity, identifies and addresses profit or quality of business concerns to ensure profitability across territory. Strategically utilizes internal reporting and tools designed to support the Independent Agent channel including all Marketing and Development programs, business development tools and internal production and profitability data and analysis. Performs other duties as assigned.
  • Serves as a subject matter specialist to assist in leading, collaborating, influencing, and supporting internal business partners (e xample underwriting, product management, claims, service ops) to identify and capitalize on opportunities, solve problems, share key competitor and industry intelligence. May mentor or coach less experienced team members in support of peer learning and developing team capabilities.

Physical Actions

Job is performed in-person at a Farmers office or virtually at an approved alternative work location. Job may include work performed at field locations. The physical work environment is indoors and climate-controlled with adequate lighting and ventilation. Normal and customary distractions include background noise produced by office equipment and chatter among people, as well as interruptions. Field work performed outdoors may include exposure to weather elements. Frequently sits or stands for prolonged periods of time, up to a full shift. Occasionally moves about the workplace including navigating stairs, ramps, and level or uneven surfaces. Occasionally moves, pushes, pulls, lifts, carries, and places objects or materials weighing up to 50 pounds without assistance. Frequently uses shoulders, arms, hands, and fingers to manipulate equipment, tools, and objects necessary to perform job duties. Frequently performs fine motor tasks such as typing, mousing, or writing, up to a full shift. Occasionally performs movements such as bending, stooping, crouching, kneeling, twisting, and reaching overhead or below the knees. Possesses clear vision, with or without correction, to visually read and verify information. Relies on depth perception and peripheral vision to navigate the work environment visually by identifying barriers, changes in terrain and locating objects. Possesses adequate hearing, with or without correction, to communicate with co-workers, respond promptly to auditory signals or alarms, and discern sounds essential for maintaining safety and productivity in the workplace. Jobs in this category may require regular travel between Farmers offices, alternative work locations, and/or field locations.

Education Requirements

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required. Bachelors degree preferred. CIC, CPCU, or insurance licenses preferred upon hire.

Experience Requirements

  • Minimum five years of field insurance sales and management work experience with progressing responsibility or similar experience.
  • Experience achieving consistent profitable premium growth and sales success.

Benefits

  • Farmers offers a competitive salary commensurate with experience, qualifications and location.

Workplace: Field/Remote - Must reside in Texas  

Job Summary

  • This position is responsible for developing and executing distribution strategies for the independent agency channel in assigned states with Regional Field Executive alignment. The role collaborates cross-functionally across teams to create and implement state-level strategies that meet short- and long-term financial goals.
  • Key responsibilities include aligning and driving strategic business plans, recruiting, coaching and developing field sales staff, managing budgets, and ensuring the profitable growth of all product lines. Performs work independently while applying knowledge of key business factors to maximize team and department performance.

Essential Job Functions

  • Collaborates in the development and execution of strategic business plans for Foremost and Bristol West products in the independent agency channel for assigned states. Drives the execution of state distribution strategies, ensuring alignment with product and underwriting partners. Directs the overall state team strategy to achieve proftiable growth across product lines. Leads the recruitment, development, training, and coaching of field sales staff. Develops and implements short-, mid-, and long-term objectives, strategies, and action plans. Supports the development of Territory Managers and agency growth plans. Manages performance of direct reports.
  • Creates and recommends training programs, policies, and practices to ensure a well-equipped sales force. Plans, directs, and coordinates all sales-related activities to achieve revenue goals. Formulates and oversees sales/marketing plans and promotions to stimulate profitable sales growth. Identifies target markets and directs efforts in training, sales, marketing support, and research. Acts as an advocate by recommending new products, services, and field initiatives. Ensures regular, clear, and consistent cross-functional communication with product management, underwriting, executive management, and agency partners.
  • Serves as a communication bridge between Foremost and other internal and external groups. Collaborates with marketing and training teams to develop educational materials and strategies. Responsible for the initiation, positioning, and distribution of products and product enhancements. Implements rate and product changes while ensuring successful communication and training. Assesses industry trends to identify new opportunities and implement them effectively. Use quantitative knowledge to influence future products and rate changes. Coordinates field-facing activities, programs, and promotions to align with business objectives.
  • Performs other duties as assigned while contributing to the overall success of the zone and organization. Reviews quarterly updates on regional objectives and makes necessary revisions to achieve goals. Evaluates and develops field sales force objectives and plans to ensure the achievement of sales goals. Tracks and reports progress of sales programs and contests to business unit management. Stays informed of competitive, legislative, and regulatory activity within assigned states. Ensures understanding and implementation of technology in the sales process to maximize effectiveness.

Physical Actions

Job is performed in-person at a Farmers office or virtually at an approved alternative work location. Job may include work performed at field locations. The physical work environment is indoors and climate-controlled with adequate lighting and ventilation. Normal and customary distractions include background noise produced by office equipment and chatter among people, as well as interruptions. Field work performed outdoors may include exposure to weather elements. Frequently sits or stands for prolonged periods of time, up to a full shift. Occasionally moves about the workplace including navigating stairs, ramps, and level or uneven surfaces. Occasionally moves, pushes, pulls, lifts, carries, and places objects or materials weighing up to 50 pounds without assistance. Frequently uses shoulders, arms, hands, and fingers to manipulate equipment, tools, and objects necessary to perform job duties. Frequently performs fine motor tasks such as typing, mousing, or writing, up to a full shift. Occasionally performs movements such as bending, stooping, crouching, kneeling, twisting, and reaching overhead or below the knees. Possesses clear vision, with or without correction, to visually read and verify information. Relies on depth perception and peripheral vision to navigate the work environment visually by identifying barriers, changes in terrain and locating objects. Possesses adequate hearing, with or without correction, to communicate with co-workers, respond promptly to auditory signals or alarms, and discern sounds essential for maintaining safety and productivity in the workplace. Jobs in this category may require regular travel between Farmers offices, alternative work locations, and/or field locations.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelors degree required. Masters degree or MBA preferred.

Experience Requirements

  • Minimum seven years of experience in the insurance industry, preferably in sales, marketing, or distribution.
  • Experience leading and managing sales teams preferred.

Additional Qualification

  • Effective leadership skills. Proven leadership, critical thinking, decision-making, problem-solving, change management, and organizational skills. Builds and manages effective teams.
  • Proven ability to coach and mentor others while fostering a high-performance culture among team. Demonstrated analytical skills. Proven ability to plan strategically and tactically.
  • Proven ability to develop and execute business plans and achieve successful results. Strong verbal communication and listening skills. Demonstrated written communication skills.
  • Demonstrated time management and priority setting skills. Ability to analyze and interpret financial data. Able to analyze financial results and market trends to manage performance and changes with products and pricing.
  • Possesses strong technical aptitude. Proficient in the use of current technology including Microsoft Office suite, agency management systems, and comparative raters.

  • Farmers offers a competitive salary commensurate with experience, qualifications and location.

Workplace: Hybrid ( #LI-Hybrid )

Farmers believes in a culture of collaboration, creativity, and innovation, which thrives when we have the ability to work flexibly in a virtual setting as well as the opportunity to be together in person. Our hybrid work environment combines the best of both worlds with at least three (3) days in office and up to two (2) days virtual for employees who live within fifty (50) miles of a Farmers corporate office. Applicants beyond fifty (50) miles may still be considered.

Job Details

To be considered for this position, candidate must reside within 50 miles of one of the following Farmers Corportate Office Locations:

Kansas City, KS ~ Caledonia, MI ~ Oklahoma City, OK ~ Phoenix, AZ ~  St. Louis, MO

Upcoming Start Dates: 

  • Monday, December 28th (If you do not currently have an Active All Lines Adjuster license) 
  • Monday, January 11th, 2027 (If you have an active All Lines Adjuster license - must be up to date on CE's)

Award Winning Paid Training Program: Monday - Friday, 8:00 am - 5:00 pm Local time, 8-12 weeks. 

Post Training Work Schedule: Monday - Friday, 8:00 am - 5:00 pm local time.

  • Department Hours of Operation: 7:00 am - 7:00 pm, Monday - Friday. You are expected to work 40 hours/week with flexibility, subject to business needs, geographic location, and Farmers Timekeeping Policy.

Compensation: The starting wage for this position is $26.01 per hour, plus you will be eligible for an annual bonus. Pay is dependent upon the candidate's geographic location and relevant claims experience. 

    • Compensation will be evaluated based on related experience.
    • Candidates with Claims Auto Handling or related industry experience are highly encouraged to apply.

Job Summary

Utilizes working knowledge and skills developed through formal training to investigate, confirm coverage, determine liability, establish damages, and negotiate settlements of auto claims, which includes single and multi-vehicle losses with basic coverage and moderate complexity of liability.

Day in the Life of an Auto Claim Handler:

  • Utilizes a broad understanding of claims adjusting to apply skills and knowledge to investigate and determine liability for claims with basic coverage issues and moderate to complex liability issues. Performs in-depth investigation and analysis on losses such as multi-vehicle losses with comparative negligence. Completes investigation by securing recorded statements of the drivers, police reports vehicle photos and estimates, and scene investigations.
  • Makes same-day contact with customers. Explains the claims process to all customers. Explains all applicable coverage benefits to the policyholder. Confirms facts of loss. Determines vehicle location and if drivable. Offers vehicle repair and rental service options to customers. Coordinates auto physical damage estimate through the proper internal method of inspection and arranges for the release of vehicles that are accruing storage fees.
  • Proactively investigates and determines coverage for Auto policy claims with coverage issues requiring in-depth investigation including but not limited to if the policy is out of force for the date of loss, unlisted or permissive drivers, excluded drivers, vehicles not on the policy, rideshare involvement, material misrepresentation issues, and new business investigations.
  • Maintains ownership of the claim and completes work with a limited degree of supervision. Serves as the primary point of contact through resolution of all exposures. Communicates and collaborates with other claim specialists to facilitate claim resolution for customers. Provides verbal and written communication to customers to explain coverage issues and decisions.
  • Communicates policy risk issues to Underwriting to facilitate their evaluation of the policy risk and exposure. Escalates complex coverage issues to supervisor.
  • Demonstrates proficient knowledge and application of venue laws for all states handled in the Region. Analyzes duties owed and breached by all potentially responsible parties and determines liability percentage for each party. Escalates claims with exposures exceeding financial authority to supervisor. Communicates liability decisions to customers, claimants, claim specialists, and Underwriting. Recognizes subrogation potential and makes referrals to the Subrogation department when appropriate.
  • With limited supervision and support, investigates and recognizes all potential claim exposures. Recognizes and escalates non-auto property damage exposures and resolves auto physical damage claims proactively and accurately. Secures estimate of damages timely through appropriate repair channels. Writes, reviews, and adjusts auto physical damage estimates for repairable vehicles with minor to moderate damages. Issues and authorizes claim payments to customers and repair facilities and explains repair process and estimate to customers.
  • Manages rental claims through communication with customers, repair facilities, rental vendors, and claim specialists. Proactively manages and mitigates storage costs. Coordinates and collaborates with auto physical damage and total loss specialists to facilitate claim resolution for customers.
  • Maintains active diary and resolution plan on open files. Handles and documents files in compliance with regulatory requirements. Responsible for ensuring professional correspondence is sent to customers including claim status updates. Completes work with a limited degree of supervision. May act as an informal resource for colleagues with less experience.

Education Requirements

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
    • Bachelor's degree preferred.
  • An active All Lines Adjuster license is required, or the ability to obtain licensure. 
    • If not currently licensed, obtaining and passing the All Lines Adjuster licensing requirements during training is a condition of employment.

Experience & Skills Required

  • Demonstrated customer service skills.
  • Effective conflict management skills. Identifies key issues and patterns from partial/conflicting data.
  • Strong verbal communication and listening skills. Strong written communication skills with the ability to convey critical decisions and information through written letters.
  • Demonstrates excellent judgment and decision-making skills.
  • Effective negotiation skills.
  • Possesses flexibility to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment; uses discretion to modify work practices and processes to achieve results or improve efficiency.
  • Demonstrated problem-solving skills. Takes a broad perspective on problems and spots new, less obvious solutions.
  • Performs work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Possesses strong technical aptitude; Proficient in Microsoft Office products. Adaptable and flexible to new technology.

Physical Environment & Actions

  • This role, whether performed virtually or in an office setting, will include normal and customary distractions, noise, and interruptions.
  • Sits or stands for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift.
  • Occasionally reaches overhead and below the knees, including bending, twisting, pulling, and stooping.
  • Occasionally moves, lifts, carries, and places objects and supplies weighing 0-10 pounds without assistance.
  • Listens to, interprets, and differentiates auditory information (e.g. others speaking) at normal speaking levels with or without correction.
  • Visually verifies and reads information.
  • Visually locates material, resources and other objects.
  • Ability to continuously operate a computer for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift.
  • Physical dexterity sufficient to use hands, arms, and shoulders repetitively to operate keyboard and other office equipment up to a full work shift.

... then this could be a great career opportunity for you!

Workplace: Field-based role covering Seattle and Western Washington.  Weekly travel (3-4 days/week) and minimal overnight travel.

Job Summary

  • This position manages an assigned territory of core Foremost Independent Agencies, including responsibilities to prospect and appoint new agencies, drive profitable premium growth, and achieve financial and operational goals. This role develops and manages agency partnerships and serves as the primary relationship between the agency and the company.
  • The position develops and successfully promotes and supports the available suite of Foremost products and services, including a portfolio of complex accounts, within an assigned territory. This role is at the forefront of building premium growth through relationships with agents to ensure market share is built successfully.
  • This position is an individual contributor who works independently with minimal guidance and direction from management and field distribution partners while performing work with business unit and enterprise impacts. It may mentor or coach less experienced team members to support peer learning but has no supervisory responsibilities. The position is remote with required weekly field travel.

Essential Job Functions

  • Owns and manages assigned territory driving profitable growth to achieve financial and operational targets. Leads, develops, and executes territory tactical plan and agency management processes (example business planning, training, compensation) to support financial and operational targets, measure results, and pivot as necessary. Independently builds and cultivates mutually beneficial agency partnerships in person with agency ownership, management, and frontline staff using a consultative sales framework. Acts as a trusted advisor while delivering product, underwriting philosophy, appetite, and system training to support retention and new business development to increase depth and maximize agency revenue.
  • Creates, maintains, and executes high quality agency strategies and plans, including holding agents accountable, to achieve written premium, profit, and new business goals. Collaborates with field distribution partners to plan and align strategic and tactical components with key business strategies such as carrier consolidation (agency book consolidation), agency storefront expansion, and new product or program rollout support. Drives and ensures quality of new business flow, appropriate mix of business, and overall risk management of both individual agency books and overall assigned territory. Provides appetite and target market clarity, identifies and addresses profit or quality of business concerns to ensure profitability across territory.
  • Strategically utilizes internal reporting and tools designed to support the Independent Agent channel including all Marketing and Development programs, business development tools and internal production and profitability data and analysis. Performs other duties as assigned. Serves as a subject matter specialist to assist in leading, collaborating, influencing, and supporting internal business partners (e xample underwriting, product management, claims, service ops) to identify and capitalize on opportunities, solve problems, share key competitor and industry intelligence. May mentor or coach less experienced team members in support of peer learning and developing team capabilities.

Physical Actions

Job is performed in-person at a Farmers office or virtually at an approved alternative work location. Job may include work performed at field locations. The physical work environment is indoors and climate-controlled with adequate lighting and ventilation. Normal and customary distractions include background noise produced by office equipment and chatter among people, as well as interruptions. Field work performed outdoors may include exposure to weather elements. Frequently sits or stands for prolonged periods of time, up to a full shift. Occasionally moves about the workplace including navigating stairs, ramps, and level or uneven surfaces. Occasionally moves, pushes, pulls, lifts, carries, and places objects or materials weighing up to 50 pounds without assistance. Frequently uses shoulders, arms, hands, and fingers to manipulate equipment, tools, and objects necessary to perform job duties. Frequently performs fine motor tasks such as typing, mousing, or writing, up to a full shift. Occasionally performs movements such as bending, stooping, crouching, kneeling, twisting, and reaching overhead or below the knees. Possesses clear vision, with or without correction, to visually read and verify information. Relies on depth perception and peripheral vision to navigate the work environment visually by identifying barriers, changes in terrain and locating objects. Possesses adequate hearing, with or without correction, to communicate with co-workers, respond promptly to auditory signals or alarms, and discern sounds essential for maintaining safety and productivity in the workplace. Jobs in this category may require regular travel between Farmers offices, alternative work locations, and/or field locations.

Education Requirements

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required. Bachelors degree preferred. CIC, CPCU, or insurance licenses preferred upon hire.

Experience Requirements

  • Minimum five years of field insurance sales and management work experience with progressing responsibility.
  • Experience achieving consistent profitable premium growth and sales success.

Benefits

  • Farmers offers a competitive salary commensurate with experience, qualifications and location.

Workplace: Hybrid ( #LI-Hybrid )

Farmers believes in a culture of collaboration, creativity, and innovation, which thrives when we have the ability to work flexibly in a virtual setting as well as the opportunity to be together in person. Our hybrid work environment combines the best of both worlds with at least three (3) days in office and up to two (2) days virtual for employees who live within fifty (50) miles of a Farmers corporate office. Applicants beyond fifty (50) miles may still be considered.

Job Summary

  • Participates in training program to learn basic policies, practices, procedures, and strategies needed to become a Claims Representative.
  • Trains to handle low to moderately complex claims promptly, proactively, and with a sense of urgency.
  • Performs work under the guidance and supervision of a trainer.
  • Trainee is required to pass an exam at certain phases of the training program.
  • Trainees who successfully complete this training program may be placed into a Claims Representative role of equivalent salary grade.

Essential Job Functions

  • In a supervised learning environment, trains to adjust low to moderately complex claims.
  • Learns skills such as conducting thorough i nvestigations, establishing damages, determining liability, negotiating settlements, making claim payments, confirming policy coverage, and explaining claim determination to parties incident to the claim.
  • Works in electronic claim files to handle assigned claims within designated authority.
  • Learns to manage diaries, update claim files and move them to closure according to established procedures and job aids provided for training purposes.
  • Trains to inspect vehicles and property to assess claim related damage.
  • Learns to estimate repair or replacement costs.
  • Learns to determine and report on subrogation potential.
  • Reports theft, fraud, and arson losses as required by state and industry regulations.
  • Trains to interact professionally and courteously with stakeholders including policyholders, claimants, agents, witnesses, repair fa cilities, contractors, police and fire departments, state and country fraud and arson specialists, special investigators, attorneys, medical professionals and other persons incident to the investigation and processing of claims.
  • Acts as a representative of the company.
  • Seeks to grow job knowledge and incorporates new information into daily tasks.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Physical Actions

  • This role, whether performed virtually or in an office setting, will include normal and customary distractions, noise, and interruptions.
  • Sits or stands for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift.
  • Occasionally reaches overhead and below the knees, including bending, twisting, pulling, and stooping.
  • Occasionally moves, lifts, carries, and places objects and supplies weighing 0-10 pounds without assistance.
  • Listens to, interprets, and differentiates auditory information (example others speaking) at normal speaking levels with or without correction.
  • Visually verifies and reads information.
  • Visually locates material, resources and other objects.
  • Ability to continuously operate a computer for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift.
  • Physical dexterity sufficient to use hands, arms, and shoulders repetitively to operate keyboard and other office equipment up to a full work shift.

Education Requirements

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
  • Bachelors degree preferred.
  • Other: Must obtain adjusters license in states where required.

Experience Requirements

Some experience in insurance or a related field preferred. Claims experience preferred.

Benefits

  • Farmers offers a competitive salary commensurate with experience, qualifications and location.
  • Bonus Opportunity (based on Company and Individual Performance)
  • 401(k)
  • Medical
  • Dental
  • Vision
  • Health Savings and Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Life Insurance
  • Paid Time Off
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Tuition Assistance
  • For more information, review “What we offer” on https://www.farmers.com/careers/corporate/#offer

Workplace: Field-based in Austin (will cover Waco as well)

Job Summary

  • This position manages an assigned territory of core Foremost Independent Agencies, including responsibilities to prospect and appoint new agencies with guidance, drive profitable premium growth, and achieve financial and operational goals. This role develops and manages agency partnerships and serves as the primary relationship between the agency and the company. The position develops and successfully promotes and supports the available suite of Foremost products and services, including a portfolio of moderately complex accounts, within an assigned territory.
  • This role is at the forefront of building premium growth through relationships with agents to ensure market share is built successfully. This position is an individual contributor who receives moderate guidance and direction from management and field distribution partners while performing work with business unit and enterprise impacts. The position is remote with required weekly field travel.

Essential Job Functions

  • Owns and manages assigned territory driving profitable growth to achieve financial and operational targets. With moderate guidance from management and field distribution partners, assists in leading, developing, and executing territory tactical plan and agency management processes (example business planning, training, compensation) to support financial and operational targets, measure results, and pivot as necessary. With coaching, builds and cultivates mutually beneficial agency partnerships in person with agency ownership, management, and frontline staff using a consultative sales framework. Establishes position as a trusted advisor while delivering product, underwriting philosophy, appetite, and system training, to support retention and new business development to increase depth and maximize agency revenue. With moderate guidance, creates, maintains, and executes high quality agency strategies and plans, including holding agents accountable, to achieve written premium, profit, and new business goals.
  • Coordinates plans with field distribution partners, including strategic and tactical components, to align with business strategies such as carrier consolidation (agency book consolidation), agency storefront expansion, and new product or program rollout support. With coaching, drives and ensures quality of new business flow, appropriate mix of business, and overall risk management of both ind ividual agency books and overall assigned territory. Provides appetite and target market clarity, identifies and addresses profit or quality of business concerns to ensure profitability across territory. Strategically utilizes internal reporting and tools designed to support the Independent Agent channel including all Marketing and Development programs, business development tools and internal production/profitability data and analysis. Performs other duties as ass igned.

Physical Actions

Job is performed in-person at a Farmers office or virtually at an approved alternative work location. Job may include work performed at field locations. The physical work environment is indoors and climate-controlled with adequate lighting and ventilation. Normal and customary distractions include background noise produced by office equipment and chatter among people, as well as interruptions. Field work performed outdoors may include exposure to weather elements. Frequently sits or stands for prolonged periods of time, up to a full shift. Occasionally moves about the workplace including navigating stairs, ramps, and level or uneven surfaces. Occasionally moves, pushes, pulls, lifts, carries, and places objects or materials weighing up to 50 pounds without assistance. Frequently uses shoulders, arms, hands, and fingers to manipulate equipment, tools, and objects necessary to perform job duties. Frequently performs fine motor tasks such as typing, mousing, or writing, up to a full shift. Occasionally performs movements such as bending, stooping, crouching, kneeling, twisting, and reaching overhead or below the knees. Possesses clear vision, with or without correction, to visually read and verify information. Relies on depth perception and peripheral vision to navigate the work environment visually by identifying barriers, changes in terrain and locating objects. Possesses adequate hearing, with or without correction, to communicate with co-workers, respond promptly to auditory signals or alarms, and discern sounds essential for maintaining safety and productivity in the workplace. Jobs in this category may require regular travel between Farmers offices, alternative work locations, and/or field locations.

Education Requirements

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required. Bachelors degree preferred. CIC, CPCU, or insurance licenses preferred upon hire.

Experience Requirements

  • Minimum three years of insurance sales and management work experience. Experience achieving profitable premium growth and sales success.

Benefits

  • Farmers offers a competitive salary commensurate with experience, qualifications and location.
  • Bonus Opportunity (based on Company and Individual Performance)
  • 401(k)
  • Medical
  • Dental
  • Vision
  • Health Savings and Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Life Insurance
  • Paid Time Off
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Tuition Assistance
  • For more information, review “What we offer” on https://www.farmers.com/careers/corporate/#offer

Job Summary

As Director, Technical Underwriting - Casualty, you will serve as Farmers' senior technical authority for commercial casualty underwriting. You will lead the development of underwriting strategy, governance, referral frameworks, and portfolio management practices while providing expertise on complex casualty exposures. This newly created role offers the opportunity to shape the future of casualty underwriting within a transforming Business Insurance organization.

This role combines deep underwriting expertise, strategic leadership, and organizational influence. The Director will help shape underwriting appetite, governance frameworks, authority structures, quality programs, and portfolio performance while building technical capabilities across the broader underwriting organization. We are particularly interested in experienced external underwriting leaders who can bring specialized expertise and innovative thinking to help advance Farmers' underwriting capabilities.

The Director will play a pivotal role in building technical excellence, enhancing underwriting quality, improving profitability, and developing the next generation of underwriting talent.

Essential Job Functions

  • Lead authority management strategy and underwriting governance framework, including corporate authority templates, referral triggers, and decision rules.
  • Define and enforce how underwriting decisions are made to ensure consistency with underwriting strategy and risk appetite.
  • Exercise elevated underwriting authority and provide guidance on complex or high-exposure risks.
  • Own underwriting performance and profitability for assigned lines of business, including accountability for loss ratio, combined ratio, growth, and retention.
  • Monitor performance and take action to achieve financial and business objectives.
  • Own underwriting quality program and control environment, including quality standards, leakage monitoring, audits, and compliance frameworks.
  • Identify control gaps and implement corrective actions to ensure adherence to underwriting guidelines, regulatory requirements, and internal policies.
  • Translate underwriting strategy and risk appetite into technical frameworks, including guidelines, authority structures, and operational rules.
  • Ensure consistent execution across lines of business through clear standards and governance mechanisms.
  • Partner with actuarial and data and analytics to develop and deploy portfolio analytics, underwriting models, and decision-support tools.
  • Establish and lead emerging risk identification and governance processes. 
  • Collaborate cross-functionally to assess impacts and drive updates to underwriting guidelines, authority frameworks, and control structures.
  • Provide direct technical guidance and support to underwriting centers, ensuring responsiveness, effective decision-making, and alignment with underwriting standards.
  • Lead, develop, and retain talent in either quality or loss control functions.
  • Build deep technical expertise and governance discipline within the organization.
  • Implement feedback loops to continuously improve underwriting decision quality, pricing discipline, and overall performance, including coordination and portfolio management of individual account reinsurance placements and collaboration with the reinsurance team on annual facility placements.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Experience Requirements

  • Commercial casualty underwriting expertise including complex casualty exposures, liability trends, and technical referral authority.
  • Minimum ten years of experience in insurance underwriting or insurance compliance required.
  • Minimum five years experience leading people required.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelors degree required. Preferably in mathematics, business, or finance.
  • CPCU or CIC designation preferred.

Additional Qualifications

  • Ability to drive multiple projects to successful completion.
  • Ability to lead cross-functional work, drive decisions, and build alignment across underwriting, product, pricing/actuarial, IT, data/analytics, and operations.
  • Demonstrated change leadership, including adoption planning, training enablement, measurement, and continuous improvement. Instills commitment to organizational goals.
  • Ability to understand the vision and direction of the business to develop and execute a plan to achieve business results.

Physical Actions

Job is performed in-person at a Farmers office or virtually at an approved alternative work location. The physical work environment is indoors and climate-controlled with adequate lighting and ventilation. Normal and customary distractions include background noise produced by office equipment and chatter among people, as well as interruptions. Frequently sits for prolonged periods of time, up to a full shift. Occasionally moves about the workplace including, navigating stairs, ramps, and level or uneven surfaces. Occasionally moves, pushes, pulls, lifts, carries, and/or places objects or materials weighing up to 25 pounds without assistance. Frequently uses shoulders, arms, hands, and fingers to manipulate equipment, tools, and objects necessary to perform job duties. Frequently performs fine motor tasks such as typing, mousing, or writing, up to a full shift. Rarely performs movements such as bending, stooping, crouching, kneeling, twisting, and reaching overhead or below the knees. Possesses clear vision, with or without correction, to visually read and verify information. Relies on depth perception and peripheral vision to navigate the work environment visually by identifying barriers, changes in terrain and locating objects. Possesses adequate hearing, with or without correction, to communicate with co-workers, respond promptly to auditory signals or alarms, and discern sounds essential for maintaining safety and productivity in the workplace. Jobs in this category require rare, if any, travel.

Job Summary

This role oversees technology audit portfolios, ensuring risk-aligned coverage, technical rigor, and consistent quality. It provides independent insight and challenge on technology and risk matters to senior leaders, translating audit results into meaningful risk insights and shaping risk-based coverage within assigned portfolios. The role develops technical audit leaders while contributing to innovation and methodology advancement

Essential Job Functions

  • Act as senior point of contact for technology audit matters within assigned portfolios.
  • Present results, risk themes, and insights to leadership.

Job Summary

Prepares various company materials for enterprise mailing within a fast paced, production environment. Processes compliance materials, transactional and marketing mail in accordance to USPS regulations for timely delivery based on internal customers' expectations.

  • Shift Hours: Sunday - Thursday from 11:00 pm to 7:30 am.
  • A 10% shift differential applies working this shift.

Essential Tasks

  • Performs manual processing of mail by utilizing large, high speed machines within production environment.
  • Utilizes knowledge of 1-2 specific machine types and models to perform quality and timely placement.

  • Less than one year of general work experience preferred.

Workplace: Remote ( #LI-Remote )

We are seeking an experienced Trial Attorney with experience handling complex matters to join our Massachusetts staff counsel team and handle cases venued primarily in the Boston area and surrounding counties. Our attorneys work from home and handle in-person appearances and trials as required. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including annual bonus potential up to 20% of the salary, generous 401k, auto allowance, PTO, medical/dental/vision, paid parental leave, and much more all without the stress of billable hours!   

Job Summary

This position is responsible for representing clients in all areas of insurance defense practice, handling cases that are primarily moderate to high complexity and exposure and/or involve unique insurance defense issues. Manages all phases of cases from intake to resolution.

Essential Job Functions

  • Litigates moderate to high complexity and exposure cases and/or cases involving unique legal or procedural issues and performs duties necessary from intake to trial and/or settlement.
  • This includes but is not limited to preparation of pleadings, motions, discovery, and briefs.
  • Acts as the lead attorney at hearings, conferences, interviews, mediations, arbitrations, and/or trials.
  • Develops strategies and arguments to thoroughly prepare for trial. 
  • Utilizes knowledge of legal precedents to analyze the probable outcomes of a case.
  • Identifies the strengths and weaknesses of approaches to a case.
  • Performs or ensures completion of any other tasks or duties necessary for the proper representation of clients.
  • Consults with Claims Executive team and renders legal strategy recommendations regarding the legal aspects of the handling of personal injury claims.
  • Provides guidance to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and industry standards.
  • Interprets applicable industry laws, rulings and regulations.
  • Functionally supervises attorneys who are assisting in the handling of cases as development opportunities.
  • Provides guidance and mentorship with the autonomy to learn.

Physical Actions

Job is performed in-person at a Farmers office or virtually at an approved alternative work location. Job may include work performed at field locations. The physical work environment is indoors and climate-controlled with adequate lighting and ventilation. Normal and customary distractions include background noise produced by office equipment and chatter among people, as well as interruptions. Field work performed outdoors may include exposure to weather elements. Frequently sits or stands for prolonged periods of time, up to a full shift. Occasionally moves about the workplace including navigating stairs, ramps, and level or uneven surfaces. Occasionally moves, pushes, pulls, lifts, carries, and places objects or materials weighing up to 50 pounds without assistance. Frequently uses shoulders, arms, hands, and fingers to manipulate equipment, tools, and objects necessary to perform job duties. Frequently performs fine motor tasks such as typing, mousing, or writing, up to a full shift. Occasionally performs movements such as bending, stooping, crouching, kneeling, twisting, and reaching overhead or below the knees. Possesses clear vision, with or without correction, to visually read and verify information. Relies on depth perception and peripheral vision to navigate the work environment visually by identifying barriers, changes in terrain and locating objects. Possesses adequate hearing, with or without correction, to communicate with co-workers, respond promptly to auditory signals or alarms, and discern sounds essential for maintaining safety and productivity in the workplace. Jobs in this category may require regular travel between Farmers offices, alternative work locations, and/or field locations.

Physical Environment

Required job duties are normally performed in a climate- controlled office environment, with some exposure to uncontrollable outside environmental conditions and travel via automobile and/or commercial transportation.

Education Requirements

Bachelors degree preferred. Licensed to practice Law in applicable states required upon hire.

Experience Requirements

Seven years of litigation experience required. Insurance defense, personal injury, and/or jury trial experience required. First and second chair trial experience in bodily injury litigation strongly preferred. Multistate jurisdictional practice preferred.

Special Skill Requirement

Public speaking, ability to function and handle high case loads in adversarial or confrontational situations, driving.

Additional Qualification

Effective leadership skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to command the attention of an audience. Demonstrated problem solving skills. Possesses a genuine interest in the defense of Insurance regulations. Ability to represent the company with external constituents. Handles conflict effectively with the ability to quickly interpret and respond to new information. Demonstrates excellent judgment and decision making skills. Ability to work within tight timeframes and meet strict deadlines. Excellent time management and priority setting skills. Articulate and responsive to colleagues. Possesses strong technical aptitude. Adept and proficient at using technology to maximize efficiency in virtual, paperless environment.

Benefits

Job Summary

Essential Job Functions

Leads, develops, and executes territory tactical plan and agency management processes (example business planning, training, compensation) to support financial and operational targets, measure results, and pivot as necessary. Independently builds and cultivates mutually beneficial agency partnerships in person with agency ownership, management, and frontline staff using a consultative sales framework.
  • Acts as a trusted advisor while delivering product, underwriting philosophy, appetite, and system training to support retention and new business development to increase depth and maximize agency revenue. Creates, maintains, and executes high quality agency strategies and plans, including holding agents accountable, to achieve written premium, profit, and new business goals. Collaborates with field distribution partners to plan and align strategic and tactical components with key business strategies such as carrier consolidation (agency book consolidation), agency storefront expansion, and new product or program rollout support.
  • Drives and ensures quality of new business flow, appropriate mix of business, and overall risk management of both individual agency books and overall assigned territory. Provides appetite and target market clarity, identifies and addresses profit or quality of business concerns to ensure profitability across territory. Strategically utilizes internal reporting and tools designed to support the Independent Agent channel including all Marketing and Development programs, business development tools and internal production and profitability data and analysis.
  • Performs other duties as assigned. Serves as a subject matter specialist to assist in leading, collaborating, influencing, and supporting internal business partners (e xample underwriting, product management, claims, service ops) to identify and capitalize on opportunities, solve problems, share key competitor and industry intelligence. May mentor or coach less experienced team members in support of peer learning and developing team capabilities.

Physical Actions

  • Job is performed in-person at a Farmers office or virtually at an approved alternative work location. Job may include work performed at field locations. Workplace: Remote ( #LI-Remote ) - This is a field role requiring travel to and from policy holder homes.   

Residency Requirement:  Candidates must currently live within the South Tarrant, Johnson, Ellis & Kaufman Counties  area to be eligible for consideration. Ideal locations include Cleburne, Burleson, Mansfield, Waxahachie, De Soto, Red Oak, or Kauffman.

The starting wage for this position is $27.67hr. or higher. Additional compensation may be offered based on relevant experience and transferable skills. 

If you are looking for the following in your next career ...

  • Paid training through the award-winning and industry-leading University of Farmers.
  • Flexibility and independence to work outside the confines of a desk job.
  • Total Rewards Benefits Package: 401K and a competitive starting salary.
  • Rapid growth potential and management opportunities for success-oriented people through education,mentorship programs, and inspirational leadership at a company you can be proud of.


… then Farmers Insurance is the place for you!

A Day in the Life of a Field Property Adjuster:

  • Conduct both virtual and on-site investigations by visiting policyholders’ residences to assess propertydamage, determine liability, evaluate the extent of loss, and negotiate fair settlements.
  • Use claims handling software, a company car, and a laptop to determine claims-related damage and write estimates in a paperless environment.
  • Evaluate and report on potential subrogation opportunities.
  • Reports incidents involving theft, fraud, or arson to appropriate state and industry agencies.
  • Perform duties independently, with work directly impacting management outcomes.
  • Acts as a company representative in public interactions, maintaining a professional demeanor consistentwith management standards.
  • Engages regularly with a variety of stakeholders, including policyholders, claimants, agents, witnesses,contractors, law enforcement, fraud and arson investigators, attorneys, medical professionals, and otherrelevant parties.
  • Use strong customer service skills to negotiate with policyholders to settle the claim.
  • Performs additional duties as assigned.
  • Promotes safety at all times and complies with safety/ergonomicstandards as outlined in relevant company published manuals.

Employees assigned to the Catastrophe team will be required to travel away from their residence for a specified period of time, usually consisting of 23 days. 

  • Although this is not a CAT-specific role, hires will be expected to commit to 1–3 CAT deployments per year.

If You Have the Following:

  • High School diploma or equivalent required. 
  • Excellent Customer service experience, preferably in a retail environment
  • Construction or Insurance experience is highly desirable and preferred.
  • Excellent communication skills – both oral and written.
  • Computer Literate: MS Word, Excel, Outlook.
  • Proficiency with smartphones and applications.
  • Eagerness to learn about insurance policies and property damage from the inside out to identify how coverage applies to a particular loss.
  • Outgoing personality that would enjoy interacting with a wide variety of people including policyholders, claimants, agents, witnesses, and fraud investigators.
  • Valid driver's license and Bondable.  Final candidates will also be subject to a Motor Vehicle Record background check as this position may include a company vehicle.

... then this could be a great career opportunity for you!

Final candidate qualifications may be reviewed against the requirements for the associated level of this role.

Candidates Must be Willing & Able to:

  • Climb Ladders to inspect roofs, and be comfortable working on rooftops, multiple times per day, 
  • Work in small, confined spaces that have been damaged; such as attics and crawlspaces.
  • Achieve a minimum passing score on all claims training exams.

Physical Actions & Environment:

  • Bending, Kneeling, Pulling, Pushing, Sorting, Carrying up to 50 lbs., Climbing, Reaching, Standing, Walking, Seeing
  • Speaking (English), Reading (English), Writing (English), & Key Entering

Required job duties are performed in the field and an in-home office environment. Exposure to some or all of the following environments when in the field: Uncontrolled outside environmental conditions, Excessive noise levels, Chemicals Chemical/Biological conditions, Moving mechanical parts, Areas considered dangerous, Conditions which could affect the respiratory system or skin such as fumes, odors, dust, mists, gases, oils, smoke, soot, or poor ventilation.

Job Summary

The Director, Decision Science leads a team of analytics and decision science professionals responsible for transforming data into actionable business insights that drive strategic decision-making across the enterprise. This role partners closely with executive leaders and cross-functional stakeholders to solve complex business challenges, identify growth opportunities, improve operational performance, and enhance profitability.
 
The Director oversees the development and application of advanced analytics, statistical modeling, experimentation, forecasting, and machine learning techniques to inform critical business decisions. This leader establishes the vision and strategy for decision science initiatives, ensures the delivery of high-impact analytical solutions, and fosters a culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement. The position leads other people leaders, acts as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, and serves as a subject matter expert in analytics and data-driven decision making.

Essential Job Functions

  • Partner with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to identify strategic business opportunities and develop data-driven solutions that improve business outcomes.
  • Lead the development and execution of the Decision Science strategy, ensuring alignment with enterprise objectives and business priorities.
  • Provide consultative leadership on complex business questions by leveraging advanced analytics, statistical methodologies, predictive modeling, forecasting, and machine learning techniques. 
  • Translate business objectives into analytical frameworks and actionable recommendations that influence strategic decisions.
  • Guide large-scale exploratory analyses to uncover trends, risks, opportunities, and drivers of performance across the organization.
  • Oversee the design, execution, and interpretation of experiments, hypothesis testing, and causal inference analyses to evaluate business initiatives and optimize outcomes.
  • Direct the development, deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement of predictive and prescriptive analytics solutions.
  • Leverage modern analytics, visualization, and decision-support tools to communicate insights effectively to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Present findings and recommendations to senior and executive leadership, influencing decisions through compelling data storytelling and business-focused communication.
  • Partner with Data Engineering, Data Science, Technology, Product, Finance, and Business Operations teams to ensure data integrity, governance, and scalable analytical solutions.
  • Establish best practices for analytical rigor, model governance, data quality, and performance measurement.
  • Drive the adoption of emerging analytical technologies, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and industry best practices to enhance business capabilities.
  • Lead, develop, and mentor leaders and teams within the Decision Science organization, fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, inclusion, and high performance.
  • Manage workforce planning, performance management, employee engagement, talent development, succession planning, and organizational effectiveness initiatives.
  • Serve as a thought leader and trusted advisor, promoting data literacy and analytical decision-making throughout the enterprise.
  • Stay current on industry trends, emerging technologies, and advancements in decision science methodologies.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Experience Requirements

  • 10+ years of experience in analytics, decision science, data science, business intelligence, statistics, actuarial analytics, operations research, or related quantitative disciplines.
  • 5+ years of progressive people leadership experience, including leading managers and developing high-performing analytics organizations.
  • Demonstrated experience influencing senior leaders and driving enterprise-level business decisions through analytics and insights.
  • Experience applying advanced statistical techniques, predictive modeling, experimentation, forecasting, machine learning, and optimization methodologies to solve business problems.
  • Strong executive communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and collaborating with business, technology, and data teams.

Education Requirements

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
  • Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Data Science, Economics, Business Analytics, Computer Science, Operations Research, or a related quantitative discipline preferred.

Physical Actions

Job is performed in-person at a Farmers office or virtually at an approved alternative work location. The physical work environment is indoors and climate-controlled with adequate lighting and ventilation. Normal and customary distractions include background noise produced by office equipment and chatter among people, as well as interruptions. Frequently sits for prolonged periods of time, up to a full shift. Occasionally moves about the workplace including, navigating stairs, ramps, and level or uneven surfaces. Occasionally moves, pushes, pulls, lifts, carries, and/or places objects or materials weighing up to 25 pounds without assistance. Frequently uses shoulders, arms, hands, and fingers to manipulate equipment, tools, and objects necessary to perform job duties. Frequently performs fine motor tasks such as typing, mousing, or writing, up to a full shift. Rarely performs movements such as bending, stooping, crouching, kneeling, twisting, and reaching overhead or below the knees. Possesses clear vision, with or without correction, to visually read and verify information. Relies on depth perception and peripheral vision to navigate the work environment visually by identifying barriers, changes in terrain and locating objects. Possesses adequate hearing, with or without correction, to communicate with co-workers, respond promptly to auditory signals or alarms, and discern sounds essential for maintaining safety and productivity in the workplace. Jobs in this category require rare, if any, travel.

Benefits

  • Farmers offers a competitive salary commensurate with experience, qualifications and location.

Job Summary

The Principal Data & Analytics Leader is a senior leadership role responsible for defining and executing enterprise data and analytics, and AI strategies that drive business performance, customer and agent experience, operational excellence, profitability, and growth. This leader partners closely with business stakeholders, the data and analytics organization, and IT leadership to transform insight into actionable recommendations, scalable products, and strategic capabilities that influence decision-making across the organization. This role requires a consultative mindset that can connect with executives on creating well developed and value-added insight solutions.

As a strategic partner to our stakeholders this role provides a clear vision to leadership on design, development, implementation, and governance of enterprise data and analytics solutions, while fostering a culture of innovation, data-driven decision making, and continuous improvement. The position will lead a high-performing team responsible for aligning capabilities to the requirement of the organization in meeting its key performance indicators and goals. Focusing on data engineering, analytics, reporting, governance, and advanced analytical capabilities to deliver measurable business value.

Essential Job Functions

  • Identifies and drives opportunities to leverage advanced analytics, predictive modeling, machine learning, and emerging technologies to create competitive advantages and business value.
  • Develops and communicates strategic roadmaps, priorities, and investment recommendations while ensuring successful execution of large-scale initiatives.
  • Partners with business leaders to establish meaningful performance metrics, measurement strategies, and actionable insights that improve operational and financial outcomes.
  • Builds, develops, and mentors high-performing teams while fostering collaboration, innovation, and professional growth.
  • Develops and executes enterprise data and analytics strategies aligned with organizational priorities and long-term business objectives.
  • Leads cross-functional teams responsible for the delivery, maintenance, and modernization of data, reporting, analytics, and AI-enabled solutions across multiple business domains.
  • Serves as a trusted advisor to executive leadership, translating complex business challenges into scalable data-driven strategies and solutions.
  • Establishes and advances enterprise data governance practices, ensuring data quality, integrity, security, compliance, and effective stewardship.
  • Leads the design and implementation of highly complex data and analytics products, platforms, and capabilities that support strategic decision-making and business transformation initiatives.
  • Champions data literacy and a culture of data-driven decision making across the organization through thought leadership, coaching, and organizational influence.
  • Drives continuous improvement initiatives, leveraging data to optimize processes, enhance customer and agent experiences, and improve organizational performance.
  • Ensures adherence to data management standards, architectural principles, governance policies, and regulatory requirements.
  • Leads multiple concurrent enterprise initiatives, balancing strategic priorities, resources, risks, and timelines to achieve business outcomes.

Experience Requirements

  • 12+ years of progressive experience in developing and solutions that are rich in data analytics, data engineering, business intelligence, data science, and information management.
  • 5+ years of leadership experience managing teams and enterprise-scale data and analytics initiatives.
  • Strong knowledge and hands-on experience in the P&C marketplace with a focus on sales, service, and claims.
  • Demonstrated success developing and executing enterprise insight strategies that drive measurable business results.
  • Experience leading large-scale transformation, modernization, analytics, or AI initiatives within complex organizations.
  • Proven ability to influence senior leaders and drive alignment across business and technology functions.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in data Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, Business, or a related field required.
  • Experience in modernization of solutions and technologies applied to the P&C industry or service / claims models.  
  • Relevant industry certifications in AI, cloud, analytics, or  data management disciplines are a plus.

Physical Actions

This role, whether performed virtually or in an office setting, will include normal and customary distractions, noise, and interruptions. Sits or stands for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift. Occasionally reaches overhead and below the knees, including bending, twisting, pulling, and stooping. Occasionally moves, lifts, carries, and places objects and supplies weighing 0-10 pounds without assistance. Listens to, interprets, and differentiates auditory information (example others speaking) at normal speaking levels with or without correction. Visually verifies and reads information. Visually locates material, resources and other objects. Ability to continuously operate a computer for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift. Physical dexterity sufficient to use hands, arms, and shoulders repetitively to operate keyboard and other office equipment up to a full work shift.

Job Summary

Essential Job Functions

  • Monitors teams daily, weekly, and monthly performance, including sales performance, customer experience, quality, efficiency, and compliance with established company and regulatory guidelines through active call listening, side-by-sides, and one-on-one coaching.

Job.JobDescription:
We are Farmers – where ambition meets opportunity.

At Farmers, we’re not just known for unforgettable jingle – we’re a team with a passion for purpose and making a real difference in people’s lives. We deliver peace of mind when it matters most.
