Requisition #: 76401

The Role at a Glance

Lincoln Financial Group is seeking a detail-oriented and delivery-focused Product Owner to join our AI Product & Delivery organization. In this role, leading innovation squads, you will own the day-to-day execution of AI product features and capabilities within an assigned product domain, working hands-on with data science, engineering, and business domain teams to bring AI solutions from backlog to production. Reporting to the VP/AVP of AI Products, you will serve as the connective tissue between business process reimagination and technical delivery — writing clear user stories, managing sprint-level priorities, supporting model evaluations, and ensuring AI features meet quality, compliance, and user experience standards. This role is ideal for a practitioner who thrives in the details and is eager to grow their AI product career in a regulated financial services environment.

What you'll be doing

AI Feature Ownership & Delivery

  • Own and maintain the product backlog for assigned AI features or squads, ensuring stories are well-defined, prioritized, and ready for sprint execution.
  • Write detailed user stories, acceptance criteria, and feature specifications for AI-driven capabilities in collaboration with engineering and data science teams.
  • Lead actively in agile ceremonies — sprint planning, standups, reviews, and retrospectives — keeping delivery on track and surfacing blockers early.
  • Coordinate UAT, QA, and launch readiness activities for AI feature releases, ensuring quality and compliance standards are met before go-live.
  • Support the AVP in managing timelines, dependencies, and risks across feature workstreams.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Serve as the day-to-day product contact for business SMEs, engineering squads, and UX designers within assigned AI feature areas.
  • Communicate feature status, trade-offs, and delivery risks clearly to the AVP and relevant business partners.
  • Facilitate working sessions and backlog refinement meetings to drive team alignment and shared understanding of requirements.
  • Support change management by helping business partners understand, test, and adopt new AI-driven capabilities.

Responsible AI & Compliance

  • Apply responsible AI principles — fairness, transparency, explainability, and privacy — in the definition and acceptance of AI features.
  • Escalate potential compliance, bias, or safety concerns identified during model evaluation or feature review to the AVP and relevant risk partners.
  • Ensure AI feature documentation, testing evidence, and release artifacts meet Lincoln's internal governance and audit standards.
  • Collaborate with Trust & Safety, Legal, and Compliance teams as needed to support feature-level risk reviews.

Performance & Insights

  • Define and track feature-level success metrics including adoption, task completion, model accuracy, and user satisfaction.
  • Analyze usage data, model performance logs, and user feedback to identify improvement opportunities and inform backlog prioritization.
  • Contribute to sprint-level reporting and help maintain product dashboards that surface key delivery and quality metrics.
  • Share learnings from evals, user testing, and post-launch monitoring with the broader AI Product & Delivery team.

Data Science & Model Evaluation Support

  • Partner with data scientists and ML engineers to understand model capabilities, limitations, and evaluation results for assigned AI features.
  • Assist in designing and executing evaluations (evals) for LLM-powered features — assessing output quality, accuracy, relevance, and safety against defined benchmarks.
  • Review and annotate model outputs as part of human-in-the-loop feedback processes, identifying failure modes, edge cases, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Support the creation of eval datasets, test case libraries, and regression frameworks to enable consistent model performance tracking.
  • Assist in prompt testing and iteration — running structured experiments to understand how prompt changes affect model behavior and output quality.
  • Help monitor model performance post-launch and flag regressions or unexpected behavior to the data science team.

What we’re looking for

Must-haves:

  • 3–10 years of experience in product management, product ownership, or a closely related role.
  • Hands-on experience working on AI, ML, or data-driven products — including direct collaboration with data science or engineering teams.
  • Familiarity with LLM concepts such as prompt engineering, model evaluation, and output quality assessment.
  • Experience with agile methodologies and backlog management tools (e.g., Jira, Linear, Productboard).
  • Strong written communication skills — able to write clear, unambiguous user stories, PRDs, and feature specifications.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Business, or a related field.

Nice-to-haves:

  • Hands-on experience with LLM APIs or enterprise AI platforms (e.g., Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Anthropic Claude, Google Vertex AI).
  • Exposure to ML evaluation frameworks, annotation workflows, or AI observability tools (e.g., LangSmith, Weights & Biases).
  • Familiarity with responsible AI practices including bias detection, fairness evaluation, and model explainability.
  • Domain experience in life insurance, annuities, retirement planning, or employee benefits.
  • Product or AI-related certifications (Pragmatic, AIPMM, data science, or ML-related).

Application Deadline

Applications for this position will be accepted through September 30, 2026, subject to earlier closure due to applicant volume.

The Role at a Glance

We are excited to bring on a Director, Clinical & Vocational Operations to our claim’s organization.  This role will be remote, or hybrid based on the proximity to Charlotte or Omaha.


As a Clinical Director, you will provide leadership and direction to drive results for clinical organization with a focus on operational effectiveness, quality, and collaboration between internal stakeholders. You will oversee and provide direction on all aspects of various assigned complex transformational projects within the clinical organization, with a focus on operational planning, transformational segmentation alignment, organizational efficiency and effectiveness, resource optimization, and operational resources & technology.   You will also function as a partner to senior leaders and internal/external stakeholders to advise on new & enhanced processes & tools to deliver best-in-class clinical model.

What you'll be doing

•    Leads transformational initiatives pertaining to the clinical organization, including the oversight and execution of approved decisions that enhance the internal and external customer experience.
•    Directs business organizational readiness planning and execution for new and ongoing projects/process enhancements that lead to an overall effective operation.
•    Conducts industry research to continually benchmark productive, quality and process improvements to enhance the customer experience. Provides senior leadership with a summary of research; makes and executes recommendations enhance process improvements and bring new insight into transformation the clinical market story. 
•    Partners with other relevant functions to enable the clinical area to be a valued thought partner for other business areas to support the mission of maximizing service capability & delivery.
•    Lead project resource and process function by acting as the point of contact for internal/external stakeholders that require collaboration with resources from clinical and claims.
•    Directs operational workforce & volume analysis, including analysis for multiple operational products, segments, and/or systems. Ensures staff is allocated to effectively load balance/optimize inventory management and process efficiencies. 
•    Plans, directs, supervises, and evaluates workflow of employees responsible for analyzing clinical trends, including work volume and patterns, staff productivity, attrition rates, and resource allocation.
•    In collaboration with senior leaders, establishes & defines objectives focused on customer service & operational effectiveness. Leads resources in gathering analytics to explain drivers of gaps & service successes.
•    Leads the development of metrics, tracking tools, and/or reporting to facilitate the evaluation of inventory management, productivity, and operational effectiveness to key stakeholders. 
•    Drives cross-functional team(s) to continually monitor service & productivity data/metrics to implement and/or further enhance tools & resources.
•    Leads the development of change management plans, including communications & trainings for applicable stakeholders, to ensure new & enhanced processes & tools are well-understood and effectively implemented & utilized.
•    Directs and evaluates individual/team performance and takes appropriate action to meet and/or exceed performance standards for assigned area(s) of responsibility by holding the team accountable for their results.

·    Leading and mentoring a team of 7 Clinical Managers.
·    Creating a strategic roadmap to transform our clinical organization through process enhancements and creating efficiencies to be a market leader.
·    Lead a clinical organization that drives consistent communication, accountability, innovation, and strategic visionary.
·    Maintaining knowledge on current and emerging developments/trends for assigned area(s) of responsibility, assessing impact, and collaborating with senior management to incorporate new trends and developments in current and future strategies.
·    Collaborate effectively with business partners and stakeholders. 
·    Evaluate training gaps and establish a training curriculum and medical protocols to establish best practices on clinical movement in claims.

What we’re looking for

Must-haves: 


•    4 Year/bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor’s) (Minimum Required)
•    7+ years of operations/clinical expertise (RN or BHC) and/or business process experience directly aligned to the specific duties for this role, including 5+ years of managerial, supervisory, and/or demonstrated leadership experience (Required)

The Role at a Glance

An exciting opportunity to take a lead role on the RPS Pricing and Risk team responsible for product strategy, pricing, and actuarial risk management. You will serve as the lead analyst on strategic projects that support the business — building the analysis, developing the recommendation, and helping senior decision makers land on a path forward. You will also deliver the key reporting that informs how leadership manages product, pricing, and risk governance, including support for our stable value rate setting process. This position is built for someone who can work independently, communicate credibly with senior leaders, and turn complex analysis into recommendations that move the business forward. 

What you'll be doing

  • Supporting strategic projects: Leading assigned workstreams on strategic initiatives from direction through implementation — developing the approach, managing timelines, coordinating with cross-functional partners, and carrying the work through to a recommendation with limited day-to-day oversight 
  • Communicating and influencing: Building the supporting analysis and presenting findings and recommendations to leaders across RPS Finance, Product, Investments, and Risk; working through differing viewpoints to help reach alignment 
  • Analyzing: Evaluating market dynamics, competitive positioning, profitability, and risk exposures to deliver actionable recommendations grounded in data 
  • Reporting and rate setting support: Delivering monthly and quarterly reporting on product performance, pricing, and risk governance, including key metrics for RPS management and corporate stakeholders; supporting the stable value rate setting process in partnership with Product, Investments, and Finance; ensuring strong controls and minimizing operational risk 
  • Innovating and automating: Identifying and implementing process improvements, automation, and enhanced data visualization that raise quality and efficiency across the team 

What we’re looking for

Must-haves: 

  • 6+ years of increasing experience in pricing, product, reporting, or risk management within financial services that aligns with the specific responsibilities of this position 
  • Demonstrated ability to carry a project from start to finish, including scoping, execution, and implementation across multiple stakeholders 
  • Executive presence — the ability to communicate clearly and credibly with senior leaders and influence outcomes through well-supported recommendations 
  • Strong technical skills and understanding of actuarial, mathematical, and financial concepts 
  • Proficiency in advanced Excel and at least one programming or analytics tool (e.g., VBA, Python, SQL, Dataiku, Power BI) 
  • Demonstrated critical thinking and the ability to analyze data, identify trends, and draw valid conclusions 
  • 4 Year/Bachelor’s Degree in a quantitative field (e.g., actuarial science, mathematics, statistics, finance, economics, data science, computer science, or engineering) 
  • Professional designation or progress toward one (e.g., FSA / ASA / CFA) 

Nice-to-haves: 

  • Retirement industry, stable value, or general insurance knowledge 
  • Experience in actuarial, pricing, or related financial roles 
  • Exposure to statistical and/or actuarial modeling 
  • Track record of identifying, recommending, and implementing process improvements

Applications for this position will be accepted through November 25th, 2026 subject to earlier closure due to applicant volume.

The Role at a Glance

As a Lead Actuary, Life Strategic Modeling you will support special modeling projects for Lincoln’s life insurance portfolio. 

What you'll be doing

Model Development
•Work within MG-ALFA/Integrate to improve processes and financial projections

Strategic Initiatives
•Support complex reinsurance agreements to improve capital management and drive company strategy

Assumption Updates

•Excellent organization and documentation of work product
•Nimble and flexible, able to quickly switch between projects as priorities change
•Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)
•Knowledge of life products
•Complex model development experience within MG-ALFA/Integrate

The Role at a Glance

The Lead Actuary on the Life Reinsurance team supports Lincoln’s traditional and complex reinsurance initiatives across Life Solutions. The role combines Life product expertise with reinsurance structuring and analytics to manage existing inforce arrangements and to execute and implement new reinsurance solutions. The Lead Actuary partners with external reinsurers and internal stakeholders to develop cost-effective reinsurance programs aligned with Lincoln’s reinsurance strategy.

What you'll be doing

Life Product Knowledge
•Partner with Pricing and Product Development to understand new product features and product changes and explain their reinsurance implications to reinsurers.
•Connect internal teams with reinsurer expertise on products emerging in the marketplace.


Reinsurance Modeling & Analysis
•Analyze reinsurance structures and retention usage to identify solutions that are cost-effective and consistent with Lincoln’s reinsurance strategy.
•Develop and present recommendations to senior management and influence decisions on reinsurance solutions.
•Build and enhance reinsurance reporting and analytics using enterprise tools (Python, SAS, Oracle SQL, Tableau).


Actuarial / Technical Support
•Maintain actuarial models and analytical tools, ensuring accuracy, efficiency and documentation consistent with model governance standards.
•Identify improvement opportunities and develop tools for business relationship managers and other stakeholders.


Reinsurance Relationship Management
•Build and maintain trusted relationships with reinsurance partners on inforce arrangements and new business solutions.
•Respond to reinsurer inquiries and communicate product updates, using product knowledge and an understanding of risk from the reinsurer’s perspective.

Collaboration & Leadership
•Serve as the reinsurance subject matter expert for internal stakeholders, helping them assess, select and recommend solutions that meet business goals.
•Lead cross-department reinsurance projects, managing scope, timelines and stakeholder communication.
•Review the work of, and mentor, other actuaries and analysts on the team.

What we’re looking for

Must-haves


•5-7+ years of experience in actuarial science directly aligned with the responsibilities above.
•Actuarial credentials (FSA or ASA with additional years of experience) 
•Bachelor’s degree, or 4+ years of comparable work experience required.
•Proficiency in SAS, SQL, Excel VBA.
•Life product knowledge and reinsurance business knowledge.

Nice-to-haves


•Experience with Python, Tableau, Dataiku and Oracle SQL databases.
•Familiarity with reinsurance-related regulatory, reserving and capital frameworks.

The Role at a Glance

The Actuarial Development Program (ADP) at Lincoln Financial is an industry-leading program that demonstrates Lincoln Financial’ s commitment to creating highly qualified business leaders.  As an ADP participant, you’ll be able to explore your unique interests while developing the essential actuarial, technical, management, communication, and leadership skills you need to succeed. The Actuarial Development Program includes a series of rotations, typically every 18-24 months. For each rotation, roles are available in different business areas including Life and Annuities, Retirement and Group Protection. Experience gained will enable participants to become well-rounded actuaries with knowledge that may include Product Development, Pricing, Valuation, Modeling, Risk Management, Asset Liability Management, Investments, Data Analytics, and Internal Audit.
 
ADP participants are expected to pass the Society of Actuaries’ exams at a prescribed pace. The program is designed to support you as you work towards your FSA and provide the training and resources necessary to become a well-rounded actuarial leader.
 
Additional Program Highlights:
•Highly competitive compensation package with salary increases and bonuses upon successful exam completion
•Social and training opportunities to enhance skills, network with ADP participants and build long-lasting industry relationships 
•Dedicated leaders and mentors to assist with career development
Work with actuarial and data science software and technologies including MG-ALFA, Axis, Prophet, Dataiku, R, and Tableau
•Generous study time allowances for each exam session
•Payment and/or reimbursement of actuarial exam fees, materials, review courses, and seminars taken during the program 

We are seeking an Associate Actuary, Internal Audit to apply actuarial knowledge in support of Internal Audit engagements involving actuarial subject matter, including market risk, product development, pricing, reserving, and other actuarial functions. The role works closely with senior actuarial and audit team members to execute defined testing procedures, evaluate risks, controls, and processes, and support audit conclusions and recommendations.

This position is designed for an actuarial professional who has completed two rotations through the company's Actuarial Development Program and is interested in applying that experience in an Internal Audit setting. Prior Internal Audit experience is not required. With guidance, coaching, and regular review from experienced team members, you will support the evaluation of actuarial assumptions, models, and controls while building both technical actuarial depth and Internal Audit knowledge.

What you'll be doing

•Apply actuarial knowledge to support the assessment of the reasonableness of methodologies, assumptions, models, and results as part of audit engagements involving actuarial activities.
•Support audit planning activities by gathering information about actuarial processes, risks, and controls, and assist in developing actuarial testing procedures under the direction of senior team members.
•Perform defined technical actuarial testing, such as recalculations, data reconciliations, benchmarking, and reasonableness and sensitivity analysis, and support the evaluation of model governance, validation, and change management practices.
•Review assumption-setting documentation, experience studies, and supporting data, and raise questions or inconsistencies with senior team members for further evaluation.
•Support the evaluation of actuarial processes and controls, including data inputs, model and end-user computing controls, peer review, and the reporting of actuarial results to management.
•Document testing results and technical observations, and contribute to the preparation of audit observations and recommendations related to actuarial risks and controls.
•Communicate clearly with Internal Audit colleagues and business partners, and participate in client meetings and walkthroughs as directed.
•Seek and incorporate coaching and feedback from senior actuarial and audit team members, and share knowledge gained through Actuarial Development Program experience with the team.
•Remain informed of emerging actuarial risks, regulatory developments, and industry trends, and bring relevant considerations to the team.
•Learn and apply audit methodology, including risk assessment, audit execution, documentation, and reporting, in accordance with department policie and standards. Prepare work papers that clearly document actuarial testing performed, sources, results, and conclusions.
•Support tracking of remediation activities for actuarial-related issues, as directed by the audit lead.
•Build working relationships with Actuarial, Risk Management, Finance, and other first and second line partners, while maintaining independence and objectivity.
•Continue developing knowledge of actuarial standards of practice, industry regulations, and best practices, and of the company's products, operations, and regulatory obligations.
•Develop working knowledge of the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission framework and carry out duties in compliance with the Institute of Internal Auditors' Global Internal Audit Standards, state and federal regulations, and company policies and procedures.

What we’re looking for

Must-haves:

•Successful completion of two rotations through the company's Actuarial Development Program (3+ years of experience).
•Bachelor's degree in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Finance, Economics, or a related field.
•Working knowledge of actuarial concepts, methodologies, and models, and practical experience applying them in areas such as market risk, asset-liability management, product development, pricing, valuation, or reserving, gained through Actuarial Development Program rotations.
•Demonstrated ability to analyze data and actuarial information, apply sound judgment, and effectively communicate findings and questions.
•Strong written and oral communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts clearly.
•Ability to manage assigned work and multiple priorities in a deadline-driven environment, with appropriate guidance and supervision.
•Willingness to learn Internal Audit methodology and apply it in conjunction with actuarial expertise. Prior Internal Audit experience and audit certifications are not required.
•Proficiency with Microsoft Office suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).
•Upon Hire Certifications/Licensures: (5-8 Actuarial Exams passed; typically has ASA designation, progressing toward FSA designation.

Nice-to-haves:


•Progress toward the Associate or Fellow of the Society of Actuaries designation.
•Exposure to model validation, peer review, or actuarial governance and controls.
•Experience with data analytics and programming tools and with actuarial modeling and valuation platforms.
•Familiarity with internal control frameworks, risk assessment, or audit concepts.
•Interest in emerging technologies, including AI, and how they may impact actuarial and business risk.

The Role at a Glance

We are seeking a Lead Actuary, Internal Audit to apply actuarial expertise in support of Internal Audit engagements involving actuarial subject matter, including market risk, product development, pricing, reserving, and other actuarial functions. The role partners closely with audit leaders and business stakeholders to evaluate risks, controls, methodologies, and processes and contributes to audit conclusions and recommendation. 

This position is designed for a Fellow of the Society of Actuaries who is interested in leveraging actuarial expertise to contribute to complex Internal Audit engagements. Prior Internal Audit experience is not required. Working under established audit methodologies and in partnership with experienced auditors, you will evaluate actuarial risks, assumptions, models, and controls while developing Internal Audit knowledge and contributing to audit conclusions and recommendations.

What you'll be doing

•Apply actuarial knowledge and professional judgment to assess the reasonableness of methodologies, assumptions, models, and results as part of audit engagements involving actuarial activities.
•Support audit planning activities by identifying actuarial risks and control objectives, and recommend the scope, nature, and extent of actuarial testing procedures for complex and higher-risk audit topics.
•Design and perform technical actuarial testing, including independent recalculation, benchmarking, sensitivity and reasonableness analysis, and evaluation of model governance, validation, and change management practices.
•Evaluate assumption-setting processes, experience studies, and the use of expert judgment, and challenge conclusions where support is insufficient or inconsistent with actuarial standards of practice, regulatory requirements, or financial reporting requirements.
•Evaluate actuarial processes and controls, including data inputs, model and end-user computing controls, peer review, and the governance and reporting of actuarial results to management.
•Develop and document technical conclusions and contribute to the preparation of audit observations and recommendations related to actuarial risks and controls.
•Communicate complex actuarial concepts clearly to Internal Audit colleagues, business partners, and senior stakeholders, including in client meetings and closing discussions.
•Share actuarial knowledge and provide peer support to team members and co-source partners, as appropriate. 
•Remain informed of emerging actuarial risks, regulatory developments, and industry trends and incorporate relevant considerations into audit activities.
•Learn and apply audit methodology, including risk assessment, audit execution, documentation, and reporting, in accordance with department policies and standards. Prepare work papers that clearly document actuarial testing performed, sources, results, and conclusions.
•Support monitoring and validation of remediation activities for actuarial-related issues, as directed by the audit lead.
•Partner with Actuarial, Risk Management, Finance, and other first and second line partners to establish strong working relationships, while maintaining independence and objectivity.
•Stay current on actuarial standards of practice, industry regulations, and best practices, while continuing to expand knowledge of the company's products, operations, and regulatory obligations.
•Apply the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission framework and carry out duties in compliance with the Institute of Internal Auditors' Global Internal Audit Standards, state and federal regulations, and company policies and procedures.

What we’re looking for

Must-haves:
•Fellow of the Society of Actuaries (FSA) designation.
•Bachelor's degree in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Finance, Economics, or a related field.
•5+ years of experience in the insurance or financial services industry, including hands-on experience in one or more areas such as market risk, asset-liability management, product development, pricing, valuation, or reserving.
•Strong working knowledge of actuarial methodologies, models, and assumptions, and of applicable actuarial standards of practice, statutory and GAAP reporting, and regulatory requirements.
•Demonstrated ability to analyze complex actuarial issues, apply sound professional judgment, and effectively communicate findings and recommendations.
•Strong written and oral communication skills, including the ability to explain technical actuarial concepts to non-actuarial audiences.
•Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and deliver quality work in a deadline-driven environment.
•Willingness to learn Internal Audit methodology and apply it in conjunction with actuarial expertise. Prior Internal Audit experience and audit certifications are not required.
•Proficiency with Microsoft Office suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).

Nice-to-haves:
•Experience with independent review, model validation, peer review, or actuarial governance and controls.
•Experience with data analytics and programming tools and with actuarial modeling and valuation platforms.
•Familiarity with internal control frameworks, risk assessment, or audit concepts.

The Role at a Glance

We are excited to bring on a Sr. Associate, Actuarial Product Specifications to support the Life Product business in a hybrid environment. We are open to candidates in any of the Lincoln key cities with preferred locations in Hartford, CT or Greensboro, NC. 

Background Details
As a Sr. Associate, Actuarial Product Specifications, you will help bring life insurance products, riders and enhancements from design through implementation. You’ll serve as an important connection between product and pricing actuaries and business partners, translating actuarial, regulatory and business requirements into clear, accurate product specifications. You’ll apply your knowledge of actuarial concepts and applicable regulations, including IRC Section 7702, to understand their impact on product features, calculations and specifications. Through collaboration with actuarial, legal, compliance, operations, administration and technology, you’ll help ensure product intent and requirements are consistently understood and implemented. If you enjoy combining analytical thinking, technical detail and cross-functional collaboration to bring products to life, please read on!

What you'll be doing

  • You will serve as a bridge between the team and pricing/product actuaries, providing technical and actuarial support during product development and implementation initiatives.
  • You will develop and maintain product specifications using established standards and guidelines to support new products and changes to existing products.
  • You will review product specifications for completeness, consistency, accuracy, and alignment with actuarial intent and identify issues requiring further review or resolution.
  • You will advise stakeholders on product design decisions, calculation methodologies, and downstream impacts.
  • You will provide actuarial input to support the development of product specifications, contract language, and related product documentation.
  • You will develop an understanding of applicable regulatory requirements, including IRC Section 7702, and interpret and apply those requirements to life insurance product features and specifications.
  • You will apply established guidelines to address challenging but non-complex specification issues and escalate matters requiring additional expertise.
  • You will collaborate with actuarial, legal, compliance, operations, administration, and technology partners to support consistent interpretation of product requirements.
  • You will support the translation of actuarial and business requirements into clear product specifications for implementation by internal and external stakeholders.
  • You will assist with product development and implementation activities for life insurance products, riders, and product enhancements.
  • You will explain product specifications, requirements, and established practices to stakeholders to support understanding and consistent execution.

What we’re looking for

  • 4 Year/Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor's)
  • 1+ Years actuarial experience or has passed three (3) actuarial exams
  • Excellent organizational skills with the ability to prioritize workload and multitask while maintaining strict attention to detail
  • Remains current in procession and industry trends, including regulations
  • Ability to evaluate information and data trends, solve challenging but non-complex problems, apply sound judgment to draw conclusions and act effectively in situations with limited standardization
  • Effectively and responsibly uses AI tools in daily work, validates AI-generated outputs, and identifies opportunities to improve productivity, decision making, and outcomes for themselves, colleagues, and the organization
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)

The Role at a Glance

The Lead Data Engineer provides technical leadership for Lincoln’s Data & Analytics platform on AWS. This role designs, builds, and maintains scalable data pipelines and optimizes data systems, with deep experience in Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon Redshift and strong knowledge of AWS services including Glue, Lambda, S3, Athena, and EC2. The role leads ETL development within an Agile team and partners with business, IT, and analytics stakeholders to deliver secure, governed, high-quality data that enables advanced analytics and reporting across Lincoln.

What you'll be doing

  • Design, build, and maintain robust batch and streaming data pipelines (including change data capture, for example AWS DMS) to support business intelligence and analytics.
  • Integrate structured and unstructured data from internal and external sources.
  • Develop ETL workflows using AWS Glue, Lambda, custom Python, PySpark, and SQL-based scripts.
  • Analyze database workloads and optimize queries, indexing, partitioning, and storage in Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon Redshift for integrity, performance, and cost.
  • Build S3-based data lake and warehouse layers (Glue Data Catalog, Athena, Parquet) with fine-grained access controls.
  • Own end-to-end data flows from source to consumption; traces and resolve issues across the full chain.
  • Apply data modeling standards (normal form, star, snowflake) and create technical designs from business requirements.
  • Orchestrate and schedule workflows (Stonebranch, Step Functions, Airflow) and monitor them with CloudWatch and automated data quality checks.
  • Ensure data security, governance, and compliance; monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize data workflows.
  • Integrate with upstream and downstream applications and collaborate with data scientists, analysts, and business stakeholders to deliver high-quality datasets; help shape data infrastructure strategy on AWS.
  • Set team standards, review code, mentor engineers, and own production support and process improvement.

What we’re looking for

Must-haves:

  • Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field.
  • 7+ years in AWS data engineering or a similar role.
  • Strong expertise in Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon Redshift, including database analysis, query optimization, advanced SQL, execution plans, indexing, distribution and sort keys, and workload tuning.
  • Holistic view of end-to-end data processing, from source to consumption, including dependencies, bottlenecks, and downstream impact.
  • Data and application integration experience with upstream source systems and downstream consumers (APIs, files, messaging, and reporting layers).
  • Hands-on AWS experience: Glue, Lambda, S3, Athena, EC2, and IAM.
  • Python / PySpark and SQL development for ETL and data integration in Agile, SDLC-based environments.
  • Data modeling, data governance, data quality, and data security practices.
  • DevOps and scheduling: Git, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, CloudFormation or similar, and Stonebranch scheduling knowledge (or a similar scheduler such as Autosys).
  • Hands-on use of approved AI-assisted development tools (GitHub Copilot or Claude Code), with validation of AI output and adherence to Lincoln data privacy and responsible AI requirements.
  • Proven ability to mentor engineers and lead delivery of complex projects.

Nice-to-haves:

  • AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate, Solutions Architect, or an AWS specialty certification.
  • EMR, Kinesis, Lake Formation, DynamoDB, and Apache Iceberg experience.
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot and Claude Cowork experience; coaching teams on safe AI use.
  • RAG data preparation, embeddings, vector stores, and AWS AI services (Bedrock, SageMaker, Amazon Q).
  • Salesforce CRM and MuleSoft (API-led integration) as upstream or downstream systems; MicroStrategy and Tableau reporting and BI background.
  • Financial data experience is a plus, especially Investment products like Mutual Funds, Alternative Funds and Fund Data management.

Core Competencies:

  • Technical leadership and AWS data engineering expertise.
  • Collaboration and Agile delivery with business, IT, and analytics teams.
  • Analytical depth, operational ownership, and a data-centric mindset (quality, governance, security).
  • AI fluency: responsible, validated use of AI tools.

The Role at a Glance

We are excited to bring on a highly motivated Sr. Associate Long Term Disability Team Lead to staff our ever-growing claims organization.

As a Sr. Associate Long Term Disability Team Lead, you will perform and deliver on long-term disability (LTD) claims assignments/projects while simultaneously leveraging and applying knowledge. You will review, investigate, and make claim determinations regarding coverage, compensability, and appropriateness assigned claims. You will provide oversight, technical information, detailed guidance and supervise the daily activities for their assigned claims area. Additionally, they will oversee and ensure the daily fair, ethical, and timely management of all claims area(s).

What you'll be doing

  • You’ll manage a caseload of complex Long Term Disability claims with varied eligibility types, policy provisions, and diagnoses.
  • You’ll apply policies and engage internal and external resources to ensure fair, ethical, and timely claim decisions.
  • You’ll make claim-related financial decisions within company guidelines.
  • You’ll use sound judgment and claims expertise to decide based on the information available.
  • You’ll explain policy details, the claims process, and determinations so customers understand the outcome.
  • You’ll keep inventory stable through timely risk management and efficient processing.
  • You’ll resolve escalated issues and elevate to management when needed.
  • You’ll research questions from the Claims team, partnering with Underwriting, Actuarial, Compliance, Account Management, and others to find answers.
  • You’ll provide technical guidance on claims adjudication and coach junior team members on medical terminology, duration, functionality documentation, and workflow.
  • You’ll monitor individual and team performance and act to meet or exceed standards.
  • You’ll analyze reports to spot trends, then propose and develop process improvements that enhance performance and the customer experience.
  • You’ll advise on how proposed process changes affect operations and system compatibility.
  • You’ll mentor others and model the behaviors that build claims knowledge and strong relationships.
  • You’ll contribute to departmental projects and lead workstreams as needed.

What we’re looking for

Must-have experience (Required):

  • 4 Year/Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor's).
  • 1+ Years of Long Term Disability claims experience directly aligned to the specific responsibilities for this role.
  • Ability to communicate effectively (verbal/written).
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).

Nice-to have experience (Preferred):

  • Strong mathematical skills for payment calculations.
  • Strong attention to detail.

Job.JobTitle: Sr. Director, AI-Native Intelligence & Data Insights
Job.JobDescription:
Alternate Locations: Radnor, PA (Pennsylvania); Charlotte, NC (North Carolina); Fort Wayne, IN (Indiana); Greensboro, NC (North Carolina)

 Work Arrangement:

Hybrid : Employee will work 3 days a week in a Lincoln office

Relocation assistance:  is not available for this opportunity.

Requisition #: 76793

The Role at a Glance

Lincoln Financial Group is building an AI Native Intelligence platform that turns enterprise data — starting with call center audio and transcripts, and expanding to claims, policy, and underwriting data — into a conversational, agentic layer the business can query directly. Instead of static reports, the platform is designed to let business users ask natural-language questions and get grounded, cited answers, backed by a real semantic understanding of Lincoln's data.

We're looking for a Senior Director to own the architecture and technical delivery of this platform end to end. This is a hands-on, builder-leader role: someone who sets the technical vision and roadmap, but who is equally comfortable reviewing a Bedrock agent's tool-calling logic, debugging a Step Functions pipeline, or sketching a knowledge graph schema on a whiteboard. You'll build and lead the team that takes this from pilot to enterprise scale.

What you'll be doing

  • Own the end-to-end architecture for the AI Native Intelligence platform on AWS — ingestion, enrichment, the semantic/business ontology layer, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), knowledge graphs, and agentic orchestration (Amazon Bedrock, Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon Neptune, OpenSearch Serverless, AWS Glue, Amazon Transcribe/Comprehend, and related services).
  • Translate diverse enterprise datasets — call center transcripts and audio, policy administration, claims, underwriting — into a unified, governed data and semantic foundation that supports natural-language querying and analytics.   
  • Design and evolve the business ontology, knowledge graph, and KPI/metrics glossary that ground the platform's AI in Lincoln's own business definitions, so answers are accurate and consistent with how the business already measures itself.
  • Lead build-vs-buy decisions across the AI/ML and data stack, and stay ahead of a fast-moving AWS AI landscape — model updates, agent frameworks, vector and graph databases, evaluation tooling.
  • Build, mentor, and scale a team of engineers, data scientists, and architects; set technical standards, run design/architecture reviews, and unblock hard technical problems.
  • Partner directly with business stakeholders — call center operations, claims, underwriting, compliance — to identify high-value insight use cases and translate them into technical requirements and delivery plans.
  • Establish guardrails, governance, and responsible-AI practices: PII handling and redaction, model evaluation, hallucination mitigation, human-in-the-loop review, and auditability.
  • Define and track success metrics for AI initiatives — retrieval/insight accuracy, adoption, time-to-insight, and cost-to-serve — and report progress to senior and executive leadership.
  • Stay technically hands-on: prototype new capabilities, review code and architecture, and work directly alongside the team rather than directing from a distance.

What we’re looking for

  • 12+ years of experience in data engineering, ML/AI engineering, or applied data science, including 5+ years in a technical leadership role (Director, Senior Manager, or Principal Architect) building production data or AI platforms.

Job.JobDescription:

In Office : Employees will work in a Lincoln office with a designated workspace.

The Role at a Glance

We are looking to add a Portfolio Management Associate Director to the Commercial Mortgage and Real Estate Investments team.


As a senior member of the Portfolio Management team, you will play a meaningful role in managing and overseeing the performance of a $17 billion commercial mortgage loan portfolio. Your primary focus is monitoring loan performance and mitigating risk and limiting loss across the portfolio. The ideal candidate is looking to grow their responsibilities in commercial real estate underwriting and credit analysis.


Primary Location: Charlotte, NC, US – In office Monday-Thursday; Fridays Flexible

What you'll be doing

Portfolio Monitoring and Risk Management
•Performs in-depth reviews of property operating statements and identifies positive and/or negative trends.
•Monitors complex loan structures and Borrower business plans reporting to senior management on a quarterly and/or ad hoc basis.
•Manages loan covenants and triggers working with internal and external partners ensuring compliance with loan documents
•Supports active management of troubled, watch, and surveillance loans on a monthly or quarterly basis.


Stakeholder Collaboration and Reporting
•Ensures data integrity at property and loan level for portfolio level analytics and reporting.
•Identifies and communicates process improvements to senior management.
•Serves as liaison partnering with the servicing and production teams to analyze underwriting related servicing requests, including but not limited to special servicing requests, lease approvals, collateral releases, substitutions, and sale and assumptions, and makes written and verbal approval recommendations to senior management.


Additional Responsibilities
•Maintains a high level of knowledge on market fundamentals such as rental rates, occupancy, capital market trends, and transaction activity for assigned geographic areas.
•Stays apprised of market related headlines affecting commercial real estate for reporting and analytics.
•Travels domestically for property inspections and conference events, as needed.
•May provide portfolio management support to real estate private equity team.
•Opportunities to collaborate across departments within the commercial real estate and overall investment team.

What we’re looking for

Must-have experience:
•4 Year/Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor’s) – minimum required in Finance, Business Administration, or similar field.
•3-5+ years’ experience required in commercial real estate finance and /or commercial real estate investment and analysis that aligns with the specific responsibilities for this position. Prior commercial real estate asset/portfolio management preferred.
•Knowledge of commercial real estate principles and valuation methods.
•Knowledge of national commercial real estate markets and macro-economic trends that affect those markets.
•Ability to understand and evaluate real estate financial statements including operating statements, balance sheets, and rent rolls.
•Knowledge of real estate legal concepts and strong understanding of loan documents.
•Ability to understand and apply financial concepts including but not limited to discounting cash flows, capitalization rates, internal rate of returns, and return on investment.
•Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.
•Experience with CoStar and Argus preferred.
•Strong attention to detail and ability to clearly and effectively communicate, in writing and verbally, complex loan and property operational concepts to senior management
•Travel 10% (intermittent)

The Role at a Glance

The Lead Software Engineer provides technical leadership for Lincoln Financial Data Strategy and Delivery team. This role designs, builds, and maintains scalable data pipelines and optimizes data systems, with deep experience in Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon Redshift and strong knowledge of AWS services including Glue, Lambda, S3, Athena, and EC2. The role leads a team of data engineers, owns delivery, sets technical vision, and partners with business, IT, and analytics stakeholders to deliver secure, governed, high-quality data that enables advanced analytics and reporting across Lincoln.

What you'll be doing

  • Lead and prioritize work, own delivery, set standards and a clear technical vision, review code, mentor engineers, and grow future leaders.
  • Design, build, and maintain robust batch and streaming data pipelines (including change data capture, for example AWS DMS) to support business intelligence and analytics.
  • Integrate structured and unstructured data from internal and external sources.
  • Develop ETL workflows using AWS Glue, Lambda, custom Python, PySpark, and SQL-based scripts.
  • Analyze database workloads and optimize queries, indexing, partitioning, and storage in Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon Redshift for integrity, performance, and cost.
  • Build S3-based data lake and warehouse layers (Glue Data Catalog, Athena, Parquet) with fine-grained access controls.
  • Own end-to-end data flows from source to consumption; trace and resolve issues across the full chain.
  • Apply data modeling standards (normal form, star, snowflake) and data quality practices; create technical designs from business requirements.
  • Orchestrate and schedule workflows (Stonebranch, Step Functions, Airflow / MWAA) and monitor them with CloudWatch and automated data quality checks.
  • Ensure data security, governance, and compliance; monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize data workflows.
  • Integrate with upstream and downstream applications and collaborate with data scientists, analysts, and business stakeholders to deliver high-quality datasets; help shape data infrastructure strategy on AWS.

What we’re looking for

Must-haves:

  • Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field.
  • 7+ years in AWS data engineering or a similar role (confirm years for Lead level).
  • Proven leadership: leading a team, owning delivery of complex projects, and communicating clearly with stakeholders; a strong vision and drive to develop as a leader.
  • Strong expertise in Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon Redshift, including database analysis, query optimization, advanced SQL, execution plans, indexing, distribution and sort keys, and workload tuning.
  • Holistic view of end-to-end data processing, from source to consumption, including dependencies, bottlenecks, and downstream impact.
  • Data and application integration with upstream source systems and downstream consumers (APIs, files, messaging, reporting).
  • Hands-on AWS experience: Glue, Lambda, S3, Athena, EC2, and IAM.
  • Python / PySpark and SQL development for ETL and integration in Agile, SDLC-based environments.
  • DevOps and scheduling: Git, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, CloudFormation or similar, and Stonebranch scheduling knowledge (or a similar scheduler such as Autosys).
  • Hands-on use of approved AI development tools (GitHub Copilot or Claude Code), validating AI output and following Lincoln data privacy and responsible AI requirements.

Nice-to-haves: 

  • AWS certification (Data Engineer – Associate, Solutions Architect, or specialty); EMR, Kinesis, Lake Formation, DynamoDB, or Apache Iceberg experience.
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot and Claude Cowork experience; coaching teams on safe AI use.
  • RAG data preparation, embeddings, vector stores, and AWS AI services (Bedrock, SageMaker, Amazon Q).
  • Salesforce CRM and MuleSoft (API-led integration) as upstream or downstream systems; MicroStrategy and Tableau reporting and BI background.
  • Financial data experience is a plus, especially insurance, annuities, or retirement (401k/403b).

The Role at a Glance

As the Lead Unified Communications & Collaboration (UCC) Systems Engineer, you will be an individual-contributor technical lead responsible for the architecture, engineering, security, reliability, and continuous improvement of Lincoln’s enterprise communications and collaboration environment. In this role leadership is demonstrated through hands-on expertise, technical direction, mentoring, and influence. You will combine deep expertise in Microsoft Teams, Exchange Online, Teams Phone, and enterprise telephony with broad knowledge of Microsoft 365 collaboration services, conference room and audiovisual technologies, SharePoint, OneDrive, Microsoft Copilot, and emerging collaboration technologies. You will guide architecture and engineering decisions, mentor engineers through complex work, and partner across technology teams to deliver secure, resilient, scalable, and user-focused solutions.

What you'll be doing

Technical Leadership and Engineering

  • Own technical direction for Lincoln’s UCC and Microsoft 365 environment, including architecture reviews, reference architectures, engineering standards, configuration baselines, and solution designs.
  • Lead complex implementations, migrations, integrations, lifecycle initiatives, and platform modernization from design through operational readiness.
  • Provide technical direction and hands-on mentoring to engineers, strengthening troubleshooting, design, and delivery capabilities without direct people-management responsibility.
  • Drive automation, standardization, platform simplification, and continuous improvement while reducing technical debt and manual effort.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies and translate Microsoft product roadmaps, industry trends, and artificial intelligence capabilities into prioritized platform roadmaps and investment recommendations.

 

 Platform and Operational Excellence

  • Serve as an escalation point for complex incidents and problem investigations, lead root-cause analysis, and drive sustainable corrective actions.
  • Support effective incident, problem, change, and service-health management practices.
  • Prepare solutions for architecture review and change governance, ensuring security, scalability, reliability, supportability, rollback planning, and operational ownership are addressed.
  • Maintain technical documentation, runbooks, and knowledge that support platform operation, troubleshooting, and knowledge transfer.

Communication, Collaboration, and Influence

  • Lead technical discussions and communicate risks, options, recommendations, and service outcomes clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Partner routinely with the Director of UCC/AV Engineering and leaders across Infrastructure, Network, Cybersecurity, Identity and Access Management, Enterprise Architecture, Artificial Intelligence, End-User Technology, Service Management, and Business Technology teams.
  • Build consensus across internal stakeholders, technology partners, and vendors while promoting accountability, knowledge sharing, and disciplined follow-through.

Leadership at Lincoln

This is an individual-contributor technical lead role with no direct reports. Leadership is demonstrated through expertise, sound judgment, accountability, mentoring, and influence. You will help engineers succeed on complex work, shape cross-team decisions, and model Lincoln’s expectation that employees demonstrate leadership within their respective roles.

Why Join Us

Join a team modernizing enterprise communications at scale. You will influence platform strategy and product roadmaps, help simplify and strengthen critical services, and shape how emerging capabilities including automation, Microsoft Copilot, and artificial intelligence are introduced securely and responsibly.

What we’re looking for

Must-Haves:

  • Expert-level capability in the architecture, engineering, administration, and troubleshooting of:
    • Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365 collaboration services
    • Exchange Online
    • Teams Phone, enterprise voice, and telephony
    • PowerShell-based administration and automation
  • Working knowledge of adjacent technologies and control domains, including SharePoint and OneDrive, Microsoft Copilot, identity and access management, collaboration governance, networking, security and compliance, monitoring, endpoint integration, and conference room and audiovisual technologies.
  • Experience designing, implementing, and supporting highly available enterprise services.
  • Experience leading complex implementations, migrations, integrations, and modernization initiatives.

The Role at a Glance

We’re looking for a senior hands-on architect to lead the technical direction of our DevOps Platforms & Engineering organization. You’ll shape how hundreds of application developers build, test, secure, and release software. That means bringing CI/CD, software supply chain, release automation, test automation, and performance engineering together into one coherent delivery platform.

This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports. You’ll set engineering standards, lead high-impact cross-functional initiatives, and advise leadership on technology strategy, while staying close to the work: designing solutions, automating, and solving the hardest production problems yourself. You’ll also help lead our adoption of AI-assisted engineering across the software delivery lifecycle.

What you'll be doing

  • Own the end-to-end architecture of our DevOps toolchain and engineering services, from source control and CI/CD through artifact management, code quality, security scanning, testing, release, and deployment, and keep the target-state architecture current.
  • Stay hands-on with design, implementation, upgrades, migrations, automation, and troubleshooting across our platforms.
  • Define engineering patterns, reference pipelines, and the standards behind our enterprise CI/CD templates and SDLC practices. Lead design on complex, enterprise-wide initiatives.
  • Set direction for test automation, service virtualization, and performance engineering, including how they plug into pipelines through quality gates and shift-left practices.
  • Drive modernization: toolchain consolidation, pipeline-based deployment, infrastructure as code, observability, and self-service capabilities for development teams.
  • Shape software supply chain security, platform resiliency, and audit readiness in partnership with Information Security.
  • Lead the evaluation and adoption of AI-assisted engineering across the toolchain, testing, and operations, including emerging patterns such as MCP, agent-to-agent integration, and AgentOps.
  • Lead architecture and design reviews, represent the team in enterprise architecture and governance forums, and act as a senior escalation point for complex, systemic incidents.
  • Mentor engineers and build depth across critical platforms, and partner with technology, security, architecture, cloud, and AI teams across the enterprise.
  • Contribute to multi-year roadmaps and give leadership clear recommendations on risks, trade-offs, vendors, and total cost of ownership.

What we’re looking for

Must-haves:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience.
  • Typically 12 or more years of progressive experience in DevOps, platform engineering, release engineering, software engineering, or test engineering, including significant time as an architect or senior technical lead.
  • Expert-level depth in one or more DevOps disciplines, such as CI/CD, artifact management and software supply chain, configuration management and infrastructure as code, or release automation.
  • Extensive hands-on experience engineering and supporting business-critical platforms such as GitLab, JFrog Artifactory, SonarQube, Puppet or Ansible, and enterprise release automation tools.
  • Practical experience with test automation (such as Selenium or Playwright) and performance testing (such as JMeter), and integrating them into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Strong skills in automation, scripting, APIs, and pipeline orchestration, plus working knowledge of AWS and of Linux and Windows environments.
  • A track record of leading complex cross-functional technical initiatives and influencing technology direction without formal authority.
  • The ability to communicate complex recommendations clearly to senior leadership.

Nice-to-haves:

  • Experience in a regulated industry, ideally insurance or financial services.
  • Experience running self-hosted enterprise platforms at scale.
  • Hands-on use of AI-assisted engineering tools in software delivery, testing, or platform operations.
  • Exposure to service virtualization or mainframe test automation.

Job.JobDescription:

The Role at a Glance

We are seeking a Lead Risk Management Analyst to join the Market Risk Governance team within Enterprise Financial Risk, part of the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) organization in Lincoln’s Chief Risk and Actuarial Office. This team provides independent second-line oversight of Lincoln’s market risk. That includes product-driven exposures in our Variable Annuities (VAs), Registered Index-Linked Annuities (RILAs), Fixed Indexed Annuities (FIAs), Guaranteed Variable Universal Life (GVUL), and Indexed Universal Life (IUL), as well as market risk that comes from General Account investment strategy. Some of these risks are managed through hedge programs, others through reinsurance or other risk transfer, and the mix changes over time. We give leadership an independent read on whether the risk mitigation is working as intended, challenge strategy and methodology, and raise concerns early when results diverge from expectations. The team also leads enterprise scenario governance.


You will partner with first-line hedging, actuarial, investments, and other risk teams. The ideal candidate will have strong quantitative skills, hands-on experience with derivatives and financial instruments, and the judgment to turn complex analysis into a clear point of view for senior stakeholders.

What you'll be doing

•Build out independent market risk reporting such as liability attribution, performance attribution of hedge programs and other risk mitigation, hedge trading activity, and risk profile.
•Review proposed changes to risk mitigation strategy (hedging, reinsurance, and other approaches), methodology, and parameters. Help prepare risk opinions that give leadership an independent view before decisions are made.
•Analyze market risk across equity, interest rate, and volatility exposures, and provide insights to management on residual and emerging risks, performance metrics, and any deviations from established risk limits.
•Help keep the market risk policy, limits, and governance documents current.
•Prepare analysis and materials for market risk committees, framed to support decisions.
•Work with other ERM teams where market risk meets liquidity, counterparty capacity, capital, and ALM.
•Provide thought leadership on whether current risk mitigation approaches still fit as products, markets, and capital rules change. 

What we’re looking for

•Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Mathematics, Actuarial Science, or a related field.
•Master’s degree or relevant professional certifications (e.g., CFA, FRM, FSA, CQF) is a plus.  
•5-7+ years of experience in market risk management, financial analysis, or a related field, preferably within the financial services or investment banking industry. Experience working in a second line market risk oversight role is a plus.
•Solid understanding of capital markets, derivatives, and annuity and life insurance products.
•Excellent quantitative and analytical skills with the ability to translate complex data into actionable insights.
•Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex risk information to senior stakeholders.
•High level of attention to detail, with the ability to identify and assess risks accurately and promptly.
•Strong programming skills (Python, VBA, SQL, etc.) 
•Working knowledge of visualization software such as Tableau, PowerBI, etc.
•Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook). 
•Familiarity with statutory capital frameworks (e.g., RBC, VM-21) is a plus.
•Ability to read, analyze and interpret both internal and external documents such as general media/publications, professional journals, technical procedures, governmental regulations, policies, proposals, and standard operating procedures.
•Ability to work collaboratively in cross-functional teams and manage multiple priorities.

In office Monday - Thursday with flexibility to work from home on Friday

We are looking to add an Associate Director to the Commercial Mortgage and Real Estate Investments team.  


In this position, within the Loan Production Team, you will provide experienced support in the annual origination of $2 billion of commercial mortgage investments throughout the United States. Additional responsibilities involve the ongoing management of the $17 billion commercial mortgage portfolio. The ideal candidate is looking for increased origination responsibilities including credit analysis and business development. 

What you'll be doing

•Support Managing Directors in business development through correspondent relationships and new transactions for assigned territory; actively manage and develop relationships with correspondent mortgage bankers. Manage transactions from origination through closing.
•Underwrite new commercial real estate loan investment opportunities providing analysis and recommendations to the Managing Directors.
•Draft term sheets, application/commitment letters, and other transaction related documents for review by senior team members. 
•Complete due diligence analysis including review of leases, rent rolls, third party reports, estoppels, and other business-related matters.
•Work with senior team members and legal counsel in the negotiation of loan terms and documentation. 
•Prepare investment committee memos working collaboratively with senior team members, while leading the due diligence process for loans in the application stage. 
•Serve as business liaison throughout the loan closing process working with appropriate internal/external stakeholders to effectuate a timely closing.
•Act as a resource in the training and mentoring of junior team members. 
•Travel for due diligence and business development trips.
•Perform quarterly reviews, including operating statements and leasing updates, for existing loans. 
•Additional investment support may include real estate equity and credit fund investments.
•Handle special servicing requests as requested.

What we’re looking for

Must- have experience: 
•4 Year/Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor's) - Minimum Required
•3-5+ Years’ experience required in commercial real estate finance and/or commercial real estate investment and analysis that aligns with the specific responsibilities for this position.
•Experience analyzing asset lending transactions.
•Knowledge of commercial real estate principles and valuation methods.
•Knowledge of national commercial real estate and mortgage markets and macro-economic trends that affect those markets.
•Ability to understand and evaluate real estate financial statements. 
•Knowledge of real estate legal concepts and understanding of loan documents.
•Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint
•Experience with Costar and Argus preferred.
•Advanced degrees and/or certifications strongly preferred. 

Travel: 20%-30% (intermittent)

The Role at a Glance

We are looking to add a Senior Associate to our Commercial Mortgage and Real Estate Investments Team to work in the Charlotte or Greensboro office 4 days per week with an option to work remotely on Fridays. In this role, you will provide day-to-day administration and servicing of our commercial mortgage loan portfolio, working closely with relationship managers, mortgage bankers, production, closers, legal, and accounting to keep loan operations running smoothly. Beyond the core servicing work, we're looking for someone who is genuinely comfortable with technology and change — someone who can learn our current systems and processes quickly, get fluent with the AI and automation tools we use, and, once up to speed, feel empowered to point out where things could work better. As the ideal candidate, you will bring both strong servicing fundamentals and a fresh, tech-forward perspective to a well-established commercial mortgage servicing team managing a multi-billion-dollar loan portfolio.

What you'll be doing

•Administering and servicing the commercial loan portfolio, including processing payments, advances, and payoffs.
•Monitoring loan covenants, insurance, and other compliance requirements throughout the loan lifecycle.
•Maintaining and updating loan documentation and records in our loan servicing system(s).
•Managing escrow accounts and insurance/tax tracking.

The Role at a Glance

As Retirement Sales Director, you will be responsible for driving growth through new retirement plan sponsor acquisition, with a primary focus on mid to large market plans ($50M+ in assets). In this role, you will develop and execute a territory business plan designed to achieve ambitious sales, AUM, and market share goals across your assigned geography. You will serve as a key external representative, building and expanding relationships with retirement plan consultants, advisors, brokers, and plan sponsors. This is a highly consultative, relationship driven sales role that requires deep retirement industry knowledge, disciplined pipeline management, and close collaboration with internal partners to deliver comprehensive retirement solutions and exceptional client outcomes.

What you'll be doing

Drive Growth & New Business Acquisition
•    Lead new retirement plan sponsor acquisition with a focus on plans with $50M+ in assets
•    Develop and execute a territory and prospecting strategy to meet or exceed annual sales and AUM targets
•    Identify, qualify, and cultivate prospective plan sponsors through proactive outreach, referrals, networking, and consultant relationships
•    Manage the full sales cycle, from initial engagement through finalist presentations, pricing, contract negotiation, and close.
Build and Deepen Influencer Relationships
•    Build, maintain, and grow strong relationships with retirement plan consultants, advisors, brokers, and other centers of influence impacting mid to large market plan decisions
•    Increase territory penetration by strengthening partnerships with influential specialists and consulting firms
•    Position the organization as a preferred retirement provider through consistent engagement, education, and thought leadership
Deliver Consultative Retirement Solutions
•    Conduct needs based discovery with plan sponsors to understand fiduciary objectives, plan design, investments, participant outcomes, and service expectations
•    Present tailored retirement solutions, including recordkeeping, investments, managed accounts, and financial wellness offerings
•    Clearly articulate value propositions around fiduciary governance, plan outcomes, fee reasonableness, and participant engagement
Territory & Sales Execution Excellence
•    Manage a large geographic territory, executing external wholesale sales programs that drive revenue and market share growth
•    Conduct in person and virtual meetings such as due diligence sessions, consultant updates, one on one meetings, and industry sponsorships
•    Represent the organization at industry conferences, client events, and networking functions
•    Maintain accurate pipeline, activity tracking, and forecasting in CRM and sales reporting systems
•    Forecast sales activity and revenue with discipline, transparency, and accountability
•    Effectively manage expense budgets to maximize territory coverage and sales impact
Collaboration & Operational Discipline
•    Partner closely with internal stakeholders including operations, product, client service, core market counterparts, and consultant relations teams to support opportunities and ensure seamless onboarding and issuance
•    Ensure sold business is properly processed from point of sale through implementation
•    Uphold the highest standards of professionalism, ethics, and compliance, adhering to all policies, procedures, and cultural expectations

What we’re looking for

Must-Haves:
•    Minimum of 5+ years of experience in Defined Contribution retirement plan sales and/or relationship management, with direct alignment to the responsibilities of this role
•    Bachelor’s degree required, or equivalent professional experience (4 additional years of relevant experience in lieu of a degree)
•    Ability to obtain FINRA Series 6, Series 63, and Life & Health licenses within 120 days of hire
•    Confident and effective communicator with strong written and verbal communication skills
•    Demonstrated ability to communicate credibly and knowledgeably with senior leaders, both internally and externally
•    Strong presentation capabilities with a proven track record of influencing stakeholders at all levels through clear, logical, and well informed discussions
•    Advanced relationship management skills, including the ability to partner collaboratively with internal teams and build trusted relationships with external clients
•    Willingness and ability to travel up to 50%
 
Nice-to-Have:
•    Strong working knowledge of ERISA rules and regulatory requirements governing retirement plans

Applications for this position will be accepted through December 11th, 2026, subject to earlier closure due to applicant volume

Supports governance portfolio planning, resource forecasting, capacity management, and prioritization to balance reviews, projects, and ad hoc requests against available resources.

Job.JobDescription:
Alternate Locations: Work from Home; Radnor, PA (Pennsylvania)

 Work Arrangement:

Hybrid : Employee will work 3 days a week in a Lincoln office

Relocation assistance:  is not available for this opportunity.

The Role at a Glance

As a Senior Lead Risk Data Engineer and Architect, you will architect and lead the design and implementation of new technology solutions for the Risk Investments and Technology team within the Chief Risk Office (CRO). You will own technical roadmaps, champion SDLC best practices, and build production grade systems that power analytics, machine learning, and cross-functional risk management.  

 Working on a centralized cloud data platform (AWS, Databricks or Dataiku), you'll design scalable data pipelines, implement data governance frameworks using modern cataloging tools, and develop advanced solutions. This role is critical to modernizing how we manage market risk, credit risk, and operational risk data on the enterprise scale. 

 You'll partner closely with risk analysts, quantitative researchers, and technology leaders to migrate business-owned processes into robust, production-controlled platforms while maintaining operational excellence. 

What you'll be doing

•Architect cloud-native data solutions using AWS services (S3, Redshift, Glue, EMR, Lambda, Athena) and Databricks (Unity Catalog, Workflows, MLflow) or similar technology to support risk analytics at scale. 
•Build and optimize data pipelines using Python, PySpark, and SQL to integrate structured and unstructured data from internal and external sources. 
•Drive modernization initiatives by migrating legacy on-premises systems to cloud platforms while ensuring zero disruption to critical business services. 
•Implement data governance frameworks including cataloging, lineage tracking, quality monitoring, and access controls aligned with internal controls and regulatory requirements. 
•Collaborate cross-functionally with data scientists, risk managers, and business stakeholders to translate requirements into scalable technical solutions, drive change management and process improvements. 
•Develop production-grade code following DevOps practices including CI/CD, automated testing, code reviews, and infrastructure-as-code. 
•Manage and optimize relational databases (MySQL, Aurora PostgreSQL, Redshift) for performance, cost efficiency, and data integrity. 
•Integrate structured and unstructured data from various internal and external sources. 
•Mentor and influence technical standards and architectural decisions across the Risk, Investments Technology organization. 
•Monitor and troubleshoot production systems, implementing observability practices and proactive performance tuning.

What we’re looking for

•Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering or related field. 
•5+ years of experience in data engineering or similar role implementing with a variety of on-premises and cloud data management, integration, and analytical technologies. 
•Production experience with relational databases such as MySQL, and SQL Server, including designing schemas, writing complex queries, optimizing performance, and ensuring data integrity for a variety of business applications. 
•Strong experience with end-to-end data architecture implementing systems that use AWS services related to data storage and management, must have advanced proficiency in SQL, Python, YAML and Bash. 
•Thorough understanding of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), including DevOps practices, CI/CD processes, application resiliency, and security measures. 
•Excellent communication skills with ability to translate technical concepts for business audiences. 
•Data governance experience: catalog tools, data quality frameworks, lineage tracking, and compliance controls is a plus. 
•AWS certifications such as SAA, Associate Developer, Data Analytics Specialty, or Databricks certification is a plus.
