The Role at a Glance

The Facilities Site Manager will consult on more complex assignments/projects and act as a resource to internal and external stakeholders, including outside contractors, to deliver various services to Lincoln facilities. This position will coordinate the work of an internal team to conduct space & occupancy analysis/planning, open workspace design, and relocations. This position will also manage projects including: moves, relocations, installations, space improvements, and general building construction.

What you'll be doing

•    Assisting in the planning & management of facilities modifications and projects from inception of design concepts through design and implementation.
•    Coordinating team to manage moves, adds, relocations, and change processes.
•    Developing cost estimates related to space planning, relocation activities, and other projects.
•    Maintaining drawings and operational effectiveness of internal team.
•    Acting as a resource for clients & planning team to identify equipment requirements and coordinate support for furniture needs.
•    Reconciling invoices & purchase orders, submitting invoices for payment, tracking trends in spending.
•    Coordinating with Corporate Marketing to ensure all LFG branding items (banners, signs, logos etc.) align with branding guidelines. Working with external vendors to develop and install new items.
•    Serving as a point of contact and ensuring contracted services (food services, security, parking, custodial services) are effectively and satisfactorily executed in a manner consistent with standard processes and contract specifications.
•    Liaising with contractors and architects to answer questions regarding furnishings, layouts, interior remodeling, and other more complex modifications.
•    Inspecting construction/installation progress to ensure conformance to drawings, specifications, and schedule.
•    Creating and monitoring scorecards & dashboards of more complex metrics such as headcount projections, capacity, occupancy/vacancy ratios, space allocations & workplace conditions.
•    Identifying key metrics to monitor project progress and ensure success; communicating effectively to keep team & internal/external stakeholders informed of progress.
•    Promoting execution with a strong sense of urgency and focus on results; influencing team & external contractors to achieve defined objectives.
•    Evaluating effectiveness of facilities services, recommending & implementing process changes and participating in the development of best practices, new tools, & other approaches for operational efficiency.

What we’re looking for

•    4 Year/Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor's) (Minimum Required)
•    3+ Years experience in space planning and design that directly aligns with the specific responsibilities for this role (Required)

Exercises independent discretion and judgment in handling or directing litigated claims.

Position Summary

This is a high-impact leadership role where you’ll develop agents and District Sales Managers, help shape regional growth strategies, and make your mark at one of the most respected companies in the industry. 

The ideal candidate will live in the state of Illinois while working remotely.  This position comes with a company car with paid gas card.

What You’ll Do

  • Partner with branch leaders to set and achieve growth, profitability, and agency development goals.

  • Serve as a hands-on mentor to Agents and District Sales Managers, building expertise in ERIE’s commercial lines products and underwriting practices.

  • Evaluate complex commercial accounts, make underwriting and pricing decisions within authority, and collaborate with senior underwriters on larger risks.

  • Foster strong relationships with Agents, branch teams, and Home Office underwriting partners.

  • Represent ERIE in the community and maintain positive relationships with policyholders and stakeholders.

Who You Are

You’re a strategic thinker who leads with influence, not just authority. You enjoy rolling up your sleeves to develop others and have the commercial acumen to guide agents toward success. You’re comfortable making judgment calls on complex accounts and thrive on balancing growth with sound underwriting.

In addition, this position trains, develops and guides Agents and district sales managers (DSM) in a designated branch territory in the promotion and sale of commercial lines products, providing assistance in the areas of production, product knowledge and application, and underwriting. Establishes and maintains relationships with branch managers and Agents to improve Agent willingness and ability to pursue and place quality commercial business with the ERIE.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Assists branch managers in establishing short- and long-range objectives related to commercial lines sales, with an emphasis on growth, underwriting profitability and agency development and training.
  • Provides hands-on training and guidance to Agents on ERIE's commercial lines products, resources, and services, including identifying web-based resources and training programs for Agent use. Builds commercial expertise of new and existing Agents for increased independence and sound judgment when pursuing commercial business.
  • Provides hands-on training and guidance to branch DSMs on ERIE's commercial lines products, resources, and services, including identifying web-based resources and training programs. Builds commercial expertise of new and existing DSMs for increased independence and sound judgment when working with Agents to pursue commercial business.
  • Identifies Agents requiring additional guidance and interaction from their DSMs on commercial lines products and services. Works directly with DSMs, branch managers, and commercial underwriting staff to develop a plan to deliver that guidance and interaction as appropriate.
  • Contacts and visits Agents regularly to evaluate quotations and applications for multiple commercial lines to determine acceptability, including larger, more complex commercial accounts.
  • Makes acceptability and pricing decisions on risks within defined binding authority. Refers risks that are beyond binding authority to a senior commercial lines underwriter, risk analyst or underwriting supervisor.
  • Develops and maintains effective relationships and contact with Home Office commercial lines underwriting management and production underwriters.
  • Serves as a company representative in maintaining favorable Policyholder relationships. Works closely with adjusters and other claims personnel on matters of mutual concern.
  • Develops and maintains strong working knowledge of ERIE's commercial product lines, including policy features and key endorsements and sources of information on ERIE's products.
  • Represents the company in community relations activities as directed.
  • For branch office accounts, handles insurance agency business as a licensed, non-commission company Agent.

Supervises, trains, and monitors the activities of assigned claims adjusters and other claims personnel. Assists the Claims Leadership in the overseeing and handling of claims.

  • Experience handling personal and commercial auto liability claims is preferred.
  • This is an in-office position based at ERIE's Peoria, Illinois Branch Office that will lead a Zone Operations Team.  Hours are Monday - Friday 8:00 am - 4:30 pm.  Schedule and work location subject to change based on business and service level needs.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Manages overall operations of designated area of authority.   Interviews, hires, trains, and directs personnel.  Prepares and conducts performance assessments, coordinates discipline and oversees Employee development as required.
  • Reviews claims on a regular basis in accordance with company policy. reviews adjusters’ files for coverage and adequate reserves, acts as a resource for answering claims questions, provides additional services as required and takes action as necessary. Reviews claim correspondence and provides counsel on further action. 
  • Resolves coverage and other unusual questions within designated authority.  Conducts related research as necessary.

Position Summary

Receives, sorts, delivers, and/or prepares all mail for delivery.  Performs clerical functions according to established schedules and deadlines.  Incumbent may be responsible for one or more of the following: Incoming Mail, Outgoing Mail, Policy Assembly, Mechanical Mailing, and Operations Support.

Schedule for this position is:  Monday - Friday 7:30am -3:30am or 8:00am -4:00pm.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Receives and sorts mail from internal/external sources. Completes all aspects of fulfillment related to mail production.
  • Processes documents utilizing the most efficient and cost-effective method of delivery.
  • Secures unopened or undistributed mail.
  • Assists with company mailing projects.
  • Maintains confidentiality. 


Specific Duties by Discipline

Incoming Mail

  • Opens, sorts and routes incoming mail for Home Office campus.
  • Picks up and delivers all inbound and interoffice mail according to prearranged schedules.
  • Sorts cash payments for processing area according to type of payment.
  • Serves as liaison for Agents regarding Policyholder address updates and system questions.
  • Prepares special handling/time sensitive documents for mailing.
  • Follows set procedures to identify and handle suspicious mail package handling for internal employees.


Imaging

  • Prepares, scans and validates documents to organize customer data for both electronic and paper documents.
  • Verifies accuracy of metadata collaborating with internal customers before sending image to document storage system.
  • Sorts, organizes, and scans paper documents into software to release for validation.
  • Prepares special handling/time sensitive documents for mailing, which includes express mailing with claims checks.
  • Updates and maintains statistical database of completed jobs to track operator/department activity.


Outgoing Mail

  • Receives, sorts and prepares documents for Agents, branch offices, postal and express deliveries with accuracy.
  • Uses online shipping software and maintains sub-agent listings.
  • Provides courier service to internal and external customers requiring immediate or time sensitive deliveries.
  • Conducts quality checks of work for efficient delivery to external customers.
  • May maintain courier vehicle (gas, tires, etc.) and refers problems to supervisor.

Duties and Responsibilities (cont'd if applicable)

Policy Assembly

  • Sorts, assembles and prepares policy packets for mailing for policyholder, Agent and others.
  • Operates, identifies and escalates issues with the mechanical folding equipment.
  • Generates documents utilizing ERIE's systems and software applications (EGCF). to assemble policy non-renewals, cancellations and additional legal documents with Proof of Mailing.
  • Reviews pertinent information on time-sensitive notices to ensure accuracy. Proofreads all typed data for accuracy and inserts proper enclosures as necessary meeting legal mailing time requirements.
  • Batches documents for bulk mailing.


Mechanical Mailing

  • Operates and maintains mechanical mail equipment to prepare outgoing mail in efficient manner using bar code scanning and camera validation. 
  • Monitors systems in place for tracking and re-printing all documents, troubleshooting issues and minor repairs authorized by service technician.
  • Complies with appropriate safety measures relating to the operation of mechanical mail equipment.
  • Ensures the use of correct materials, verifies job contents, counts and palletizing mail.
  • Ensures vendor is consistent in scheduling weekly preventative and general maintenance of mailing equipment with established procedures.
  • Supports multiple areas across as needed.  Identifies and escalates issues which lead to inaccurate or otherwise incorrect mailing.

Operations Support

  • Organizes and prepares incoming mail for distribution to internal stakeholders, Agents, and financial institutions.
  • Processes cancelations and non-renewals within regulatory timeframe; creates corresponding postal record and/or certified mail.
  • Prepares outgoing mail pieces.
  • Manages Agent transfer process.
  • Processes requests for financial institutions.
  • Verifies proof of coverage for Department of Motor Vehicles.
  • Reviews policies to create customer number or match to existing policyholder account.
  • Supported basic inquiries via phone, mail, and e-mail.

Recruits, trains and guides assigned Agents in matters of sales, underwriting and re-underwriting, profitability, agency management and related matters. Serves as a company representative in maintaining favorable Policyholder relationships. Interacts with, supports, coaches and motivates Agents.

Position Summary

Exercises independent discretion or judgment in handling all types of property claims. Also assists or acts on behalf of the claims supervisor when required.

  • This is a remote, work from home position in Indiana
  • The selected candidate will ideally live in Hamilton County and/or surrounding areas.
  • The hiring manager will also consider candidates for Property Adjuster I.  Level of position offered will be based upon the depth and breadth of selected candidate's experience and qualifications.
  • A company car and equipment to work from home will be provided
  • Good time management and organization skills preferred
  • Ability to drive/travel regularly within the assigned territory

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Completes industry-related training programs and continues to attend training programs to remain informed on policy changes, interpretation or new legislation.

Position Summary

Represents ERIE  and its insureds in litigated matters in Pennsylvania. Handles a diverse caseload involving personal injury, property damage, and other insurance-related disputes. Manages all phases of litigation, including discovery, depositions, motion practice, hearings, mediations, arbitrations, and trials.

  • Candidates may be considered for the Trial Attorney I (F13) or Senior Trial Attorney (F17). Number of years and scope of experience will be used to determine the level.
  • This is a hybrid position with flexibility in working location.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Represents ERIE and its insureds in civil litigation from inception through trial and appeal. 
  • Assesses liability arguments and damages presented and offers timely insights and recommendations to support effective claims resolution. Collaborates with claims professionals, experts, and other stakeholders to ensure effective case management and consistent legal strategy. 
  • Conducts discovery; takes depositions; prepares witnesses for testimony; drafts and argues motions, pleadings, and other court filings; and attends court hearings, pretrial conferences, mediations, settlement conferences, arbitrations and trials.
  • Collaborates with senior attorneys on strategy, trial preparation, and case evaluation in complex or high-value matters.
  • Participates in training and development programs to enhance litigation and trial advocacy skills.

Position Summary

Assists with providing legal counsel and guidance on ordinary and special business activities and operations, and/or insurance claims and litigation, to ensure maximum protection of ERIE's legal rights and maintenance of operations and activities within the limits prescribed by law. Directs or interfaces with outside legal counsel in the defense of ERIE against lawsuits or claims, or the prosecution of ERIE's claims against others.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Assists with the organization and direction of the company's legal activities.

  • Provides legal research, advice and guidance on insurance claims.
  • Reviews proposed and existing legislation affecting the Erie Insurance Group and advises and consults with General Counsel, Deputy General Counsel and Senior Counsel on the position of the company with regard to such matters.
  • Counsels and advises corporate personnel on legal issues including, but not limited to, those related to real and personal property, taxes, advertising, trademarks, copyright and promotion programs, contracts, personnel matters, public relations, underwriting and claims interpretation.
  • Participates in trade associations and regulatory and legislative hearings and meetings as directed or requested.
  • Handles legal assignments as directed or requested.

Opportunity to Join Our Future Focus Internship Program as an ERIE Experience & Customer Service Intern 

Erie Insurance is committed to helping you learn and grow through a challenging internship experience that provides relevant, real-world business opportunities. 


As an ERIE Experience & Customer Service Intern, you will have the opportunity to contribute to meaningful business priorities within Experience or Customer Service while developing a broader understanding of how the two areas support ERIE and the experiences we deliver. 


Interns may have a primary alignment within Experience or Customer Service while participating in shared learning, networking, developmental and cross-functional opportunities across Experience & Customer Service. 


The specific scope of each internship is intentionally flexible. Projects, assignments and areas of focus will be determined by Program and Business Leads based on current business priorities, business need and developmental opportunities available at the time of the internship. 


Who Should Apply? 

  • Applications are accepted from college students currently enrolled at an accredited college or university to pursue a four-year degree or to complete a master's degree program full-time. 

  • A four-year degree student should be completing sophomore, junior or senior year based on applicable 2027 Future Focus eligibility requirements. 

  • A minimum cumulative grade point average of 3.0 is highly preferred. 


About the Internship 

The internship includes orientation to the company and insurance industry through: 

  • A variety of challenging assignments in a stimulating work environment. 

  • A personal mentor. 

  • A variety of educational, social and community service events with other interns. 

  • Social events and other networking activities with senior leaders. 

  • Opportunities for professional development and exposure to multiple areas of the organization. 

  • Additional Future Focus programs and initiatives offered by ERIE Insurance.

Gains practical business experience and a broader understanding of how Experience and Customer Service contribute individually and collaboratively to the experiences ERIE delivers. Performs special projects as required. 

Interns may be primarily aligned with either Experience or Customer Service based on business need and program planning. Specific assignments, projects and areas of focus will be determined by Program and Business Leads based on priorities and needs leading into the internship.

  • Participate in Future Focus Internship Program activities, networking opportunities and professional-development experiences. 
  • Perform additional assignments and special projects as determined by Program and Business Leads.

Position Summary

Exercises independent discretion or judgment in handling all types of property claims. Also assists or acts on behalf of the claims supervisor when required.

  • This is a remote, work from home position in Indiana
  • The selected candidate will ideally live in Marion County and/or surrounding areas
  • The hiring manager will also consider candidates for Property Adjuster I.  Level of position offered will be based upon the depth and breadth of selected candidate's experience and qualifications.

  • Good time management and organization skills preferred

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Conducts investigations, interviews, and inspects damage, driving to site of damage within assigned territory or other if required. Prepares estimates, makes recommendation, and handles coverage questions, and litigation.
  • Sets and maintains reserves, reviews reports and related materials, directs experts, determines coverage and claim value, issues or declines payment, and negotiates claims with plaintiff attorneys when necessary.
  • Documents claim files and submits report for closure.
  • Recognizes subrogation situations and initiates appropriate action.
  • Services assigned territory and brings assigned claims to conclusion.
  • Interacts with Agents and district sales managers on matters of mutual concern.
  • Assists claims supervisor or acts on his/her behalf, including representing the company at legal proceedings, as required.
  • Completes industry-related training programs and continues to attend training programs to remain informed on policy changes, interpretation or new legislation.
  • Assists in training of new claims adjusters.
  • Participates on Catastrophe Team when required.

Position Summary

With limited supervision, translates near-term and long-term business needs of moderate to high complexity into (technical) initiative solution options across multiple portfolios. Provides enterprise-level context to the architecture team to enable team members to focus, mature domains, and create future-state architectures.  Provides leadership visibility on complex initiatives by facilitating discussions, leading conceptual and high level design sessions, capturing the results in artifacts, and ensuring the architectural design is realized through delivery for multiple enterprise stakeholders.  


What You’ll Do

As a Senior Solutions Architect – Data, you’ll play a key role in shaping ERIE’s enterprise data strategy. You’ll design and implement scalable, modern data architectures that ensure accuracy, consistency, and accessibility across the organization. You’ll collaborate closely with data engineering, analytics, and business partners to align data initiatives with enterprise goals and deliver trusted, high-quality data solutions that power decision-making.

Your expertise will guide the design and integration of enterprise data systems—connecting traditional on-premises environments with modern, cloud-based ecosystems that support ERIE.


Preferred Experience & Skills

  • Hands-on experience designing and implementing enterprise data architectures that promote data quality and consistency.
  • Proficiency with Master Data Management (MDM) tools such as Informatica MDM, Reltio, SAP MDG, or IBM InfoSphere.
  • Strong understanding of data integration, governance, metadata management, and data stewardship principles.
  • Experience with data modeling, APIs, ETL design, and modern cloud data platforms (AWS, Azure, or similar).
  • Proven ability to collaborate across disciplines to define strategy and deliver scalable data solutions.
  • Familiarity with AWS services such as S3, Glue, or Redshift is a plus.


What Makes You Stand Out

You’re a strategic thinker with a builder’s mindset. You connect architecture vision with practical delivery—creating data systems that drive measurable business value. You balance innovation and structure, ensuring ERIE’s data assets are both trusted and transformative.

You stand out because you:

  • Combine deep MDM expertise with practical cloud architecture experience.
  • Have a track record of integrating on-premises and cloud data environments.
  • Foster strong partnerships between IT and business, translating data strategy into real outcomes.
  • Bring curiosity, adaptability, and a continuous improvement mindset to every challenge.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Serves as the single point of accountability for architecture function to portfolio owner customers and technology leadership.
  • Provides architectural guidance on initiatives of moderate to high complexity across multiple enterprise portfolios, while managing multiple customers with differing priorities on the organization’s most strategic initiatives.
  • Provides full-stack architectural options that enable business objectives while ensuring long-term technology goals for all aspects of a solution.
  • Collaborates with team members for technical validation during design and planning phases.
  • Informs aspects of portfolio maturity regarding technology and ability to achieve target technology alignment, while facilitating a minimum viable architecture.
  • Monitors large-scale project execution and considers and interprets architectural tradeoffs occurring during delivery. Escalates for appropriate context sharing and decision making, as necessary.
  • Proactively enables portfolio owners to see technical debt clearly, provides appropriate context to inform plans to achieve elimination of technical debt in a comprehensive plan across multiple portfolios, delivery teams, programs, or projects.
  • Serves as a mentor for other members of the team, builds an environment for analysts, engineers, architects, and other technology leaders to grow and have high impact.
  • Directs and drives closure on investment decisions within the enterprise while also identifying cross-portfolio impacts on significant delivery initiatives.
  • Serves as a subject matter expert for multiple portfolios, providing actionable recommendations via consultation services, adapted to stakeholder context, to technology leadership and organizational stakeholders.
  • Collaborates with architects, portfolio owners, and other job families to achieve an enterprise view; provides project and program level views to project and program teams in context of enterprise strategies and directions with light supervision.
  • Supports business agility through agile engagement across multiple delivery operations.
  • Interprets business needs, assesses solution choices, applies technology, and provides project guidance within a long-term enterprise lens.

Position Summary

Exercises independent discretion or judgment in handling property claims within designated level of authority. Also responsible for servicing assigned territory and may handle litigated claims.

  • This position operates from a home office but requires daily travel to conduct property inspections within the assigned territory. 
  • The selected candidate will ideally live within Eastern Allegheny County or surrounding areas (Monroeville, PA).
  • A company car and equipment to work from home will be provided.
  • Good time management and organization skills preferred.
  • Ability to drive/travel regularly within the assigned territory.
  • The hiring manager will also consider candidates for Property Adjuster II. Level of position offered will be based upon the depth and breadth of selected candidate's experience and qualifications.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Contacts Policyholders regarding property claims within level of authority. Conducts investigations, interviews insureds and witnesses, inspects damage and prepares estimates. Evaluates and makes recommendations regarding coverage of claims.
  • Handles property claims within designated authority. Sets and maintains adequate reserves. Obtains and reviews reports, statements, records and related materials as required. Evaluates information to determine coverage and total value of claim. Determines payments and issues checks or declines payment as required.
  • Documents claim files and submits final report to file for closure.
  • Identifies subrogation situations and initiates appropriate action.
  • Services assigned territory and brings assigned claims to conclusion.
  • Interacts with Agents and district sales managers on matters of mutual concern.
  • Handles property claims involving damages or coverage. May handle litigated claims, including negotiating with plaintiff attorney, or coordinates litigation with defense counsel as required.
  • Develops and applies a working knowledge of estimating practices and procedures relating to the adjustment of property claims.
  • Attends industry-related training programs and attends other training sessions to stay current on policy changes, interpretation or new legislation.
  • Successfully completes Technical Learning Center Training within one year of hire date.
  • Participates on Catastrophe Team when required.

Position Summary

Life Sales Manager

ERIE Family Life is seeking a Life Sales Manager to drive life insurance and annuity growth across Central and Eastern Pennsylvania. In this highly visible field leadership role, you'll partner with independent ERIE Agents to expand life insurance production, identify cross-sell opportunities, develop agency growth strategies, and provide consultative sales coaching that helps agencies strengthen customer relationships and grow their business.

Success in This Role

Within the first year, successful Life Sales Managers will:

  • Build trusted relationships with agency partners throughout the territory
  • Increase life insurance and annuity production
  • Identify and execute agency growth opportunities
  • Conduct joint sales calls and field coaching sessions
  • Help agents develop sustainable life insurance sales strategies
  • Partner with branch leadership to drive territory performance and business growth

Territory

This territory-based position supports agencies throughout Central and Eastern Pennsylvania, including Harrisburg, Lancaster, Reading, Allentown, Bethlehem, Easton, and surrounding communities.

Candidates should reside within or near the Harrisburg or Lehigh Valley markets and be willing to travel throughout the assigned territory.

A company vehicle is provided.

Additional Opportunity

The hiring manager will also consider candidates for the Senior Life Sales Manager (F13) level. The level offered will be based on the selected candidate's experience, qualifications, and demonstrated success in life insurance sales leadership, agency development, and territory management.

Trains and guides Agents in a designated branch territory as well as additional assigned branch offices in the promotion and sale of life insurance and annuity products, providing assistance in the areas of production, product knowledge and application, underwriting, and agency management. Also assists Agents in examining and evaluating their current books of business for potential prospects and serves as company representative in maintaining favorable agency and Policyholder relationships. Scope: Life Sales Manager role is assigned to one branch. Sr Life Sales Manager is assigned to multiple branches.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Assists branch managers and district sales managers in establishing short- and long-range objectives related to life insurance and annuity sales, with emphasis on production, underwriting and Agent training.
  • Provides training and direction to ERIE Agents regarding the promotion and sale of life insurance and annuity products. Interacts with Agents as necessary, educating them regarding approved marketing and sales tools and techniques.
  • Educates Agents regarding the products available through Erie Family Life, including policy features and benefits. Assists Agents in reviewing their current books of business in order to identify cross selling opportunities for life insurance and annuity sales. Collaborates with Agents to identify prospecting opportunities.
  • Accompanies Agents on sales calls and assists with servicing existing customers and writing new business.
  • Serves as a liaison between the Home Office and the field. Clarifies and resolves issues, implements new programs and communicates program changes as necessary.
  • Represents the company in community relations activities as directed.
  • Develops marketing and prospecting programs to assist Agents in the sale of life insurance and annuity products.
  • Collaborates with Home Office and Branch Office marketing personnel regarding the design and promotion of incentive campaigns related to the sales of life insurance and annuity products.
  • Assists in the selection and training of newly appointed Agents, life producers and customer service representatives.
  • Handles Agency relationships and business, as a licensed life insurance Agent, according to company policy.
  • Advises appropriate Home Office personnel of competitive intelligence issues related to Agents and agency management.

Position Summary

In collaboration with management and senior staff serves as subject matter expert on project teams or team lead for technical security systems and security elements throughout ERIE’s footprint. Advises project teams on security elements and technical security system designs. Assists with coordinating or conducting security assessments, inspections, and audits. Installs, programs, implements, operates, and manages ERIE’s technical security systems, including card access, physical security, network video systems, pedestrian control, proprietary databases, fire alarm, life safety systems for the Home Office and designated field offices. Provides specialized technical analysis of user input, testing, and specifications to inform modifications and new technology implementations. Coordinates with internal and external teams on design, implementation, operation, and maintenance of all related technical security systems.

  • The position is based out of our Corporate Office in Erie, PA.
  • The hiring team will consider candidates for a Security Design Engineer or Senior Security Design Engineer position. The level of position offered will be based on depth and breadth of selected candidate's qualifications and experience.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Evaluates user input, specified threats, operational goals, and industry best practices to determine design recommendations including specifications, hardware requirements and software.
  • Uses scans and measurements in conjunction with 2D and 3D modeling (REVIT, AutoCAD) to develop security systems and elements within the virtual world before recommending for use the real world. This includes prototyping of computer-based systems, software coding, and physical hardware. 
  • Develops and maintains strong proficiency and knowledge of industry standards and best practice modeling and diagramming techniques. Conducts related research and communicates relevant industry news and information to the Advanced Technical Systems team. Maintains and applies an in-depth knowledge of ERIE’s technical security systems. Provides direct support to the company and section on all technical security system related initiatives and problem resolutions.
  • Maintains knowledge of current and emerging technologies and industry best practices related to all technical security systems. Conducts related research and communicates relevant industry news and information to staff. Proposes and implements best practices and tools supporting these technologies and practices. Develops system integration skills and works closely with the Security Systems Integration Engineer.
  • Collaborates with other team members and contract resources to install, test, troubleshoot, or replace low voltage electrical equipment, all ERIE’s Technical Security Systems, including card access, physical security, intrusion, CCTV, digital video, recording, fire detection systems, and complex wireless applications.
  • Routinely represents the Advanced Technical Security Systems section on project teams. Assists with the design and/or configurations of integrated technical security systems. 
  • Participates in and assists senior staff with conducting on-going risk analysis and physical security audits at all ERIE facilities and corporate functional areas to identify points of vulnerability. Documents and evaluates all points of vulnerability and recommends risk avoidance and reduction strategies.

Duties and Responsibilities (cont'd if applicable)

  • Performs both mechanical and electronic service for all technical security system hardware components, including door electronics, detection devices, card readers, cameras, and video recorders in accordance with all manufactures specifications, internal quality controls and productivity standards.
  • Performs scheduled system wide inspections of all hardware, device components and software. Inspections will include adjusting, cleaning, and calibrating hardware devices to insure proper operation. Creates and maintains test records and formal inspection documentation. Performs complete testing and commissioning of all technical security systems, including intelligent fire detection life/safety systems. 
  • Responds to calls for service, including emergency and customary. Analyzes, troubleshoots, repairs, and restores equipment/systems to full operation and recommends revisions when necessary for effectiveness. Alerts senior staff to equipment/systems requiring further analysis or potential replacements. Monitors problem resolution progress and quality. Ensures completion of required quality tasks, reviews, documentation and compliance with problem management and best practices. Prepares detailed problem management reports and metrics for existing knowledge databases.

Qualifications

Minimum Educational and Experience Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in IT, MIS, Engineering, Security Management, Project Management, or closely related field, plus five years related experience, including two years in security systems design and three years in security principles; or
  • Associate degree in a technical field, plus seven years related experience, including two years in security systems design and three years in security principles; or
  • Industry certification (APP, PSP, CPP, CSC (IAPSC), NICET IV, PMP, CSPM, or equivalent), plus eight years related experience, including two years in security systems design and three years in security principles; or
  • High school diploma plus nine years related experience, including two years in security systems design and three years in security principles.
  • Additional industry certifications may count towards years of related experience.


Additional Experience

  • Advanced understanding of digital and analog signaling protocols, network communications, information systems and network architecture required.
  • Understanding of how to design building systems and physical elements to protect assets. (PSP, CPP, or CSC strongly preferred)
  • Security project subject matter expert experience.

At Erie Insurance, you’re not just part of a Fortune 500 company; you’re also a valued member of a diverse and inclusive team that includes more than 6,000 employees and over 13,000 independent agencies.  Our Employees work in the Home Office complex located in Erie, PA, and in our Field Offices that span 12 states and the District of Columbia. 

Benefits That Go Beyond The Basics

We strive to be Above all in Service® to our customers—and to our employees. That’s why Erie Insurance offers you an exceptional benefits package, including:

  • Premier health, prescription, dental, and vision benefits for you and your dependents. Coverage begins your first day of work.
  • Low contributions to medical and prescription premiums. We currently pay up to 97% of employees’ monthly premium costs.
  • Pension. We are among the 2% of Fortune 500 companies to offer a traditional pension plan.  Full-time employees are vested after five years of services.
  • 401(k) with up to 4% contribution match. The 401(k) is offered in addition to the pension.
  • Paid time off. Paid vacation, personal days, sick days, bereavement days and parental leave.
  • Career development. Including a tuition reimbursement program for higher education and industry designations.
     

Additional benefits that include company-paid basic life insurance; short-and long-term disability insurance; orthodontic coverage for children and adults; adoption assistance; fertility and infertility coverage; well-being programs; paid volunteer hours for service to your community; and dollar-for-dollar matching of your charitable gifts each year.

Position Summary

Supervises, trains, and monitors the activities of assigned claims adjusters and other claims personnel. Assists the Claims Leadership in the overseeing and handling of claims.

    • This position will report to Wisconsin branch office
    • This position will be supervising Field Property Adjusters in the Milwaukee area.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Manages overall operations of designated area of authority.   Interviews, hires, trains, and directs personnel.  Prepares and conducts performance assessments, coordinates discipline and oversees Employee development as required.
  • Reviews claims on a regular basis in accordance with company policy. reviews adjusters’ files for coverage and adequate reserves, acts as a resource for answering claims questions, provides additional services as required and takes action as necessary. Reviews claim correspondence and provides counsel on further action. 
  • Resolves coverage and other unusual questions within designated authority.  Conducts related research as necessary.
  • Maintains and applies working knowledge of adjusters’ files and statutory laws.
  • Makes recommendations to and participates with the Claims Manager in developing and evaluating claims procedures.  
  • Handles claim complaints and inquiries. 
  • Assists the Claim Manager and may act on manager’s behalf as necessary.
  • Receives and directs the processing of legal papers served upon ERIE involving claims action and directs activities of outside legal counsel as required.
  • Assists in preparation for trial procedures and attends pre-trial functions and trials as necessary. 
  • Reviews reports, payments and buyer information; and, in some instances, negotiates with salvage auctions and salvage yards on behalf of the company as required.
  • Contributes to projects, initiatives, teams, or other assignments to support business strategy, objectives, expectations, or operational outcomes.
  • This position requires the incumbent to serve on the Catastrophe Team, which may include travel on short notice to other locations for periods in excess of two consecutive weeks.

The first five duties listed are functions identified as essential to the job.  Essential functions are those job duties that must be performed in order for the job to be accomplished. 

Regular and predictable attendance is an essential job function. For certain positions at ERIE, including leadership roles, regular and predictable onsite presence may also be an essential job function based on business and operational needs.

This position description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the incumbent. Employees are required to follow any other job-related instruction and to perform any other duties as requested by their supervisor, or as become evident.

Capabilities

  • Collaborates (Leader)
  • Cultivates Innovation (Leader)
  • Customer Focus (Leader)
  • Decision Quality (Leader)
  • Develops Talent (Leader)
  • Drives vision and purpose (Leader)
  • Ensures Accountability (Leader)
  • Instills Trust (Leader)
  • Nimble Learning (Leader)
  • Persuades (Leader)
  • Plans and Aligns (Leader)
  • Values Diversity (Leader)
  • Self-development (Leader)
  • Optimizes Work Processes (Leader)

Qualifications

Minimum Education and Experience Requirements 

  • High school diploma or equivalent and six years of claims related experience required; or
  • Associate degree and four years of claims related experience required; or
  • Bachelor’s degree and two years of claims related experience required.

Additional Experience 

  • Experience using estimating software preferred.
  • Experience in a leadership role preferred.
     

Designations and/or Licenses 

  • Completion of Associate in Claims (AIC) designation preferred. 
  • Appropriate license(s) as required by applicable state(s), including the ability to secure and maintain dual or multiple licenses as business needs require.
  • Valid driver’s license required.

Aon is hiring for a Health Solutions Senior Consultant in Kansas City or St. Louis, MO! This is a hybrid position. Are you intellectually curious with a passion to solve problems? AON is looking for a Global Benefits Vice President in Chicago - (Hybrid Position) This great career opportunity offers diversified project and client exposure. The essential duties of the selected candidate will include, but not necessarily limited to: International benefits consulting: The candidate is expected to provide advice to senior global HR leaders on an array of global employee benefits topics including benefit strategy, audits, benchmarking, opening for business, M&A, multinational pooling, governance, risk management, global DC consulting, and other relevant work products and projects with very little direction. The candidate will be responsible for managing strategic as well as tactical interaction with assigned clients and coordinating the efforts of a multidisciplinary team of consultants in numerous locations around the world. The candidate will lead internal resources in the formulation and execution of appropriate solutions for clients and prospects. New business development – The candidate is expected to grow existing client revenue by identifying and converting new global benefits projects and cross selling opportunities with other Aon practices. The role entails building, maintaining and managing a steady pipeline of prospects and sales opportunities including regular interaction with a sales reporting application. Client relationship management – The candidate will leverage their solid business acumen to develop and maintain strong connections with senior client contacts while providing global benefits technical expertise. Internally, the candidate will serve as a project management lead including fee setting, invoice management, revenue projections, team optimization, and service escalations. Intellectual capital development and training – The candidate is expected to leverage their global benefits knowledge as a leader/member of special project taskforces or subject matter expertise teams. The ideal candidate will also be able to train and mentor junior team members to support their career development and improve their understanding of global benefits and consulting skills. Communication skills – The candidate is expected to have excellent written/verbal communication and presentation skills. The candidate must work well with an array of multi-disciplinary Aon team members, with an extended client team or work independently, based on project needs. Qualifications and Educational Requirements: Priority will be given to candidates with a minimum of 8 to 12 years of international or non‐US benefits experience in an HR consulting firm or professional services firm. International benefits consulting experience is strongly desired. Other requirements include: Strong management and strong analytical ability Strong organizational, problem solving and critical thinking skills Ability to handle multiple projects in as fast‐paced and time‐sensitive environment Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including strong presentation skills Functional knowledge of Excel and other MS Office products Bachelor’s degree (mathematics, finance, economics, or other degrees where quantitative skills are required is an advantage) Advanced degree or project management certification is an advantage For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position intended for U.S. applicants is $160.000K to $200.000 annually. Job.JobTitle: Business Development Director, Mergers & Acquisition and Transactional Solutions
Job.JobDescription:
Business Development Director, Mergers & Acquisitions and Transaction Solutions Aon is seeking an AMATS Business Development Director to lead market development activities across AMATS clients and prospects. This role will be responsible for expanding AMATS revenue opportunities through targeted engagement of existing Aon clients, private equity sponsors, portfolio companies, law firms, and other M&A ecosystem participants. The Business Development Director will serve as the primary AMATS growth leader for the market, working closely with AMATS producers, AEs, Enterprise Client Leaders, Market Leadership, business development, and marketing partners to identify opportunities, build relationships, and execute a coordinated go-to-market strategy. The role is expected to create new opportunities, strengthen key referral channels, and improve AMATS visibility across the private equity and M&A community. This is a hybrid opportunity with the ability to work out of the following Aon offices: New York City or Chicago, IL. We may consider other Aon offices on a case-by-case basis. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like The AMATS Business Development Director will spend significant time engaging clients, prospects, referral sources, and Aon stakeholders to accelerate growth across Transaction Solutions, Transaction Advisory Services, and Portfolio Solutions offerings. This individual will be expected to create and execute a market-level growth strategy that aligns AMATS capabilities with the private equity, corporate M&A, and legal advisor ecosystem. The role will act as both a relationship builder and strategic connector, helping AMATS gain greater access to opportunities while improving collaboration across Aon's client-facing teams. Key Responsibilities: Market Development & Go-to-Market Leadership Develop and execute a comprehensive AMATS growth strategy. Partner with Aon Leadership, AMATS leadership, business development, and marketing teams to identify priority growth segments and target accounts. Build annual and quarterly market plans focused on revenue generation, pipeline development, relationship expansion, and strategic growth initiatives. Identify market trends, industry changes, competitive developments, and M&A activity that may create new business opportunities. Existing Aon Client Engagement Partner with Enterprise Client Leaders, Account Executives, and Producers to identify existing Aon clients with potential need for Transaction Solutions, Transaction Advisory Services, or Portfolio Solutions capabilities. Build relationship maps and engagement plans across priority accounts. Identify whitespace opportunities within strategic Aon clients and coordinate pursuit strategies. Facilitate introductions between AMATS specialists and client stakeholders. Increase awareness and adoption of AMATS capabilities across existing Aon client relationships. Private Equity Sponsor Development Identify, prioritize, and engage private equity firms that align with Aon's target client profile. Develop relationships with deal professionals, operating partners, portfolio leaders, and firm leadership. Create strategic coverage plans for priority private equity firms and their portfolio companies. Coordinate AMATS engagement strategies with regional sales teams and industry leaders. Drive awareness of Aon's differentiated capabilities across the deal lifecycle. Law Firm and M&A Advisor Channel Development Partner with AMATS colleagues who are focused on building relationships with law firms and other advisors. Develop referral and relationship-building strategies focused on attorneys, transaction advisors, investment bankers, and other deal participants. Increase AMATS visibility through networking, thought leadership, educational programs, and market events. Partner with marketing and AMATS leadership to develop advisor-specific value propositions and engagement programs. Create and maintain a structured advisor coverage strategy and referral tracking process. Relationship Management & Client Leadership Build and maintain executive-level relationships across key market stakeholders and buying centers. Act as a trusted advisor by understanding business objectives, transaction activity, growth strategies, and emerging risks. Coordinate internal resources to deliver a unified Aon experience. Leverage Aon's full suite of capabilities to create value for clients and prospects while identifying appropriate opportunities for AMATS engagement. Marketing & Commercial Collaboration Partner closely with business development, marketing, and sales enablement teams to execute campaigns aligned with priority growth segments. Support development of market events, roundtables, webinars, sponsorship opportunities, and thought leadership initiatives. Help shape messaging, target lists, promotional strategies, and follow-up plans. Ensure marketing activities support measurable pipeline creation and relationship development goals. Pipeline Development & Opportunity Management Generate, qualify, and advance new opportunities through proactive market engagement. Maintain visibility into target accounts, key relationships, prospecting activities, and sales pipeline. Utilize CRM, relationship mapping, and market intelligence platforms to support business development activities. Coordinate pursuit efforts with AMATS producers and solution leaders. Track key business development metrics, pipeline progression, and market performance indicators. How this opportunity is different The AMATS Business Development Director will spend significant time engaging clients, prospects, referral sources, and Aon stakeholders to accelerate growth across Transaction Solutions, Transaction Advisory Services, and Portfolio Solutions offerings. This individual will be expected to create and execute a market-level growth strategy that aligns AMATS capabilities with the private equity, corporate M&A, and legal advisor ecosystem. The role will act as both a relationship builder and strategic connector, helping AMATS gain greater access to opportunities while improving collaboration across Aon's client-facing teams. Skills and experience that will lead to success 10+ years of business development, sales, client leadership, consulting, insurance brokerage, transaction advisory, investment banking, legal advisory, or private equity-related experience. Demonstrated success building executive relationships and generating new business opportunities. Strong understanding of the M&A ecosystem, including private equity sponsors, portfolio companies, law firms, investment banks, and transaction advisors. Experience developing and executing market-level growth strategies. Strong understanding of consultative selling and strategic relationship management. Proven ability to work effectively within a complex, matrixed organization. Experience partnering with senior leaders and influencing without direct authority. Leadership Characteristics Commercially driven and growth oriented. Strategic thinker capable of translating market opportunities into actionable plans. Exceptional relationship builder with strong executive presence. Collaborative and highly effective in cross-functional environments. Strong communication, presentation, and networking skills. Self-starter with the ability to independently identify and pursue opportunities. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of industry experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $225,000 to 250,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-CC1 2590365

Join Aon’s Digital Finance transformation as a Senior Manager, Finance Systems, where you’ll play a key role in shaping the future of finance. In this highly visible position, you’ll work at the intersection of finance, data, and technology — leading the modernization of financial systems and leveraging platforms like Databricks, Workday, TM1 and Power BI to deliver scalable solutions, real-time insights, and advanced analytics. This is a unique opportunity to drive innovation, enable AI-powered decision-making, and partner across the business to transform planning, forecasting, and reporting at scale. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Lead digital transformation efforts across financial systems, driving automation and scalable architecture. Partner with Finance, IT, and Business stakeholders to define requirements, deliver solutions, and ensure alignment with enterprise goals. Architect and maintain complex, multi-dimensional financial data models that support dynamic planning, forecasting, and scenario analysis Leverage Databricks, Snowflake and other AI platforms to manage large-scale financial data and enable predictive analytics and machine learning. Develop and maintain interactive dashboards using Power BI or similar tools to deliver real-time insights. Conduct systems analysis to identify inefficiencies and implement process improvements. Manage reconciliation processes between Workday, IBM Planning Analytics (TM1), and other financial subsystems, ensuring data accuracy and consistency. Maintain documentation and enforce data governance and internal control standards. How this opportunity is different Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Information Systems, or related field; Master’s or CPA preferred. Expertise in financial systems, including Workday and IBM Planning Analytics (TM1). Strong proficiency in data modeling and dashboarding tools (e.g., SQL, Python, Power BI, Anaplan, Tableau). We are looking for an experienced Tax and Treasury Technology Leader to develop and implement the worldwide technology strategy and roadmap for tax and treasury systems, data, integrations, and digital capabilities. The person in this position brings expertise across direct and indirect tax, tax provision and compliance! Also transfer pricing, cash and liquidity management, payments, banking connectivity, debt and investments, foreign exchange, data and analytics, Agentic AI, and workflow automation. Translate priorities into secure, resilient, well-governed, and data-driven technology solutions. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world! As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Serve as the senior technology leader responsible for both tax functions and treasury management, owning the strategy, architecture, roadmap, delivery, and operational health of the global technology ecosystem. Be responsible for the portfolio of technologies, including tax provision and reporting: Global tax provision, effective tax rate, deferred tax, tax accounting, disclosure, and close-support solutions. Direct tax compliance: Corporate income tax, withholding tax, statutory reporting, return preparation, filing, and jurisdictional compliance platforms. Indirect tax: VAT, GST, sales and use tax, determination, calculation, invoicing, reporting, reconciliation, and e-filing technologies. Transfer pricing: Intercompany policy, calculation, documentation, operational transfer pricing, and country-by-country reporting solutions. Oversee treasury management: Cash positioning, liquidity forecasting, bank account administration, payments, collections, in-house banking, netting, and reconciliation platforms. Financial risk and capital markets: Foreign exchange, interest rate and commodity risk, hedging, debt, investments, guarantees, and associated accounting and valuation capabilities. The person in this role will be responsible for banking connectivity and payments: Bank portals, host-to-host connections, APIs, SWIFT connectivity, payment factories, file transmission, fraud controls, and payment status monitoring. Information analysis, computational insights, and artificial intelligence: Financial and liquidity data products, governed data models, dashboards, predictive insights, scenario modeling, intelligent automation, and Agentic AI capabilities Ensure end-to-end process integrity and data consistency across tax determination, provision, compliance, statutory reporting, payments, cash positioning, liquidity forecasting, bank reconciliation, hedging, debt, and investment processes. Partner closely with senior Tax, Treasury, Finance, Accounting, Risk, Compliance, Internal Audit, Data, Cybersecurity, and Technology leaders to align platform capabilities with business priorities and regulatory obligations. Define and maintain the platform governance model for the technology solutions supporting Tax and Treasury functions, including demand intake, prioritization, architecture, security, change control, release management, access governance, and communication. Take charge of the IT service model across application support, incident and problem management, monitoring, batch and interface operations, disaster recovery, business continuity, vendor support, and service-level performance. Oversee evaluation, adoption, and rollout of new platform features and releases; perform impact assessments and guide configuration, integration, controls, testing, deployment, and hypercare. Drive adoption and support for new capabilities, ensuring teams are equipped to use systems, data, analytics, and AI effectively in day-to-day operations. Champion data quality, lineage, standardization, retention, security, and controls across the landscape; establish clear ownership and collaborate with Data, Risk, Legal, Privacy, and Compliance teams. Complete the AI strategy related to Tax and Treasury, prioritizing responsible use cases such as anomaly detection, reconciliation support, cash forecasting, scenario analysis, document intelligence, research assistance, workflow orchestration, and control monitoring. Ensure effective integrations and data flows between Tax and Treasury platforms and adjacent ecosystems, including ERP, HR and payroll, procurement, billing, banking networks, market data, consolidation, regulatory reporting, and enterprise data platforms. This role goes well beyond maintaining current tools. You will: Implement the strategic vision for an integrated Tax/Treasury technology ecosystem, connecting operational processes, enterprise platforms, banking partners, authoritative data, analytics, automation, and AI. Play a significant role in enterprise-wide transformation programs, including: Global modernization and standardization of Tax/Treasury platforms, processes, controls, integrations, and data AI-enabled automation and advanced analytics for cash forecasting, tax data preparation, reconciliations, exception management, regulatory change analysis, and aiding decision-making Real-time and API-enabled banking, payment, and data connectivity, with resilient security and control frameworks Blend executive level influence with hands-on leadership, from driving multi-year roadmaps and major transformations to engaging in architecture reviews, operational risk decisions, and proofs of concept. Shape the day-to-day experience of teams by reducing manual effort, improving clarity, strengthening controls, and enabling faster, data-driven decisions. Your work will directly support tax compliance, liquidity, financial risk management, payment integrity, operational resilience, and better enterprise decisions through technology, data, AI, and process excellence. Skills and experience that will lead to success Extensive experience, typically 7+ years, leading Tax, Treasury, Finance, or corporate technology portfolios in a global, matrixed organization. Deep hands-on and strategic experience with: Tax provision, tax accounting, direct tax compliance, indirect tax, transfer pricing, and statutory reporting technologies Treasury management systems supporting cash, liquidity, payments, bank account management, debt, investments, foreign exchange, hedging, and reconciliation Bank connectivity and payment technologies, including SWIFT, host-to-host, APIs, payment files, bank portals, and fraud-control capabilities ERP, consolidation, sub ledger, payroll, procurement, billing, market data, data platform, and regulatory integrations that support Tax and Treasury processes Data architecture, master and reference data, data lineage, reporting, analytics, and data product operating models AI, machine learning, workflow automation, document intelligence, and agentic solutions, with responsible AI and governance controls Proven success leading complex, multi-year transformations, global deployments, process standardization, platform rationalization, and operating model change across Tax and Treasury. Experience establishing reliable application support and service management for time critical close, filing, payment, cash, and market-facing processes. Experience driving adoption of AI, automation, and analytics in Tax and Treasury while maintaining appropriate human review, security, auditability, and regulatory compliance. Solid background partnering with senior business collaborators to translate Tax/Treasury strategies, risks, controls, and performance measures into technology roadmaps and investment priorities. Leadership & collaboration: Demonstrated ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing, global teams across business, technology, data, architecture, delivery, and operations skills. Excellent collaborator management and interpersonal abilities, with the ability to work with senior leaders in Tax, Treasury, Finance, Accounting, Risk, Compliance, Audit, Data, and Technology. Experience managing portfolio prioritization, budgeting, capacity, resource planning, and delivery across concurrent programs, enhancements, regulatory commitments, and operational needs. Strong vendor and partner management skills, including contracts, performance, service levels, product roadmaps, security requirements, implementation accountability, and risk allocation. Strategic problem solver who can connect Tax and Treasury technology, data, controls, and AI capabilities to outcomes such as compliance, liquidity visibility, risk reduction, payment integrity, operational resilience, and improved efficiency. Demonstrated experience identifying and implementing automation, AI/ML, advanced analytics, and agentic workflows in controlled financial processes. Ability to define a governed data strategy that improves data quality, accessibility, lineage, reuse, and decision support across jurisdictions and business divisions. Comfortable operating in a matrixed, global environment, balancing enterprise standardization with local tax, banking, legal, regulatory, and market requirements. Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Finance, Accounting, Tax, Treasury, Business, or a related field. An advanced degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Tax, Information Systems, Data, or a related field, or equivalent experience, is preferred. Technology, data, cloud, cybersecurity, project management, or AI-related certifications are advantageous, particularly where they demonstrate skill in leading secure and well governed enterprise platforms. Job.JobTitle: Assistant Vice President, Financial Services Group - Private/Nonprofit
Job.JobDescription:
AVP/Broker II, Financial Services Group – Private/Nonprofit Currently we have an exciting career opportunity for a Broker II within Aon Commercial Risk Solutions’ Financial Services Group (“FSG”). Are you ready to begin a new challenge and work with the best Insurance Professionals in the business? Then this just maybe the new opportunity you are looking for! This Broker role is responsible for developing and implementing strategic risk management solutions for large, global clients. This includes the design, marketing and service management of insurance programs in numerous industry sectors. This individual should have proven peer market relationships and emerging senior market relationships. This opportunity is a hybrid role to work from our Chicago, IL; New York, NY; Los Angeles, CA; or San Francisco office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Responsible for assessing client needs, designing solutions and negotiating with insurance carriers to obtain coverage that is in a client’s best interests. Professional who develops and manages client relationships, account strategies and insurance marketing activities for book of business. Acts as the primary negotiator in obtaining the most effective insurance programs to address client needs. Works closely with Team Leaders, Producers, Account Executives and other client facing team members to understand and deliver on client’s needs. Identifies and analyzes client exposures with routine assistance of junior team members to develop effective client risk treatment and placement strategies. Obtains the most appropriate program coverage based upon client objectives by developing and executing, in conjunction with the client, an agreed upon structure and strategy. Serves as a source of information concerning market trends, pricing practices and other underwriting policies. May participate in development of department policies and procedures and implements them in assigned areas. Provides guidance to more junior staff Directs the overall development and growth of personal book of business and assists in the development of the team members. Capable of working on complex accounts with autonomy. AVP’s and New VP’s play a supporting role in larger, more complex accounts. Support team in the solicitation and servicing of clients and the broking of their insurance programs. Directing, placing and servicing mid-size accounts with minimal supervision for own portfolio of clients. Expert comparison and analysis of insurance policies and determination of needed enhancements. How this opportunity is different The broker will be instrumental in the analysis of clients’ exposures to identify and mitigate risk as well as responsible for the coordination of the placement and day-to-day activities on accounts. Skills and experience that will lead to success Attention to detail, ability to multi-task, exceptional organizational skills, ability to make and communicate difficult decisions. Minimum of 5+ years of financial lines insurance brokerage and/or underwriting experience with a concentration on Directors & Officers Liability, Employment Practices, Fiduciary, Crime and Special Risk. Effective working knowledge of carrier underwriting practices & processes. Proven leadership skills in working with teams and ability to work with clients and to successfully exceed client expectations. Proven client-facing skills including effective presentations & communications. Proven organization and ability to work with others. Experience in resource deployment and utilization management. Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact effectively at various levels. Successfully operates in a fast-paced driven environment that requires the ability to handle multiple tasks simultaneously. Sales experience preferred and finance background a plus. Must maintain appropriate broker’s license. Proficient in Microsoft Office suite of products. Education: Bachelor’s degree required or equivalent years of industry experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $105,420 - $168,630 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. The salary range reflected is based on a primary work location of California. The actual salary may vary for applicants in a different geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-KA1 #LI-HYBRID 2588737

This position will support Aon’s K&K Insurance group Mass Merchandising business group within Aon Affinity. Aon is in the business of better decisions: At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like: Lead, mentor, and develop a team of underwriters, including performance reviews, coaching, and training on various platforms. Conduct interviewing/hiring potential candidates. Oversee the underwriting of complex or high‑value accounts, ensuring consistent application of underwriting guidelines and risk‑selection criteria. Develop and implement underwriting strategies, policies, and procedures in alignment with Aon Service Corporation’s overall business objectives. Monitor portfolio performance, identify trends, and recommend corrective actions to maintain profitability and support growth. Collaborate with sales, claims, and product development teams to identify market opportunities, resolve client issues, and enhance product offerings. Review and approve underwriting decisions that exceed team members’ authority limits. Ensure compliance with all relevant regulatory requirements and internal audit standards. Participate in client meetings and presentations as a subject matter expert, as needed. Contribute to the development and implementation of underwriting tools and technology enhancements to drive efficiency and improve decision quality. Skills and experience that will lead to success: Strong verbal, written, analytical and leadership skills. P&C license preferred/must be obtained within 6 months of hire. Ability to handle multi-tasking effectively Strong time management skills. Proficiency with the Microsoft Office suite products including Excel and Word. Insurance industry experience. Customer Service experience including verbal/telephone skills. Strong organizational and interpersonal skills with attention to detail. Education: High School Diploma or Equivalent. College Degree preferred. How we support our colleagues: In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce.
