Job.JobDescription:
Early Careers Launch - Broking Commercial Risk - NPG Trucking Launch Your Career in Broking Aon is looking for soon-to-be graduates and recent graduates to join our Early Careers Launch Development Program as Brokers, with opportunities across Commercial Risk and Reinsurance. You do not need to be an insurance expert on day one. Through our Launch Program and on-the-job learning, you will learn how brokers help clients understand risk, navigate insurance and reinsurance markets, and make better decisions, that support resilience and growth. Location: Little Rock, Arkansas As a Broker, you will build the skills, confidence and market knowledge needed to translate complex risk exposures into structured insurance programs and serve as a credible intermediary between clients and insurers. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What is Commercial Risk Commercial Risk Aon’s Commercial Risk team helps organizations around the world identify, understand, and manage the risks that could impact their people, assets, and performance. We partner with clients across industries to design and deliver innovative risk and insurance solutions - from property and casualty to cyber and specialty risks - using data, analytics, and deep market insight to help them make better decisions and protect their business. What You Will Do As a Broker, you will build hands-on broking experience while developing an understanding of how risk, markets, clients and strategy come together to create value for clients. Technology, including AI, Aon’s risk analyzers and global delivery teams increasingly support routine execution, allowing Brokers to focus earlier on commercial judgment, market strategy and client value. Analyze Risk and Build Market Insight Assess risk exposures using data, analytics and market intelligence while learning to validate results across coverage lines. Conduct market analysis to benchmark pricing, identify coverage gaps and support effective program recommendations. Support Market Strategy and Placements Help prepare market submissions, renewal materials, placement documentation and client deliverables. Engage insurers and underwriters to secure competitive pricing and terms, applying market knowledge where AI-suggested terms need tailoring. Build experience coordinating renewals, reviewing contracts and maintaining accurate documentation for smaller placements and account activity. Build Client Relationships and Advisory Skills Participate in client meetings, presentations and follow-up materials with growing confidence. Leverage technology, data analytics, and market insights to translate complex risk information into clear, actionable recommendations that help clients make informed business decisions. Build trust as a credible point of contact while developing client and market relationships. Coordinate Projects and Improve How Work Gets Done Support placement workflows across broking, account management, analytics, operations, specialist teams and global delivery partners. Review documents and client materials for accuracy, consistency and quality before they are used with markets or clients. Identify opportunities to improve broking processes and support efficient client delivery. Qualifications  College Seniors graduating between Spring 2026 to Spring 2027 with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 Please Note: For this role you must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future. The Launch Development Program Launch is a structured 10-month Early Career development program that combines meaningful work, business learning, professional development and relationship-building across Aon. The program helps you build a strong foundation for a long-term broking and advisory career through: On-the-job learning with brokers, client teams, account managers and solution line specialists. Business and professional development in Commercial Risk, Reinsurance, client service, communication, collaboration, problem solving and commercial awareness. Exposure to data, analytics and technology that support risk assessment, market analysis, workflow coordination and client-ready recommendations. Networking, mentorship and coaching opportunities to build relationships across Aon and develop your career path. What Will Help You Succeed and Grow We are looking for candidates who are curious, motivated and excited to learn. Through the Launch Program, you will continue developing the same skills and capabilities that support a successful broking and advisory career, including: An interest in business, risk, insurance, reinsurance, analytics, finance, economics, client service or global markets. A desire to pursue a career in Commercial Risk and/or Reinsurance - Broking. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and professionally with a range of stakeholders. Analytical and critical thinking, problem-solving ability and attention to detail. A collaborative mindset, alongside initiative, adaptability and a willingness to contribute as part of a team. Excellent organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines. Confidence using technology and a willingness to learn new tools, internal AI platforms and technology-enabled ways of working. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint and Word. Interpersonal skills and the ability to build positive working relationships with colleagues, clients and external partners. Initiative and a commitment to continuous learning, growth and professional development. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $57,000 to $63,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. #LI-MM3 #LI-KM1 #LI-SC3 #LI-KC3 #LI-CS6 #LI-HYBRID #RiskUS #LI-HYBRID #AonLaunchUS #CommercialRiskReinsuranceUS 2589414

Captive Client Leader | Aon Captive & Insurance Management (ACIM) Are you a client leader who turns strong relationships into long‑term strategic value? Do you thrive in complex client environments where success depends on judgment, influence, and cross‑functional collaboration? Join us to help clients make better captive and risk financing decisions! This is a virtual role with the flexibility to work virtually across the U.S. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like This role exists to strengthen client outcomes through consultative captive leadership. As a Captive Client Services Director, you will act as the principal interface between captive clients and Aon, ensuring clients receive high‑quality service, strategic insight, and access to the right expertise across the business. You will help clients make better decisions about captive performance, risk financing strategy, and long‑term value creation. Typical activities include: Leading strategic client engagement for a portfolio of captive clients, acting as the primary relationship lead for senior executives Running annual account planning discussions aligned to client priorities, service requirements, and commercial objectives Coordinating strategy check‑ins with subject matter experts to provide external perspectives, market insight, and forward‑looking recommendations Reviewing stewardship reports, performance data, and service metrics to find opportunities for improvement and additional value creation Orchestrating internal teams across domiciles, Global Capability Centres, and wider Aon businesses to deliver integrated client outcomes Finding opportunities to strengthen client relationships, improve account profitability, and expand relevant Aon services Translating technical, financial, and performance information into clear client narratives and actionable recommendations Coaching and supporting more junior colleagues to strengthen client leadership capability and consistency of service delivery Maintaining delivery discipline across service schedules, governance commitments, and regulatory requirements How this opportunity is different This role is differentiated by the level of client influence, strategic ownership, and cross‑functional coordination involved. You will operate as the central connector between captive clients and Aon, bringing together expertise from across the organization to support better client decisions and stronger long‑term partnerships. The role is shifting from transactional service delivery toward consultative client leadership. Success depends on your ability to deeply understand client priorities, proactively find opportunities, and build value through strategic conversations, insight‑led communication, and effective orchestration of Aon capabilities. You will help shape the future‑state client leadership model within ACIM, supporting a more proactive, data-driven, and commercially focused approach to client engagement. Skills and experience that will lead to success Demonstrated advisory client engagement, building deep understanding of client priorities, challenges, and risk financing objectives and operating as a trusted advisor Strong strategic and commercial thinking, connecting client strategies, commercial opportunities, and Aon capabilities to create measurable value and support profitable growth Confirmed ability to orchestrate expertise across a matrixed organization, influencing without formal authority and aligning teams around shared client objectives Track record of owning client service delivery, managing service schedules and stewardship activity, and maintaining high standards of execution and governance Excellent communication skills, with the ability to turn technical information, market insight, and performance data into compelling narratives for senior collaborators Comfort operating in ambiguous or evolving situations, with sound judgment, learning agility, and the ability to draw on specialist expertise when needed Experience leading, coaching, or mentoring colleagues to build capability and consistent client leadership standards across teams Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in business, finance, risk management, or a related field. How we support our colleagues In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions for our colleagues as well. Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share, and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued. Aon values an innovative and inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Aon provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran, marital, domestic partner status, or other legally protected status. People with criminal histories are encouraged to apply. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering an inclusive workplace. If you require accommodations during the application or interview process, please let us know. You can request accommodations by emailing us at ReasonableAccommodations@Aon.com or your recruiter. We will work with you to meet your needs and ensure a fair and equitable experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is [$X to $X] annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. Typical activities include: Leading strategic client engagement for a portfolio of captive clients, acting as the primary relationship lead for senior executives Running annual account planning discussions aligned to client priorities, service requirements, and commercial objectives Coordinating strategy check‑ins with subject matter experts to provide external perspectives, market insight, and forward‑looking recommendations Reviewing stewardship reports, performance data, and service metrics to find opportunities for improvement and additional value creation Orchestrating internal teams across domiciles, Global Capability Centres, and wider Aon businesses to deliver integrated client outcomes Finding opportunities to strengthen client relationships, improve account profitability, and expand relevant Aon services Translating technical, financial, and performance information into clear client narratives and actionable recommendations Coaching and supporting more junior colleagues to strengthen client leadership capability and consistency of service delivery Maintaining delivery discipline across service schedules, governance commitments, and regulatory requirements How this opportunity is different This role is differentiated by the level of client influence, strategic ownership, and cross‑functional coordination involved. You will operate as the central connector between captive clients and Aon, bringing together expertise from across the organization to support better client decisions and stronger long‑term partnerships. The role is shifting from transactional service delivery toward consultative client leadership. Success depends on your ability to deeply understand client priorities, proactively find opportunities, and build value through strategic conversations, insight‑led communication, and effective orchestration of Aon capabilities. You will help shape the future‑state client leadership model within ACIM, supporting a more proactive, data-driven, and commercially focused approach to client engagement. Skills and experience that will lead to success Demonstrated advisory client engagement, building deep understanding of client priorities, challenges, and risk financing objectives and operating as a trusted advisor Strong strategic and commercial thinking, connecting client strategies, commercial opportunities, and Aon capabilities to create measurable value and support profitable growth Confirmed ability to orchestrate expertise across a matrixed organization, influencing without formal authority and aligning teams around shared client objectives Track record of owning client service delivery, managing service schedules and stewardship activity, and maintaining high standards of execution and governance Excellent communication skills, with the ability to turn technical information, market insight, and performance data into compelling narratives for senior collaborators Comfort operating in ambiguous or evolving situations, with sound judgment, learning agility, and the ability to draw on specialist expertise when needed Experience leading, coaching, or mentoring colleagues to build capability and consistent client leadership standards across teams Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in business, finance, risk management, or a related field. How we support our colleagues In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions for our colleagues as well. Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share, and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued. Aon values an innovative and inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. This position is responsible for handling submissions involving complex exposures and medium to high coverage limits. In addition, this position is responsible for the sales/marketing and premium production objectives in an assigned region/territory and programs. The role may also require an ability to effectively conduct loss control surveys and make recommendations within the parameters of the insurability guidelines for the carrier. Some travel may be required. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like: Review and evaluate insurance applications and related documents, including inspection reports, financial statements, loss data, MVR 's, and other information needed to properly evaluate and classify the degree of risk in relation to proposed coverage limits. Obtain all relevant information not included with the initial submission to ensure a thorough evaluation of the risk. Review and evaluate new/renewal business and recommend appropriate actions to attain premium/rate and loss ratio Prepare own or review other quotations/proposals for presentation to clients. Approve coverages requested within specified underwriting authority, either as submitted or on a modified basis, or decline the risk in its entirety; refer with recommended action if risk exceeds underwriting Review policy forms used in specific programs to ensure consistency and keep clients and brokers informed of coverage Complete underwriting assignments at the direction of the Underwriting Manager or Underwriting Director. Travel to fulfill field underwriting responsibilities that may be a part of assigned accounts including client visits, sales presentations, industry conventions and loss control Conduct and complete or order all loss control surveys/reports in the required timelines for each assigned program. Sell and market all coverage lines and products available to direct clients and brokers when Requirements: P&C/ A&H Licenses or ability to secure licenses within 6 months of hire. Bachelor 's degree or commensurate education and/or work experience 3-5 years underwriting experience or experience within the motorsports industry. Direct sales/marketing Advanced verbal and written communication For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $60,000 to $70,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Job.JobTitle: Bilingual Strategic Account Manager, Commercial Risk - Taiwan/Greater China Global Solutions (U.S. Based)
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Commercial Lines Account Manager, Customer Service / Account Support, Insurance Customer Service Representative
Job.JobDescription:
As a part of Taiwan/Greater China Global Solutions in U.S., you will manage and coordinate accounts and prospects, building and maintaining strong relationships with key client stakeholders and internal account service teams. The ideal candidate must have insurance industry experience. Aon is in the business of better decisions Aon is in the business of better decisions. At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the Day Will Look Like The role involves production and strategic account coordination of key U.S. Taiwan/Greater China clients & prospects, frequently interacting with client leadership externally and Aon's Account Service Teams. Proactively identify and develop new business opportunities, expanding the book of business and strengthening overall client relationships. Act as the lead Account Executive within Aon U.S. for Taiwan clients’ U.S. risks, serving as the primary point of contact for Taiwan-headquartered clients on their U.S. exposures. Serve U.S. local client entities directly, answering questions and resolving issues during U.S. business hours to ensure timely responses and issue resolution Collaborate with practice & geographical offices to advance opportunities, support account plans, and contribute to pipeline development and revenue growth initiatives. Facilitate client-facing discussions and internal alignment to ensure opportunities are effectively positioned and progressed. Act as a bilingual bridge between clients and Aon teams, working closely with Commercial Risk and other solution groups to coordinate tailored solutions and address client needs. Work closely with Aon Taiwan and client headquarters in Taiwan on strategy, program design, placement approach, and key account decisions to ensure alignment with the overall client relationship and client expectations from Taiwan. Coordinate with Aon U.S. local offices and specialty practices on placement execution, renewals, servicing, and complex risk solutions. Support Mexico-related client needs and coordinate with relevant Aon teams, recognizing the growing expansion of Taiwan clients into Mexico as part of their North American operations strategy. How this opportunity is different This role is specifically designed to support Taiwan/Greater China multinational clients and requires a unique combination of bilingual communication skills and cultural fluency. You will play a key role in identifying opportunities, building relationships, and advancing business initiatives in close partnership with internal stakeholders. Success in this role comes from the ability to bridge cultural and organizational gaps, communicate effectively across languages, and translate client needs into actionable strategies. By aligning internal resources and coordinating across stakeholders, you will help strengthen client relationships, advance business opportunities, and deliver consistent, high-quality solutions. The ideal candidate must have insurance industry experience. In particular, success will depend on deeply understanding Taiwan clients’ business models, culture, and expectations, and ensuring that U.S. servicing is tightly aligned with strategies and decisions driven from Taiwan HQ. Skills and Experience That Will Lead to Success Bilingual in business-level Mandarin Chinese and English, both spoken and written. The ideal candidate must have insurance industry experience. 10+ years of sales, consulting, account management, marketing, or client advisory experience (preferably in commercial risk or insurance). Taiwanese background preferred. Ability to communicate in Taiwanese dialect would be an advantage. Client-facing experience at a brokerage, insurance company, financial institution, or professional services firm serving Taiwan/Greater China clients. Complex project management experience. Strong stakeholder management skills, influence cross-functional teams across multiple locations and time zones. Deep understanding of Taiwan business culture, decision-making processes, and the expectations of Taiwan-headquartered multinational clients. Experience managing strategic or multinational accounts and navigating complex organizational structures. Willingness to acquire a Property & Casualty license within 90 days of employment (Aon pays for training materials and exam). Education: Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $140,000 - $175,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-RB1 #LI-Hybrid 2584897

Aon is looking for a Claims Manager As part of an industry-leading team, you will help empower results for our clients by delivering innovative and effective solutions. Aon Affinity's Travel Practice is a leader in the provision of customized travel insurance and protection programs for many of the world's most renowned travel companies. Our services include program consultation, brokerage and administration as well as data-based marketing, analytics and merchandising expertise. This is a full-time, on-site Monday - Friday position located in our Plainview, NY office. Job Responsibilities: Lead and develop a team of Claims Support Specialists and Claims Adjusters. Ensure compliance with client SLAs and performance standards. Manage high-profile client accounts, including Carefree Assistance. Monitor claim inventory, turnaround times, and operational metrics. Oversee shared mailboxes and client communications. Coordinate collection of missing claim documentation. Manage claim escalations and service issues. Partner with Finance on payment audits and financial controls. Maintain accurate claim payment records and documentation. Oversee salvage recovery activities. Monitor and report on SLA performance and account metrics. Manage claims approval workflows and authority requests. Ensure compliance with record retention requirements. Oversee file room administration and office operations. Manage office supply inventory and operational resources. Identify and implement process improvement opportunities. Ensure compliance with company, client, and regulatory requirements. Support business continuity and operational excellence. Required Experience: Possess State insurance adjuster’s license. Excellent communication and customer service skills. 5+ years of experience in leading teams of Claims Examiners. Strong organizational, problem solving, and analytical skills. Change champion; Process Improvement experience. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience. How we support our colleagues: In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile, inclusive environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions, but we also recognize that flexibility goes beyond just the place of work... and we are all for it. We call this Smart Working! Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued. Aon values an innovative workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Aon provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran, marital, domestic partner status, or other legally protected status. People with criminal histories are encouraged to apply. Job.JobTitle: Health Reinsurance Actuarial Leader, Managed Care Analytics and Advisory
Job.JobDescription:
Title: Health Reinsurance Actuarial Leader, Managed Care Analytics and Advisory Location: Flexible - United States About the Role In this role, you will serve as a senior client-facing leader, blending deep health actuarial expertise, managed care knowledge, and strategic insight. You will lead a team of actuaries and analysts delivering advanced analytics that shape risk strategies in the healthcare industry, including provider risk arrangements, health insurer reinsurance strategies, and employer stop loss. You will help clients understand the nature of the risk they face, how that risk shifts in different scenarios, and how to structure risk transfer and mitigation solutions that are aligned with their strategic, operational, and financial objectives. You will also oversee traditional stop loss and reinsurance placement analyses. This role carries significant responsibility for client leadership, team development, innovation, and business growth in the US market. Key Responsibilities Client Leadership & Strategic Advisory Serve as the lead actuarial and analytics advisor for a portfolio of US-based health plan and healthcare provider clients. Shape client risk strategies for commercial value-based care arrangements and CMS ACO programs, including upside/downside risk contracts, global budgets, and other alternative payment models. Translate complex actuarial and financial analyses into clear, concise, and actionable recommendations for C-suite and senior leadership audiences. Lead executive-level client meetings and presentations, representing Aon as a trusted advisor and thought leader in the managed care and value-based care space. Value-Based Care & Risk Analytics Direct the design and review of models to project utilization, cost, and performance distributions under value-based contracts and ACO arrangements. Oversee analyses of historical and prospective performance, including scenario and sensitivity testing around contract parameters, population characteristics, and care management interventions. Quantify the financial impact of alternative program designs (e.g., shared savings vs. full risk, partial vs. full capitation, global budgets) and advise on contract structure selection. Integrate quality, utilization, cost, and operational inputs to support clients in making informed, data-driven strategic decisions. Lead the development of standardized frameworks, tools, and best practices for value-based care analytics across the practice. Reinsurance Analytics Oversee health reinsurance and stop loss placement strategy Articulate cost-benefit tradeoffs of various risk transfer structures Develop innovative health risk solutions including emerging risks Provide technical negotiation support with reinsurers and carriers Leadership, Talent Development & Technical Oversight Lead and develop a team of junior actuaries and analysts, providing coaching, feedback, and career development guidance. Set expectations and standards for actuarial rigor, documentation, and peer review, ensuring that all work meets Aon’s quality and professional standards. Oversee multiple concurrent projects and workstreams, ensuring timely, high-quality delivery and a positive client experience. Encourage experimentation with new methods, data sources, and tools, while maintaining appropriate controls and governance. Growth, Innovation & Business Development Play a key role in business development activities including pipeline management, go-to-market strategies, proposal development, and pitch meetings. Contribute to and help shape Aon’s intellectual capital and solution portfolio in the managed care and value-based care domains, including participation in thought leadership, external speaking, and publishing as appropriate. Required Skills and Qualifications 12+ years of progressive health actuarial experience at leading actuarial consulting firms, health insurers, provider-sponsored plans, or similar organizations. Deep expertise in the US managed care environment, including commercial and government programs, with substantial hands-on experience in value-based payment models and/or ACO arrangements. Demonstrated leadership of complex actuarial projects involving value-based contracts, shared savings/shared risk arrangements, capitation, and/or global budgets. Strong experience with traditional health actuarial work, including pricing, reserving, trend analysis, and financial projections. Proven track record as a senior client leader, including responsibility for executive-level relationships and strategic advisory engagements. Pricing Strategies - Advanced; Process Improvements - Experienced; Profitability Analysis - Advanced; Reinsurance - Advanced; Report Writing - Advanced; Risk Analysis - Experienced; Risk Management - Experienced; Trend Analysis - Experienced; Actuarial Science - Advanced; Data Management - Experienced; Insurance - Advanced; Market Pricing - Experienced; Model Building - Adva Education & Credentials FSA (Fellow of the Society of Actuaries) strongly preferred; experienced ASA with a particularly strong track record will be considered. Bachelor’s degree in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, or a related quantitative field. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $235,000-$255,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive [an annual discretionary bonus] in addition to base salary. The amount of any [bonus] varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-KT1 #LI-HYBRID 2590425

Job.JobTitle: Account Executive II, Power & Renewables Practice - Aon Global Natural Resources
Job.JobDescription:
Account Executive II, Power & Renewables – Aon Global Natural Resources Are you energized by the transition to a low‑carbon future? Do you want to sit at the center of the global Power & Renewables market, advising some of the world’s most sophisticated utilities and renewables companies on their most complex risks? If so, this could be the role for you! Join Aon’s industry‑leading Global Natural Resources team as a Senior Account Executive III focused on Power & Renewables, and help our clients make better decisions in an era of unprecedented change. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better—to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. We are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like In this role, you will be the strategic quarterback for a portfolio of major Power & Renewables clients. You will: Own and grow key client relationships, engaging directly with senior decision-makers while remaining a trusted, day‑to‑day partner for client teams. Lead the end‑to‑end renewal process, assembling and guiding cross‑functional Aon teams to craft and implement tailored renewal strategies. Partner closely with Brokers to design and deliver innovative risk transfer and placement strategies that reflect current and emerging market dynamics. Orchestrate critical relationships between clients, Aon account and risk services teams, and insurers to drive differentiated outcomes. Ensure the client service team deeply understands each client’s business, risk profile, and goals—and that our service model and economic framework are aligned to them. Lead stewardship planning and delivery, clearly demonstrating the value Aon brings through insights, outcomes, and execution. Manage overall account profitability, taking a value‑based approach to scope, pricing, and the Client Service Standards Structure and negotiate Aon’s compensation for services, whether fee‑ or commission‑based, ensuring transparency and alignment. Educate clients on risk management and risk transfer options, market conditions, and key trends in the Power & Renewables landscape, supported by benchmarking and analyzer data. Mobilize the right Aon experts and resources when clients face unusual or high‑severity situations, such as major claims or new project developments. Collaborate across geographies (including international markets), functions, and business divisions to build coordinated solutions and capture growth opportunities. Coordinate invoicing and receivables for assigned clients, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and a high‑quality client experience. How this opportunity is different This is a high‑impact, visible role at the intersection of global power, infrastructure, and risk. You will: Serve as the primary relationship owner for some of Aon’s most important Power & Renewables clients. Lead and mentor cross‑disciplinary client service teams to deliver outstanding service and unlock new value for clients. Play a strategic role in helping clients navigate the energy transition, new technologies, evolving regulatory pressures, and increasingly sophisticated risk landscapes. Build and grow a profitable book of business, with room to innovate on service, structure, and solutions in partnership with Aon’s broader Global Natural Resources platform. Through strategic advice, differentiated service, and compelling insight, you will showcase the full power of Aon to our clients—and help define what “best in class” looks like in the Power & Renewables sector. Skills and experience that will lead to success 10–15+ years of Property & Casualty (P&C) experience, with a strong track record serving complex, multinational clients. Deep experience managing large, sophisticated accounts in the Power, Renewables, and/or broader Natural Resources sector. Proven ability to lead client relationship strategy, drive growth, and manage profitability across a portfolio of accounts. Strong organizational, interpersonal, and project management skills, with the ability to prioritize effectively and manage multiple complex initiatives simultaneously. Sharp critical thinking and executive‑level communication skills; able to translate complex concepts into clear, compelling narratives for a range of stakeholders. High level of digital fluency, including advanced use of Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and comfort with data‑driven insights. Active Property & Casualty license required. Bachelor’s degree preferred, or equivalent years of relevant industry experience. Pay Transparency Laws The salary range for this position is $150,000 to $185,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on your education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. Salary may also be adjusted based on geographic location. This role is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans, including a discretionary bonus and production incentives in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus and production incentives varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. If you’re ready to help shape the future of Power & Renewables risk management—and to grow your career with a global leader—we encourage you to apply! For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-JG1 2579081

Job.JobTitle: Senior Finance Director, North America Reinsurance Solutions
Job.JobDescription:
The Senior Finance Director, North America, Reinsurance Solutions will act as the senior finance partner for Aon’s Reinsurance North America (US, Canada and Caribbean) leadership team, holding full responsibility for financial strategy, performance management, capital allocation, and decision support throughout the North America Reinsurance business. The role plays a crucial part in driving principled growth, margin expansion, and returns, while ensuring rigorous financial governance in a sophisticated, and market‑sensitive business. Reporting to the Global Chief Financial Officer Reinsurance, this role will bring strong strategic judgment, deep financial acumen, and executive presence. The role requires a leader who can operate at both altitude and detail—translating market dynamics, portfolio decisions, and capital deployment into clear, actionable financial insights for senior leadership. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Strategic Finance & Decision Support Act as the primary finance advisor to the leadership team of North American Reinsurance, providing clear, actionable insights on growth, profitability, and capital deployment. Lead financial input into the North American reinsurance operating plan and long‑range business planning, ensuring alignment with enterprise objectives and return thresholds. Evaluate critical initiatives, including organic investments, talent deployment, pricing and portfolio mix, and M&A, with a focus on return on investment, return on invested capital, and value creation. Provide forward‑looking analysis on market cycles (hard, soft, and transitional markets), pricing trends, capacity dynamics, and client segment profitability. Performance Management & Analytics Own financial performance management for the reinsurance operations in North America, including monthly results, forecasts, and variance analysis. Establish and refine leading and lagging critical metrics that predict performance and enable early course correction. Drive deeper portfolio‑level analytics across products, client segments, and capital solutions. Translate sophisticated financial data into concise, executive‑ready materials for senior management. Capital Allocation & Financial Governance Partner with Corporate Planning, Treasury, and Controllership on capital allocation decisions, including investment prioritization, expense discipline, and balance sheet considerations. Ensure strong financial controls, governance, and compliance throughout the North American reinsurance finance division. Support disciplined execution against approved arguments, with clear accountability and transparency on delivery versus plan. Leadership & Collaboration Lead and develop a high-performing finance team within the North American reinsurance sector, encouraging strong engagement, accountability, and talent development. Partner closely with Regional CFOs, Solution Line finance leaders, Strategy, ABS, and other enterprise functions to ensure consistency of data, insights, and execution. Serve as a trusted thought partner to senior leaders, balancing challenge and support within a cross-functional organization. Skills and experience that will lead to success 10+ years of progressive finance leadership experience in sophisticated, global organizations. Strong background in strategic finance, FP&A, performance management, and capital allocation. Proven experience supporting senior business leaders in dynamic, cyclical, or financial services environments; experience in insurance, reinsurance, or capital markets is strongly preferred. Proven ability to lead teams, influence across a matrix, and operate effectively at the executive level. Deep financial modeling and analytical expertise, including assessment of profitability against capital employed, valuation, and scenario planning. Solid understanding of accounting, cash management, tax, and financial controls. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Finance, Accounting, or a related field; MBA, CFA, or equivalent advanced degree preferred. Critical Leadership Capabilities Executive Presence & Judgment: Clear, confident communicator with the ability to distill complexity into actionable insight and influence senior partners. Strategic Agility: Ability to connect financial outcomes to business strategy, market dynamics, and long‑term value creation. Operational Rigor: Strong bias toward execution, accountability, and delivery against commitments. Collaborative Leadership: Trusted partner who builds positive relationships and leads effectively in a matrixed environment. Integrity & Accountability: Highest standards of professionalism, rigor, and ethical conduct. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $180,000 to $230,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plan in addition to base salary. The amount of any incentives varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance. This role does not accrue vacation. Rather, this role is eligible to take paid time off at the discretion of the employee and management in accordance with company policy and practices. Various other types of leaves of absence; paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Do you understand the unique risks facing ship owners, ports, and other maritime businesses? Are you ready to grow your career in Marine Hull & Liability brokerage? This is a hybrid role based in our Chicago office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. We are looking for a Broker I to join our Marine Hull & Liability team in Chicago. In this role, you will partner with ship owners, operators, ports, and other marine clients to design insurance and risk management programs that protect their operations and support their growth. How this opportunity is different Aon’s Global Marine Specialty Practice is structured to deliver global capabilities locally. As the world’s leading broker, and as experts in marine coverages and market alternatives, Aon has unparalleled access to world insurance markets and new sources of capital, enabling us to design the optimal insurance and risk management program for each client. You will work closely with a diverse client base – ship owners and operators, cruise, ferry and other passenger vessels, charterers, ports, terminals, and shipyards, as well as other firms with marine exposures – to interpret their needs. Using a data-driven approach and technology that collects and analyzes global market data in real time, you will support carrier selection and negotiation as part of an industry-leading team, with direct guidance from the N.Y. Hull & Liability Practice Leader. You will also benefit from continuing education and training, and tremendous potential for growth within a worldwide organization. What the day will look like As a Broker I within the Marine practice of Aon Risk Solutions in Chicago, you will help empower results for our clients by delivering innovative and effective insurance and risk management solutions. Reporting directly to the Chicago Hull & Liability Practice Leader, you will: Identify and analyze client exposures and determine which markets to utilize, ensuring a thorough evaluation of qualified companies in the marketplace Participate in client discussions to understand needs and develop strategies Act as the primary negotiator in obtaining the most appropriate coverage from a variety of insurance carriers Create submissions for all accounts, ensuring quality to Aon standards, including details of any midterm changes, new operations, exposure schedules, and claims summaries Assemble, check, and issue binders and insurance/renewal documentation, ensuring timely delivery to clients Calculate premiums, fees, post-policy adjustments, and taxes Provide support, guidance, and training to others Skills and experience that will lead to success Minimum of 2 years of insurance industry or related experience Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, with proficiency in Microsoft Office applications Excellent interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills, with the ability to work effectively in a team-based environment Good sales and presentation skills, with the desire and aptitude to quickly develop effective sales techniques and a commitment to delivering the highest level of customer service and quality Goal-oriented and highly motivated, with the ability to organize a wide range of tasks from various sources, prioritize workload to meet deadlines, and travel when required Education: Bachelor’s degree For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. Job.JobTitle: Equine Farm and Ranch Account Executive Broker Specialist
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Account Executive, Insurance Sales, Insurance Broker
Job.JobDescription:
Aon is looking for a Equine Farm and Ranch-Account Executive/Broker Specialist for our Private Risk Management Group. This is a virtual position, that can be located anywhere in the United States. As part of an industry-leading team, you will help empower results for our clients by delivering innovative and effective solutions. Aon is in the business of better decisions: At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like: An emerging team member who is responsible for assisting a team of Account Executives with day-to-day account management and broking of personal insurance programs. Supports the Account Executive by working to build, expand, and solidify relationships with existing clients and prospective clients. Promotes the value that Aon delivers to clients through superior service, pricing, consultation, and reporting. Assist with new business and remarketing of equine, farm, and ranch insurance programs for current clients. Updating applications within our agency management system, quoting online with insurers, and completing coverage comparisons or proposals for the Account Executives in Microsoft Word or Excel. Prepare and input summary of coverages for Account Executives. Prepare and maintain summary of values for Account Executives. Assist with conducting annual reviews for clients. Process changes and endorsements within 48 hours of receipt. The time service standard: returning a phone call within 24 hours and responding to emails by the end of the day. Assist the Account Executive with complex claim activity. Including contacting claims adjusters when necessary. Assisting the Account Executive with client billing issues- including contacting the carrier and/or internal accounting team to coordinate, track, resolve billing/payment issues. Access carrier websites/systems to process changes, retrieve documents and information as required. Skills and experience that will lead to success: Minimum of 3 years experience with high-net-worth personal lines insurance. Experience with complex equine or farm and ranch accounts a plus. Experience with Applied Epic is preferred. Proficiency in applying carrier management platforms (American Reliable, Chubb Agribusiness, Travelers Agribusiness, etc.). Intermediate experience with Microsoft Word and Excel. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of industry experience is preferred. Must have a valid P&C license. AFIS, CPRIA, CPCU, CIC, or ARM completed or in process is preferred. How we support our colleagues In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions for our colleagues as well. Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued. Aon values an innovative and inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Aon provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran, marital, domestic partner status, or other legally protected status. People with criminal histories are encouraged to apply. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering an inclusive workplace. If you require accommodations during the application or interview process, please let us know. You can request accommodations by emailing us at ReasonableAccommodations@Aon.com or your recruiter. We will work with you to meet your needs and ensure a fair and equitable experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $65,000 to $75,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-KH2 #LI-REMOTE 2590158

Job.JobTitle: Broker, Life Sciences | Clinical Trials Liability
Job.JobDescription:
As part of an industry-leading team, you will help empower results for our clients by delivering innovative and effective Clinical Trial solutions for our clients as part of our Life Science Practice Group. This position will be based in Philadelphia, PA. We are open to considering candidates located in Philadelphia as well as other East Coast states, including but not limited to New York, Charlotte, Boston, and Connecticut (Hartford). This role offers flexibility for hybrid work, with a combination of in-office and remote work options. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Responsible for broking/placing primarily Clinical Trials Liability as well Products Liability, Errors & Omissions Liability, and Excess Liability Market new and renewal business, handling all aspects of the placements from initial market selection through the long-term servicing until the clinical trials these policies are covering are over. Demonstrate effective negotiation skills on behalf of clients and prospects. Ensure that placements are handled timely and correctly Develop productive business relationships with key insurance underwriters and Aon local office teams Identify and analyze prospect and client exposures. Coordinate activities with other internal units as required to meet customer needs. Create presentations such as Renewal Strategies and Coverage Proposals. Responsible for planning, scheduling, resourcing and executing complex projects/programs. Frequently interacts with senior level colleagues and clients, normally involving matters between functional areas, other company divisions or units, or clients and the company. How this opportunity is different Join Aon’s industry-leading team in the Life Sciences sector, where you’ll provide innovative Clinical Trial Liability solutions to clients in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries. This role offers flexibility for hybrid work, with opportunities to work from Philadelphia or other East Coast locations. You’ll manage complex insurance placements, build key relationships with underwriters, and contribute to vital clinical trials that support the approval of life-saving drugs and devices. With a focus on collaboration, trust, and professional growth, this is an exciting opportunity to make a significant impact in healthcare. Skills and experience that will lead to success Unlike most insurance programs, the primary purpose of Clinical Trial Liability insurance is to support Pharma and Biotech companies through regulatory approvals and contractual compliance while simultaneously protecting these trial sponsors and their research partners from financial liability in case of injury or harm. Clinical trials are essential for the approval of new drugs and medical devices, as they provide the data needed to assess safety and efficacy in humans, a requirement for regulatory approval by agencies like the FDA. To generate this volume of data, clinical trials must take place in many countries who closely regulate the activity including the clinical trial liability insurance. Our team of specialized brokers, through global and local insurance partners, provides the necessary local insurance ensuring no trial is ever delayed due to insurance reasons thus supporting our clients in their mission of saving and improving lives. Attention to detail, ability to multi-task, exceptional organizational skills, ability to present complex insurance programs. Minimum of 5+ years of insurance brokerage and/or underwriting experience (preferred Life Sciences in Clinical Trials Liability and/or Casualty Line experience) Effective working knowledge of carrier underwriting practices & processes. Proven client facing skills including effective presentations & communications. Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact effectively at various levels in the organization. Ability to independently manage a dynamic book of clients Successfully operates in a fast-paced driven environment that requires the ability to handle multiple tasks simultaneously. Must maintain appropriate broker’s and Surplus Lines licenses. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of industry experience. A Property and Casualty Brokers License is required or must be obtained within 90 days of hire if not already active. How we support our colleagues In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions for our colleagues as well. Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued. Aon values an innovative and inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Aon provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran, marital, domestic partner status, or other legally protected status. People with criminal histories are encouraged to apply. We welcome applications from all and provide individuals with disabilities with reasonable adjustments to participate in the job application, interview process and to perform essential job functions once onboard. If you would like to learn more about the reasonable accommodations we provide, email ReasonableAccommodations@Aon.com For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $88,000 -$115,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. The salary range reflected is based on a primary work location of Pennsylvania. The actual salary may vary for applicants in a different geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-CF1 #LI-HYBRID #LI-Mid-Seniorlevel 2587262

Associate Director – P&C Actuarial Pricing Location: Hybrid (Chicago, Minneapolis, New York) Role Overview Aon’s Strategy & Technology Group (STG) is seeking an experienced credentialed actuary to help grow an advisory capability focused on property & casualty insurance. This role supports complex client engagements across pricing and predictive modeling use cases and contributes to the development of a differentiated actuarial pricing offering within STG. The role blends hands-on analysis with client advisory work. The successful candidate will develop and evaluate pricing strategies, and build and refine rating structures, while working closely with client stakeholders to ensure solutions are practical, interpretable, and aligned with business objectives. Key Responsibilities Develop, refine, and support actuarial pricing analyses across P&C insurance use cases, including rate adequacy, territorial analysis, and rating plan development. Apply GLMs to model pure premium using large, complex insurance datasets. Translate business problems into analytical solutions and clearly communicate results to both technical and non-technical audiences. Effectively manage client engagements from problem definition through delivery, ensuring analytical rigor and actionable outcomes. Partner with reinsurance brokers and senior team members to deliver industry-leading client solutions. Provide technical leadership, training, and development to junior team members. Support proposal development, client presentations, and RFPs as needed in collaboration with senior leadership. Qualifications 7+ years of actuarial pricing experience within property & casualty insurance. Bachelor’s degree FCAS credential preferred. Prior experience conducting rate filing research using SERFF, including review of filing support, exhibits, regulatory correspondence, and objection handling. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex analytical concepts clearly and concisely.
