Job.JobTitle: Representations & Warranties M&A Insurance- Vice President
Job.JobDescription:
Representations & Warranties M&A Insurance- Vice President The San Francisco office of Aon is seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Vice President to join its market-leading M&A and Transaction Solutions team. This is an outstanding opportunity for a corporate attorney with 3-5 years of M&A experience to transition from private practice into a client-facing advisory role supporting some of the most sophisticated private equity and strategic clients in the market. This role is a hybrid role, with the flexibility of working both virtually and form our San Francisco office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. How this opportunity is different As a Vice President you will work alongside senior and junior brokers, underwriters, private equity sponsors, corporate clients and leading law firms to structure and place Representations & Warranties Insurance (RWI) on domestic and cross-border transactions. We will provide hands-on experience, industry-leading training and mentorship in a collaborative environment. This position offers a broad range of responsibilities and will allow candidates to remain deeply involved in complex corporate transactions while developing commercial negotiation and client relationship skills in a fast-paced M&A environment. We value continued growth and learning, collaboration and pride in delivering exceptional work. If you are looking to take the next step in your career and gain hands on MA& transaction insurance experience, we encourage you to reach out and explore this opportunity! Key Responsibilities: Advise private equity sponsors, strategic buyers and their advisors on transactional risk insurance solutions. Review purchase agreements, disclosure schedules, diligence reports and transaction documentation to identify underwriting considerations and coverage issues. Coordinate the underwriting process with leading insurance carriers from initial marketing through policy binding. Analyze legal and commercial risks associated with mergers and acquisitions across a broad range of industries. Draft and negotiate policy terms and facilitate discussions between insurers and transaction parties. Manage multiple transactions simultaneously while meeting demanding deal timelines. Build and maintain relationships with law firms, investment bankers, private equity firms and corporate clients. Support business development initiatives and participate in client presentations, industry conferences and educational seminars. Collaborate with colleagues across Aon’s global Transaction Solutions platform on domestic and international transactions. Qualifications: The ideal candidate must have a strong academic record, excellent analytical and oral communication skills. In addition, the candidate must be a proven self-starter willing to take on a good deal of responsibility with the ability to problem solve and advise clients involved in complex transactions. J.D. from an accredited law school. 3-5 years of experience practicing corporate/M&A law at a nationally recognized law firm. Strong experience negotiating and drafting acquisition agreements and supporting private M&A transactions. Effective presentation, reporting and interpersonal skills. Excellent analytical skills with exceptional attention to detail. Outstanding written and verbal communication skills. Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment while managing multiple active transactions as part of a team and with minimal direction. Strong commercial judgment and an interest in developing relationships within the TS team and wider Aon, as well as developing trust and confidence with clients as well as carrier partners. Collaborative, proactive and entrepreneurial mindset. Skilled in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint. Ability to attain a Broker’s License within 90 days of employment. Preferred Qualifications Experience representing private equity sponsors and strategic buyers. Exposure to cross-border transactions. Interest in insurance, risk management or financial services. Why Join Aon Transaction Solutions? Aon’s Transaction Solutions practice is one of the industry’s leading advisors on transactional risk insurance. Our professionals work on many of the largest and most complex M&A transactions globally, partnering with premier private equity firms, Fortune 500 companies and top-tier law firms. This position provides the opportunity to leverage your legal training while building a long-term career in a dynamic, client-facing advisory business that combines law, finance, insurance and M&A strategy. You will gain: Exposure to complex and high-profile M&A transactions and industry-leading clients Collaborate in an entrepreneurial team environment Career growth opportunities within a growing, high impact practice Be a part of a vibrant and inclusive culture that values collaboration diversity of thought and the opportunity to work alongside talented driven colleagues Competitive compensation and benefits package Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $275,000 - $350,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. #LI-YT1 #LI-HYBRID 2580357

Job.JobTitle: Workday PSA, Professional Services Automation Architect
Job.JobDescription: We are seeking an experienced Workday Professional Services Automation (PSA) Architect to implement the strategy, roadmap, architecture, and ongoing evolution of our enterprise Workday PSA platform. Serving as both design authority and hands-on technical lead, the PSA Architect will translate complex finance and operational requirements into scalable solutions spanning project and contract setup, time and expense capture, resource and utilization management, customer accounts, billing, invoicing, revenue recognition, accounts receivable, and collections. Partnering closely with Finance, Operations, Technology, and regional collaborators, this role will lead major PSA initiatives from discovery through implementation, stabilization, and ongoing support in a global, matrixed environment! Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world! As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Implement the vision, roadmap, governance, and lifecycle management of Workday PSA, aligning platform capabilities with global finance, order-to-cash, project delivery, and operational priorities. Serve as the enterprise design authority for Workday PSA. Lead solution architecture across Projects, Project Billing, Customer Contracts, Customer Accounts, Time Tracking, Expenses, Revenue Management, Accounts Receivable, and Collections. Lead technical solutioning for major PSA initiatives from discovery and process design through configuration, testing, deployment, hypercare, and transition to steady state support. Translate complex business requirements into scalable Workday configurations, business processes, security designs, integrations, and operating procedures. Architect end-to-end professional services processes that support: Project, contract, customer, and worktag setup. Time and expense capture, approval, and corrections. Billing schedules, billable transactions, invoice creation, adjustments, and special handling Revenue schedules, revenue recognition, intercompany activity, and accounting alignment Accounts receivable, cash application, collections, write-offs, and customer account management Utilization, project performance, margin, operational, and financial reporting Define architectural standards and guardrails for configuration, business processes, calculated fields, custom validations, reporting, security, and data governance. Partner with Workday Financials and HCM architects to ensure PSA designs align with the broader Workday platform, enterprise architecture, chart of accounts, organizational structures, worker data, and time entry requirements. Architect and oversee integrations between Workday PSA and adjacent platforms, including CRM, contract lifecycle management, ERP, tax, banking, data warehouses, reporting, payroll, and other enterprise applications. Own data integrity and control design across customer, contract, project, worker, time, billing, revenue, invoice, and receivables data, with clear reconciliation and auditability. Support the Workday security build, including security groups, domain and business process policies, role assignments, access controls, and separation of responsibilities. Lead reporting and analytics architecture using Workday report writing, calculated fields, dashboards, worksheets, and downstream data platforms to support operational and executive decision making. Evaluate Workday releases and new PSA capabilities, assess business and technical impacts, oversee regression testing, and guide adoption decisions. Provide support for complex production issues, root-cause analysis, defect resolution, and business critical support while strengthening preventive controls. Partner with application management service providers, implementation partners, and internal teams to establish clear delivery responsibilities, quality standards, documentation, knowledge transfer, and support boundaries. Support training, change management, and adoption by helping collaborators understand solution design, process impacts, controls, and new ways of working. Provide architecture reviews and design guidance across concurrent initiatives. How this opportunity is different This role goes well beyond maintaining current tools. You will: Shape the future of a strategic enterprise platform that connects project delivery, time, billing, revenue, receivables, and financial reporting in one integrated operating model. Balance global standards with regional and business requirements, designing solutions that are scalable across countries, legal entities, currencies, tax regimes, and professional services business models. Play a central role in finance and operations transformation by simplifying fragmented processes, strengthening controls, improving data quality, and enabling more consistent client and colleague experiences. Operate with a high degree of autonomy and ownership in a fast paced, matrixed environment, explaining complex designs, dependencies, risks, and tradeoffs to both technical and business audiences. Influence platform strategy, sequencing, and investment decisions while remaining close enough to the technology to validate designs and solve difficult problems. Skills and experience that will lead to success Extensive hands-on experience architecting, configuring, and supporting Workday PSA and related Workday Financials capabilities in a complex global environment. 7+ years of demonstrated experience with enterprise financial systems or professional services technology, including 5+ years of Workday Financials and PSA implementation, configuration, architecture, or consulting experience. Deep functional knowledge of Workday Projects, Project Billing, Customer Contracts, Customer Accounts, Revenue Management, Time Tracking, Expenses, Accounts Receivable, Collections, and related accounting processes. Demonstrated success designing scalable global solutions for project-to-cash or order-to-cash processes across multiple countries, legal entities, currencies, and business models. Strong Workday configuration expertise, including business processes, condition rules, validations, calculated fields, custom reports, dashboards, worksheets, security, and release management. Solid understanding of financial controls, data governance, reconciliation, auditability, and segregation of duties. Experience leading testing strategy and execution across unit, end-to-end, integration, regression, user acceptance, and post-production validation. Experience working with implementation partners and application management service providers, including design review, quality assurance, delivery governance, and knowledge transfer. Good sense of ownership and accountability, with the ability to lead architecture and delivery decisions through ambiguity. Solid ability to translate business needs into technical builds and clearly explain complex options and tradeoffs. Demonstrable ability to lead and influence multi-functional, global initiatives without direct authority. Ability to build trusted partnerships with Finance, Accounting, Operations, Commercial, HR, Data, Risk, Audit, and Technology collaborators. Ability to manage multiple priorities, resolve design conflicts, and maintain momentum across concurrent projects and operational commitments. Experience mentoring team members and raising the quality and consistency of solution design and delivery practices. Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, Finance, Accounting, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered. Ability to connect PSA technology decisions to business outcomes such as billing accuracy, revenue integrity, cash collection, utilization visibility, operational efficiency, and client service. Experience defining platform roadmaps, governance models, architecture principles, and release strategies. Strategic, systems thinking attitude with strong architecture capabilities and a focus on scalability, standardization, control, and user experience. Curiosity about emerging Workday capabilities, automation, analytics, and AI-enabled opportunities that can improve professional services operations and finance processes. Comfort operating in an environment passionate about delivering clear results, defined service responsibilities, and ongoing improvement. Workday Pro Financials certification preferred; current Workday Financials and PSA certifications are highly desirable. Advanced knowledge of professional services, project accounting, order-to-cash, billing, revenue recognition, and accounts receivable processes preferred. Experience with global Workday deployments and complex matrixed organizations strongly preferred. PMP, Agile, or related delivery certification preferred. Demonstrated dedication to continuous learning and knowing the latest in Workday PSA, Financials, integration, reporting, security, and industry developments. The Financial Operations Manager serves as the strategic finance and operations lead for Aon’s Marketing & Communications (MarComm) and People Organization, acting as the primary liaison to Finance. Reporting to the Chief of Staff, this role leads a team responsible for financial planning, workforce investment governance, and oversight of events, project, and program expenditures. The role combines people leadership, financial stewardship, and cross-functional partnership to drive operational excellence, align investments with business priorities, and ensure adherence to enterprise standards. The successful candidate develops talent, fosters accountability, and collaborates with senior leaders to deliver strategic initiatives and organizational objectives. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like People Leadership & Team Development Directly manage a team of two colleagues, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, inclusion, growth, and high performance. Establish annual team goals and individual performance objectives aligned to MarComm, People Organization, and enterprise priorities. Lead performance management activities, including goal setting, performance reviews, ongoing feedback, talent assessment, and recognition of colleague contributions. Hold regular 1:1 meetings and quarterly 4x4 development conversations to support colleague growth, engagement, career progression, and development planning. Provide coaching, mentorship, and stretch opportunities that build financial acumen, business partnership skills, operational discipline, and future leadership readiness. Monitor workload distribution, clarify priorities, remove barriers, and ensure successful delivery of key planning, reporting, governance, and operational objectives. Support succession planning and building capability by identifying development opportunities, strengthening team knowledge, and encouraging continuous learning. Enterprise Integration & Cross-Functional Leadership Serve as a key integration point across enterprise stakeholders to ensure alignment on financial targets, strategic priorities, investments, operational activities, governance requirements, and execution plans. Coordinate planning, workforce investments, vendor engagements, organizational changes, and new initiatives across a broad stakeholder network. Drive cross-functional collaboration to support organizational effectiveness, resource optimization, financial transparency, and successful execution of strategic initiatives. Lead integration efforts for new programs, projects, technologies, and business processes, ensuring effective implementation, operational readiness, and clear ownership. Partner with business leaders and enterprise stakeholders to identify process improvements, governance enhancements, and operational efficiencies. Facilitate decision-making by aligning diverse stakeholder groups around common objectives, priorities, investment trade-offs, and execution timelines. Support enterprise-wide initiatives, organizational transformations, and operating model changes by ensuring appropriate financial, operational, and governance structures are in place. Strategic Financial Planning & Workforce Investment Governance Lead the annual planning, budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning processes for the MarComm and People Organization functions. Oversee governance and review of Salary, incentive and Benefits (SIB) talent investments and hire requests, ensuring alignment with business cases, organizational priorities, and approved plans. Partner with functional leaders to evaluate workforce needs, investment impacts, financial trade-offs, and prioritization decisions. Develop financial models, planning inputs, and operating reviews that support informed decision-making and resource allocation. P&L Oversight, Variance Management & Financial Structures Key liaison between MarComm and the People Org with the Finance function. Partner with functional leaders to ensure visibility into P&L performance, including SIB and non-salary, incentive, and benefits variances (NSIB). Provide analysis of actuals, forecasts, risks, opportunities, and year-end outlooks to strengthen transparency and accountability. Own the governance and maintenance of cost-center structures, financial hierarchies, and organizational reporting frameworks. Ensuring financial structures align with evolving functional structures, operating models, organizational redesigns, and new initiatives. Oversee financial governance for projects, programs, vendor engagements, and operational expenditures, including budget management and investment prioritization. How this opportunity is different The ideal candidate is a strategic and collaborative people leader who combines strong coaching and talent development capabilities with financial and operational expertise in Marketing and HR costs. They create clarity, build trust, and develop high-performing teams through regular feedback, quarterly 4x4 development conversations, thoughtful coaching, and clear expectations. This leader excels at connecting people, processes, financial structures, and business objectives. They are comfortable navigating complex, matrixed environments, influencing senior stakeholders, and aligning diverse groups around shared priorities. They bring discipline to planning, governance, financial transparency, and operational execution while enabling successful delivery of organizational priorities and strategic investments. Skills and experience that will lead to success Significant experience in financial operations, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), workforce planning, business operations, or related finance leadership roles. Demonstrated experience managing and developing colleagues, including performance reviews, goal setting, coaching, mentoring, and development planning. Proven ability to partner with senior leaders in a complex, matrixed organization and translate financial insights into business actions. Strong understanding of annual planning, forecasting, P&L management, variance analysis, cost-center governance, and organizational financial structures. Experience supporting projects, programs, vendor engagements, organizational changes, and cross-functional initiatives. Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, influence, problem-solving, and operational execution skills. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Solution Line: Global Reinsurance Solutions/Risk Capital Global Strategy & Execution Manager Role Overview - Virtual Role The Global Strategy and Execution Manager is accountable for driving and accelerating the development and execution of global strategic initiatives across solution lines to deliver business outcomes. The role offers a blend of strategic planning, business planning, execution planning, change management and implementation. Success in this role will requires a clear understanding of Aon’s global strategy, strong insight into business needs, and the ability to build effective stakeholder relationships The role holder will have clear ownership of a set of strategic priorities, with accountability for delivering agreed outcomes. This includes working across the business to ensure global alignment, consistent change management and effective execution. The role will also work closely with leaders and teams across Risk Capital to support and help deliver broader cross‑solution strategies that create differentiated client value and commercial value for the firm. Build strong relationships with stakeholder of all levels from across the enterprise. Partner with key business functions (Risk, Operations, Finance, HR) to accelerate execution of initiatives critical to delivering growth objectives. Work closely with the Global Strategy & Execution team to ensure coordination, alignment and prioritisation across initiatives. Job.JobDescription:
Senior Vice President, Broker, Construction Casualty Our Construction & Infrastructure Practice is looking for a Senior Casualty Broker. This is a great opportunity to join the Construction & Infrastructure team to broker/consult on behalf of a diversified client base with insurance underwriters in the Casualty insurance discipline. This is a hybrid role that can based out of our Atlanta, Chicago, Los Angeles, New York City or St. Louis office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like You’ll be responsible for assessing client needs, designing solutions and negotiating with insurance carriers to obtain coverage that is in a client’s best interests Professional who develops and manages client relationships, account strategies and insurance marketing activities. Act as a trusted advisor to the client, in broking, designing, selling and servicing complex accounts Provide outstanding and timely service and support to clients, relationship managers and originator Identify and analyze client exposures and ensure policy coverage addresses all such exposures Facilitate the compilation of submission information in conjunction with clients, relationship managers, originators and service center support Finalize market submission and product design options to clients, relationship managers, and originators Review and analyze quotes and binders to ensure appropriate coverage Detailed knowledge of the existing and prospected business within the segment Insurance Carrier relations specific to the segment Bespoke Broking and account reviews Detailed knowledge of the market dynamics within the segment Retain and grow assigned clients / prospects Adhere to the highest standards of professionalism and ethical behavior in all activities and able to work well in a team environment Travel as required for client, prospect and industry events Skills and experience that will lead to success Minimum 15+ years construction/infrastructure customer service and brokerage support experience Agent/Broker License Proven collaboration skills – Prioritizes team success over individual recognition Strong oral presentation skills and the ability to clearly articulate complex written messages A network of carrier relationships Strong negotiation skills Strong work ethic Develop proficiency in use of in-house account management systems (CRBA, CRA and future Aon brokerage and analytics tools) Preferred Experience Broking experience on major complex risks Management Skills Preferred Computer knowledge: Adept with Microsoft Office Suite Education Bachelor’s degree required The salary range for this position is $176,200 - $250,000 annually. This salary range is an estimate and the actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. How we support our colleagues Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions for our colleagues as well. Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued. Aon values an innovative and inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Aon provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran, marital, domestic partner status, or other legally protected status. People with criminal histories are encouraged to apply. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering an inclusive workplace. If you require accommodations during the application or interview process, please let us know. You can request accommodations by emailing us at ReasonableAccommodations@Aon.com or your recruiter. We will work with you to meet your needs and ensure a fair and equitable experience. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you said yes, then apply to join our Account Executive team in New York City! Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. Coordinates with Brokers in the development and delivery of renewal strategies. Facilitates critical relationships between clients, ARS and insurers. Ensures client service team understanding of client needs, service delivery methods, and the economic framework relevant to services delivered. Leads stewardship planning and delivery Ensures overall account profitability with a value-based approach for the scope of service and costs associated with the Client Promise Plan. Arranges Aon compensation for services, whether fee or commission-based, accordingly. Educates clients in risk management, risk transfer, market issues and relevant trends including appropriate benchmarking and GRIP data. Manages input to and follow-up on invoicing and receivables process for assigned clients, ensuring timely collections. You will lead client service teams to identify and meet client needs and thereby retain and grow a profitable book of business. Through service, pricing, consultation, and reporting, you will promote the value Aon delivers to clients. Critical thinking skills with the ability to clearly express thoughts and concepts at various levels. Excellent digital literacy, including working experience with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook). Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Account Executive, Insurance Sales, Insurance Broker
Job.JobDescription:
As a leader in the industry, Aon is one of the largest surety brokers representing both contract and commercial clients both domestically and globally. We are the top broker with the majority of the large surety companies. Aon is seeking candidates for a Surety Account Executive/Broker Position to join our Construction Services Group (CSG)! This hybrid role (2–3 days onsite weekly) from a local Aon office in Dallas, Houston, Oklahoma, and Louisiana. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. How this opportunity is different At Aon, you won’t just manage accounts—you’ll lead strategy. As a top broker with strong, long-standing relationships across all major surety markets, you’ll gain direct access to decision-makers and play a central role in shaping complex, high-impact bonding programs for major domestic and global clients. This role offers a rare blend of autonomy and support—allowing you to operate with the agility of a boutique team while leveraging Aon’s unmatched scale, resources, and reputation in the surety space. What the day will look like Responsible to manage and grow a portfolio of surety clients. Continuously provide advisory services by outlining the surety program options and providing guidance on the recommended structures specific to the client’s needs. Consult with clients regarding surety market conditions and the surety companies. Secure and manage surety facilities to meet the clients’ surety bond requirements. This process involves the receipt and review materials including but not limited to financial, organizational, operational, and strategic that are necessary to prepare a placement memorandum, negotiation of terms, conditions, indemnity, and completion of the requisite documentation. Management of the existing surety relationships on client surety programs. Including participation in, establishing and moderating meetings, when necessary, with the sureties. Continuously monitor clients company structure, operations, and credit profile in support of the surety program. This includes reviewing financial presentation. Work with client service team as client team lead in managing day to day account management of the surety business. Deliver new solutions for clients by reviewing their needs and ensuring surety credit is maximized Drive growth by working collaboratively with internal sales producers, the Insurance Account Executives and other surety team members to bring in new clients or prospects. This includes contributing to the sales process and responding to RFPs. Preparing and presenting surety proposals and presentations. Skills and experience that will lead to success 5+ years of experience in the Surety industry. Relationship builder – internally and externally. Ability to travel. Well-developed communication and presentation skills. Attention to detail and technical proficiency is critical. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of industry experience. Must have the willingness to obtain an active Property and Casualty license within four months of hire (90 days) For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $134,000 to $225,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-RW1 #LI-HYBRID #LI-Mid-Seniorlevel 2583896

This process involves the receipt and review materials including but not limited to financial, organizational, operational, and strategic that are necessary to prepare a placement memorandum, negotiation of terms, conditions, indemnity, and completion of the requisite documentation. Management of the existing surety relationships on client surety programs. Including participation in, establishing and moderating meetings, when necessary, with the sureties. Continuously monitor clients company structure, operations, and credit profile in support of the surety program. This includes reviewing financial presentation. Work with client service team as client team lead in managing day to day account management of the surety business. Deliver new solutions for clients by reviewing their needs and ensuring surety credit is maximized Drive growth by working collaboratively with internal sales producers, the Insurance Account Executives and other surety team members to bring in new clients or prospects. This includes contributing to the sales process and responding to RFPs. Preparing and presenting surety proposals and presentations. Skills and experience that will lead to success 5+ years of experience in the Surety industry. Relationship builder – internally and externally. Ability to travel. Well-developed communication and presentation skills. Attention to detail and technical proficiency is critical. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of industry experience. Must have the willingness to obtain an active Property and Casualty license within four months of hire (90 days) For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Account Executive, Insurance Sales, Insurance Broker
Job.JobDescription:
Construction Practice Account Executive/Broker II In this Construction Practice Account Executive / Broker II role, the successful professional serves as a primary point of contact for a large construction client. The position is highly service‑oriented and requires someone who can manage complex insurance and risk management needs while maintaining strong, daily communication with client personnel. The Account Executive is expected to respond promptly to client requests, take ownership of each assignment from initial inquiry through delivery, and ensure that all services are completed accurately and on schedule. This position resides within a non-conformed dedicated client service team. The unit is a very flat organization where members’ roles and responsibilities are dependently interrelated, ie, not siloed – we collectively own our successes. This is a hybrid role with the flexibility to work three to four days per week in our Houston, TX, Chicago, IL, New York, NY, or Dallas, TX offices and virtually from home. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like This Construction Practice Account Executive / Broker II position serves as the primary day‑to‑day contact for a large construction client, delivering high‑quality insurance and risk management services on schedule. In addition to managing placements and daily service needs, the position carries responsibility for training and overseeing junior staff, ensuring consistent quality of work and contributing to a collaborative, client‑focused team environment. The ideal candidate will thrive in a fast‑paced, client‑centric environment, balancing daily service delivery with broader account management, broking, and leadership responsibilities, all while consistently meeting deadlines and maintaining high standards of quality and professionalism. Engage client daily to assess areas where Aon can best provide resources and support to their risk management function. Problem solving - can be any topic requiring an array of skills or connections. Proactively manage and coordinate new business and renewals to ensure all necessary steps are completed in a timely fashion by gathering exposure information, producing submissions, communicating quotations/options with the client, ensure coverage is bound prior to the effective dates and binders are continually refreshed as required prior to policy receipt. Clear all coverage subjectivities and contingencies and ensure that policy documentation accurately reflects the coverages, terms, and conditions agreed. Complete regulatory documentation as required. Meet compliance standards. Day-to-day servicing activities. Prepare coverage comparisons, letters, and reports as required. Ensure all communications, both written and verbal, received from clients, markets, other Aon offices, and third parties are acknowledged promptly. Coordinate activity with other Aon offices or third parties to ensure smooth coordination of all client activity and delivery of services. Assist in development of documents and presentations for specific client construction and management projects. Utilize the Aon billing and policy management systems, other data management platforms some of which are hosted by the client. Monitor, summarize and report on claims. Undertake various duties as assigned by unit leads and client. How this opportunity is different This role offers a unique blend of strategic consulting and client advocacy, with exposure to diverse coverage lines and direct influence on risk outcomes. It supports professional growth through business development, high-level collaboration, and leadership opportunities in a key regional market. Skills and experience that will lead to success Minimum 10 years construction related Property, Casualty and associated coverages experience, with emphasis on liability coverage. Active listener and participant engaged in all aspects of client’s risk management function. Develop positive productive working relationships with client personnel. Maintain a strong sense of urgency, the ability to prioritize concurrent assignments, and the flexibility to navigate between projects. Able to organize, pay attention to detail, monitor, and control work flow to meet competing deadlines. Work independently as well as collaboratively within the unit and office. Able to communicate effectively, both written and verbal, in a clear and concise manner Possess very good mathematical and analytical skills, and can understand industry financial concepts. Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Excel, Word, Acrobat, Outlook, including OneNote, Teams and other office applications (successful candidate will intensively use Excel, especially formulas and pivot tables, Word and Acrobat to generate and manage documents, create content, reports, submissions, etc.) Leadership and ability to mentor and assist the professional growth of other unit members. CPCU, ARM, ARe or CRIS designations desired P&C Broker License required. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of industry experience. Must have and maintain an active Property and Casualty insurance license Pay Transparency: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $175,000 to $200,000. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. How we support our colleagues Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions for our colleagues as well. Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued. Aon values an innovative and inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Aon provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran, marital, domestic partner status, or other legally protected status. People with criminal histories are encouraged to apply. Job.CustomJobTypeName: Human Resources & Training, Operations & Policy Administration
Job.JobDescription:
We're seeking a Project Workers Compensation Administrator! This is an exciting opportunity to help manage complex workers' compensation programs supporting large-scale projects while partnering with project leadership, insurers, medical professionals, and legal teams to deliver positive claim outcomes and reduce organizational risk. *******This is a fully onsite role, working directly with the client at their Brownsville, TX location.******* Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. How this opportunity is different The Claims Administrator is responsible for implementing all aspects of the project workers’ compensation program (statutory and USL&H) for Rio Grande LNG Project and all Contractor Coordinated Insurance Program (CCIP) enrollees. This position will also assist with the administration of auto and other insured claims. The osition is located at the project construction site, in Brownsville, TX with an anticipated work schedule of 48 hours per week. While this is an Aon position, the employee is seconded to Bechtel. The Claims Administrator works under the direction of Bechtel's Head of Workers' Compensation and the Aon Claims Director, acting independently to manage routine matters while keeping Bechtel Insured Claims team fully informed at all stages. What the day will look like Communicates effectively with injured workers, medical professionals, insurers, brokers, internal/external counsel, corporate management, and various related regulatory agencies. Develops and maintains project-specific workers’ compensation claims manual, medical panel, related processes and procedures for statutory and USL&H claims. Implements improvements based on lessons learned, legislative changes or Court decisions, and Bechtel operating imperatives. Assists with subcontractor CCIP enrollment and provides workers’ compensation orientation to subcontractors. Develops and provides onsite training related to workers’ compensation. Under the guidance of the Workers’ Compensation Risk Manager, develops and prepares regular reports outlining project claims performance. Monitors claims activity to identify early negative claim trends or other issues that may negatively impact project performance. Is responsible for oversight and processing of workers’ compensation claims: Responsible for initiating, preparing, and maintaining all documentation associated with claims. Investigates and documents eligibility for workers’ compensation benefits and communicates same to insurer and related interested parties. Assists with investigation and coordination of issues surrounding subrogation. Interprets laws and regulations, determines appropriate courses of action, and presents solutions to resolve the claims. Identifies potential subrogation issues. Monitors claim resolution activities implemented by insurer(s) and employers. Maintains Project Risk Management Information System (RMIS). Directs and monitors the activities and performance of Bechtel’s insurance provider to ensure compliance with applicable regulations. Implements, monitors, and ensures compliance of “Special Account” requirements. Conducts regular claim reviews, claim audits and prepares related reports. Interfaces with insurer to effectively manage claims, including but not limited to authorizing claim reserve changes, authorizing insurer referral to outside counsel, and assessing and approving settlement strategies. Coordinates and supports early return to work. Manages relationships with onsite clinic, panel/network physicians and other medical providers, to ensure effective claims management and return to work. Works with injured worker and supervision on developing and implementing return to work plan. Assists in management fitness for duty and ADA accommodation issues as needed. Assists Bechtel Risk Management in the defense of litigation or other complex case support. (i.e., responding to interrogatories and other discovery requests). Assists with gathering information and filing auto and other insured claims. Assists with administration of auto and other insured claims as needed. Performs other tasks as required by Bechtel Risk Management. Skills and experience that will lead to success 5+ years of experience in the field or in a related area or in a related area. Extensive knowledge of / experience with workers’ compensation and occupational rehabilitation procedures, practices and processes. Extensive knowledge of claim’s resolution techniques and strategies, legal principles related to claim resolution and familiarity with all phases of the litigation process. Working knowledge of / experience with bodily injury and 1st and 3rd party property damage claims practices and processes. Working knowledge of / experience with auto and other insured claims practices and procedures. Relies on experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals. Highly skilled in written and verbal communication. Bilingual language proficiency (i.e., English and Spanish) is a plus. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of industry Workers’ Compensation experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $60,000 to $80,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. LI-JF1 #LI-Onsite 2589795

Job.JobDescription:
Aon is looking for an experienced Vice President, Risk Management (Affinity Healthcare) to own and advance risk management strategies and best practices for the organization’s internal and external clients. This person is accountable for identifying, evaluating and developing risk-related mitigation education and techniques to support Aon Affinity’s Healthcare Division business and clients of Aon Affinity’s Healthcare Division brands. The Vice President, Risk Management will manage a Senior Risk Consultant as well as a Junior Risk Consultant. The Vice President, Risk Management will collaborate with Aon Affinity’s Healthcare Division business leaders regarding professional liability insurance programs to plan, organize, and direct all aspects of risk management activities for internal and external clients that comply with state laws, regulations, standards of the profession, and accrediting and approval agencies. This position also manages the Business Continuity program. Manage content development of the team and 3rd party partners Prepare and present material Healthcare conferences and webinars. Manage/oversee 3rd party vendor relationships Create continuing education materials for healthcare’s various CE programs. Research, create, and manage ad hoc risk control content for internal and external partners. Analyze claims and legal implications to develop customized risk assessment tools for internal and external partners. Captive Client Leader | Aon Captive & Insurance Management (ACIM) Are you a client leader who turns strong relationships into long‑term strategic value? Do you thrive in complex client environments where success depends on judgment, influence, and cross‑functional collaboration? Join us to help clients make better captive and risk financing decisions! This is a hybrid role with the flexibility to work from our Burlington, Vermont office and from home in line with Aon’s U.S. smart working policy. This role must be based in Vermont. Candidates will need to already reside in the state or be willing to relocate. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like This role exists to strengthen client outcomes through consultative captive leadership. As a Captive Client Services Director, you will act as the principal interface between captive clients and Aon, ensuring clients receive high‑quality service, strategic insight, and access to the right expertise across the business. You will help clients make better decisions about captive performance, risk financing strategy, and long‑term value creation. Typical activities include: Leading strategic client engagement for a portfolio of captive clients, acting as the primary relationship lead for senior executives Running annual account planning discussions aligned to client priorities, service requirements, and commercial objectives Coordinating strategy check‑ins with subject matter experts to provide external perspectives, market insight, and forward‑looking recommendations Reviewing stewardship reports, performance data, and service metrics to find opportunities for improvement and additional value creation Orchestrating internal teams across domiciles, Global Capability Centres, and wider Aon businesses to deliver integrated client outcomes Finding opportunities to strengthen client relationships, improve account profitability, and expand relevant Aon services Translating technical, financial, and performance information into clear client narratives and actionable recommendations Coaching and supporting more junior colleagues to strengthen client leadership capability and consistency of service delivery Maintaining delivery discipline across service schedules, governance commitments, and regulatory requirements How this opportunity is different This role is differentiated by the level of client influence, strategic ownership, and cross‑functional coordination involved. You will operate as the central connector between captive clients and Aon, bringing together expertise from across the organization to support better client decisions and stronger long‑term partnerships. The role is shifting from transactional service delivery toward consultative client leadership. Success depends on your ability to deeply understand client priorities, proactively find opportunities, and build value through strategic conversations, insight‑led communication, and effective orchestration of Aon capabilities. You will help shape the future‑state client leadership model within ACIM, supporting a more proactive, data-driven, and commercially focused approach to client engagement. Skills and experience that will lead to success Demonstrated advisory client engagement, building deep understanding of client priorities, challenges, and risk financing objectives and operating as a trusted advisor Strong strategic and commercial thinking, connecting client strategies, commercial opportunities, and Aon capabilities to create measurable value and support profitable growth Confirmed ability to orchestrate expertise across a matrixed organization, influencing without formal authority and aligning teams around shared client objectives Track record of owning client service delivery, managing service schedules and stewardship activity, and maintaining high standards of execution and governance Excellent communication skills, with the ability to turn technical information, market insight, and performance data into compelling narratives for senior collaborators Comfort operating in ambiguous or evolving situations, with sound judgment, learning agility, and the ability to draw on specialist expertise when needed Experience leading, coaching, or mentoring colleagues to build capability and consistent client leadership standards across teams Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in business, finance, risk management, or a related field. How we support our colleagues In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions for our colleagues as well. Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share, and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued. Aon values an innovative and inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran, marital, domestic partner status, or other legally protected status. Broker I, National Casualty The National Casualty Practice is a premier team of casualty brokerage professionals with extensive experience in representing buyers of primary and umbrella/excess liability. We are looking to add a broker to our Primary Casualty team! We are considering applicants in Dallas and Houston, Texas! This is a hybrid role with at least three days a week in the office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. How this opportunity is different Our primary brokers are experts in their field and handle a variety of clients and program structures. You'll work closely with a diverse team of seasoned brokers, accounts executives, and risk analysts, each bringing a wealth of knowledge and experience to the table. This position offers you a unique opportunity to develop professionally, expand your expertise, and make an impact in the world of primary casualty. Thank you for your time and consideration. What the day will look like Thorough analysis of current risk transfer programs to include coverage and cost analysis and a graphical representation of the program. Insurance program structure planning and design of alternatives. Provide benchmarking analysis related to limits and coverage terms. Prepare all marketplace insurance submissions, coordinate and conduct market meetings and negotiations as appropriate in coordination with Account Executives. May include some travel. Finalize all quotes and complete a thorough comparison of program options as part of the client proposal presentation. Comparison to include changes in exposures, losses, collateral, coverage terms and conditions and cost of risk. Serve as a primary or secondary market contact as assigned and in accordance with established policy. As part of a team, you are expected to educate and advise fellow team members on coverage issues, markets, and related developments. Serve as team member for Aon’s broking library and periodically contribute to the library and related best practices. Skills and experience that will lead to success Casualty broker with 2+ years of experience working in primary placements and/or in casualty. Will be asked to work directly with clients as lead broker or secondary broker to build primary casualty programs, as well as participate on new business opportunities. Attention to detail, ability to multi-task, exceptional organizational skills, ability to make and communicate difficult decisions. An experienced primary casualty broker or underwriter with a solid understanding of and relationships with insurance company management and underwriting teams/personnel. Strong written and communication skills necessary to communicate in a professional manner with clients and the marketplace. A strong team player who understands the roles and responsibilities of other Aon professionals on the team, assumes responsibility for the timely delivery of a professional work product in accordance with assigned roles, and facilitates communication among team members. Promote creativity in presenting new ideas and approaches for clients or prospects; promote a positive attitude in always trying to improve a program. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of industry experience. Property and Casualty Brokers License is required (can be attained on the job) For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. We are seeking a Senior Managing Director OR Managing Director to join our Actuarial Consulting team, with a particular focus on strategic and actuarial analyses for insurance and reinsurance clients and on building and scaling differentiated service offerings. Drive complex, consultative sales processes from opportunity identification through proposal, structuring, and closing. Leverage internal and external networks to build a high‑quality pipeline of opportunities and drive revenue growth. Ensure high‑quality, timely delivery and a consistent client experience across engagements and geographies. Serve as a trusted advisor in key meetings and workshops, including leading technical and strategic discussions with executives, regulators, boards, and other stakeholders. Mentor and develop team members, helping them grow consultative skills, solution‑building capability, and commercial acumen. Champion an environment of continuous improvement, innovation, and learning across the actuarial consulting team. Background and credentials FCAS (or equivalent casualty actuarial credential) required. Typically 15+ years of experience in an analytics‑centric environment, preferably in property/casualty insurance, reinsurance, or actuarial consulting. Demonstrated track record leading complex actuarial and strategic engagements for insurance or reinsurance clients. Familiarity with R, Python, SQL or similar analytics tools preferred; strong proficiency in MS Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint, required. Job.JobTitle: Assistant Vice President – Intellectual Property Insurance Broker
Job.JobDescription:
Assistant Vice President – Intellectual Property Insurance Broker Are you seeking an opportunity to be a part of our growing, full-service IP Risk Solutions team by brokering strategic approaches to Intellectual Property policies? Join our industry leading IP Broking team! This is a hybrid role to work from our Chicago, IL office. Aon is in the business of better decisions. At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like. Demonstrate detailed knowledge of the Intellectual Property insurance marketplace and our team’s offerings. Demonstrate ability to place a layered program ($50M+) from start to finish. You will have direct communication with executive level client contacts (C-Suite). Own all aspects of client service for your assigned book of business and new business opportunities in coordination with other team members and by using the deal flow process; optimally connect with other team members and administrative staff to ensure accurate prioritization of workflow. Apply effective negotiation skills to improve broking results for clients. Use data, own experience, others’ perspectives, and a clear methodology improve client programs and build opportunities with prospective client programs. Work in an Aon United fashion to cross-sell IP Risk products and services. Successfully apply the claims and legal advocacy group for claim administration and counsel to assist with claim resolution. Apply effective underwriter relationships to improve broking results. Proactively develop and complete a pipeline strategy for new business. Function as a mentor to more junior team members Drive utilization of all available technology throughout broking process and client service process Understand the causes of E&O and avoid and adopt practices to reduce exposure. How this opportunity is different This is a unique opportunity to be a part of a growing, fast-paced insurance space. An estimated 80% of the value of the S&P 500 is derived from company’s intellectual property, yet most companies are not yet insuring against their intellectual property risks. Aon’s IP team is educating companies (both current clients and prospective clients) about their IP risks and how the surrounding insurance marketplace can help them to manage their risks. The Aon IP team is experienced, yet still small, so operates with a “start-up” environment and feel. Personal autonomy is highly encouraged and self-motivated individuals will find an opportunity to quickly advance their career. Skills and experience that will lead to success. REQUIRED: 4+ years of years in brokering and/or underwriting experience within IP, Cyber, E&O, D&O, or other Financial/Professional lines. Project Management - Experienced Report Writing - Experienced Insurance Strategies - Advanced Retail Brokerage - Advanced Team Management - Advanced Performance Management (PM) - Experienced Business Development - Experienced Conflict Resolution - Experienced Organizational Leadership - Experienced Customer Relationship Management (CRM) - Experienced Stakeholder Management - Experienced Account Management - Advanced Documentations - Experienced Talent Management - Experienced Team Development - Advanced OPTIONAL: Financial Planning - Advanced Business Planning - Experienced Training and Development - Experienced Market Research - Experienced Strategic Planning - Experienced Policy Development - Experienced Data Analysis - Experienced Organizational Strategy - Experienced Process Improvements - Intermediate Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience. Ability to obtain/maintain P&C license within 120 days of hire. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $120,000 to $190,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. The salary range reflected is based on a primary work location of Illinois. The actual salary may vary for applicants in a different geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-HYBRID #LI-KA1 2588743

This individual is accountable for acting as the AGCN representative for the local office or region on new business opportunities and any training needs for internal and external clients. How this opportunity is different This individual leads by example as a strong supporter of Aon’s values; Committing to acting as One Firm; United as one diverse and inclusive team; Passionate about making colleagues and clients successful. Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Sales Manager, Insurance Sales, Insurance Sales Representative
Job.JobDescription:
Resident Sales Director, Northern California Are you looking to drive growth across Aon’s various solution lines? Can you develop and lead a team to meet revenue goals? If you are looking to take the next step in your career, this is the role for you! Aon is in the business of better decisions As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like As part of a leading team in the industry, you will provide creative and successful solutions within our sales group. This will help drive impactful outcomes for our clients. As a Resident Sales Director, you will report directly to the Northern California Market Leader and will have direct reports in the Northern California office. Drive growth: Achieve or exceed the quarterly and annual new business revenue goals set for the office. Lead all aspects of crafting and carrying out direct reports, personal and other revenue producing colleagues go to market plans and sales goals. Build and maintain a sales-focused culture across the state’s personnel. Support the execution of the National Sales and Marketing platform and initiatives. Mentor and develop, problem-solve and strategize with the office’s producers, Account Executives, and broking and solutions line leaders to build, develop and close specific revenue opportunities. Educate producers, Account Executives, and broking leaders on new products, approaches, services and solutions and Aon’s capabilities and thought leadership with training on the segment or client applicability and recommend dialoguing with clients and prospects. Work with the risk and health leader to ensure that the office’s clients and prospects receive regular written communication applicable to their business(es), exposures and needs. Build, tailor and/or implement email campaigns, mailings, seminars, webinars, seminars, roundtables, and Forums to drive revenue opportunities tailored to the office’s new business priorities and market area(s). Proactively and consistently communicate and meet with clients, prospects, insurers, and competitors to maintain a current knowledge of talent in the office’s market area(s). Maintain an accurate pipeline of new business results for confident revenue forecasting and helpful sales metric analysis. Supervise and assess ongoing new business results and related pipeline activity across the office’s personnel and promptly anticipate and address negative new business variances or trends and/or activity issues. Maintain a fair marketplace in terms of prospect allocation across the office and firm’s resources and follow protocols for pipeline documentation and production credit disputes. Recruit and present your recommendation and business plan for the best business development personnel (producers, Account Executives, and support personnel to enable others to produce more) for the market area’s needs. Onboard business developers with a clear understanding of their role and responsibilities and specified sales goals, and training on Aon Connect, Aon’s office, national and global resources, and systems. Identify and champion focus centers of influence in the accounting, legal, financial, and other segments of the business community in the office’s market areas for office-wide teamwork.
