Job.JobDescription:
We're seeking a Project Workers Compensation Administrator! This is an exciting opportunity to help manage complex workers' compensation programs supporting large-scale projects while partnering with project leadership, insurers, medical professionals, and legal teams to deliver positive claim outcomes and reduce organizational risk. *******This is a fully onsite role, working directly with the client at their Cameron, LA location.******* Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. How this opportunity is different The Claims Administrator is responsible for implementing all aspects of the project workers’ compensation program (statutory and USL&H) for Sabine Pass LNG Project and all Contractor Coordinated Insurance Program (CCIP) enrollees. This position will also assist with the administration of auto and other insured claims. Position is located at the project construction site, in Cameron, LA with an anticipated work schedule of 48 hours per week. While this is an Aon position, the employee is seconded to Bechtel. The Claims Administrator works under the direction of Bechtel's Head of Workers' Compensation and the Aon Claims Director, acting independently to manage routine matters while keeping Bechtel Insured Claims team fully informed at all stages. What the day will look like Communicates effectively with injured workers, medical professionals, insurers, brokers, internal/external counsel, corporate management, and various related regulatory agencies. Develops and maintains project-specific workers’ compensation claims manual, medical panel, related processes and procedures for statutory and USL&H claims. Implements improvements based on lessons learned, legislative changes or Court decisions, and Bechtel operating imperatives. Assists with subcontractor CCIP enrollment and provides workers’ compensation orientation to subcontractors. Develops and provides onsite training related to workers’ compensation. Under the guidance of the Workers’ Compensation Risk Manager, develops and prepares regular reports outlining project claims performance. Monitors claims activity to identify early negative claim trends or other issues that may negatively impact project performance. Is responsible for oversight and processing of workers’ compensation claims: Responsible for initiating, preparing, and maintaining all documentation associated with claims. Investigates and documents eligibility for workers’ compensation benefits and communicates same to insurer and related interested parties. Assists with investigation and coordination of issues surrounding subrogation. Interprets laws and regulations, determines appropriate courses of action, and presents solutions to resolve the claims. Identifies potential subrogation issues. Monitors claim resolution activities implemented by insurer(s) and employers. Maintains Project Risk Management Information System (RMIS). Directs and monitors the activities and performance of Bechtel’s insurance provider to ensure compliance with applicable regulations. Implements, monitors, and ensures compliance of “Special Account” requirements. Conducts regular claim reviews, claim audits and prepares related reports. Interfaces with insurer to effectively manage claims, including but not limited to authorizing claim reserve changes, authorizing insurer referral to outside counsel, and assessing and approving settlement strategies. Coordinates and supports early return to work. Manages relationships with onsite clinic, panel/network physicians and other medical providers, to ensure effective claims management and return to work. Works with injured worker and supervision on developing and implementing return to work plan. Assists in management fitness for duty and ADA accommodation issues as needed. Assists Bechtel Risk Management in the defense of litigation or other complex case support. (i.e., responding to interrogatories and other discovery requests). Assists with gathering information and filing auto and other insured claims. Assists with administration of auto and other insured claims as needed. Performs other tasks as required by Bechtel Risk Management. Skills and experience that will lead to success 5+ years of experience in the field or in a related area or in a related area. Extensive knowledge of / experience with workers’ compensation and occupational rehabilitation procedures, practices and processes. Extensive knowledge of claim’s resolution techniques and strategies, legal principles related to claim resolution and familiarity with all phases of the litigation process. Working knowledge of / experience with bodily injury and 1st and 3rd party property damage claims practices and processes. Working knowledge of / experience with auto and other insured claims practices and procedures. Relies on experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals. Highly skilled in written and verbal communication. Bilingual language proficiency (i.e., English and Spanish) is a plus. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of industry Workers’ Compensation experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $60,000 to $80,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. LI-JF1 #LI-Onsite 2589798

Partner, Enterprise Rewards We are seeking a senior, client-facing Partner, Enterprise Rewards to lead complex, enterprise-wide rewards transformations for some of the world’s most sophisticated organizations. This role offers the opportunity to combine deep rewards expertise with strategic advisory capabilities and strong commercial acumen to drive meaningful client impact and business growth! Locations: Atlanta, GA; Chicago, IL; New York, NY; Philadelphia, PA; San Francisco, CA; Washington, D.C. (Hybrid) Role Overview As a Partner, you will serve as a trusted advisor to executive leadership, working closely with CHROs, CFOs, and business leaders to address critical workforce and talent challenges. You will play a central role in crafting and delivering coordinated rewards and workforce strategies that align with business priorities and help organizations attract, retain, and empower talent in an increasingly competitive environment. Key Responsibilities A key focus of this role is business development and market leadership. You will originate and close new opportunities with large, multinational clients while expanding existing relationships. Success requires the ability to quickly establish credibility, translate sophisticated challenges into actionable solutions, and position innovative offerings in the market. You will contribute to go-to-market strategy, develop thought leadership, and champion a highly collaborative, cross-solution approach across Human Capital and Risk. As a steward of our Aon United model, you will connect clients to the full breadth of capabilities to deliver integrated, differentiated outcomes. In parallel, you will lead large, complex client engagements spanning multiple geographies and workstreams. These engagements require strong program leadership, coordination across multidisciplinary teams, and a commitment to delivery excellence. Your work will include the design and implementation of global job architecture and career frameworks, position profiles, job evaluation, and market benchmarking. You will advise clients on pay competitiveness and help design data-driven compensation structures aligned to market conditions and internal equity. You will also lead the development of base pay structures and incentive programs, including the design and alignment of short- and long-term incentives. In doing so, you will balance strategic objectives with governance, regulatory, and operational considerations. Your work will extend to rewards governance design and the integration of reward programs into HR systems and broader technology platforms to ensure sustainability and scalability. Beyond traditional rewards, you will contribute to broader enterprise transformation initiatives, helping clients develop forward-looking roadmaps that align rewards with talent and workforce strategies, including organizational design, operating model evolution, and the transition toward skills-based organizations. You will advise on emerging topics such as AI-enabled workforce strategies, job and skills design, talent assessment, and workforce planning. The role also includes supporting clients in using people analytics and advancing pay transparency and pay equity strategies—critical components of modern, high-performing and equitable organizations. As a senior leader, you will guide and inspire large, cross-geography teams, building strong internal networks and fostering collaboration across teams. You will play a key role in developing talent within the practice, mentoring team members, and reinforcing a culture of excellence, inclusion, and client focus. The ideal candidate brings extensive experience in human capital consulting, with deep expertise in rewards and total rewards strategy, and a proven track record of leading multifaceted global engagements and driving business growth. You will demonstrate strong executive presence, critical thinking, and skill in influencing senior collaborators in complex environments. Commercial acumen, combined with the ability to lead through ambiguity and deliver results, is essential. This role offers the chance to work at the forefront of enterprise rewards and workforce transformation. You will work in a highly collaborative environment with the platform and resources to make a significant impact with clients and in the market. Qualifications and Skills Extensive experience in total rewards consulting or senior in-house rewards leadership within large, complex, or global organizations. You have a proven track record advising C-suite and Boards. Demonstrated success originating, leading, and closing complex, multi‑year consulting engagements and consistently meeting or exceeding revenue and growth targets with enterprise‑scale clients. Deep expertise in global total rewards strategy, program development, analytics, and governance, including experience with large‑scale employee‑focused research and survey methodologies. Strong quantitative, analytical, and commercial skills, with the ability to translate complex data and modeling into clear, enterprise‑relevant narratives and arguments. Outstanding relationship management, communication, and influencing skills, with demonstrated ability to navigate complex collaborator environments, including global and regional leadership teams. Established skill in directing international, diverse teams, handling several major projects simultaneously, and providing excellent outcomes in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $275,000 to $315,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. The salary range reflected is based on a primary work location of Chicago, IL. The actual salary may vary for applicants in a different geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance. This role does not accrue vacation. Rather, this role is eligible to take paid time off at the discretion of the employee and management in accordance with company policy and practices. Various other types of leaves of absence; paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-MB1 #LI-HYBRID 2026-101934

Are you looking to be a member of an industry-leading team? Do you want to deliver innovative and effective solutions to clients in the healthcare industry? If you said yes, then apply to join our Account Executive team in Florida! As an Account Executive, you will handle predominantly strategic risk and healthcare clients, including health systems, hospitals, physician groups, and other health care organizations. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like: Retains and grows Aon’s business, cultivating relationships with senior-most client decision-makers in the client organization as well as with day-to-day client contacts. Drives the renewal process, assembling the appropriate team to develop and implement the client-specific renewal strategy. Coordinates with Brokers in the development and delivery of renewal strategies. Facilitates critical relationships between clients, ARS and insurers. Ensures client service team understanding of client needs, service delivery methods, and the economic framework relevant to services delivered. Leads stewardship planning and delivery Ensures overall account profitability with a value-based approach for the scope of service and costs associated with the Client Promise Plan. Arranges Aon compensation for services, whether fee or commission-based, accordingly. Educates clients in risk management, risk transfer, market issues and relevant trends including appropriate benchmarking and GRIP data. Marshals appropriate Aon resources to support clients in unusual circumstances such as large claims, etc. Involves others across geographic (including international), functional and business unit boundaries to define interdependent responses to opportunities to grow the business. Manages input to and follow-up on invoicing and receivables process for assigned clients, ensuring timely collections. How this opportunity is different: We are looking for a leader who is responsible for the day-to-day, account management of Aon’s relationships with assigned clients as their primary role. You will lead client service teams to identify and meet client needs and thereby retain and grow a profitable book of business. Through service, pricing, consultation and reporting, you will promote the value Aon delivers to clients. Experience Must have a minimum of 5 - 7 years of appropriate risk insurance experience coupled with account management experience Background working with healthcare clients (such as hospitals, health systems, physician groups, or other healthcare organizations). Able to handle large, sophisticated, multi-national clients Able to lead a book of business of at least $2.5 Million - $3 Million in annual revenue Strong sales skills Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite products such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook Must have an active Property & Casualty license. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of industry experience. The salary range for this position is $125,500 - $163,200. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive production incentives in addition to base salary. The amount of any production incentives varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. How we support our colleagues Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions for our colleagues as well. Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. Are you a Technology Leader in AI Architecture/Delivery with deep experience architecting enterprise scale delivery of Agentic workflows and AI Platforms for Data Ingestion? This could be a superb opportunity to explore! Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world! As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like As the Director for Aon's Ai Architecture/Delivery for Agentic and AI Platforms, you will be part of a global AI Architecture center of excellence. Spanning public and private cloud, helping to define and support the services, processes, and technology platforms that teams across Aon can leverage in an autonomous, governed, and secure way. We are looking for an expert technical architecture leader with a strong, self-directed work ethic who can partner with global teams to establish and evolve enterprise standards. Also reference architectures, and patterns for Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning and cloud-based data services. This will ultimately enable Aon to deliver greater value and insight to its clients. Responsibilities: Provide strategic leadership for the design and evolution of enterprise-wide AI and ML architectures that address key business and client needs. Define, refine, and communicate the organization’s AI and innovation strategy, ensuring clear alignment with business objectives, risk appetite, and regulatory requirements. Own and govern innovation frameworks, including AI sandboxes, labs, and experimentation platforms—particularly for generative AI—ensuring they are scalable, reliable, secure, and compliant. Own the creation and implementation of generative AI solutions and AI-enabled data products, setting standards and patterns that can be reused across business units. Partner with senior technology, data, business leaders to integrate AI and data products into existing platforms, workflows, and client-facing solutions, driving measurable business outcomes. Establish and maintain reference architectures, guardrails, and standard methodologies for AI/ML, MLOps, DataOps, and experimentation at enterprise scale. Guide and mentor architecture, engineering, and data science teams. Help to build organizational capability in AI and advanced analytics. Stay ahead of the latest advancements in AI, machine learning, and data technologies. Proactively translate these developments into actionable roadmaps and investment recommendations. Skills and experience that will lead to success 8 or more years of demonstrated ability across technology domains such as software development, cloud computing, systems engineering, and data and AI, with a focus on architecture and strategy. Deep expertise in one or more AI subdomains, such as natural language processing, generative AI, recommendation systems, or computer vision. Experience architecting and deploying large-scale solutions on major cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud). Solid understanding of AI architecture and trends. Experience designing sophisticated integrations across cloud platforms, SaaS applications, APIs, headless, composable and enterprise systems. Knowledge of modern architecture patterns including cloud-native, composable architecture, microservices, event-driven design, and API-first development. Experience leading large-scale technology modernization and digital transformation initiatives. Experience leading architecture reviews, governance forums, and long-term planning activities. Strong collaborator management and relationship-building skills. Ability to influence technology and business leaders without direct authority. Exceptional communication and presentation skills with executive audiences. Proven track record of leading and delivering enterprise-wide AI or ML programs across multiple business units in large, complex organizations. Demonstrated experience defining and governing AI/ML platforms, reference architectures, and standards in a hybrid or multi-cloud environment. Hands-on experience with AI/ML frameworks and platforms such as Amazon SageMaker, Google Cloud Vertex AI, TensorFlow, PyTorch, or similar. Experience with vector databases and graph technologies, and their application in modern AI/ML and knowledge-graph use cases. Hands-on experience designing and orchestrating multi-agent systems and agentic workflows using frameworks such as LangGraph, Google Agentic Framework, or similar. Deep understanding of agentic orchestration patterns, This includes planning and task decomposition, tool and function calling, memory and context management, human-in-the-loop controls, and agent-to-agent communication using emerging standards such as Model Context Protocol (MCP). Experience crafting enterprise workflow automation that integrates AI agents with APIs, event-driven services, and business process platforms, with built-in observability, evaluation, guardrails, and auditability to keep agentic workflows reliable, controlled, and protected. Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field. Job.JobTitle: North America Technology Industry Practice Leader
Job.JobDescription:
Aon is seeking a senior Technology industry leader to develop and advance our Technology client strategy across North America. This opportunity suits an experienced executive who brings deep industry insight, strong market relationships, and a consistent record of driving growth through trusted client partnerships. As the North America Technology Industry Leader, you will be a visible ambassador for Aon in the Technology sector - recognized externally for your point of view and internally for your leadership. You will work closely with senior clients, colleagues, and global counterparts. You will support business expansion, strengthen client retention, and elevate Aon’s position as a leading advisor to Technology companies. Success in this role will be measured by steady business development, expansion and retention of key client relationships, and sustained market impact. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Market & Revenue Leadership Lead Aon’s Technology industry growth strategy across North America, with accountability for measurable revenue outcomes. Drive expansion and retention of key client relationships by delivering differentiated insights and solutions tailored to the Technology sector. Partner with regional and national leaders to support sophisticated sales opportunities, major renewals, and strategic pursuits. Collaborate across Aon’s capabilities to bring combined, cross-disciplinary solutions to Technology clients. Industry Engagement & Thought Leadership Serve as a recognized leader in the Technology industry, with a strong external profile among clients, prospects, and industry leaders. Lead and participate in industry forums, executive roundtables, conferences, and client events. Develop and share forward-looking perspectives on trends, risks, and opportunities shaping the Technology sector. Contribute to white papers, executive briefings, and other market-facing content that strengthens Aon’s industry reputation. Stay closely connected to Aon’s global Technology community to ensure alignment and leverage global insights for North America clients. Client & Colleague Impact Act as a trusted advisor to senior client executives, bringing informed, strategic perspectives to their most important business challenges. Support colleagues across markets and regions by sharing industry knowledge and helping teams deliver outstanding client experiences. Play a visible role in firmwide initiatives that advance Aon’s Technology strategy and long-term growth objectives. Talent & Culture Attract, engage, and develop a strong community of Technology-focused leaders and colleagues from various backgrounds. Develop a culture of teamwork, inclusion, and continuous learning. Serve as a role model and mentor, helping others grow their industry expertise and client impact. Skills and experience that will lead to success 10+ years of experience in the Technology industry, with proven success in senior leadership, client engagement, and business growth. Established network of senior Technology executives and industry leaders. Proven track record to influence at the executive level and serve as a trusted advisor to sophisticated organizations. Strong commercial savvy, strategic approach, and executive presence. Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree or equivalent experience preferred. Job.JobTitle: Experienced Associate - Health and Benefits Strategy
Job.JobDescription:
Experienced Associate, Strategy Consulting, Health and Benefits This is a hybrid role with the flexibility to work both virtually and from our New York City, Atlanta, GA, or Chicago, IL office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we build decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Aon’s Life, Health & Benefits Strategy Consulting team, part of Aon Advisory, is hiring an Experienced Strategy Associate. We work with many of the most prestigious companies across the global life, health and benefits, property & casualty, insurtech, and (re)insurance markets. Leveraging Aon’s proprietary data and global network of experts, we help clients navigate a fast‑changing environment and turn insights into practical strategies and tangible business results. As an Experienced Associate, you will work in a client-facing role alongside Client Leaders, Project Managers, and Aon leadership. You will support and lead project workstreams that deliver business-focused initiatives and strategic recommendations. This will include understanding client objectives, evaluating business challenges, conducting business and market analysis, assessing risk, and defining strategies that build growth opportunities and competitive advantages. As a Strategy Associate, you will be a key member of high‑impact project teams, helping clients address their most important strategic questions. You will: Support end‑to‑end client engagements, from defining strategic questions to delivering and implementing recommendations Perform quantitative and financial analyses to evaluate markets, products, segments, and growth opportunities Conduct market and competitor research across life, health & benefits, and insurtech to inform client strategies Use Aon’s proprietary data and market intelligence to uncover trends and derive insights into sources of competitive advantage Translate complex analyses into clear, compelling client materials (PowerPoint, Excel, written reports, white papers) Participate in client interviews, workshops, and discovery sessions with Aon subject matter experts Help synthesize findings, identify key insights, and shape storylines and strategic recommendations Contribute to proposals, marketing materials, and thought leadership to support business development Support internal initiatives for Aon Advisory, including recruiting, marketing, communications, and practice operations You bring knowledge and expertise Characteristics of an ideal candidate: Strong analytical abilities and comfort with data analysis and financial modeling, with a track record of academic and/or professional achievement Excellent communication skills – you can turn complex analyses into simple, compelling stories in both written and verbal formats Curiosity about how insurance, health and benefits, and insurtech are evolving – and a desire to help clients navigate that change Ability to manage multiple workstreams, prioritize effectively, and deliver high‑quality work under tight deadlines Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build relationships with colleagues and clients at all levels Proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint and Excel Willingness to travel up to 20% for client and internal meetings, depending on project needs Experience with analytics tools such as Alteryx, Power BI, or similar data analytics platforms preferred Prior exposure to life, health & benefits, (re)insurance, or insurtech markets preferred Education and experience Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Risk Management, Insurance, Finance, Business Administration, Data Analytics, Economics, or a closely related field, or a comparable mix of education and pertinent industry experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $60,000 to $90,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-AR1 #LI-HYBRID 2588506

Job.JobDescription:
Aon's Private Risk Management Group is hiring for a Private Client-Account Executive/Broker Specialist. This is a virtual position, with preference based out of the state of Texas. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like: Supports the Account Executives by working to build, expand, and solidify relationships with existing clients and prospective clients. Assists in leading appropriate resources to address the client/prospective client’s risk needs, thereby assisting in the retention and growth of a profitable book of business. Promotes the value that Aon delivers to clients through superior service, pricing, consultation and reporting. Assist with new business and remarketing of personal insurance programs for current clients. Updating applications within our agency management system, quoting online with insurers and completing coverage comparisons or proposals for the Account Executives in Word and Excel. Prepare and input summary of coverages for Account Executive’s review. Manage a small book of assigned clients. Assist with conducting annual reviews for clients. Process changes and endorsements within 48 hours of receipt. Respond to client issues as directed by the Account Executive. The time service standard: returning a phone call within 24 hours and responding to email by the end of the day. Assist the Account Executive with complex claim activity, including contacting claims adjusters when necessary. Assisting the Account Executive with client billing issues – including contacting the carrier and/or internal accounting team to coordinate, track, resolve billing / payment issues. Build and maintain important working relationships with insurers, clients, referral sources and colleagues through regular contact and interaction. Access carrier websites / systems to process changes, retrieve documents and information as required. Aon's Private Risk Management Group is hiring for a Private Client-Account Executive/Broker Specialist. This is a virtual position, with preference based out of the state of Texas. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. Job.JobTitle: Korea Global Solutions - U.S. Account Executive I
Job.JobDescription:
Korea Global Solutions - U.S. Account Executive I Aon has an established network of Aon Korea Global Solutions (AKGS) desks that source and service investments and projects from Korean entities worldwide. This role is a hybrid role working from our New York, NY office. The network demonstrates desks in Asia-Pacific, EMEA, and the Americas. Each desk has three primary objectives: Leading development and servicing of Korean overseas business opportunities that emerge within a defined geography. Working with Aon Korea to progress opportunities emanating out of Korea. Acting as local “ambassadors” to facilitate visits by project sponsors and investors visiting from Korea. Each desk, while reporting to the local leadership and historically working quite independently, is now expected to work much more closely together and with AKGS Global Leaders. The Korea Global Solutions – USA will be an Account Executive, reporting through the Korea Global Solutions Team, and shall be a strong communicator, influencer, and team leader, with extensive business experience and exposure to Korean business environment. Insurance knowledge would be a notable advantage. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Strategic Client Engagement Serve as a resource for global client teams and account management on Korean client relationships / prospects Work closely with Aon Korea, Aon resources and wider Korea Global Solutions (KGS) network to develop Korea outbound business strategy, account management and alignment Act as a senior advisor on strategic Korean multinational client relationships on a global basis, including ECG accounts Provide leadership strategy in managing global client relationships across all aspects of Korean MNC clients Coordinate and lead global Client Planning process on select accounts to find opportunities across solution line and geography, on a global scale Direct involvement supporting and driving Enterprise Client Group (ECG) strategy for select Korean multinationals, working with Enterprise Client Leaders Help colleagues expand their professional knowledge for clients and utilize Aon resources and product solution lines. Growth Strategy Implementation Work with Market & Regional Leaders to implement growth strategies that increase KGS revenue Extend KGS position in all Aon global geographies and work with solution line colleagues to better engage Korean multinationals with Aon product and solution offerings Promote the Aon brand through initiated marketing events and on social platforms Understand and track the growth of the KGS business globally to support the budget process and ensure timely hiring to progress targets Leadership Build trusted relationships with the leadership of Korea, Risk Capital and Human Capital and Enterprise Client Group that facilitates and encourages collaboration and Aon United opportunities May manage talent at a Regional level, hiring within a regional framework, setting career paths, and developing expertise Build high performing teams, developing HiPo talent and address the gaps in expertise How this opportunity is different Act as the ambassador of AKGS and contribute actively to the development of AKGS brand globally Compile and maintain a global sales pipeline in partnership with Aon Korea and all AKGS Desks Support multi-country sales/service processes by coordinating with relevant AKGS desks, resources in Aon Korea, Enterprise Client Group and other Aon units Suggest and implement processes and mechanism for further communication and collaboration among all AKGS Desks, Aon Korea, and other relevant Aon units Actively facilitate the flow of market intelligence among different AKGS desks and Aon Korea Present the best Aon solutions to clients with Aon’s overall best interest in mind Skills and experience that will lead to success Strong command of both Korean and English language in business and bi-cultural context 5+ years of experience in leading and handling client relationships that grow and develop into key business relationships and account management experience Successfully implemented growth plans and budget for client portfolio, contributing to the annual planning cycle Ability to work collaboratively with Aon partners to effectively prospect for and acquire new clients, resulting in revenue growth Built inclusive teams, fosters an environment in which all employees are valued and heard Multi-culturally aware and able to influence and build strong C-level relationships across borders Motivates and inspires others, creating an environment for continuous learning and connection Insurance experience preferred Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of industry experience For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $110,000 ~ $125,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. The salary range reflected is based on a primary work location of New York. The actual salary may vary for applicants in a different geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-KA1 #LI-HYBRID 2590399

Job.JobTitle: Assistant Vice President, Health Analytics Data Scientist
Job.JobDescription:
Aon is looking for an Assistant Vice President, Health Analytics Data Scientist Chicago, IL; Atlanta, GA; Denver, CO; Seattle, WA are preferrable locations but open to other Aon locations or possibly remote for the right fit We are seeking a hands-on, statistically grounded health data scientist, health actuary or medical economics expert to work on cost-of-care measurement, causal inference and predictive modeling workstreams and development of Aon analytics capabilities. You will own the design, validation, documentation, and delivery of the statistical and machine learning / predictive modeling algorithms and analyses that help employers and their partners understand cost, risk, and the impact of health programs – including total-cost-of-care predictive modeling and causal evaluations of programs and vendors using matched cohort trial emulation, difference-in-differences, and risk adjustment. You will work to evolve capabilities and model performance, review code and models, document and present results to clients and senior leaders, and take models from development into governed, monitored production, working closely with actuaries, consultants, clinical and innovation specialists, Aon Business Solutions / Technology (ABS), technology architects, and engineering teams. The ideal candidate has 7+ years of experience including commercial health insurance and/or health benefits consulting, a strong foundation in applied statistics and causal inference, and a track record of building and deploying tabular predictive models on large medical and pharmacy claims datasets. The ability to document methods rigorously and present results clearly to technical and non-technical audiences is critical. Practical experience with MLOps and model governance, and with partnering with enterprise technology and distributed engineering teams to move models into scalable, supported production, is essential. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Develop and deliver causal inference and predictive modeling workstreams for the US Health Analytics practice, ensuring methodological rigor while staying hands-on in building, reviewing, and validating models and code within project timelines Collaborate closely with Aon Business Solutions / Technology (ABS), cloud architects, and offshore engineering and data science teams to align on data pipelines, model architecture, and deployment standards, coordinate delivery across locations and time zones, and move models from development into scalable, supported production Design, build, and tune tabular analyses and predictive models including gradient-boosted, statistical methods and emerging AI modeling techniques– such as cost and utilization forecasting, high-cost claimant prediction, risk stratification, and program engagement propensity – on large eligibility, medical claims, and pharmacy claims datasets from multiple sources Design and execute medical economics and causal inference studies that estimate the impact of programs, treatments, vendors, and point solutions on financial, utilization, and clinical outcomes, using matched cohort target trial emulation (explicit eligibility, time zero, and follow-up definitions; propensity score matching or weighting), difference-in-differences and event-study designs with parallel-trends and sensitivity testing, and risk adjustment Document methods, assumptions, data definitions, and results thoroughly – methodology write-ups, technical appendices, model cards, and reproducible analysis records – and present findings, uncertainty, and limitations clearly to clients, carriers, consultants, and senior leaders through polished reports and presentations Ensure MLOps and model governance end-to-end, including experiment tracking, model registries, reproducible training pipelines, automated testing, CI/CD, drift and performance monitoring, and model documentation, validation, and approval workflows aligned with Aon’s risk, privacy, and compliance standards Serve as senior technical, code, and methodology reviewer for analytics deliverables, and set standards for model validation, explainability, bias and fairness review, and quality control Partner with senior leaders across Aon’s health actuarial, consulting, clinical, innovation, and specialty practice areas, and stay current on emerging vendors and startups in healthcare navigation, digital health, and care delivery Mentor and coach data scientists, and lead multiple projects with clear priorities, timelines, and milestones Skills and experience that will lead to success Minimum 7 years of total experience, including health insurance, with a track record of delivering value to clients and colleagues Strong foundation in applied statistics or medical economics, including model training and validation, statistical testing, regression and generalized linear models, and experimental and quasi-experimental design Deep hands-on experience building, tuning, and interpreting tabular predictive models, including feature engineering, cross-validation, hyperparameter optimization, calibration, class imbalance, and explainability methods Hands-on experience applying causal inference to observational health data / medical economics, including matched cohort target trial emulation, propensity score methods, difference-in-differences (including staggered-adoption and event-study approaches), sensitivity analysis, and risk adjustment, with financial, utilization, and clinical outcomes metrics Detailed understanding of US health data, including eligibility, medical and pharmacy claims, and coding standards such as ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS, CPT, DRG, and related industry standards Experience with MLOps and model governance – such as MLflow or similar tooling, model registries, automated training and scoring pipelines, version control, drift and performance monitoring, and model risk documentation and review Experience partnering with enterprise technology and architecture teams and working with offshore or distributed engineering teams to deploy and support models in production Expert Python and/or R and strong SQL; Databricks, Spark, Azure, Docker, and CI/CD experience a plus High-performing individual contributor who can mentor junior data scientists and work independently across multiple projects Excellent written and verbal communication, with a track record of documenting methods and assumptions clearly and presenting statistical results, uncertainty, and limitations to actuaries, consultants, clients, and non-technical audiences Education: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in statistics, biostatistics, mathematics, economics, health services / public health research, data science, computer science, actuarial science, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent professional experience; advanced degrees are a plus For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $160,000 to $190,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-HP1 #LI-HYBRID #LI-REMOTE 2585949

Are you an experienced construction claims professional who understands the challenges encountered by general contractors? Do you have hands-on experience with construction-related general liability insurance claims, job-site accidents, risk transfer, coverage analysis, construction defect cases, and litigated matters? This is a remote-based role with the flexibility to work virtually or from an Aon office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like As a Construction Claim Advocate, you will advocate for general contractors and other construction clients throughout the claim and dispute-resolution process, helping them navigate all aspects of general liability claims arising out of. You will evaluate coverage and contractual risk-transfer opportunities, coordinate with insurers, and counsel, and keep matters moving toward effective resolution. Problem solving, responsiveness, and follow-through are critical. Clients rely on you to identify issues early, report claim status, deliver practical solutions, communicate clearly, and own progress. This is a hands-on advocacy role requiring strong construction claims knowledge, good judgment, initiative, and skills in encouraging positive connections between clients and claim collaborators. Represent general contractors and construction clients on construction general liability claims, including job-site accidents, bodily injury, property damage, and complex casualty matters. Partner with clients, insurance carriers, TPAs, and defense and coverage counsel to assess liability, damages, coverage, and contractual obligations and develop coordinated resolution strategies. Analyze coverage and construction contracts, including insurance requirements, indemnity provisions, additional insured coverage, and priority of coverage, to maximize available insurance recovery. Develop and pursue risk-transfer strategies, including tenders to subcontractors and their insurers, additional insurance coverage, contractual indemnification, and contribution from other responsible parties. Support construction defects and completed operations claims and help resolve disputes involving defense and indemnity obligations, additional insured coverage, priority of coverage, allocation, and retentions. Manage and provide guidance on New York Labor Law claims, including §§ 200, 240(1), and 241(6). Actively manage litigated claims, including liability, defense strategy, damages, risk transfer, and settlement posture, and participate in claim reviews. Review coverage positions, reservations of rights, tenders, denials, pleadings, and claim reports, and recommend appropriate action. Stay highly responsive, anticipate obstacles, maintain follow-up with all parties, and escalate carrier, coverage, or defense concerns when intervention can improve the client's position. Translate complex liability, coverage, contract, and litigation issues into clear recommendations, and maintain thorough claim documentation and action plans. Identify claim trends that can inform risk management, contract practices, and insurance placement, and support stewardship meetings, renewals, and new-business presentations as needed. How this opportunity is different This role goes beyond traditional claim reporting or administrative claim monitoring. As a Construction Claim Advocate, you will bring together your construction claims expertise, critical thinking skills, and client perspective to help clients make better decisions and navigate complex claims. You will take ownership of issues, identify practical solutions, and collaborate with clients, carriers, TPAs, counsel, and other stakeholders to move claims forward. Success in this role means being responsive, proactive, and focused on achieving the best possible outcomes for our clients. Skills and experience that will lead to success Strong experience with construction general liability claims, including job-site accidents and significant casualty matters. Strong understanding of coverage analysis, including additional insured coverage, contractual indemnity, priority of coverage, tenders, and risk transfer. Experience managing litigated construction claims, including construction defect and completed operations matters, alongside defense and coverage counsel. Ability to interpret construction contracts, insurance requirements, pleadings, and coverage correspondence, and to evaluate liability, damages, and resolution strategies. Strong negotiation, written communication, and client-facing skills, with the ability to explain complex issues in plain language. Client-service orientation with a commitment to responsiveness, ownership, and follow-through, plus sound judgment on when to intervene or escalate. Ability to manage a portfolio of complex claims with competing priorities. Experience 7+ years of commercial insurance, construction claims, carrier, TPA, brokerage, legal, or risk-management experience, including construction general liability and casualty claims involving general contractors or major construction projects. Direct experience with claims involving job-site accidents, coverage analysis, contractual risk transfer, construction defect, and/or litigated construction claims strongly preferred. New York Labor Law experience, particularly §§ 200, 240(1), and 241(6), strongly preferred. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent related experience. Must have the willingness to obtain an active Property and Casualty license within four months of hire (90 days). Relevant insurance or claims designations, such as AIC, ARM, CPCU, CRIS, or SCLA, are beneficial but not required. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent related experience. Must have the willingness to obtain an active Property and Casualty license within four months of hire (90 days). Relevant insurance or claims designations, such as AIC, ARM, CPCU, CRIS, or SCLA, are beneficial but not required. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $140,000 to $200,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental, and vision insurance; various types of leaves of absence; paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year; 15 days of paid vacation per year; paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws; short-term disability and optional long-term disability; a health savings account; health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts; employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies; adoption assistance; tuition assistance; commuter benefits; and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-JF1 #LI-REMOTE 2587016

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Surety Underwriter, Underwriting, Insurance Customer Service Representative
Job.JobDescription:
Surety Account Manager III Are you a surety professional who thrives at the intersection of client service, underwriting strategy, and operational execution? Join a high-performing team and take on a meaningful role managing and delivering surety bond solutions for many clients! This hybrid position requires working 3 days a week from an Aon office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we build decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Provides analytical and operational services for a portfolio of surety bond clients, with an emphasis on accuracy, client interaction, underwriting pricing rigor & negotiation, and execution quality. Partners closely with clients to facilitate timely issuance of surety obligations. Reports to the regional Surety Operations leader. (Director or Team Lead). Operates with a high degree of autonomy and judgment across complex or strategically significant accounts and in dealing with markets. Takes primary accountability for handling selected key accounts, including coordination of large bond programs and sophisticated underwriting submissions. Possesses strong, in-depth knowledge of surety bonds, including contract and commercial surety, indemnity structures, and market dynamics. Serves as a technical lead within the team; assists in training, mentoring, and developing internal team, and contributes to improvement in execution initiatives. Collaborates daily with carriers on complex needs. Prepares and processes a broad range of surety instruments, including but not limited to bid, final, miscellaneous, and court bonds, ensuring alignment with underwriting parameters and client requirements. Collaborates daily with clients on complex needs. Completes Consents of Surety, Prequalification Letters, Riders, and other client required obligations per State requirements. Determines appropriate documentation to finalize issuance, i.e. power-of-attorney, resident license, etc. with attention to contractual, legal, and financial implications. Prepares General Indemnity Agreements and bond applications, coordinating with and advising clients to obtain complete, accurate financial and corporate information for underwriting review – including any other nuanced client needs or requirements. Maintains and facilitates data integrity and enabling proactive management of bond programs in AonBondLink (ABL). Works closely with internal collaborators to build and maintain accurate, complete electronic bond files in AonBondLink (ABL). It also confirms and manages client financial and underwriting records while following internal controls and audit requirements to avoid E&O. Manages countersignature requirements and related jurisdictional nuances to support compliant bond issuance across multiple states and territories. Provides technical surety guidance and support to non-surety colleagues, helping interpret bond forms, indemnity requirements, and program structures for internal stakeholders. Coordinates receipt and organization of pertinent client related underwriting information (e.g., financial statements, work-in-progress schedules, bank information, organizational documents) to support timely carrier decisions. Verifies that all bonds are issued within established surety lines of credit and brokerage authority; assists in structuring and negotiating approvals for bond requests that exceed standard limits or fall outside delegated authority. How this opportunity is different Unlike many surety operations roles focused mainly on transaction processing, this position combines technical surety expertise with client advisory duties and meaningful market involvement. You will work directly with complex bonding programs, underwriting negotiations, and carrier relationships while acting as a trusted resource for clients and internal colleagues. The role also allows for broader influence through mentoring, participation in operational improvement, and responsibility for critical compliance and underwriting workflows. For professionals wanting to move beyond administrative bond issuance and act as a strategic partner in the surety process, this is an outstanding chance to increase visibility, expand impact, and grow within a leading organization. Skills and experience that will lead to success Is able to effectively interpret a wide range of technical instructions and documentation involving abstract and concrete variables, including financial analyses, contractual provisions, and underwriting guidelines. Possesses experience or formal education in Risk Management, Insurance, and/or Surety, and applies this background to enhance client and market outcomes. Demonstrates strong organizational, time-management, and multi-tasking skills, consistently managing high-volume and complex workloads. Maintains Notary Public designation. Maintains Power of Attorney appointments with major surety markets and is regarded as a trusted signatory. Maintains appropriate Producer license Is proficient in all required technology platforms, including AonBondLink, Bridge, and Outlook, and utilizes these systems to manage data, analyze bond portfolios, and support decision-making. Education and licensing requirements: A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience is preferred for this position. Maintain Notary Public designation and hold the appropriate Property and Casualty license. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $90,000 - $110,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. Surety Account Manager III Are you a surety professional who thrives at the intersection of client service, underwriting strategy, and operational execution? Join a high-performing team and take on a meaningful role managing and delivering surety bond solutions for many clients! This hybrid position requires working 3 days a week from an Aon office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we build decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Provides analytical and operational services for a portfolio of surety bond clients, with an emphasis on accuracy, client interaction, underwriting pricing rigor & negotiation, and execution quality. Partners closely with clients to facilitate timely issuance of surety obligations. Reports to the regional Surety Operations leader. (Director or Team Lead). Operates with a high degree of autonomy and judgment across complex or strategically significant accounts and in dealing with markets. Takes primary accountability for handling selected key accounts, including coordination of large bond programs and sophisticated underwriting submissions. Possesses strong, in-depth knowledge of surety bonds, including contract and commercial surety, indemnity structures, and market dynamics. Serves as a technical lead within the team; assists in training, mentoring, and developing internal team, and contributes to improvement in execution initiatives. Collaborates daily with carriers on complex needs. Prepares and processes a broad range of surety instruments, including but not limited to bid, final, miscellaneous, and court bonds, ensuring alignment with underwriting parameters and client requirements. Collaborates daily with clients on complex needs. Completes Consents of Surety, Prequalification Letters, Riders, and other client required obligations per State requirements. Determines appropriate documentation to finalize issuance, i.e. power-of-attorney, resident license, etc. with attention to contractual, legal, and financial implications. Prepares General Indemnity Agreements and bond applications, coordinating with and advising clients to obtain complete, accurate financial and corporate information for underwriting review – including any other nuanced client needs or requirements. Maintains and facilitates data integrity and enabling proactive management of bond programs in AonBondLink (ABL). Works closely with internal collaborators to build and maintain accurate, complete electronic bond files in AonBondLink (ABL). It also confirms and manages client financial and underwriting records while following internal controls and audit requirements to avoid E&O. Manages countersignature requirements and related jurisdictional nuances to support compliant bond issuance across multiple states and territories. Provides technical surety guidance and support to non-surety colleagues, helping interpret bond forms, indemnity requirements, and program structures for internal stakeholders. Coordinates receipt and organization of pertinent client related underwriting information (e.g., financial statements, work-in-progress schedules, bank information, organizational documents) to support timely carrier decisions. Verifies that all bonds are issued within established surety lines of credit and brokerage authority; assists in structuring and negotiating approvals for bond requests that exceed standard limits or fall outside delegated authority. How this opportunity is different Unlike many surety operations roles focused mainly on transaction processing, this position combines technical surety expertise with client advisory duties and meaningful market involvement. You will work directly with complex bonding programs, underwriting negotiations, and carrier relationships while acting as a trusted resource for clients and internal colleagues. The role also allows for broader influence through mentoring, participation in operational improvement, and responsibility for critical compliance and underwriting workflows. For professionals wanting to move beyond administrative bond issuance and act as a strategic partner in the surety process, this is an outstanding chance to increase visibility, expand impact, and grow within a leading organization. Skills and experience that will lead to success Is able to effectively interpret a wide range of technical instructions and documentation involving abstract and concrete variables, including financial analyses, contractual provisions, and underwriting guidelines. Possesses experience or formal education in Risk Management, Insurance, and/or Surety, and applies this background to enhance client and market outcomes. Demonstrates strong organizational, time-management, and multi-tasking skills, consistently managing high-volume and complex workloads. Maintains Notary Public designation. Maintains Power of Attorney appointments with major surety markets and is regarded as a trusted signatory. Maintains appropriate Producer license Is proficient in all required technology platforms, including AonBondLink, Bridge, and Outlook, and utilizes these systems to manage data, analyze bond portfolios, and support decision-making. Education and licensing requirements: A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience is preferred for this position. Maintain Notary Public designation and hold the appropriate Property and Casualty license. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances.
