Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world! As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed! What the day will look like Responsibilities: Serve as the senior technology leader for FP&A, partnering with the Finance organization to define the strategy and roadmap for Aon's global planning, forecasting, performance management, cost transparency, and financial analytics technology ecosystem. Manage the portfolio of FP&A technologies, including: Enterprise Planning & Forecasting: Workday Adaptive Planning and IBM Planning Analytics (TM1), including budgeting, forecasting, scenario modeling, workforce planning, long-range planning, management reporting, and multidimensional analysis. Technology Business Management & Cost Transparency: Apptio applications supporting technology financial management, cost allocation, planning, reporting, and business value insights. Financial Data & Analytics: Finance data platforms, enterprise reporting, Power BI, executive dashboards, predictive analytics, and insights generated by technology. Finance Operations & Workflow: Planning workflows, approvals, controls, automation, workflow orchestration, and process optimization. Data Management & Governance: Financial hierarchies, master data, chart of accounts. Planning dimensions, organizational structures, allocation structures, and reference data management. Integration & Enterprise Platforms: ERP, HR, financial data, reporting, and other enterprise platforms supporting end-to-end FP&A processes. Ensure end-to-end process integrity and data consistency across annual planning, long-term planning, rolling forecasts, workforce planning, cost allocation, management reporting, variance analysis, and executive decision support. Partner closely with senior leaders across FP&A, Corporate Finance, Operations Finance, Accounting, Data, Technology, and business functions. Align platform capabilities with enterprise financial objectives and transformation strategies. Lead and develop a team spanning product ownership, solution architecture, business analysis, development, integration, and platform administration. Clear accountability for delivery, operations, controls, and continuous improvement. Collaborate with peer Finance Technology leaders across the organization to align roadmaps, architecture, delivery priorities, data standards, support models, and shared business outcomes. Define and maintain the governance model for the FP&A Technology portfolio, including demand intake, prioritization, change control, release management, testing, deployment, and collaborator communications. Responsible for the evaluation, adoption, and rollout of new capabilities across Workday Adaptive Planning, IBM Planning Analytics (TM1), Apptio, and supporting FP&A technologies; perform impact assessments and guide configuration, testing, deployment, and operational readiness. Drive adoption and change management for new capabilities, ensuring FP&A and business finance teams are equipped to employ technology effectively to improve planning, forecasting, analysis, and decision-making. Champion finance data quality, governance, standardization, security, and controls across the FP&A technology landscape; collaborate with Risk, Compliance, Audit, and Data Governance teams to meet internal requirements. Ensure effective integration and data flows between FP&A platforms and adjacent ecosystems including ERP, HR, enterprise data warehouses, analytics platforms, collaboration tools, and corporate reporting solutions. Lead FP&A Technology modernization initiatives including integrated business planning, connected planning, predictive forecasting, AI-enabled analysis, self-service reporting, and finance process automation. Establish measurable product and service outcomes, including platform reliability, delivery performance, user adoption, data quality, control effectiveness, and business value realization. Act as the technology leader responsible for ensuring Aon has the accurate financial data available. How this opportunity is different This role goes well beyond maintaining current tools. You will: Drive the strategic vision for Aon's FP&A Technology ecosystem, including how enterprise planning, cost transparency, reporting, analytics, and finance data work together to provide a trusted performance management platform. Play a central role in enterprise-wide transformation programs, including: Global FP&A modernization and connected planning initiatives Workday Adaptive Planning and IBM Planning Analytics (TM1) platform optimization and rationalization Apptio-enabled cost transparency and technology financial management AI-enabled forecasting, variance analysis, scenario modeling, and decision support Enterprise finance data governance and reporting transformation Blend executive-level influence with hands-on leadership by driving multi-year roadmaps and major transformation programs while engaging in architecture reviews, vendor strategy discussions, and emerging technology evaluations. Shape the day-to-day experience of FP&A and business finance teams around the world by providing scalable, reliable, and innovative technology capabilities. Skills and experience that will lead to success Extensive experience (typically 8+ years) leading Finance Technology, FP&A Technology, Enterprise Performance Management (EPM), Technology Business Management, or Corporate Finance Systems portfolios within a global, matrixed organization. Deep hands-on and strategic experience with: Enterprise planning, budgeting, forecasting, and performance management platforms Financial analytics, reporting, and data platforms Financial data, integration, security, and control architectures Understanding of-Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), Budgeting and forecasting, Long-range planning. In addition, workforce planning, scenario modeling and variance analysis. Management reporting and performance analytics Proven success leading sophisticated, multi-year transformation programs across planning, performance management, reporting, cost transparency, data, and integration domains, including global deployments and process standardization. Experience driving adoption of AI, automation, and analytics within finance use cases including forecast recommendations, variance analysis, scenario modeling, planning optimization, and executive dashboards. Strong track record partnering with Finance executives to translate financial strategies, key performance indicators, and business objectives into scalable technology capabilities. Demonstrated ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing, global teams. Direct responsibility for people leadership, performance management, succession planning, mentoring, and capability development. Demonstrable ability to lead through influence across peer teams and matrixed organizations, aligning collaborators who do not directly collaborate with the role around shared roadmaps, standards, and outcomes. Excellent collaborator management and communication skills. Ability to influence and collaborate with senior leaders across FP&A, Finance, Accounting, Data, Risk, Audit, business functions, and Technology. Experience managing portfolio prioritization, budgeting, resource planning, and delivery capacity across multiple concurrent products, projects, and operational commitments. Strong vendor and partner leadership skills, including negotiating contracts, managing performance, supervising managed service providers, and aligning partner roadmaps with enterprise objectives. Experience operating within a product-centric delivery model and driving accountability through measurable business outcomes. Strategy and Innovation Strategic problem solver who can connect FP&A technology, data, and process capabilities to business outcomes. This includes planning agility, forecast accuracy, cost transparency, financial insight, and operational efficiency. Proven track record of identifying and implementing automation, AI/ML, predictive analytics, and advanced reporting capabilities across planning and performance management processes. Experience establishing governance, operating models, architecture principles, and decision-making frameworks that balance innovation, risk management, standardization, and business agility. Comfortable operating in a matrixed, global environment, balancing enterprise standards with regional and business requirements. Finance Data Strategy and the role data governance plays in enabling trusted planning, reporting, analysis, and decision-making capabilities. Education & credentials Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, Finance, Accounting, or a related field. MBA, CPA, CFA or equivalent experience, PMP, or other advanced certification preferred. Workday Adaptive Planning, IBM Planning Analytics (TM1), and/or Apptio certifications preferred. Demonstrated commitment to continuous learning and knowing the latest with emerging finance technologies, AI capabilities, enterprise planning, technology financial management, and performance management standard processes. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-KH1 2586731

Aon is looking for an Executive Services Coordinator! Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. How this opportunity is different The Executive Services Coordinator provides an elevated level of in-person support for senior leaders through personalized concierge services, coordination of executive activities, and high touch customer service. This role focuses on creating a seamless executive experience by managing day-of logistics, coordinating special arrangements, supporting onboarding activities, and responding to ad hoc requests. This position is a full-time, on-site role requiring five days per week in the office. The role does not perform traditional administrative support responsibilities but serves as a dedicated resource for executive services and limited support for select marketing events. This role is ideal for a highly polished, service-oriented professional who enjoys creating exceptional experiences for senior leaders. You'll serve as a trusted on-site resource, anticipating needs, managing high-priority requests, and coordinating across workplace teams to ensure executive activities run smoothly. The position combines executive concierge services, hospitality, onboarding, priority materials management, and limited event support in a fast-paced professional environment. Working Model Full-time, five days per week in the office in our Houston, TX office. Requires consistent on-site presence to support senior leaders, executives, designated guests, and executive-facing activities. High-visibility, front-facing position involving regular interaction with executives, colleagues, visitors, vendors, and workplace partners. What the day will look like Executive Services & Experience Deliver high-touch executive support across planned and ad hoc needs, including: Personalized executive onsite support, including special arrangements and private meeting coordination Senior leader day-of-onsite support, including agenda execution, stakeholder coordination, and transitions between activities Executive meeting coordination, room readiness, and logistics support Priority reception and visitor support for executives, and designated guests Executive onboarding support, including workspace readiness and coordination of technology setup Priority document preparation, printing, deliveries, catering, and materials tied to executive needs Triaging urgent, sensitive, or miscellaneous ad hoc requests and tracking them through completion On-Site Event Support Provide limited support for select Marketing events and executive-facing activities, including guest greeting, registration, basic setup, and logistical coordination. Support executive accommodations, hospitality, and event logistics to create a seamless and professional attendee experience. Partner with Marketing and other workplace teams as needed to support smooth event execution while maintaining a premium service experience. Hospitality, Executive Meeting Support, and Organization Coordinate catering, food and beverage requests, deliveries, special arrangements, and hospitality needs for executive meetings and activities. Ensure executive and client-facing spaces are organized, professional, welcoming, and prepared for meetings and scheduled activities. Provide priority reception and hospitality support for executives and designated guests while maintaining a high standard of professionalism, discretion, and service. Deliver a personalized, hospitality-focused experience for senior executives, clients, and visitors while managing multiple priorities with exceptional attention to detail. Anticipate needs, respond quickly to time-sensitive requests, and ensure consistent follow-through while maintaining a polished and professional service experience. Skills and Experiences that Will Lead to Success Communication & Relationship Building Communicate clearly and professionally with executives, colleagues, visitors, vendors, and other participants through strong verbal and written communication. Build trusted relationships and coordinate effectively across Facilities, IT, General Location Services, administrative teams, and other business partners. Discretion, Judgment & Adaptability Exercise sound judgment, professionalism, and discretion when handling confidential information, sensitive executive requests, and high-visibility interactions. Demonstrate a proactive and adaptable approach, anticipating needs, resolving issues efficiently, and adjusting to changing priorities in a fast-paced environment. Technology Proficiency Proficiency with Microsoft Office and workplace productivity tools. Comfortable using workplace technology and coordinating technology support with IT and other workplace partners to support executive meetings and activities. Education & Experience High school diploma or equivalent years of industry experience. Success Measures Consistently deliver a high-quality executive experience through seamless coordination of day-of activities, meetings, onboarding, hospitality, and logistics. Respond to concierge and ad hoc requests promptly and effectively while maintaining exceptional standards of professionalism, confidentiality, service, and discretion. Job.JobTitle: Senior Vice President - Global Benefits Consultant
Job.JobDescription:
Senior Vice President - Global Benefits Consultant Are you a Global Benefits (GB) expert interested in a great career opportunity that offers diversified leadership and global project and client exposure? Do you want to work for successful and growing leader in the field? This is a hybrid role that will work 3 days per week from our New York office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like The Senior Vice President - Global Benefits Consultant will report to the Global Benefits Northeast Leader. Manage a group of experienced consultants and help to develop and mentor less experienced staff. Help to shape the business strategy and growth of the North America market. Responsible for new business development including expansion of existing business and new business revenue goals and prospect/ opportunity management. Lead large client relationships and complex projects including: delivery of key client solutions, project management, fee setting, and revenue projections. Help multinational clients solve and manage multifaceted benefits issues by providing consulting support to their operations outside of the US in areas including, but not limited to, global benefit strategy, benefit audit, benchmarking, non-US insured benefit placement and renewals, opening for business, M&A, multinational pooling, governance, risk management, etc. Use our innovative and state-of-the-art technology platform, make analytical conclusions/ recommendations to drive client’s business decisions. Lead financial and strategic client discussions and identify potential additional work and/or out-of-scope services requested by clients. Guide end-to-end project delivery including: initiating strategic discussions, establishing an action plan, finalizing reporting materials, coordinating the client team in responding to client inquiries, and monitoring time and project budget Use your concrete and thorough understanding of Global Benefits to take a leadership role that helps advance and enhance task forces, special projects, and team capabilities within the Global Benefits practice. Conduct meetings, monitor and execute deliverables and accountabilities based on project scope and statement of work. Drive sales by developing cross-selling opportunities with other Aon practices. Keep informed on market activities and look for innovations to enhance our offerings and educate our clients regarding industry trends, new product information, legislation, coverages and technology to continuously improve knowledge and performance. Interact with others effectively by utilizing good communication skills, cooperating purposefully and providing information, as needed, to achieve the business goals of the company. Participate in training opportunities to remain current with the regulatory environment. How this opportunity is different This is a great career opportunity that offers diversified leadership, project and client exposure. Skills and experience that will lead to success Fifteen years or more of direct experience in an HR consulting firm or professional services firm. In addition, international or non-US benefits consulting experience is strongly desired. We also value demonstrated consultative skills to effectively work in a cohesive team environment, help clients via problem solving, as well as the ability to communicate with a variety of internal and external parties. Direct experience on managing a team of experienced consultants. Strong management and analytical ability. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including strong presentation skills. Strong organizational skills, ability to handle multiple projects in a fast-paced and time-sensitive environment. Demonstrated interest in the global environment, other cultures and language. Strong functional knowledge of Excel specific to creating, formatting and evaluating formulas and working with templates. Proficiency in Word, Power Point and other MS Office products along with Adobe products. Problem solving and critical thinking skills. Education: Bachelor’s degree in relevant discipline or 15 equivalent years of industry experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $250,000 to $290,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance. This role does not accrue vacation. Rather, this role is eligible to take paid time off at the discretion of the employee and management in accordance with company policy and practices. Various other types of leaves of absence; paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-LC1 #LI-Executive #LI-HYBRID 2570282

Senior Vice President - Global Benefits Consultant Are you a Global Benefits (GB) expert interested in a great career opportunity that offers diversified leadership and global project and client exposure? Do you want to work for successful and growing leader in the field? This is a hybrid role that will work 3 days per week from our New York office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like The Senior Vice President - Global Benefits Consultant will report to the Global Benefits Northeast Leader. Manage a group of experienced consultants and help to develop and mentor less experienced staff. Help to shape the business strategy and growth of the North America market. Responsible for new business development including expansion of existing business and new business revenue goals and prospect/ opportunity management. Lead large client relationships and complex projects including: delivery of key client solutions, project management, fee setting, and revenue projections. Help multinational clients solve and manage multifaceted benefits issues by providing consulting support to their operations outside of the US in areas including, but not limited to, global benefit strategy, benefit audit, benchmarking, non-US insured benefit placement and renewals, opening for business, M&A, multinational pooling, governance, risk management, etc. Use our innovative and state-of-the-art technology platform, make analytical conclusions/ recommendations to drive client’s business decisions. Lead financial and strategic client discussions and identify potential additional work and/or out-of-scope services requested by clients. Guide end-to-end project delivery including: initiating strategic discussions, establishing an action plan, finalizing reporting materials, coordinating the client team in responding to client inquiries, and monitoring time and project budget Use your concrete and thorough understanding of Global Benefits to take a leadership role that helps advance and enhance task forces, special projects, and team capabilities within the Global Benefits practice. Conduct meetings, monitor and execute deliverables and accountabilities based on project scope and statement of work. Drive sales by developing cross-selling opportunities with other Aon practices. Keep informed on market activities and look for innovations to enhance our offerings and educate our clients regarding industry trends, new product information, legislation, coverages and technology to continuously improve knowledge and performance. Interact with others effectively by utilizing good communication skills, cooperating purposefully and providing information, as needed, to achieve the business goals of the company. Participate in training opportunities to remain current with the regulatory environment. How this opportunity is different This is a great career opportunity that offers diversified leadership, project and client exposure. Skills and experience that will lead to success Fifteen years or more of direct experience in an HR consulting firm or professional services firm. In addition, international or non-US benefits consulting experience is strongly desired. We also value demonstrated consultative skills to effectively work in a cohesive team environment, help clients via problem solving, as well as the ability to communicate with a variety of internal and external parties. Direct experience on managing a team of experienced consultants. Strong management and analytical ability. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including strong presentation skills. Strong organizational skills, ability to handle multiple projects in a fast-paced and time-sensitive environment. Demonstrated interest in the global environment, other cultures and language. Strong functional knowledge of Excel specific to creating, formatting and evaluating formulas and working with templates. Proficiency in Word, Power Point and other MS Office products along with Adobe products. Problem solving and critical thinking skills. Education: Bachelor’s degree in relevant discipline or 15 equivalent years of industry experience. Aon Is looking for a Sales Executive for our 401(k) Pooled Employer Plan Team - Based in Northeast Region Be part of the industry-leading team bringing Aon’s innovative defined contribution 401(k) savings plan to employers across the U.S. – the Aon Pooled Employer Plan (Aon PEP). At Aon, we believe that PEPs are the next generation of retirement savings as they 1) reduce work for employers, 2) reduce risk for fiduciaries, and 3) reduce costs and improve results for employees. In 2021, we introduced our Aon PEP to meet this growing market demand and to date have over $7B in assets and commitments in our new program. We are targeting this multi-trillion dollar market with a dedicated sales team. The sales executive will be responsible for creating internal and external demand for the Aon PEP, driving our go-to-market strategy, creating and nurturing a personal pipeline of prospects in your territory, and coordinating and directly participating in sales efforts. Your Impact as a Sales Executive Responsibilities Achieve annual Aon PEP sales goals. Establish and coordinate sales strategy and execution across all assigned markets. Identify and pursue opportunities with both a) existing Aon clients and b) self-developed pipeline of non-Aon clients via relationships and digital marketing and prospecting. Effectively integrate with other Aon sales leaders across practices to identify opportunities, actively work the pipeline to create leads, and move leads to opportunities. Build and maintain the Aon PEP prospect pipeline and other sales reporting responsibilities. Effectively introduce lead generation resources at the appropriate time in the selling process. Collect and communicate market intelligence on products/services and incorporate it into sales client planning process. Creatively eliminate barriers for clients entering new markets; support the team in navigating alternative paths to making the sale. Ensure most efficient use of Aon Connect, Aon’s internal CRM/pipeline management tool. Partner with Aon PEP and DC Leadership teams to advance marketing, investments and solution development. Regular/minimum of 30% travel expected, depending on sales opportunities. Collaborate and share approaches and findings with other regional Master Trust sales teams globally as we expand this offering in other markets. Qualifications and Expertise 5+ years of direct or equivalent sales experience in the defined contribution market (or similar institutional assets) with demonstrated sales success. Established network of contacts in the DC industry. Ability to create a personal pipeline of non-Aon clients to pursue in your territory. Proven history of success in developing new products in various markets, and establishing and executing a sales strategy. Demonstrated history of building and maintaining a substantial pipeline. Ability to communicate the value of a product to clients, deliver insights on how the service will impact the client’s business, and effectively close opportunities. Subject Matter Expertise: Broad knowledge and expertise of defined contribution plan design, administration, investments, and delivery. Excellent relationship management abilities: Capability to build trusted advisor relationships at multiple levels in a potential client company, including members of the fiduciary, financial, and administrative committees who are responsible for the defined contribution plan. Experienced in maintaining productive, internal relationships to leverage those resources when necessary. Outstanding Communication and Project Management skills: Ability to manage multiple, complex sales processes at the same time. Very strong internal and external communication skills, with the ability to listen comprehensively and deliver clear instructions and/or recommendations. Sales Forecasting, Sales, Marketing Strategies, Data Analysis, Risk Management, CRM, Report Writing, Customer Experience, Project Management, Training Workshops, Product Management, Customer Engagement, Meeting Facilitation, Customer Communications Management, Strategic Selling, Sales Training, Channel Management, Account Management, Sales Process, Sales Presentations Education Bachelor’s Degree required. Advanced Degree is preferred and/or equivalent work-related experience and success. FINRA license is not required, but preferred. Job.JobTitle: Senior Account Executive, C&I - South Region
Job.JobDescription:
Positioned uniquely between strategic advisory and brokerage functions, this role is part of Aon’s well-known construction and infrastructure platform. As a Senior Account Executive, C&I - South Region, you will employ Aon’s rich data, analytics, and market connections to develop and execute integrated, multi-line insurance solutions for complex projects. You will lead specialist teams in different regions, influence risk management from project launch through completion, and provide outstanding solutions that surpass standard placements. This position is hybrid, offering the option to work from Atlanta, GA, Houston, TX or one of our Florida offices in Tampa, Jacksonville, or Miami. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like As a Senior Account Executive, you will advise clients on effective risk transfer, insurance design, and contract risk oversight to deliver outstanding results. The position also acts as a client representative with contracting and financing partners and leads collaborative brokerage teams across various insurance lines, including Workers’ Compensation or equivalent experience, General Liability, Professional Liability, Environmental Liability, and Builders Risk. Strategic Advisory & Risk Management Serve as a subject matter expert on construction-phase risk transfer, risk financing, and risk control strategies Evaluate project-specific risks and provide assessments of risk allocation, insurability, and market appetite Advise clients on value-for-money risk transfer strategies applying Aon’s proprietary data, benchmarking, and analytics Provide guidance to ensure seamless and effective risk transfer among all project collaborators Establish and maintain insurance cost benchmarks to support informed client decision-making Client Advocacy & Contract Advisory Act as a trusted advisor and advocate for clients in discussions with contractors, lenders, and joint venture partners Provide contract risk advisory services, including insurance and indemnity review and negotiation support Deliver thought leadership and client education sessions, including insights on U.S. versus international construction risk and insurance practices Insurance Program Development & Brokerage Delivery Lead the design and placement of best-in-class, project-specific insurance programs in collaboration with Aon product and specialty leaders Coordinate brokerage teams across multiple lines of coverage to provide integrated, efficient insurance solutions Prepare and lead insurance market presentations and insurer engagement strategies Collaborate with internal analytics teams and external experts on EML/PML analyses and related risk modeling Project & Collaborator Management Act as the project manager across Aon’s brokerage, advisory, analytics, and global service teams Drive alignment across geographies, fields, and service lines to deliver consistent client outcomes Translate complex insurance structures and coverage concepts into clear, practical guidance for non-insurance collaborators How this opportunity is different This role sits at the dynamic intersection of strategic advisory and brokerage execution within Aon’s global construction and infrastructure platform. As a Senior Account Executive, you will use Aon’s comprehensive data, analytics, and market relationships to design and place integrated, multi-line insurance solutions for complex, large-scale projects. You’ll coordinate specialist teams across geographies, influence risk outcomes from project inception through delivery, and deliver distinctive, impactful solutions that go well beyond traditional placement. Skills and experience that will lead to success 10–15+ years of experience in construction risk advisory, insurance brokerage, or related project risk roles Deep expertise across multiple construction-related insurance lines Experience advising senior client collaborators on complex, large-scale construction and infrastructure projects Strong understanding of construction contracts, risk allocation, and delivery models An active P&C License is required, or you must be willing to obtain one within 90 days of your hire date. Education: Bachelor’s degree or relevant experience considered equivalent. How we support our colleagues Alongside our extensive benefits package, we promote a diverse and welcoming workforce. Additionally, our flexible work setting enables you to prioritize your wellbeing and maintain a healthy work/life balance, helping you be your best self at Aon. Moreover, every team member receives two “Global Wellbeing Days” annually, giving you the opportunity to concentrate on your personal needs. We also provide several options for different working styles to support our colleagues. Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued. Aon values an innovative and inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Aon provides equal access to employment for all employees and applicants without discrimination based on race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, marital or domestic partner status, or any other legally protected category. Applicants with criminal histories are welcome. We are dedicated to offering equal employment opportunities and promoting an inclusive environment. If you need accommodations during the application or interview process, please inform us. You can ask for accommodations by emailing ReasonableAccommodations@Aon.com or contacting your recruiter. We will collaborate with you to address your needs and provide a fair and just experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from recruiting agencies for this position. If you are a recruiting agency, you will not receive any compensation for submitting a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $163,200 to $261,100 annually. The final salary will depend on the applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, along with internal fairness and comparison with market information. The salary might also be altered depending on the applicant’s geographic location. The salary range shown corresponds to a primary work location of The actual salary may differ for candidates in another geographic area. This role qualifies for participation in one of Aon’s yearly incentive programs to earn an annual discretionary bonus or production incentives alongside the base salary. The bonus or production incentives amount differs and depends on the rules of the relevant incentive program A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-HYBRID #LI-Mid-Seniorlevel #LI-CF1 2573716

We currently have an exciting underwriting career opportunity as a PEO Underwriter I. This position is part of Aon’s Underwriting Center of Excellence and supports Aon’s Tampa, FL based PEO and Staffing vertical and offers flexible work arrangements: If you reside in the Tampa or Miami areas: the role is hybrid, with an expectation of at least three days per week in the office. If you reside outside the Tampa/Miami areas: the role is fully remote and may be performed virtually from your home anywhere in the U.S. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like As a Health Insurance Underwriter, your day will be a blend of strategic analysis and collaboration, focused on developing tailored health insurance solutions for Professional Employer Organizations (PEOs). You’ll work with both internal teams and external partners to deliver the best results for our clients. Assess and underwrite employer-sponsored medical plans for PEO clients Analyze data such as census information, claims experience, and premium history to calculate insurance premiums Collaborate with insurance carriers to collect data and provide quote recommendations Support the PEO sales team by preparing and distributing proposals and responding to client inquiries Work with team members, health insurance carriers, and brokers to solve complex client challenges Help develop and enhance underwriting models and tools, driving efficiency and innovation How this opportunity is different At Aon, you will not only work closely with leading insurance carriers but also with a dynamic and supportive team that thrives on collaboration. You'll be part of a strategic process that ensures client satisfaction while also innovating within the underwriting field. Your contributions will help shape the future of how PEO clients structure their health plans. Job.JobDescription:
Aon currently has an exciting career opportunity for a Licensed Customer Service Specialist I in our Fort Washington, PA office. This position will support Aon’s Affinity Insurance Services group in the AICPA Insurance Trust department. This role is office based the first 6 months in our Fort Washington, PA location. From 6-12 months it can be hybrid working 1 day a week remotely. After one year, it can be hybrid working 2 days per week remotely. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: - Handle inbound and outbound calls via 800 lines with multi-product portfolio- both Life and Health products as well and Property and Casualty products - Respond to customer communications via email and written correspondence - Maintain service, quality and timeliness standards - Interact with other departments on various projects including new programs, products and technology - Support knowledge management transfer within the department through training, quality and intranet projects - Evaluate individual customers’ needs and propose additional insurance products based on personal and business needs - Maintains customer records by updating account or policy information. - Provide analysis support and prepare reports for accurate business results for the carrier - Reconcile client payments against the policy administration system . REQUIRED SKILLS: Possess active Property & Casualty licenses and obtain Life, Health & Accident within 90 days - Demonstrated skills and abilities to be goal oriented and solve complex issues - Learn multiple products to support revenue growth for program business - Possess excellent organizational and verbal communication skills - Strong multi-tasker - Experience with CRM- Customer Relationship Management System preferred - Possess excellent written communication skills for customer correspondence, be able to speak broadly and question customer’s needs - Ability to provide excellent quality service to customers - Demonstrated ability in handling details and key follow up capability - Strong PC skills with solid knowledge based in Word, Excel and PowerPoint software - Ability to identify process efficiencies and handle daily activities in a thorough and accurate fashion - Ability to work independently and as a team member - Ability to think critically and use sound judgment when serving clients - Demonstrated relationship-building skills evaluating individual insurance needs and offering appropriate products/solutions MINIMUM EDUCATION: Bachelor’s Degree preferred, or commensurate work experience MINIMUM REQUIRED EXPERIENCE: - 1-3 years’ experience in sales and service supporting multiple insurance products and/or financial services products - Property & Casualty active licenses and P&C license preferred and must obtain within 90 days. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. LI-BK1 2584436

Do you like applying your critical thinking and analytical skills to tackle problems and help clients? Are you interested in making a difference in someone’s life and enjoy working with others? We would love to have you join our outstanding team! This Pension Specialist role is a hybrid role with the flexibility to work both virtually and from our Woodlands, TX office. Initially this role will require daily in person attendance in the office until after training and assessment has taken place. Upon approval, in office requirements are Tuesday and Wednesday but could change or be increased at any time. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. How we onboard You will participate in a comprehensive and selective rotation on client teams to build your pension knowledge and develop a deep understanding of pension processes and concepts needed to support employees. Job.JobTitle: North America Industrials & Manufacturing Industry Leader, Chemicals Specialty
Job.JobDescription:
Aon is seeking an influential industry executive to lead our North America Industrials & Manufacturing practice and serve as the trusted advisor, growth catalyst, and market-facing leader. In addition, experience in the Chemical sector including specialty chemicals, polymers, industrial chemicals and petrochemicals would be accretive to the role. In this highly visible role, you will define and implement the vision for the North America Industrials & Manufacturing Industry Vertical. You will partner with market leaders and cross-functional teams to provide innovative ways that help clients navigate risk. Using your industry expertise, relationships, and commercial savvy, you will accelerate revenue growth, strengthen client engagement, and elevate Aon's presence across the industrial and manufacturing sectors. This is an outstanding opportunity for a strategic, client-centric executive who combines industry credibility with a consistent track record of business development, market leadership, and team building. Preferred location: Midwest-based, with consideration for exceptional candidates located on the East Coast or in the Southeast. Responsibilities: Business Development Drive incremental sales growth for the Industrial Manufacturing Industry. Lead and drive accountability for sales activity. Develop, plan, and implement industry-specific sales strategies with market sales leaders. Work with other leaders within Aon to collaborate on cross-practice sales. Represent the practice in strategic business initiatives and innovative solutions. Colleague Assistance Expand current client relationships and new client opportunities by: Participating in RFP’s and deal coaching. Meeting with Aon teams at a Market and/or Regional level to discuss industry specific topics. Meeting with current clients and bring industry insights to meet their needs. Making meaningful contributions to a high-profile initiative which has significantly built or impacted the business. Industry Engagement and Thought Leadership Host industry events for clients and prospects. Host periodic industry calls for clients and prospects and Aon colleagues. Is viewed in local market and/or internally as a known “brand” – is sought out by clients, prospects and colleagues for advice. Develop innovative new solutions for clients that result in revenue growth with viable margins. Provide practice and/or thought leadership at a national level. Find opportunities for your team for development and to improve client experiences. Author white papers and other industry collateral. Recruiting Recruit, retain and engage a skilled and committed team. Develop a culture of collaboration and inclusion. What You'll Bring: Deep expertise and established relationships within the industrials & manufacturing industry, and insurance markets. Preferred experience within the chemicals sector. Proven success leading revenue growth, business development, and large-scale client engagements. Strong executive presence with the ability to influence C-suite partners internally and externally. Proven experience building and leading high-performing teams composed of individuals with different perspectives. Recognized thought leadership and a passion for developing innovative solutions that tackle sophisticated client challenges. A Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience is required; an advanced degree and/or significant industry leadership experience is preferred. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $275,000 to $350,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in Aon’s annual incentive plans in addition to base salary. The amount of any incentive varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance. This role does not accrue vacation. Rather, this role is eligible to take paid time off at the discretion of the employee and management in accordance with company policy and practices. Various other types of leaves of absence; paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-CB1 #LI- Executive 2587054

Job.JobTitle: US Health Analytics Models and Engineering Leader
Job.JobDescription:
Aon is looking for a US Health Analytics Models and Engineering Leader This is a hybrid role preferrably in Denver, Chicago, or Atlanta, with flexibility for other US Aon offices. Fully remote may be considered We are seeking a hands-on Health Analytics Models and Engineering leader to lead the development of analytics solutions, systems, and technology for Aon’s US Health Analytics practice. You will own the design, delivery, and quality of the models, analytics applications, and AI-enabled systems that power our benefits financial modeling – including risk simulations, underwriting models, financial analytics, network modeling, benchmarking, plan design and cost-sharing modeling, migration modeling and related capabilities. You will set technical direction, lead a team, and write and review production code, working closely with actuaries, consultants, Aon Business Solutions (ABS), technology architects, and offshore engineering teams. The ideal candidate has 8+ years of US Health experience, a track record of scaled model development using modern technologies, a deep understanding of US health data and employer benefits financial modeling, and a track record of building analytics applications end-to-end and leading technical teams. Experience translating actuarial and underwriting methods, peer review, and controls into well-engineered, maintainable code is essential. What a day will look like Lead analytics technical solution development and engineering, AI-enabled analytics solution development, and priority analytics roadmap workstreams for the US Health Analytics practice, setting technical direction while staying hands-on in writing, reviewing, and shipping production code Collaborate closely with Aon Business Solutions (ABS), technology architects, and offshore engineering teams to align on architecture, standards, and priorities, coordinate delivery across locations and time zones, and move models into scalable, supported production Design, build, and maintain modeling engines – simulations, underwriting and renewal tools, cost and risk modeling, reserving (IBNR), pricing and contribution setting, plan design valuations, and migration modeling – and extend them across domains such as Actuarial and Financial, Clinical and Pharmacy, Time Away Solutions, Audit, Network Analytics, and Consumer Benefits Partner with actuaries, consultants, and subject matter experts to turn actuarial and underwriting methods into tested, governed, and documented code with consistent assumptions and outputs Design and productionize AI systems and modular capabilities, including agent graphs, harness engineering, and orchestration, and advance AI-assisted development practices Own quality and reliability end-to-end through strong DevOps practices, including infrastructure as code, automated testing, model validation, and CI/CD Lead and coach technical colleagues, and run delivery through agile Scrum with clear priorities and objectives You Bring Knowledge and Expertise Minimum 8 years of experience in US Health & Benefits consulting, with a track record of delivering value to clients and colleagues Strong understanding of employer benefits financial modeling, including health risk, underwriting forecasting, trend and seasonality, reserving, pricing, plan design valuations, and migration modeling, and of actuarial techniques such as completion factors, credibility, and Monte Carlo simulation Expert knowledge of US health data, including benefit plan design, medical and pharmacy claims, eligibility, plan design, and benefits structure Deep experience building and scaling analytics applications end-to-end Experience partnering with enterprise technology and architecture teams and leading work with offshore or distributed engineering teams Experience designing and productionizing AI systems; familiarity with AI-assisted and autonomous development including GitHub Copilot and Claude Code. Experience leading technical teams, with strong agile Scrum and DevOps practices (infrastructure as code, testing, CI/CD, version control, Linux/WSL) Python, C#, and R mastery are required; Docker, Azure, Databricks, and Terraform experience a plus Ability to explain technical and modeling decisions clearly to actuaries, consultants, and non-technical audiences ASA or FSA credential is viewed as a strong plus Education Bachelor’s or master’s degree in actuarial science, mathematics, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $185,000 to $225,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-HP1 #LI-HYBRID #LI-REMOTE 2587252

Aon is hiring for a Health Solutions Senior Consultant in San Francisco - (Hybrid position) At Aon, we do not just advise clients on employee benefits. We help them make better decisions about one of their most important investments: their people. As a Health Solutions Senior Consultant, you will partner with sophisticated employers to design and deliver innovative health and benefits strategies that balance cost, risk, competitiveness, and employee experience. You will lead complex projects, influence client decisions, collaborate with industry-leading subject matter experts, and help shape solutions that impact employees and their families. This is an opportunity for an intellectually curious consultant who enjoys blending analytics, strategy, relationship management, and leadership to solve real-world business problems. This hybrid role offers flexibility to work virtually and from our San Francisco office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like You will serve as a trusted advisor to clients and a key leader within the client team. You will help employers navigate complex healthcare and workforce challenges by delivering thoughtful analysis, strategic recommendations, and exceptional client service. Specifically, the Health Solutions Senior Consultant will: Lead health and benefits consulting engagements for a portfolio of clients, taking ownership of project strategy, execution, and outcomes. Analyze healthcare, financial, and workforce data to identify trends, uncover opportunities, and develop actionable recommendations. Partner with clients to address challenges related to cost management, employee wellbeing, benefits strategy, vendor performance, and evolving workforce needs. Translate complex concepts and analytics into clear, compelling presentations and recommendations for HR, finance, and business leaders. Coordinate across Aon’s specialized resources, including actuarial, pharmacy, wellbeing, compliance, broking, legal, audit, and data analytics teams, to deliver integrated solutions. Build trusted relationships with client stakeholders, insurance carriers, and vendor partners while serving as a primary day-to-day client contact. Anticipate client needs, exercise strong business judgment, and develop innovative, practical solutions that balance cost, risk, competitiveness, and employee experience. Lead project planning and execution, delegate work effectively, review work product, manage issues, and maintain accountability for high-quality client deliverables. Guide and mentor analysts and consultants, helping them strengthen their technical knowledge, consulting capabilities, and client leadership skills. Contribute to Aon’s intellectual capital, best practices, and market-leading solutions through collaboration, knowledge sharing, and participation in practice initiatives. Learn about Aon’s broader capabilities and thoughtfully introduce relevant resources when they can help address a client’s people, risk, or capital challenges. How this opportunity is different What makes Aon different are the people and the culture. Aon colleagues support each other, across geographies and solution lines. Aon has the tools plus depth and breadth of experience to drive great outcomes for our clients, while providing the optimal environment for the career and personal growth of our colleagues. Skills and experience that will lead to success Five to ten years of experience in health and benefits consulting, brokerage, insurance, or a related field, with strong working knowledge of employee benefits. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, including the capacity to interpret financial and healthcare data and turn findings into meaningful insights. Experience leading client projects and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. Excellent communication, facilitation, and presentation skills, with the ability to simplify complex concepts for diverse audiences. Proven ability to build trusted relationships with clients, colleagues, carriers, and external partners. Demonstrated business and financial acumen, with the ability to connect benefits strategy to broader organizational objectives. Strong project management and organizational skills, sound judgment, and exceptional attention to detail. Experience coaching, mentoring, or developing colleagues. Proficiency with Microsoft PowerPoint, Excel, Word, and related business tools. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of industry experience Must have appropriate insurance license/life and health (can be fulfilled post-hire) For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Job.JobTitle: Corporate Public Affairs Director- State and Local
Job.JobDescription:
Bring your policy expertise to a role where research, relationships, and advocacy come together to help shape Aon’s response to an evolving regulatory landscape! This role will report to the Vice President of Government and Public Affairs. The position is office-based in our Chicago office. This role may require ability to travel to 2-3 time per month. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one engaged team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like In this position, you’ll serve as a key point of contact for monitoring and analyzing legislative and regulatory developments that could impact Aon and our industry. You’ll translate policy developments into clear insights for business leaders while supporting government relations, advocacy efforts, regulatory meetings, and industry partnerships. Be the point-of-contact for assigned States Assist with the development and compilation of materials (leave behinds, fact sheets, etc.) for meetings and advocacy work across North America Monitor and track activities in state legislation and for policies relevant to Aon. Review and provide analysis on state legislation and regulatory activities and actions that impact to Aon and the insurance industry. Draft regular legislative activity reports. Attend State regulatory meetings if needed. Administer, manage, assist, and participate in events/meetings as assigned by the Vice President of Government and Public Affairs (Tasks include meeting planning, registration, logistics, speaker recruitment, content development and presenting) How this opportunity is different The Public Affairs Director initiates, prepares, interprets, reviews and monitors legislation and regulations affecting Aon in coordination with Aon business units. This individual will be primarily focused on activities on assigned state regulatory activities as they relate to the insurance industry. They will work directly with business leaders across Aon as well as participate in various capacities with trade associations, advocacy groups as well as industry events. Skills and experience that will lead to success A bachelor’s degree firm an accredited college or university (required); graduate degree in public policy, administration, or business administration (preferred). Policy Analysis: Experience assessing policies to inform decision-making and drive organizational effectiveness and efficiency. Government Relations & Affairs: Experience Managing interactions and relationships with government entities to influence public policy and regulatory decisions; Building and maintaining correspondence with government officials and agencies to influence public policy and decision-making. Researching & Communication: Expertise gathering, analyzing, and synthesizing information from various sources to support decision-making, problem-solving, and strategic planning. Conveying accurate and relevant information to a variety of internal and external audiences through various channels (e.g., emails, meetings, reports, and presentations). MS Office, internet research and database information systems, e-advocacy systems and bill tracking programs preferred. Proficiency managing client relationships to build partnerships, enhance reputation, and achieve organizational objectives. Collaborating with external partners, vendors, and stakeholders to achieve organizational goals and objectives. Efficient, organized work style and an ability to prioritize quickly and confidently and manage multiple deadlines. Ability to understand the long-term impact of policy decisions and strategies. Knowledge of insurance industry (preferred) For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $130,000 - $150,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-RB1 2589861

How this opportunity is different The Executive Services Coordinator provides an elevated level of in-person support for senior leaders through personalized concierge services, coordination of executive activities, and high touch customer service. This role focuses on creating a seamless executive experience by managing day-of logistics, coordinating special arrangements, supporting onboarding activities, and responding to ad hoc requests. This position is a full-time, on-site role requiring five days per week in the office. The role does not perform traditional administrative support responsibilities but serves as a dedicated resource for executive services and limited support for select marketing events. This role is ideal for a highly polished, service-oriented professional who enjoys creating exceptional experiences for senior leaders. You'll serve as a trusted on-site resource, anticipating needs, managing high-priority requests, and coordinating across workplace teams to ensure executive activities run smoothly. The position combines executive concierge services, hospitality, onboarding, priority materials management, and limited event support in a fast-paced professional environment. Working Model Full-time, five days per week in the office in our Chicago, IL office. Requires consistent on-site presence to support senior leaders, executives, designated guests, and executive-facing activities. High-visibility, front-facing position involving regular interaction with executives, colleagues, visitors, vendors, and workplace partners. What the day will look like Executive Services & Experience Deliver high-touch executive support across planned and ad hoc needs, including: Personalized executive onsite support, including special arrangements and private meeting coordination Senior leader day-of-onsite support, including agenda execution, stakeholder coordination, and transitions between activities Executive meeting coordination, room readiness, and logistics support Priority reception and visitor support for executives, and designated guests Executive onboarding support, including workspace readiness and coordination of technology setup Priority document preparation, printing, deliveries, catering, and materials tied to executive needs Triaging urgent, sensitive, or miscellaneous ad hoc requests and tracking them through completion On-Site Event Support Provide limited support for select Marketing events and executive-facing activities, including guest greeting, registration, basic setup, and logistical coordination. Support executive accommodations, hospitality, and event logistics to create a seamless and professional attendee experience. Partner with Marketing and other workplace teams as needed to support smooth event execution while maintaining a premium service experience. Hospitality, Executive Meeting Support, and Organization Coordinate catering, food and beverage requests, deliveries, special arrangements, and hospitality needs for executive meetings and activities. Ensure executive and client-facing spaces are organized, professional, welcoming, and prepared for meetings and scheduled activities. Provide priority reception and hospitality support for executives and designated guests while maintaining a high standard of professionalism, discretion, and service. Deliver a personalized, hospitality-focused experience for senior executives, clients, and visitors while managing multiple priorities with exceptional attention to detail. Anticipate needs, respond quickly to time-sensitive requests, and ensure consistent follow-through while maintaining a polished and professional service experience. Skills and Experiences that Will Lead to Success Communication & Relationship Building Communicate clearly and professionally with executives, colleagues, visitors, vendors, and other participants through strong verbal and written communication. Build trusted relationships and coordinate effectively across Facilities, IT, General Location Services, administrative teams, and other business partners. Discretion, Judgment & Adaptability Exercise sound judgment, professionalism, and discretion when handling confidential information, sensitive executive requests, and high-visibility interactions. Demonstrate a proactive and adaptable approach, anticipating needs, resolving issues efficiently, and adjusting to changing priorities in a fast-paced environment. Technology Proficiency Proficiency with Microsoft Office and workplace productivity tools. Comfortable using workplace technology and coordinating technology support with IT and other workplace partners to support executive meetings and activities. Education & Experience High school diploma or equivalent years of industry experience. Success Measures Consistently deliver a high-quality executive experience through seamless coordination of day-of activities, meetings, onboarding, hospitality, and logistics. Respond to concierge and ad hoc requests promptly and effectively while maintaining exceptional standards of professionalism, confidentiality, service, and discretion. Build strong relationships with senior leaders and workplace partners while coordinating Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $61,500 to $84,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-RW1 #LI-Onsite 2590916
