Job.JobTitle: Account Specialist II - Hybrid, Bannockburn, IL
Job.JobDescription:
Aon is Looking for an Account Specialist II! We currently have a career opportunity for an Account Specialist II to work hybrid out of our Bannockburn, IL office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. Your impact as an Account Specialist II! Resolve inquiries associated with all aspects of Aon Client Services (ACS) service delivery (e.g. output delivery, basic invoice inquiries, etc.) and is accountable for more complex inquiries and client projects. What the day will look like: Identify and retrieve relevant compliance documentation necessary to process renewals, invoices, surplus lines filing and any other ACS deliverables. Perform necessary activities or support in initiating a renewal, processing an invoice, issuing auto IDs, processing surplus lines, issuing emergency certificates, resolving premium account discrepancies, initiating endorsements, processing vehicle suspensions and processing other client requests. Mentor and assist junior staff with more complex account functions. React to field office requests via Broker Desktop tools that require actions in a timely manner. Ensure system of record (Bridge & Broker Desktop) is accurate and current to ensure outputs and client deliverables will be produced according to guidelines and policy detail. Liaise and be responsive to inquiries from outsourced provider to manage and ensure the timeliness and quality of outputs. Upload, index or attach documents in Document Management System. Perform pre – renewal account review with the field office to meet client expectations related to timelines and to ensure accuracy of deliverables (certificates, invoices, endorsements, etc.). Help colleagues troubleshoot and resolve client issues within the ACS team.. Upon policy placement creates policy summaries, schedules of insurance, calculates premium allocations, and provides quality review of all post placement outputs. Manage; Monitor and complete special client projects. Participate in office and client visits Skills and experience that will lead to success: 2 + years of commercial insurance experience highly preferred Property & Casualty brokers license highly preferred P&C license must be maintained or obtained within 6 months of hire Ability to effectively communicate both verbally and written with external and internal clients on client servicing activities Understands operation processes and methodologies; proven ability to work effectively with moderate guidance and supervision. Must have strong Excel skills to import/export data, strong Word skills, some v-look up experience a plus. Successfully operates in a fast-paced output driven environment that requires staff members to multi-task, react quickly and perform task that are not routine. Required: Customer Experience (CX) - Experienced; Customer Relationship Management (CRM) - Experienced; Customer Satisfaction - Experienced Optional: Training Workshops - Intermediate; Troubleshooting - Experienced; Process Improvements - Experienced; Customer Experience Transformation - Experienced; Data Management - Experienced; Operational Excellence - Experienced; Operations Management - Experienced; Data Analysis - Experienced; Performance Analysis - Experienced; Project Management - Intermediate; Quality Control (QC) - Experienced; Report Writing - Experienced; Risk Management - Experienced; Strategic Consulting - Intermediate; Change Management - Intermediate; Client Relationship Management - Experienced Pay Transparency Laws The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $60,000 - $77,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. #LI-HYBRID #LI-MM2 2589118

Effective verbal and written communication and presentation skills. Ability to work collaboratively with clients, carriers, Account Executives, Producers and other internal brokerage resources. What the day will look like Our National Casualty Brokers negotiate and place large, loss-sensitive primary casualty programs for major clients. We seek an individual with experience managing client relationships, strong business acumen, analytical and problem-solving skills, interpersonal skills, effective communication and presentation skills, and the ability to work collaboratively as part of a team. Establish the ability to work with moderately complex National Casualty accounts. Develop skills over time to handle an assigned book of business. Develop and present casualty renewal presentations to clients. Develop and utilize negotiation skills throughout the casualty brokerage process. Establish client-facing skills, including effective oral and written presentations. Develop knowledge of and interaction with casualty markets and establish carrier relationships. Interact with Aon Account Executives, Producers and other internal brokerage resources. Prepare primary casualty submissions. Analyze carrier quotations and perform coverage reviews. Interpret and utilize actuarial results. Develop basic competency in casualty coverage forms and exclusions. Review contractual insurance requirements. Travel as needed for onsite client visits and meetings. Skills and experience that will lead to success 1-3 years of National Casualty Broker or Underwriter experience. Experience in client-facing roles, preferably with commercial clients. Strong analytical, organizational and problem-solving skills. Effective verbal and written communication and presentation skills. Ability to work collaboratively with clients, carriers, Account Executives, Producers and other internal brokerage resources. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Insurance, Risk Management or equivalent years of industry experience. Must have the willingness to obtain an active Property and Casualty license within 90 days of hire. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-JF1 #LI-HYBRID

We are seeking an experienced Workday Adaptive Planning Architect to implement the strategy, roadmap, and architecture of our enterprise planning platform! Serving as both design authority and hands on technical lead, the Architect drives the technical solutioning for major FP&A initiatives from discovery through implementation and support across budgeting, forecasting, workforce planning, scenario modeling, and reporting. Partnering closely with Finance, FP&A, and HR collaborators, this role also provides support for business-critical issues. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed! What the day will look like In this role, you will: Implement the vision, roadmap, governance, and lifecycle management of the Workday Adaptive Planning platform, defining planning technology strategies that support budgeting, forecasting, long range planning, workforce planning, and scenario analysis. Lead the design of complex, scalable Adaptive Planning solutions, ensuring data integrity and seamless information flow across the enterprise. Lead the technical solutioning for all major Adaptive Planning initiatives, from initial discovery and design through implementation and postproduction support. Translate complex business requirements into technical specifications and model architecture, ensuring alignment with overall business strategy, and continuously find opportunities for process improvement and tool optimization for FP&A and other business teams. Architect multidimensional planning models and structures, including dimensions, assumptions, versions, levels, and hierarchies that support: Revenue, expense, and headcount planning. Workforce and long-range goal setting, Driver based forecasting and scenario modeling Own and provide hands on support for urgent and business critical production issues, ensuring swift resolution and minimal business disruption. Serve as a domain authority for business collaborators, fixing process and technical issues in a timely manner, with a focus on upholding guidelines. Configure and maintain Adaptive Planning models, sheets, formulas, assumptions, dimensions, attributes, and workflows, optimizing model performance, usability, and maintainability. Develop and maintain executive reporting solutions and establish governance standards for OfficeConnect reporting, dashboards, scorecards, and key performance indicators. Architect and oversee integrations between Workday Adaptive Planning and Workday Financials, Workday HCM, ERP, data warehouses, payroll, and BI platforms. Apply deep expertise in data modeling, system integration, and performance optimization. Manage security architecture, user provisioning, access controls, and segregation of duties. Own the evaluation and adoption of new Adaptive Planning capabilities, including bi-annual release adoption and AI/LLM enabled planning and forecasting features. Serve as the enterprise design authority for planning architecture, defining standards, and governance for the Adaptive Planning platform. Skills and experience that will lead to success Extensive hands-on Adaptive Planning experience designing, building, and maintaining models, with a proven portfolio of successfully architected and delivered large scale, high impact Adaptive Planning projects. 7+ years of experience supporting FP&A, EPM, or enterprise planning platforms, including 5+ years of hands on Workday Adaptive Planning experience as an architect, lead administrator, or consultant. Deep expertise in data modeling, system integration, and performance optimization within a sophisticated enterprise environment. Deep functional knowledge across adaptive modeling, workforce planning, financial planning and forecasting, OfficeConnect, reporting and dashboards, security administration, and version management. Solid understanding of financial statements, FP&A processes, budgeting, forecasting, workforce planning, and scenario analysis. Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Information Systems, Finance, Accounting, Business, Computer Science, or a related area of study. Workday Pro Adaptive Planning Certification preferred. Background and experience in Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A) preferred. Familiarity with Workday ways of working. Experience integrating planning, ERP, HCM, and other financial systems strongly preferred. PMP, Agile, or related project management certification preferred. Demonstrated commitment to continuous learning and knowing the latest with emerging Adaptive Planning, FP&A, and AI capabilities. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $150k to $160k annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-KH1 2587595

Job.JobTitle: Senior Managing Director, Reinsurance, Treaty Broking
Job.JobDescription:
Senior Managing Director, New Business Treaty Production - Reinsurance Aon is seeking a business development professional to join our Treaty Reinsurance Team. This role will have a direct focus on producing new business, generating new client opportunities, and assisting in the development of sales and marketing strategy designed to cultivate revenue generation opportunities. This role can be based in any of the following locations: Chicago, NY City, Boston, Stamford/Southport, Philadelphia, Atlanta, West Palm Beach, Minneapolis, Dallas, Seattle, San Francisco, Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Works closely in collaboration with broking teams across solution lines to focus efforts on the development of new business and building relationships with clients and prospects that align with business targets. Identifies specific client and prospect needs and develops innovative and cost-effective solutions. Maintains a thorough understanding and knowledge of all available Aon resources and solutions available and matching those to client business requirements. Achieves high client satisfaction by providing exceptional service. Fosters and promotes a team approach to both internal and external business relationship. How this opportunity is different At Aon, we work as one team across geographies and lines of business. Our team approach, collective engagement, and comradery define our culture making Aon a great place to work. As a flat organization, our production brokers will have the ability to create as many opportunities as possible in an entrepreneurial setting that is fully backed by a large organization. This is a unique opportunity to join a firm with established name recognition and have the full support of seasoned placement brokers, world class analytics, dedicated contracts and claims professionals and the backing of the largest global intermediary in the world. Skills and experience that will lead to success Prior business development/sales experience in the reinsurance industry Knowledge of insurance company financial statements to determine best entrance into a company to present Aon in the most optimal position. Exceptional interpersonal skills with capability to interact with major clients to cultivate and maintain strong relationships at a most senior level. Strong market presence within the broking industry Entrepreneurial attitude with high level of accountability for profitability and client satisfaction Ability to drive team(s) to deliver the highest in client service, quality, and results. Known problem-solver who anticipates issues and suggests creative solutions. How we support our colleagues In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions for our colleagues as well. Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued. Aon values an innovative and inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Aon provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran, marital, domestic partner status, or other legally protected status. People with criminal histories are encouraged to apply. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering an inclusive workplace. If you require accommodations during the application or interview process, please let us know. You can request accommodations by emailing us at ReasonableAccommodations@Aon.com or your recruiter. We will work with you to meet your needs and ensure a fair and equitable experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $250,000 to $350,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans in addition to base salary. The amount of any incentive varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance. This role does not accrue vacation. Rather, this role is eligible to take paid time off at the discretion of the employee and management in accordance with company policy and practices. Various other types of leaves of absence; paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. 2578570

Senior Communications Consultant – Consumer Benefit Solutions Are you interested in a communications position that allows you to work as a content writer, project manager, and client consultant? Do you have a knack for explaining sophisticated concepts in easy-to-understand language across multiple platforms? Aon Consumer Benefit Solutions is hiring for a Senior Communications Consultant in a hybrid role with the flexibility to work both virtually and from our Hammonton, NJ office. Although we would prefer a candidate to work in a hybrid role, we are willing to consider a virtual work arrangement for a strong candidate. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Senior Communications Consultants develop open enrollment communications campaigns for clients’ annual benefits enrollment periods. Materials range from posters and postcards to benefit guides, microsites, videos and more. A typical day includes 60% content development, 20% project management, and 20% client consulting. Responsibilities include: Attend client meetings and lead discussion of communications initiatives with a consultative approach creating engagement strategies based on client’s needs Develop and update various benefit communication materials including benefit guides, educational inserts, and other materials as directed Manage various projects from start to finish while coordinating deadlines and prioritizing tasks for multiple projects with short turnaround times Prepare content, while being responsible for edit rounds and proofreading finalized materials Provide product education and assist with special communications projects as needed Assist in reviewing other materials and supporting colleagues as necessary Continuously discover and implement new functions and industry best practices to maximize efficiency Keep abreast of communication and benefit trends How this opportunity is different Senior Communications Consultants work autonomously as the communications subject matter experts for their clients. They manage open enrollment campaigns from design and content creation to distribution and web development. Yet they have the support of the full-service communications team including production, design, and web development. They also collaborate with Health Solutions and Account Management to tailor campaigns to meet clients’ needs and reach their employee populations. Skills and experience that will lead to success 5+ years of experience in content writing or project management; HR and benefits content experience preferred Ability to organize and simultaneously handle multiple projects while working as an integral part of a team, cultivating relationships, and working independently or with minimal direction Effective client service expertise with excellent written and verbal communication skills Ability to think critically and work consultatively across departments and with clients Experience delivering accurate, timely and engaging messages, through print and online channels Education Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Marketing or a related degree Pay Transparency: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $80,000 to $85,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location.The salary range reflected is based on a primary work location of Hammonton, New Jersey. The actual salary may vary for applicants in a different geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. Are you looking to be a member of an industry-leading team? Do you want to deliver innovative and effective solutions to clients? If so, we invite you to join our Account Executive team in Grand Rapids or Southfield, Michigan. We are looking for a client-focused Account Executive who will be responsible for the day-to-day management of Aon’s relationships with assigned clients. You will lead and coordinate client service teams to understand client needs, deliver solutions, and help retain and grow a profitable book of business. Through service, pricing, consultation, and reporting, you will demonstrate the value Aon delivers to clients. This position may be hired at the Account Executive I or Account Executive II level, depending on the candidate’s experience, skills, and qualifications. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Serve as a primary day-to-day contact for assigned clients and coordinate the delivery of services across the Aon client service team. Build, strengthen, and maintain relationships with client contacts and key decision-makers. Understand client needs and coordinate the appropriate Aon resources and capabilities to help achieve client objectives. Lead and coordinate renewal activities, partnering with brokers and other colleagues to develop and deliver client-specific strategies. Develop and evaluate program and coverage options across lines of business and provide recommendations based on client needs. Lead stewardship planning and discussions, communicating the value and results delivered by the Aon team. Retain existing business while identifying opportunities to expand services and coverage with current clients. Support new business opportunities and collaborate with producers and colleagues as appropriate. Prepare and negotiate fee- and commission-based pricing for services, with consideration for client needs and account profitability. Provide clients with information and guidance related to risk management, risk transfer, market conditions, and relevant industry trends. Coordinate resources across Aon teams, business areas, and geographies to address client needs and opportunities. Participate in strategic account planning and complete agreed-upon client strategies. Support invoicing and receivables activities for assigned clients and help ensure timely collections. Run an assigned book of business with responsibility for client service, retention, growth, and overall account performance. How this opportunity is different This opportunity provides the ability to build and handle important client relationships while collaborating with colleagues across Aon to deliver solutions that address clients’ evolving needs. You will have the opportunity to coordinate client strategy, bring together Aon resources, and help strengthen and grow client relationships. The scope and complexity of assigned accounts and level of independent account leadership will vary based on experience. Skills and experience that will lead to success 3–7+ years of relevant insurance experience, including account management, client service, or related experience. Knowledge of the insurance business, major lines of coverage, and client account management. Experience building and maintaining client relationships and coordinating service delivery across internal teams. Ability to handle client relationships and a book of business with a focus on retention, growth, and account profitability. Strong client service, communication, relationship management, and negotiation skills. Ability to identify opportunities to expand services and coverage with existing clients. Ability to collaborate across teams, functions, and business areas to bring appropriate resources and solutions to clients. Experience working with complex client needs and sophisticated insurance programs. Sales or business development experience is a plus. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook. Insurance licensing as required. Education Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of industry experience. Compensation The salary range for this position is $96,500 - $163,200 annually. This salary range is an estimate and the actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus and production incentives in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus and production incentives varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Job.JobTitle: Regional Real Estate & Hospitality (RE&H) Practice Leader, South Region
Job.JobDescription:
Aon Is Looking For A Regional Real Estate & Hospitality (RE&H) Practice Leader As part of an industry-leading team, you will help empower results for our clients by delivering innovative and effective solutions for our Commercial Risk business group in our South Region (Texas, Florida, Atlanta, Carolinas, Nashville). As a Regional RE&H Practice Leader, you will report directly to the Regional Sales Leader with a helix reporting relationship to a local market Account Executive Practice Leader. Your Impact As A Regional RE&H Practice Leader Job Responsibilities: Develop and implement strategy for growth (organic and inorganic) and client retention in alignment with ARS US Retail Regional Leadership: Create and promote organic growth through additional services to meet the needs of existing clients, support of new business opportunities, and new product development Own/develop a personal book of Risk RE&H business of at least $2 million Lead and/or motivate the Real Estate team of brokers, AEs, and salespeople to drive specific regional and national sales and retention plans Partner and lead with regional leadership to drive a comprehensive RE&H strategy across Risk Capital Align and partner with brokerage, sales, account executives as well as regional leadership and other Aon business practices to bring One Aon to current and prospective clients. Support Regional leadership with client and prospect facing meetings in each market where RE&H has been designated as a focused segment. Develop and nurture reliable market relationships to address any client issue which may arise. Organize and lead a RE&H Industry Council comprised of clients and prospects from various geographies within the South region that will meet once annually in person and meet virtually quarterly. Establish standards and oversee national training and implementation in the areas of Client Focus, Differentiation, Carrier Partnerships and Talent. Create industry insights and provide thought leadership based on Aon data, client feedback, insurance carrier input, etc.. Deliver high level consulting analysis and feedback which will feed into specific insurance and risk management product engagements. Meet with clients, prospects and markets to understand current macro risk trends and develop innovative solutions to address emerging risks. In coordination with Regional Leadership, identify, recruit and develop best in class talent with differentiating RE&H industry knowledge. Partner with marketing to promote the Aon brand as a leading advisor to the RE&H industries. Study data (both internal and external) that will help develop customer insights that are unique and useful to meet their needs You Bring Knowledge and Expertise Required Experience: Minimum of 10 years’ experience in Real Estate and/or Hospitality risk management and insurance. Real Estate and/or Hospitality Insurance industry specific experience in meeting with C-suite leaders at all subsectors of real estate including private real estate owners and managers, real estate investment trusts (REITs), commercial real estate service companies and brokers, financial institutions with real estate portfolios, private equity real estate funds, pension funds and their investment managers and advisors, and developers. Knowledge of and experience in building teams and working with both product and geography leadership to enhance results. Great teammate (track record of working as part of and motivating a team). Strong understanding related to complex property exposures including but not limited to catastrophic risk, weather risk, complex shared and layered programs, alternative risk programs, modelling, enhanced casualty risks as well as already established insurance carrier relationships. Strong understanding of alternative risk financing for Real Estate organizations including the use of captive insurance companies. Ability to discuss high level traditional and enterprise risk issues with senior leadership at clients, prospects, and markets. Strong understanding of macro risk trends as well as governance and compliance issues. Real Estate and/or Hospitality Risk Management or other relevant RE&H risk and insurance experience necessary. Track record of involvement in associations and other efforts for the advancement of risk management and risk financing. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience MBA and other advanced degree preferred CPCU preferred. The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $250,000 to $325,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus or production incentives in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus or production incentives varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. How we support our colleagues Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions for our colleagues as well. Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued. Aon values an innovative and inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Aon provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran, marital, domestic partner status, or other legally protected status. People with criminal histories are encouraged to apply. If you would like to learn more about the reasonable accommodations we provide, email ReasonableAccommodations@Aon.com For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Job.JobTitle: Health Solutions Pharmacy Financial Senior Consultant
Job.JobDescription:
Aon is looking for a Pharmacy Financial Sr. Consultant The Pharmacy Financial Sr. Consultant will work within the Pharmacy Financial Analytic Team in supporting the broader Pharmacy Team on a range of activities, including but not limited to providing technical, financial and consultative support to consulting staff on a variety of client projects. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive, team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like: Active member of the Pharmacy Financial Team Exceptional quantitative and analytical skills: Analytical thinking systematically tests and probes to discover trends and eliminate potential problems Project management experience: Establishes priorities for multiple tasks/projects based on timeliness, importance, and urgency of project completion. Assist with the execution of some or all of the following types of consulting projects: RFPs Market Checks Preparing engagement/client materials for sales and marketing efforts Procurement/Renewal projects Vendor management, including negotiations, problem resolution, and regional/local interface Benefit strategy and clinical program review Plan design benchmarking Support Pharmacy team in the area of pharmacy benefits, developing knowledge on best practices and market trends, and contributing to the developments and enhancement of new and existing products and services Responds quickly to client and colleague requests and works to provide timely and accurate information and documentation; Works with a high level of interest, energy and enthusiasm to meet or exceeds client expectations. Teamwork and Resource Management: Understands and values all roles and functions needed to complete client projects and provide on-going service; Communicates and works well with colleagues at all levels and is viewed as a team player Ethical Behavior: Adheres to professional standards and ethics in one’s field and demonstrates the highest level of integrity and honesty in all interactions Skills and experience that will lead to success 3+ years of industry experience Proficiency in PBM pricing structures and guarantees Experience analyzing pharmacy data Deep understanding of the relationship between PBMs and Employer Groups Ability to strategically interpret the financial impact of PBM formularies and programs on Employer Group contracts Self-starter with the aptitude to serve clients and manage project work from start to finish Strong presentation and communication skills Experience working with large claim data sets; experience with SQL is a bonus Education: Bachelors degree. Preferred majors: Economics, Finance, Accounting, Mathematics, Statistics, Risk Management, Actuarial Science Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $80,000.00 - $130,000.00 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. #LI-LR1 #LI-HYBRID #LI-REMOTE 2583205

As part of an industry-leading global communications team, you will help our firm share stories with external stakeholders and grow awareness and understanding of how Aon shapes decisions for the better – to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Communications plays a critical role in shaping perceptions within Aon and outside our firm about how we help clients make better decisions and deliver positive outcomes for colleagues, clients and shareholders. We’re a team that works hard, supports each other and has fun while making an impact, and we’re looking to further build on the senior talent within our global communications team. Aon’s Senor Director, media relations will be responsible for day-to-day media engagement – maintaining strong relationships with tier one, business and trade reporters – serve as a key storyteller and spokesperson for the firm, lead Aon’s social media strategy and execution, and lead and mentor a proactive, strategic, resourceful media relations team. This Aon leader will also lead a global Center of Excellence for media relations and external positioning to further develop and align standard methodologies across the firm. Job Responsibilities: Develop journalist relationships, pitch and secure media coverage and respond to media queries to advance commercial objectives and influence positive perceptions of Aon's reputation, thought leadership and social impact. Build Aon’s share of voice across four key mega trends shaping client need across our Risk Capital and Human Capital capabilities. Implement distribution of corporate press releases, media advisories and updates shared via Aon’s newsroom. Partner with multiple team members developing integrated, aligned messaging plans and content articulating our firm’s growth strategy, brand strategy, progress with key initiatives and thought-leadership perspectives. Lead a global Center of Excellence for media engagement to drive an aligned and coordinated approach to proactive and reactive media relations and issues management throughout the firm, including Aon’s Marketing & Communications organization and agency relationships. Lead Center of Excellence media monitoring and reporting platforms allowing Communications teams throughout Marketing & Communications to generate consistent reports on coverage (trends, share of voice, sentiment, etc.), social media conversation and other indicators that enable us to articulate the impact we drive and find opportunities for refining our approach. Develop and lead a program preparing key leaders and others throughout the firm to participate in media interviews and public speaking opportunities. Skills and experience that will lead to success Experience/Credentials: 10+ years in communications and a proven track record of producing and leading the creation of compelling, sophisticated communications in support of global business objectives. A bachelor's degree. Experience with developing and leading national and local media relationships for a publicly traded and global brand, preferably in the professional/financial services, consulting, or technology industry. Ability to lead sophisticated, sensitive communication initiatives, carefully navigating each situation to balance individual and organizational agendas. Proven track record of advising and building trusted relationships with senior leaders, including C-suite-level executives, to support media relations and external positioning strategies and achieve corporate objectives. Crisis and issues management experience preferred. Characteristics: Creative problem solver with a desire and ability to seek opportunities for continuous improvement. Ability and willingness to perform both strategic and tactical elements of the role with a steadfast commitment to quality and detail. A principled commitment to quality and detail. Self-motivated, goal-oriented self-starter with a sense of urgency and strong desire to work entrepreneurially. Team-oriented with a strong sense of commitment to colleagues and internal clients, projecting a positive attitude and excelling at encouraging and coaching team members. A leader who projects a positive demeanor and excels at encouraging and coaching team members. Experience and comfort level leading through influence and helping leaders arrive at consensus. Skills: Exceptional writing and editing skills with proven expertise using different styles and “voice” to reflect the nature of the individual, audience and message. Ability to communicate sophisticated concepts simply and visually. Equally comfortable telling the story in “words” and “numbers.” Exceptional organizational skills, including an ability to run multiple priorities and projects. Strong project management skills with the ability to complete programs with speed, accuracy and efficiency. Experience using traditional owned and earned channels, including multi-media and social media. How we support our colleagues In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage a diverse workforce. Plus, our agile, inclusive environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions, but we also recognize that flexibility goes beyond just the place of work... and we are all for it. We call this Smart Working! Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. Job.CustomJobTypeName: Human Resources & Training, Operations & Policy Administration
Job.JobDescription:
We're seeking a Project Workers Compensation Administrator! This is an exciting opportunity to help manage complex workers' compensation programs supporting large-scale projects while partnering with project leadership, insurers, medical professionals, and legal teams to deliver positive claim outcomes and reduce organizational risk. *******This is a fully onsite role, working directly with the client at their Port Arthur, TX location.******* Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. How this opportunity is different The Claims Administrator is responsible for implementing all aspects of the project workers’ compensation program (statutory and USL&H) for Port Arthur LNG and all Contractor Coordinated Insurance Program (CCIP) enrollees. This position will also assist with the Administration of auto and other insured claims. Position is located at the project construction site with an anticipated work schedule of 48 hours per week. While this is an Aon position, the employee is seconded to Bechtel. The Claims Administrator works under the direction of Bechtel's Head of Workers' Compensation and the Aon Claims Director, acting independently to manage routine Matters while keeping Bechtel Insured Claims team fully informed at all stages. What the day will look like Communicates effectively with injured workers, medical professionals, insurers, brokers, internal/external counsel, corporate management, and various related regulatory agencies. Develops and maintains project-specific workers’ compensation claims manual, medical panel, related processes and procedures for statutory and USL&H claims. Implements improvements based on lessons learned, legislative changes or Court decisions, and Bechtel operating imperatives. Assists with subcontractor CCIP enrollment and provides workers’ compensation orientation to subcontractors. Develops and provides onsite training related to workers’ compensation. Under the guidance of the Workers’ Compensation Risk Manager, develops and prepares regular reports outlining project claims performance. Monitors claims activity to identify early negative claim trends or other issues that may negatively impact project performance. Is responsible for oversight and processing of workers’ compensation claims: Responsible for initiating, preparing, and maintaining all documentation associated with claims. Investigates and documents eligibility for workers’ compensation benefits and communicates same to insurer and related interested parties. Assists with investigation and coordination of issues surrounding subrogation. Interprets laws and regulations, determines appropriate courses of action, and presents solutions to resolve the claims. Identifies potential subrogation issues. Monitors claim resolution activities implemented by insurer(s) and employers. Maintains Project Risk Management Information System (RMIS). Directs and monitors the activities and performance of Bechtel’s insurance provider to ensure compliance with applicable regulations. Implements, monitors, and ensures compliance of “Special Account” requirements. Conducts regular claim reviews, claim audits and prepares related reports. Interfaces with insurer to effectively manage claims, including but not limited to authorizing claim reserve changes, authorizing insurer referral to outside counsel, and assessing and approving settlement strategies. Coordinates and supports early return to work. Manages relationships with onsite clinic, panel/network physicians and other medical providers, to ensure effective claims management and return to work. Works with injured worker and supervision on developing and implementing return to work plan. Assists in management fitness for duty and ADA accommodation issues as needed. Assists Bechtel Risk Management in the defense of litigation or other complex case support. (i.e., responding to interrogatories and other discovery requests). Assists with gathering information and filing auto and other insured claims. Assists with administration of auto and other insured claims as needed. Performs other tasks as required by Bechtel Risk Management. Skills and experience that will lead to success 5+ years of experience in the field or in a related area or in a related area. Extensive knowledge of / experience with workers’ compensation and occupational rehabilitation procedures, practices and processes. Extensive knowledge of claim’s resolution techniques and strategies, legal principles related to claim resolution and familiarity with all phases of the litigation process. Working knowledge of / experience with bodily injury and 1st and 3rd party property damage claims practices and processes. Working knowledge of / experience with auto and other insured claims practices and procedures. Relies on experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals. Highly skilled in written and verbal communication. Bilingual language proficiency (i.e., English and Spanish) is a plus. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of industry Workers’ Compensation experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $60,000 to $80,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-RW1 #LI-Onsite 2587758

Aon is hiring for a Reverse Flow- Account Executive/Broker for our Small and Medium Enterprise group. This is a hybrid role with the flexibility to work both virtually and from any of our Aon offices. As an Account Executive-Reverse Flow with Aon, you will engage with existing clients and pre-identified prospects to ensure appropriate coverage for their needs and recommend additional solutions, where warranted. Each of your clients will be a US subsidiary of a foreign-owned parent company, whose Global Program is managed and directed by Aon partners overseas. Aon is a leader in the Insuretech space, and this is a unique opportunity for your input as an Account Executive to contribute to the strategic direction of the company. If a client-focused, technology-driven, and fast-paced environment are something you’re looking for, look no further Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Job.JobDescription:
Vice President/Broker II - FSG Currently we have an exciting career opportunity for a Vice President/Broker II (FSG) within Aon Commercial Risk Solutions’ Financial Services Group (“FSG”). Are you ready to begin a new challenge and work with the best Insurance Professionals in the business? Then this just maybe the new opportunity you are looking for! This opportunity is a hybrid role to work from our Chicago, IL office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Responsible for assessing client needs, crafting solutions and negotiating with insurance carriers to acquire coverage that is in a client’s best interests. Coverages include: Directors and Officers Liability, Employment Practices Liability, Crime, Fiduciary Liability, and Kidnap/Ransom. Analyze and present sophisticated insurance contract concepts. Effectively communicate renewal strategies and results to clients, including product/structure overviews, insurance market dynamics, litigation trends and contract features. Utilize refined technical skills including client analysis / underwriting and insurance program diagnostic skills to continually improve client programs and build opportunity with prospective client programs. Maintain effective working relationships with all external client contacts, prospects (primarily in the department of treasury, legal departments, or risk management). Build internal working relationships with Aon product specialists, brokers, producers and account executives. Develop and deliver client and prospect presentations in conjunction with senior team members. Utilize effective underwriter relationships to improve broking results via a deep understanding of marketplace, carrier appetite and capabilities to be able to leverage carriers effectively. Engage the Aon FSG claims and legal advocacy group for claim administration and counsel as per established protocols and as advised by senior team member. Apply effective negotiation skills to secure optimal broking results for clients. How this opportunity is different The Financial Services Group (FSG) is Aon’s dedicated management liability insurance specialty practice with deep experience in directors’ and officers’ (D&O), employment practices liability (EPL), fiduciary, crime, and kidnap, ransom, and extortion (KRE). FSG works closely with Aon’s Cyber Solutions Cyber Broking team to deliver seamless advice and insurance placement across key financial lines, including errors and omissions (E&O). The FSG team comprises insurance professionals dedicated to serving the needs of our clients. Skills and experience that will lead to success Required Experience 5+ years in brokering, underwriting, and / or other relevant executive liability proven experience. Excellent negotiation skills. Strong experience using Microsoft Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel and Outlook) Clear and effective written and verbal expression. Property & Casualty license required within 6 months of hire date. Education: Bachelor’s degree required or equivalent years of industry experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. The salary range reflected is based on a primary work location of Illinois. The actual salary may vary for applicants in a different geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. Job.JobTitle: Senior Manager, Financial Controls and SOX
Job.JobDescription:
The Aon Global SOX Team is seeking an experienced Senior Manager, Financial Controls & SOX to help shape and strengthen financial controls across a complex, global organization. This hybrid role may be based virtually or from one of Aon’s US offices. This is an opportunity for a seasoned controls professional to serve as a subject matter expert and transformation leader, partnering across Finance, Technology and business teams to embed effective controls into evolving processes, systems and operating models. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Serve as a financial controls and SOX subject matter expert, providing guidance on complex financial reporting risks, control design and governance matters. Provide controls leadership for significant Finance, technology and organizational transformation initiatives, including process redesign, system implementations, automation, shared-service transitions, M&A integrations and operating model changes. Partner with Finance, Technology and business leaders to identify financial reporting risks and embed effective controls into future-state processes and systems. Translate changes in processes, systems, data and organizational responsibilities into clear risk and control requirements. Design and influence scalable, sustainable control solutions, including preventive and detective controls, segregation of duties, governance and monitoring. Lead risk and control transition planning, including implementation milestones, dependencies, readiness assessments, interim controls and post-implementation stabilization. Apply strong project management discipline to controls initiatives by establishing clear scope, workplans, deliverables, ownership, milestones, risks and escalation protocols. Challenge transformation programs constructively to ensure control requirements are incorporated early in the design and implementation lifecycle. Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, centralize and automate controls while maintaining appropriate risk mitigation. Evaluate control readiness ahead of critical transformation milestones and communicate gaps, risks and recommendations to leadership. Review and challenge control design, testing conclusions, deficiencies and remediation plans to promote effective and sustainable outcomes. Support the Global SOX Program, including SOX 302 and 404, risk assessment, control evaluation, testing, deficiency assessment and remediation. Lead cross-functional controls initiatives across multiple businesses, functions and geographies, driving alignment, accountability and timely execution. Partner with control owners, transformation teams, Finance and Technology leadership, internal assessors and external auditors. Communicate significant control matters, transformation risks, key decisions and remediation progress clearly and effectively to senior leadership. How this opportunity is different The Senior Manager will bring deep financial controls and SOX expertise together with strong transformation and project management capabilities. The successful candidate will help translate complex business and technology change into practical, scalable and sustainable control solutions, while helping drive the continued evolution of Aon’s Global SOX Program. Skills and experience that will lead to success Deep knowledge of SOX, internal controls and financial reporting risk, including experience with both manual and automated control environments. Strong understanding of key Finance and accounting processes, such as record-to-report, procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, payroll, treasury and financial close and reporting. Demonstrated experience designing, evaluating and implementing controls within a large, complex, global organization. Experience serving as a controls subject matter expert within major business, Finance or technology transformation programs. Ability to understand complex process and technology changes and translate them into practical financial reporting risks and control solutions. A transformation mindset with demonstrated success developing simplified, standardized, scalable and sustainable controls. Strong project and program management capabilities, including experience managing scope, workplans, milestones, dependencies, risks and multiple stakeholder groups. Demonstrated ability to lead complex initiatives and drive outcomes through others in a matrixed organization. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify root causes and develop sustainable solutions. Ability to balance business objectives, transformation timelines and control requirements while maintaining appropriate risk management. Strong executive presence and the ability to influence, advise and constructively challenge senior stakeholders. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to make complex control matters clear and actionable. Ability to successfully manage multiple priorities across functions, businesses and geographies. High level of ownership, accountability and comfort operating in a changing environment. Education and experience Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business or a related field; advanced degree preferred. 8+ years of progressive experience in SOX, internal controls, audit, controllership, finance transformation or a related discipline. Experience working within a large, multinational or complex organization strongly preferred. Demonstrated experience supporting or leading controls activities associated with Finance transformations, system implementations, organizational redesign, shared-service transitions, automation or M&A integrations. Experience leading complex, cross-functional projects with multiple stakeholders and dependencies. Professional certification such as CPA, ACA, ACCA, CIA or CISA preferred. Project management or process improvement credentials such as PMP, PRINCE2 or Lean Six Sigma are beneficial. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $130,000 - $155,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. The salary range reflected is based on a primary work location of Chicago, Illinois. The actual salary may vary for applicants in a different geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-SP1 #LI-HYBRID 2592114

Job.JobTitle: Executive Benefits Analyst - Individual Disability Insurance
Job.JobDescription:
Executive Benefits Analyst Join the Aon Executive benefits team and develop meaningful relationships with clients and plan participants through administration of their supplemental benefit program. This is a hybrid role with the flexibility to work both virtually and from our Bloomington, MN or Atlanta, GA offices. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Own day-to-day administration of individual disability insurance (IDI) plans, including status changes, enrollment, implementation, and renewal activities Recognize out of scope requests and seek appropriate guidance Audit and analyze census, policy, and plan data Drive accurate financial reporting and revenue recognition by updating revenue forecasts Run queries to extract, validate, and analyze data in support of plan administration and decision-making. Adjust queries as necessary Manage master enrollment files and email distribution lists Consistently track tasks and deadlines to ensure accuracy and avoid misses Prepare renewal files and related documentation, ensuring alignment between plan design, pricing, and administrative processes Interface directly with clients and carriers to support enrollments and renewals, ensuring accuracy and timely execution Address most participant inquiries independently Use strong written and verbal communication skills to create clear, professional client and internal communications, and support stewardship discussions Demonstrate a growing understanding of plan design, service strategies, and risk mitigation Offer ideas for process or plan improvements and participate in operational task forces Contribute to training efforts and serve as an informal mentor to junior staff, sharing technical expertise and best practices within the solution line Skills and experience that will lead to success Experience with relevant executive benefit programs and plan administration Customer service or client-facing experience Strong written and verbal communication skills High attention to detail and strong organizational skills Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook) Ability to handle confidential information with discretion Analytical thinking and problem-solving capability Ability to effectively leverage AI tools to enhance work quality and efficiency Education Bachelor’s degree in relevant field or equivalent years of industry experience. Pay Transparency The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $60,000 - $75,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location.
