Job.JobTitle: M&A Due Diligence Consultant - Vice President
Job.JobDescription:
Aon Is looking for a risk & insurance due diligence consultant in Aon’s M&A and Transaction Advisory Solutions practice in New York, New York. We currently have an exciting career opportunity for an experienced P&C professional within our Transaction Advisory Services team! As part of an industry-leading team, you will help empower results for our clients by delivering innovative and effective solutions as part of a global team delivering M&A services to Private Equity and Corporate clients. As a risk & insurance due diligence consultant, you will work closely with NY region team reporting into the regional leader. How this opportunity is different: Work on sophisticated Property and Casualty due diligence projects within our M&A team. Aon has an inclusive culture, where you get to work with many different personality types while working with a lively team! There are opportunities for growth, as we are generating new opportunities throughout this division. Work Style: Hybrid - In office 3 days a week. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. Job Responsibilities: Lead due diligence projects of varying complexity. Communicate internally with brokers, coverage / exposure experts, producers, client service team and M&A team members and collaborate to develop findings and solutions. Communicate externally on daily basis as trusted advisor with private equity firms, target companies or their representatives. Execute and deliver accurate and professional due diligence reports to clients. Analyze and provide technical input on insurance coverage, claims history, insurance-related collateral, insurance-related financial expense, surety bonds and insurance sections of the draft purchase agreement. Identify transaction issues and work with clients’ other third-party advisors to develop resolution. Collaborate with producers to build and maintain relationships with ongoing clients and convert due diligence targets to ongoing clients. Communicate and capture the value that Aon brings even to the most challenging situations. Prepare spreadsheets and analyze data. Prepare proposals and make presentations to clients and prospects. Some travel required. Required Skills & Experience: You Bring Knowledge and Expertise Property and Casualty insurance technical proficiency. Broad knowledge of specialty insurance including property, casualty, cyber, E&O, financial lines, environmental, group captives and others. Financial – basic understanding of financial statements, accounting. Project management – coordinate activities and information flow from a group of people within specified time frame. Strategic and analytical skills – attention to detail but able to draw conclusions. Strong communication skills (written and oral) – ability to communicate well and at the appropriate level with a wide range of people. Ability to perform under stress / tight time frames. Ability to develop relationships / build confidence of others (both internally and externally) based upon work performed. Ability to work on multiple projects at one time. Results oriented. Proficiency with Word, Excel, Power Point. Broker’s license 10+ years of insurance experience are highly preferred. Preferred Experience: CPCU a plus MBA, CPA or JD a plus Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in related field The salary range for this position (for U.S. applicants) is $140,000 to $180,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. #LI-YT1 #LI-HYBRID 2587714

Job.JobTitle: Assistant Vice President, Financial Services Group
Job.JobDescription:
Assistant Vice President/Broker II – Financial Services Group Are you ready to begin a new challenge and work with the best Insurance Professionals in the business? Then this just maybe the new opportunity you are looking for! This Broker role is responsible for developing and implementing strategic risk management solutions for large, global clients. This includes the design, marketing and service management of insurance programs in numerous industry sectors. This individual should have validated peer market relationships and emerging senior market relationships. This opportunity is a hybrid role to work from our Chicago, IL office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Responsible for assessing client needs, designing solutions and negotiating with insurance carriers to obtain coverage that is in a client’s best interests. Professional who develops and leads client relationships, account strategies and insurance marketing activities for book of business. Acts as the primary negotiator in obtaining the most effective insurance programs to address client needs. Works closely with Team Leaders, Producers, Account Executives and other client facing team members to understand and deliver on client’s needs. Identifies and analyzes client exposures while regularly collaborating with junior associates to develop effective client risk treatment and placement strategies. Obtains the most appropriate program coverage based upon client objectives by developing and executing, in conjunction with the client, an agreed upon structure and strategy. Serves as a source of information concerning market trends, pricing practices and other underwriting policies. May participate in development of department policies and procedures and implements them in assigned areas. Provides guidance to more junior staff Advises the overall development and growth of personal book of business and assists in the development of the team members. Capable of working on sophisticated accounts with autonomy. AVP’s and New VP’s play a supporting role in larger, more sophisticated accounts. Support team in the solicitation and servicing of clients and the broking of their insurance programs. Advising, placing and servicing mid-size accounts with minimal direct supervision for own portfolio of clients. Expert comparison and analysis of insurance policies and determination of needed enhancements. How this opportunity is different The broker will be instrumental in the analysis of clients’ exposures to identify and mitigate risk as well as responsible for the coordination of the placement and day-to-day activities on accounts. Skills and experience that will lead to success Attention to detail, ability to multi-task, exceptional organizational skills, ability to make and communicate difficult decisions. Minimum of 5+ years of financial lines insurance brokerage and/or underwriting experience with a concentration on Directors & Officers Liability, Employment Practices, Fiduciary, Crime and Special Risk. Solid understanding of carrier underwriting practices & processes. Proven leadership skills in working with teams and experience collaborating with clients to successfully exceed client expectations. Confirmed client-facing skills including effective presentations & communications. Validated organization and ability to work with others. Experience in resource deployment and utilization management. Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact effectively at various levels. Effectively operates in a fast-paced driven environment that requires managing multiple tasks simultaneously. Sales experience preferred and finance background a plus. Must maintain appropriate broker’s license. Proficient in Microsoft Office suite of products. Education: Bachelor’s degree required or equivalent years of proven experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $120,000 - $165,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. The salary range reflected is based on a primary work location of Illinois. The actual salary may vary for applicants in a different geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. #LI-KA1 #LI-HYBRID 2582877

This includes the design, marketing and service management of insurance programs in numerous industry sectors. This individual should have proven peer market relationships and emerging senior market relationships. This position offers a hybrid arrangement to work from our New York, NY office. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Responsible for assessing client needs, designing solutions and negotiating with insurance carriers to obtain coverage that is in a client’s best interests. Professional who develops and manages client relationships, account strategies and insurance marketing activities for book of business. Acts as the primary negotiator in obtaining the most effective insurance programs to address client needs. Works closely with Team Leaders, Producers, Account Executives and other client facing team members to understand and deliver on client’s needs. Identifies and analyzes client exposures with routine assistance of junior team members to develop effective client risk treatment and placement strategies. Obtains the most appropriate program coverage based upon client objectives by developing and executing, in conjunction with the client, an agreed upon structure and strategy. Serves as a source of information concerning market trends, pricing practices and other underwriting policies. May participate in development of department policies and procedures and implements them in assigned areas. Provides guidance to more junior staff Advises the overall development and growth of personal book of business and assists in the development of the team members. Capable of working on complex accounts with autonomy. AVP’s and New VP’s play a supporting role in larger, more complex accounts. Support team in the solicitation and servicing of clients and the broking of their insurance programs. Advising, placing and servicing mid-size accounts with minimal direct supervision for own portfolio of clients. Expert comparison and analysis of insurance policies and determination of needed enhancements. How this opportunity is different The broker will be instrumental in the analysis of clients’ exposures to identify and mitigate risk as well as responsible for the coordination of the placement and day-to-day activities on accounts. Skills and experience that will lead to success Attention to detail, ability to multi-task, exceptional organizational skills, ability to make and communicate difficult decisions. Minimum of 3+ years of financial lines insurance brokerage and/or underwriting experience with a concentration on Directors & Officers Liability, Employment Practices, Fiduciary, Crime and Special Risk. Effective solid understanding of carrier underwriting practices & processes. Validated leadership skills in working with teams and ability to work with clients and to successfully exceed client expectations. Confirmed client-facing skills including effective presentations & communications. Shown organization and capacity to collaborate effectively with others. Experience in resource deployment and utilization management. Strong communication skills, enabling effective interaction at various levels. Successfully operates in a fast-paced driven environment that requires the ability to handle several tasks simultaneously. Sales experience preferred and finance background a plus. Must maintain appropriate broker’s license. Proficient in Microsoft Office suite of products. Education: Bachelor’s degree required or equivalent years of validated experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Job.JobTitle: Early Careers: RMI Summer Internship - Risk Capital & Reinsurance
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Risk Management / Loss Control, Accounting / Finance
Job.JobDescription:
Aon invites ambitious college rising seniors to join our 2027 Summer Internship Program in Risk Capital and Reinsurance Solutions. These opportunities are designed for students pursuing a Risk Management & Insurance (RMI) degree or who have gained relevant insurance experience through a prior internship. Immerse yourself in a unique and exciting environment as you sample a career that offers global reach and makes a tangible impact on our clients! Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What is Reinsurance? Reinsurance is insurance for insurance companies; it's a sophisticated, growing and exciting area to launch and develop a career. Insurers are at the heart of creating a more resilient world but face an increasingly dynamic environment with interconnected, emerging risks and blustery competition. Now more than ever, insurers require more comprehensive services and global insight to better understand and address their strategic, multi-faceted business needs across growth, capital, operational efficiency and talent. Embedded in the insurance industry, we live its impact, complexities and potential - so we know how to listen better and interpret clients’ needs. We provide risk transfer, claims advocacy and capital management solutions to help our re/insurance clients reduce volatility and build more resilient businesses, governments and communities. What the day will look like in Reinsurance Solutions Interns within Aon's Reinsurance Solutions team gain valuable experience by assisting account executives through both client work and internal projects. With the opportunity to learn and grow as you collaborate with cross-functional teams, you'll gain experience and exposure across a broad segment of clients as well. What is Risk Capital? Businesses and communities face a constantly evolving range of interconnected risks. Our Risk Capital advisors bring the breadth of our expertise, relationships and analytics to unlock capital, which we access across markets, geographies and a variety of financial instruments to help organizations grow. This distributed team assesses and advises on the risk a company has, or could have, and mitigates it through the placement of various insurance products and policies. What the day will look like in Risk Capital Interns within Risk Capital gain valuable experience assisting account executives on assigned accounts across various industries. You'll collaborate with expert colleagues to assess and mitigate risks across diverse industries while you engage in innovative solutions to deliver tailored risk management strategies, fostering profit, growth, and continuity for our clients. How this opportunity is different This is a 10-week paid program across various U.S. offices with access to leaders through weekly learning sessions and a chance to interact with colleagues globally. You will engage in challenging client projects with the benefit of continuous formal and informal feedback and the enjoyment of social outings and community service activities throughout your internship! Skills and experience that will lead to success Desire to work on a team with the capability for independent work Driven by results and accomplishing tasks Strong critical thinking, problem-solving and analytical skills Alignment with values of integrity, client commitment and community dedication Adaptability, quick learning ability and professional demeanor Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel Involvement in extracurricular activities Qualifications Rising seniors graduating between December 2027 – June 2028, with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0, who meet at least one of the following criteria: Pursuing a degree in Risk Management & Insurance (RMI); or Have relevant insurance experience through a prior internship. Additional Summer 2027 internship opportunities open to students across a broader range of academic backgrounds and experiences are expected to be posted in January. Please Note: For this role you must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future. What sets our program apart from the rest? Explore Aon’s culture and business areas, developing practical skills vital for future success and postgraduate opportunities. Engage in weekly spotlights, community outreach events and networking opportunities with peers, fostering an understanding of exceeding client expectations and delivering distinct products and services. Development Planning Participate in a comprehensive development plan that includes deeply understanding Aon’s business areas, ethical standards, professional environment, networking opportunities, learning internal systems, and honing interpersonal and team-building skills through collaboration events and colleague networking opportunities. Future Opportunities Our program offers meaningful exposure to Aon, preparing interns for short-term and long-term career opportunities. Outstanding interns may potentially receive offers to join Aon’s Launch Program, an early careers development opportunity, as a full-time colleague with generous benefits and a tangible career path. How we support our colleagues In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage a diverse workforce. Plus, our agile, inclusive environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions, but we also recognize that flexibility goes beyond just the place of work... and we are all for it. We call this Smart Working! The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $21.60 - $27.60 hourly. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. Aon offers a benefits package for temporary and seasonal employees who will work 20 or more hours per week including: medical, dental, and vision insurance at the employee’s expense, critical illness insurance, 10 Company holidays per calendar year (paid, if eligible), paid sick leave as provided under state and local law, and a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions. Eligibility for benefits are governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued. Aon values an innovative, diverse workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Aon provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran, marital, domestic partner status, or other legally protected status. People with criminal histories are encouraged to apply. We welcome applications from all and provide individuals with disabilities with reasonable adjustments to participate in the job application, interview process and to perform essential job functions once onboard. If you would like to learn more about the reasonable accommodations we provide, email ReasonableAccommodations@Aon.com For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Capital Modeling Associate Actuarial Director Location: Chicago IL, New York, New York, Bloomington MN. Other Locations will be considered for the right candidate. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. The Strategy and Technology Group (STG) is Aon’s global consulting and technology business serving insurers, reinsurers, MGAs, program administrators, and other participants across the insurance value chain. STG pairs Aon’s proprietary data, analytics, and global network of insurance experts with a consulting model built on senior-level expertise and distinctive insight. What the Day Will Look Like Lead Risk & Capital Modeling Engagements Design, build, enhance, validate, and interpret stochastic risk and capital models for P&C insurers, reinsurers, and other insurance clients. Apply hands-on expertise in capital modeling platforms (ReMetrica experience preferred but not required) to deliver client solutions from day one. Lead risk, volatility, and asset parameterization, including calibration, dependency structures, scenario design, validation, and documentation. Develop multi-year financial and cash flow projections integrating underwriting, reserving, reinsurance, investments, taxation, liquidity, and management actions. Perform economic capital, rating agency, stress testing, capital allocation, and capital adequacy analyses. Support enterprise risk management initiatives, including risk appetite frameworks, tolerances, limits, targets, and management reporting. Translate complex modeling results into actionable recommendations on capital strategy, reinsurance, growth, business mix, liquidity, and risk management. Maintain strong model governance through rigorous controls, documentation, peer review, and quality assurance. Manage Client Engagements Lead small to mid-sized consulting engagements, managing scope, timelines, budgets, staffing, quality, and client communication. Serve as a trusted advisor to actuarial, risk, finance, underwriting, treasury, investment, and executive stakeholders. Contribute as a workstream lead on large, multidisciplinary projects across actuarial, strategy, reinsurance, finance, and analytics teams. Structure complex business problems, develop analytical approaches, and deliver defensible, decision-ready solutions. Communicate technical findings clearly, highlighting implications, trade-offs, limitations, and recommendations. Support Strategic & Transactional Advisory Work Contribute to complex assignments including mergers and acquisitions, capital raises, sidecars, loss portfolio transfers, reinsurance strategies, and legal entity restructuring. Assess the impact of transaction structures, financing, investments, reinsurance, and management actions on risk, earnings volatility, liquidity, and capital. Partner with senior colleagues to integrate actuarial, financial, strategic, and transaction advisory solutions. Contribute to Business Growth Help clients define problems, clarify objectives, and develop solutions that address strategic business needs. Support proposals, RFP responses, client presentations, thought leadership, benchmarking studies, and industry events. Collaborate across Aon to develop integrated solutions spanning capital modeling, enterprise risk management, reserving, pricing, reinsurance, and transaction advisory. Identify growth opportunities within client relationships and contribute to the continued expansion of the practice. Qualifications Required Approximately 5-9 years of P&C actuarial, risk, capital modeling, or insurance consulting experience. Job.JobDescription:
Aon is looking for a US Human Capital Due Diligence Assistant Vice President in Aon’s M&A and Transaction Advisory Solutions practice in New York, New York. We currently have an exciting career opportunity for an experienced US Human Capital professional within our Transaction Advisory Services team! As part of an industry-leading team, you will help empower results for our clients by delivering innovative and effective solutions as part of our M&A and Transaction Advisory Services business group within Commercial Risk Solutions. As a US Human Capital Due Diligence Assistant Vice President, you will work closely and report into our US Human Capital Diligence team in New York. This is a hybrid role with the flexibility to work both virtually and from our New York, NY office (3 days in office per week). Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like: Lead US human capital due diligence projects of varying complexity. Work directly with private equity or corporate clients as well as their other outside advisors, which typically include accounting and financial, legal, and tax experts. Coordinate with internal resources to develop findings, including international, pension, and executive compensation experts, Reps and Warranties brokers, originators, and other M&A team members. Manage and execute client deliverables including interim email updates, phone conversations, data request lists, and a final report. Analyze and provide technical input, compliance review, and benchmarking on health & welfare, retirement, employment agreements, equity plans, and human capital sections of the draft purchase agreement. Collaborate with originators in establishing relationships, converting due diligence targets to ongoing clients, and helping to develop opportunities. Provide ongoing relationship management oversight to private equity clients. Be viewed as a thought leader (creative thinking and innovation), with proven credibility (knowledge/ trust), both externally and internally. Write and present due diligence reports, proposals and presentations, etc. Communicate and capture the value that Aon brings even to the most challenging situations. Skills and experience that will lead to success: US Human Capital technical proficiency. Broad knowledge of health & welfare, defined contribution retirement, and executive compensation. Knowledge of defined benefit and multi-employer pension, retiree medical, and international benefits a plus. Project management – coordinate activities and information flow from a group of people within specified time frames. Financial – proficiency in reviewing financial statements and accounting in relation to benefits insurance costs. Life, Accident & Health License or willingness to obtain. Ability to work on multiple projects at one time. Ability to work independently and/or in working groups to complete projects. Experience in collaborating and training fellow project managers. Strategic and analytical skills – attention to detail while also being able to draw connections in order to provide overall conclusions. Communication (written and verbal) – ability to communicate well and at the appropriate level with a wide range of individuals. Ability to perform under stress / tight time frames. Ability to develop relationships / build confidence of others (both internally and externally) based upon work performed. Outstanding verbal and written communication skills. Results oriented – focus on conversion opportunities (including full and partial). Proficiency with Word, Excel, and Power Point. Copilot and AI proficiency a plus. Preferred Experience 2 or more years of human capital due diligence experience 5 or more years of experience working as a human capital or health & welfare consultant, corporate benefits manager, or underwriter Education Bachelor’s degree in related field Pay Transparency The salary range for this position (for U.S. applicants) is $100,000-$140,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. Job.JobDescription:
We're seeking a Project Workers Compensation Administrator! This is an exciting opportunity to help manage complex workers' compensation programs supporting large-scale projects while partnering with project leadership, insurers, medical professionals, and legal teams to deliver positive claim outcomes and reduce organizational risk. *******This is a fully onsite role, working directly with the client at their Pecos, TX location.******* Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. How this opportunity is different The Claims Administrator is responsible for implementing all aspects of the project workers’ compensation program (statutory) for Kilby Power Project and all Contractor Coordinated Insurance Program (CCIP) enrollees. This position will also assist with the administration of auto and other insured claims. Position is located at the project construction site, in Pecos, TX with an anticipated work schedule of 48 hours per week. While this is an Aon position, the employee is seconded to Bechtel. The Claims Administrator works under the direction of Bechtel's Head of Workers' Compensation and the Aon Claims Director, acting independently to manage routine matters while keeping Bechtel Insured Claims team fully informed at all stages. What the day will look like Communicates effectively with injured workers, medical professionals, insurers, brokers, internal/external counsel, corporate management, and various related regulatory agencies. Develops and maintains project-specific workers’ compensation claims manual, medical panel, related processes and procedures for statutory and USL&H claims. Implements improvements based on lessons learned, legislative changes or Court decisions, and Bechtel operating imperatives. Assists with subcontractor CCIP enrollment and provides workers’ compensation orientation to subcontractors. Develops and provides onsite training related to workers’ compensation. Under the guidance of the Workers’ Compensation Risk Manager, develops and prepares regular reports outlining project claims performance. Monitors claims activity to identify early negative claim trends or other issues that may negatively impact project performance. Is responsible for oversight and processing of workers’ compensation claims: Responsible for initiating, preparing, and maintaining all documentation associated with claims. Investigates and documents eligibility for workers’ compensation benefits and communicates same to insurer and related interested parties. Assists with investigation and coordination of issues surrounding subrogation. Interprets laws and regulations, determines appropriate courses of action, and presents solutions to resolve the claims. Identifies potential subrogation issues. Monitors claim resolution activities implemented by insurer(s) and employers. Maintains Project Risk Management Information System (RMIS). Directs and monitors the activities and performance of Bechtel’s insurance provider to ensure compliance with applicable regulations. Implements, monitors, and ensures compliance of “Special Account” requirements. Conducts regular claim reviews, claim audits and prepares related reports. Interfaces with insurer to effectively manage claims, including but not limited to authorizing claim reserve changes, authorizing insurer referral to outside counsel, and assessing and approving settlement strategies. Coordinates and supports early return to work. Manages relationships with onsite clinic, panel/network physicians and other medical providers, to ensure effective claims management and return to work. Works with injured worker and supervision on developing and implementing return to work plan. Assists in management fitness for duty and ADA accommodation issues as needed. Assists Bechtel Risk Management in the defense of litigation or other complex case support. (i.e., responding to interrogatories and other discovery requests). Assists with gathering information and filing auto and other insured claims. Assists with administration of auto and other insured claims as needed. Performs other tasks as required by Bechtel Risk Management. Skills and experience that will lead to success 5+ years of experience in the field or in a related area or in a related area. Extensive knowledge of / experience with workers’ compensation and occupational rehabilitation procedures, practices and processes. Extensive knowledge of claim’s resolution techniques and strategies, legal principles related to claim resolution and familiarity with all phases of the litigation process. Working knowledge of / experience with bodily injury and 1st and 3rd party property damage claims practices and processes. Working knowledge of / experience with auto and other insured claims practices and procedures. Relies on experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals. Highly skilled in written and verbal communication. Bilingual language proficiency (i.e., English and Spanish) is a plus. Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of industry Workers’ Compensation experience. For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances. Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate. Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Pay Transparency Laws: The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $60,000 to $80,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location. This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan. A summary of all the benefits offered for this position: Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. LI-JF1 #LI-Onsite 2589794

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Customer Service Representative, Customer Service / Account Support
Job.JobDescription:
Company Details

Berkley One is a modern insurance provider for a modern generation of affluence. We serve clients who live dynamic, adventurous lives and expect their insurance experience to match. Our mission is to deliver highly personalized risk and claims management through a blend of expert independent agents, cutting-edge digital tools, and the strength of the W.R. Berkley brand.

Why Join Us?At Berkley One, you’ll be part of a forward-thinking team that’s reimagining personal insurance. We’re building solutions that are as sophisticated and agile as the clients we serve—individuals and families who value innovation, simplicity, and exceptional service. You’ll collaborate with passionate professionals, leverage modern technology, and help shape the future of our industry.

What We Value

A client-first mindset with a passion for delivering exceptional experiencesCuriosity, creativity, and a drive to challenge the status quoCollaboration across disciplines to build smarter, more intuitive solutionsIntegrity, expertise, and a commitment to excellenceJoin us in creating a new standard in personal insurance—where protection meets possibility.

The Company is an equal employment opportunity employer. #LI-AV1 #LI-hybrid  

Responsibilities

This role will be based in our Wilmington, DE office.  We offer a hybrid work schedule with 4 days in the office; and 1 day remote where it makes sense to do so.

As a Customer Service Delivery Manager, you'll be a key member of the Berkley One team focusing on Property & Casualty insurance for the high net worth market.  You'll be responsible for the successful operation of a customer friendly, omni-channel service delivery operation for the discerning high net worth customer and their agents. You'll manage a team of professionals who will act with the customer’s best interest in mind to deliver the best service experience in the high net worth insurance space. You will join a team of experienced, successful professionals with deep expertise in this market as they grow Berkley One.

You'll closely partner with the AVP of Customer Experience to oversee all steps in our customers’ and agents’ interactions. We'll trust you to manage all aspects of the customer journey: onboarding, policy changes, billing and claims support through multiple channels. You'd also work closely with our digital team to ensure that our customers experience the same level of excellent service, whichever channel they choose. The ideal candidate will have experience building successful customer service teams and establishing world class service across multiple channels.

What you can expect:

ServiceNow Platform Lead owns ServiceNow as an enterprise product. This person is accountable for its 1–3 year roadmap, governance, financial performance, architecture alignment and measurable business value. The role leads the platform team and sets direction with executives, product owners and the architect. It turns technical work into business outcomes such as faster resolution, higher change success, lower audit risk and greater self-service adoption.

Platform Delivery & Team Leadership

  • Lead and manage a team of ServiceNow developers and administrators delivering enhancements, integrations and defect fixes.
  • Own execution quality, velocity and technical standards. Act as the onshore/offshore delivery bridge.
  • Plan sprints and backlog, prioritize with product owners, and make sure work is delivered predictably and is production-ready.
  • Coach and mentor engineers. Set expectations, track throughput and cycle time, and drive continuous improvement.

Platform Roadmap, Releases & Upgrades

  • Plan and run platform upgrades, patches and release cycles, including testing, readiness checklists, cutover and post-upgrade validation.
  • Partner with the Platform Architect and product owners to turn the roadmap into deliverable work.
  • Manage demand intake, capacity and stakeholder expectations.

Product Management

  • Manage ServiceNow as a product: customer needs, user adoption, KPIs, backlog prioritization and value delivery.
  • Decide what to stop doing, what creates the most value and what moves up the roadmap.
  • Lead the platform team and delivery pods, including onshore/offshore partners, with accountability for quality, velocity and predictable, production-ready delivery.

Platform Governance & Health

  • Establish and enforce standards for customization, integrations, code review and change control.
  • Monitor platform health, performance, instance scans and technical debt. Remediate against targets.
  • Drive data-quality and ownership practices across CMDB/CSDM, discovery, application tagging and foundational data.
  • Maintain ticket-health governance, including SLA definitions, role-based access and problem-management controls.

Financial Management

  • Own the platform budget, licensing, renewals and vendor relationships.
  • Govern license entitlements and usage, and drive cost optimization.
  • Own value realization and report it against investment.

CMDB, ITOM & Integrations

  • Oversee delivery of CMDB, Discovery, and Service Mapping capabilities.
  • Ensure integrations (REST, SOAP, MID Servers, messaging) are secure, scalable and well documented.

Automation & Innovation

  • Drive automation, workflow modernization and employee/customer experience improvements, including Catalogs , Virtual Agent and Employee Center.
  • Evaluate and adopt AI and agentic capabilities within platform governance and licensing boundaries.

Security, Risk & Compliance

  • Ensure the platform meets enterprise security, audit and compliance standards, including access controls and segregation of duties.
  • Participate & lead major incident response for platform issues.

Stakeholder Management

  • Communicate status, risks and outcomes to IT leadership and business partners.
  • Collaborate with enterprise architecture, security, infrastructure, application owners and vendors/MSPs.

Qualifications

Responsibilities

The Vice President, AI Security & Automation Enablement leads the Information Security capability responsible for secure artificial intelligence adoption, AI security, and reusable automation across W. R. Berkley Corporation. The role sets strategy, establishes priorities and investment plans, leads people and partners, and remains accountable for measurable security and business outcomes. 

This executive builds organizational capability rather than serving as the primary developer. The VP translates emerging AI risk and opportunity into a governed portfolio, equips existing security teams to adopt AI and automation safely, and ensures that architecture, engineering, governance, operations, and business stakeholders have clear standards, reusable patterns, and accountable decision paths. 

Primary Responsibilities 

  • Strategy, Portfolio and Investment Leadership 
    • Define and maintain the multi-year AI security and automation strategy, roadmap, operating model, and investment priorities for Information Security. 
    • Convert enterprise objectives and emerging risks into a prioritized portfolio with clear owners, funding needs, delivery milestones, operational acceptance criteria, and measurable outcomes. 
    • Advise the CISO and senior technology leadership on AI-related risk, capability gaps, investment tradeoffs, tool overlap, and opportunities to improve security delivery. 
  • People Leadership and Organizational Capability 
    • Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team spanning AI security, automation, architecture, engineering, security data, and related enablement capabilities. 
    • Establish clear accountability, role expectations, talent plans, succession coverage, performance objectives, and sustainable delivery practices. 
    • Build a force-multiplier model that enables existing Information Security teams to use approved AI and automation rather than creating a centralized team that becomes the sole builder for every use case. 
  • AI Security Governance and Enterprise Partnership 
    • Represent Information Security in enterprise AI governance and provide accountable security recommendations for AI use cases, platforms, vendors, and material changes. 
    • Align AI review activities with existing architecture, third-party risk, legal, procurement, privacy, and Building Permit processes to reduce duplication while preserving required oversight. 
    • Define escalation criteria for high-risk, restricted-data, autonomous, externally hosted, or materially changed AI use cases. 
  • Secure AI Adoption and Control Framework 
    • Establish and govern security standards, reference architectures, and control patterns for generative AI, machine learning, AI agents, model and data pipelines, and AI-enabled applications. 
    • Ensure appropriate controls for identity, access, data protection, secrets, logging, monitoring, human oversight, output validation, change control, resilience, and incident response. 
    • Maintain a risk-based approach that enables approved experimentation and production use while identifying and reducing unmanaged or unsanctioned AI use. 
  • AI and Automation Delivery Enablement 
    • Oversee delivery of reusable capabilities such as governed AI experimentation environments, security workflow automation, evidence generation, control validation, AI-assisted analysis, and security data integrations. 
    • Set technical direction and challenge designs while assigning detailed architecture, prototyping, coding, integration, testing, and operational runbook development to qualified team members and partners. 
    • Require production readiness, support ownership, measurable adoption, quality controls, rollback capability, and acceptance criteria before automated capabilities are operationalized. 
  • Visibility, Measurement and Risk Reduction 
    • Establish reliable visibility into AI systems, AI usage, agents, integrations, and material data flows within the scope of Information Security oversight. 
    • Define executive and operational measures for control coverage, review cycle time, automation reliability, adoption, realized capacity, risk reduction, and exceptions. 
    • Use trusted data to identify gaps, prioritize remediation, and demonstrate whether investments are producing the intended outcomes. 
  • Vendor, Partner and Financial Management 
    • Lead evaluation of AI security and automation vendors, strategic partners, and professional services based on risk, capability, interoperability, supportability, cost, and measurable value. 
    • Own portfolio-level commercial and sourcing recommendations, including build-versus-buy decisions, statements of work, acceptance of partner deliverables, and avoidance of unnecessary tool overlap. 
    • Manage the approved budget and communicate material cost, schedule, delivery, and residual-risk decisions to executive stakeholders. 
  • External and Industry Leadership 
    • Maintain current knowledge of AI security threats, regulatory expectations, industry standards, and relevant technology developments. 
    • Represent WRBC in selected industry, peer, and strategic-vendor forums and translate external developments into practical internal action. 
    • Provide clear executive and board-ready communications on AI security posture, priorities, decisions, and progress. 

    Decision Authority and Accountability 

    • Accountable for the AI security and automation enablement strategy, portfolio priorities, organizational capability, resource recommendations, and delivery outcomes within the assigned scope. 
    • Approves technical standards, patterns, and acceptance criteria within delegated authority and escalates policy exceptions, material residual risk, and enterprise-level investment decisions through established governance. 
    • Retains human accountability for risk decisions, production access, material changes, vendor commitments, and executive representations. AI and automation may support analysis and execution but do not replace accountable leadership judgment. 

    Qualifications

    Required Qualifications

    • 10 or more years of progressive experience across information security, technology, architecture, engineering, automation, data, or related disciplines, including significant leadership responsibility.
    • Demonstrated success setting strategy, building teams, managing a portfolio, and delivering cross-functional technology or security capabilities in a complex enterprise.
    • Strong working knowledge of AI and automation risks and controls, including data protection, identity and access, model and application security, agent authority, monitoring, human oversight, and operational resilience.
    • Ability to evaluate technical designs and make difficult tradeoffs without becoming the primary hands-on developer for the function.
    • Experience leading vendors and service partners, developing investment recommendations, and communicating with executive and business stakeholders.
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex risk and technology decisions in plain language.

    Preferred Qualifications

    • Leadership experience in insurance, financial services, or another regulated enterprise.
    • Experience with cloud platforms, enterprise security architecture, AI development platforms, workflow automation, security data and analytics, and modern software delivery practices.
    • Familiarity with recognized cybersecurity, AI risk, and AI management frameworks and with regulatory expectations relevant to WRBC.
    • Relevant security, architecture, cloud, risk, or AI credentials. Equivalent demonstrated experience should be considered.

    Leadership Competencies

    • Enterprise strategy and prioritization
    • People leadership and talent development
    • Technical judgment and intellectual curiosity
    • Executive communication and influence
    • Financial and vendor stewardship
    • Cross-functional collaboration
    • Outcome ownership and operational discipline

Company Details

Berkley Alternative Markets IO (BAM IO) is a strategic enablement engine for certain Berkley businesses.

We bring together advanced analytics, data-driven insights, and operational expertise to help Berkley Businesses make faster, more informed decisions and run more efficient, scalable operations.

By standardizing capabilities and translating complex data into action, we reduce friction, increase consistency, and enable growth across the segment; so our businesses can focus on underwriting, distribution, and delivering results.

Responsibilities

The Director, Segment Operations leads operations functions, operating teams, and improvement work for BAM IO and the Berkley operating companies it supports. The role reports to the SVP, CFO, BAM IO.

The role has two parts. First, it directly leads operations functions and teams assigned to it by BAM IO or an operating company, with accountability for service, quality, cost, controls, and people results in those areas. Second, it leads project management, BPO and third-party governance, and process, automation, and AI-enabled improvement work at the operating company and segment level.

Assigned functions and teams will change over time as work moves among operating companies, BAM IO, and shared or third-party services. When the role is assigned to an operating company, the Director takes day-to-day direction and priorities from that operating company’s President and is accountable for results in the assigned areas. BAM IO remains responsible for employment, compensation, and performance administration. The position works across Finance, Underwriting, Claims, Operations, IT, Compliance, and other functions to improve service, controls, scalability, cost, and decision-making.

Operations leadership (assigned functions)

• Lead operations functions assigned by BAM IO or an operating company. These may include policy services, premium audit, customer service, and claims operations support.

• Directly manage managers and supervisors and, through them, frontline staff. Set goals, coach, manage performance, allocate workload, and make hiring, staffing, and succession recommendations.

• Own service standards, service level agreements, workload and capacity, quality, cycle time, backlog, and issue escalation for assigned functions.

• For claims operations support, own non-technical claims work, meaning administrative, processing, and support workflows. Technical claims decisions, including compensability, reserving, settlement, and litigation strategy, remain with claims leadership.

• Manage premium audit operations and lead transitions to shared or enterprise audit services when approved.

Project and program management

• Lead project management for reorganizations, operating model changes, and cross-functional initiatives at the operating company and segment level, including workplans, milestones, decision logs, risks, dependencies, and status reporting.

• Lead approved organizational and operating model changes from design through implementation, staffing, and sustained adoption.

BPO and third-party governance

• Own BPO and third-party operational governance for assigned functions and initiatives, including scope, service levels, KPIs, performance reviews, escalation, risk management, and transitions of work in or out.

• Recommend, with business owners, which work stays in-house, moves to BPO, or moves to shared services, based on cost, quality, control, and risk.

Process, controls, data, and AI

• Design, document, and standardize processes, controls, and standard operating procedures to improve consistency, compliance, audit readiness, and scalability.

• Build operating metrics, dashboards, and executive-ready analysis on service, capacity, quality, cost, control, and progress against plan.

• Lead approved process improvement, automation, data, and AI-enabled workflow initiatives from diagnosis through implementation, adoption, and benefit realization.

• Own or support business continuity planning for assigned companies and functions, including documentation, testing coordination, remediation, and readiness reporting.

Segment enablement

• Partner with the VP, Operations Strategy & Transformation and segment leadership to translate priorities into workplans, decision points, measures, and accountability.

• Turn proven operating company practices into segment playbooks where a common approach adds value, while preserving clear ownership of results.

• Facilitate cross-company and cross-functional problem solving. Do not shift work or risk to another team without clear agreement on ownership.

• Develop change management, communication, and training plans so affected teams adopt and sustain new processes, tools, and ways of working.

• Perform other duties as assigned by the SVP, CFOO or, during an assignment, the operating company President.

This role may be aligned to any segment office.

Qualifications

• Extensive experience leading insurance operations, such as policy services, premium audit, customer service, or claims operations support, in a regulated environment. Workers’ compensation experience preferred.

• Demonstrated leadership of managers and supervisors, including setting expectations, managing performance, and developing teams.

• Strong record of diagnosing operating problems and delivering measurable improvements in service, quality, cost, controls, or cycle time.

• Strong project and program management, including leading reorganizations or operating model changes through implementation.

• Strong background in BPO or third-party operational governance, including service level management, performance management, escalation, and risk mitigation.

• Experience with business continuity planning, operational resilience, or related governance.

• Experience designing processes, controls, standard operating procedures, and operational performance measures.

• Ability to translate automation and AI-enabled tools into practical workflows that teams adopt and sustain.

• Ability to work in a matrix, take direction from more than one leader, and keep priorities clear for teams. Strong judgment and written and verbal communication with senior leaders.

Education 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations, Finance, Accounting, or a related field. Relevant certifications are a plus.

Responsibilities

As a Finance and Accounting Intern, you will work directly with the Accounting/Finance Team to perform month-end close processes, help with the annual budgeting process for revenues and expenses, and complete various projects that will include scenario analyses and pro forma financial projections. You will be valued as a team member.

The CWG internship and development program seeks high potential candidates that demonstrate creativity, curiosity, and innovativeness. In addition to your Finance tasks, the program provides access to the company’s senior leaders while also introducing a broad overview of insurance operations in claims, marketing, underwriting, analytics and the independent agency system.

The program was developed to provide interns with a valuable, rewarding experience and help connect the knowledge from academics with the reality of an Accounting/Finance career. Key functions will include but are not limited to:

Internship Responsibilities

  • Support month-end close activities and financial reporting processes.

  • Gain exposure to corporate finance, accounting operations, and strategic planning processes.

CWG Experience

The program was developed to provide interns with a valuable, rewarding experience and help connect the knowledge from academics with the reality of today’s insurance careers.

The first phase of a CWG internship includes an introduction to CWG and the W. R. Berkley Corporation, including the historical path of our 100-year-old company. General training about CWG’s product, distribution channel, and company-specific business processes will lay the groundwork for an intern’s comprehensive learning experience. Technical training necessary to perform analysis and complete program projects will follow the general training. Sessions focused on developing innovation, creativity, risk-taking, and entrepreneurial drive will be held regularly for all program interns.

Each intern may be assigned to a business area within CWG, such as Claims, Underwriting, Actuarial, Marketing, or Finance. After completing the general rotational training, interns will manage project responsibilities specific to this designated department.

Additional Experience

The CWG internship program will include social activities aimed at building strong networking relationships with fellow interns and CWG staff. Activities may include CWG key management sessions, team building, and volunteer/community service opportunities.

Your Experience

So what do you want your experience to be? At CWG, we’re dedicated to making your time with us unique and rewarding! Competitive pay, exposure to the complete business operation, real responsibility, fun activities, and full-time employment opportunities!

  • Pursuing a degree in Accounting, Finance, Information Systems, Business Analytics, or a related field.
  • Interest in financial reporting, forecasting, and business analytics.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills.
  • Demonstrated proficiency with Microsoft Excel
  • Interest in leveraging technology and AI solutions to support business and financial processes.
  • Ability to work effectively in a collaborative, team-oriented environment.

Responsibilities

Berkley Southwest is seeking a Manager, Human Resources to join their team.  This role is located in our Coppell, TX headquarters on a hybrid basis.

As Manager, Human Resources, you will be a key contributor within the Berkley organization, who partners with the VP of Human Resources and Operating Unit Leadership to support the execution of talent strategies and business initiatives. This role serves as a trusted advisor, providing guidance on key HR functions including recruitment, retention, performance management, talent development, succession planning, compensation, and employee relations.

Responsibilities:

In conjunction with the VP, Human Resources Manager

  • Guides and coaches leaders through actions related to formal disciplinary procedures, jointly determines appropriate course of actions; reviews and provides suggestions for performance improvement plans; and ensures legal compliance with aid of VP HR and/or legal counsel when necessary
  • Proactively identifies areas for process improvement, innovation, and opportunities for efficiency and synergy
  • Partners with management on engagement strategies that improve employee satisfaction, this includes coordination of community or company events, e.g.
  • Confers with leaders to identify staffing needs, job specifications, job duties, qualifications, skills and competencies

  • Assists in the development and delivery of management and/or employee training sessions related to strategic initiatives, performance management, employee engagement, succession planning, etc.
  • Actively researches, creatively designs and implements effective methods to educate, enhance performance and recognize performance, advising and collaborating on the development and administration of recognition programs with Shared HR Services
  • May lead or participate in special and/or cross-functional project teams related to Company strategic initiatives
  • Assist in administration and communication of ADA process as needed
  • Identifies, evaluates and resolves employee relations issues such as employee complaints, harassment allegations and civil rights complaints with the aid of VP HR and/or legal counsel when necessary

The AI Product Manager - Claims owns the product direction for AI-enabled capabilities across the claims lifecycle - first notice of loss, triage, document intake and indexing, and straight-through processing. This person works directly with claims operations leaders and adjusters to understand where automation and AI can reduce manual work and improve outcomes, and partners with engineering and data science to turn that understanding into a prioritized, well-scoped roadmap. The role sits between the claims business and the technology teams building these capabilities, and is accountable for whether what gets built actually solves the problem it was meant to solve.

Key responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Product Strategy and Roadmap

  • Translate claims operations pain points into clear problem statements, requirements, and acceptance criteria.
  • Make prioritization calls using both data and judgment, and be able to explain the reasoning behind them.
  • Decide what not to build, and say so plainly when a request doesn't hold up.

Claims and AI Domain Application 

  • Apply working knowledge of P&C claims processes - FNOL, triage, adjusting, reserving, litigation, subrogation - to identify where AI and automation add real value versus where they don't.
  • Partner with engineering and data science to scope AI features appropriately: understanding what's realistic to build, how to evaluate model or automation quality, and where human review needs to stay in the loop.
  • Define and track the metrics that determine whether an AI feature is actually working in production, including accuracy, false-positive rate, and adoption - not just whether it shipped.
  • Stay current on how AI is being applied to claims across the industry, and bring that perspective back into roadmap decisions.

Stakeholder Relationships and Communication

  • Build direct, trusted relationships with claims supervisors, adjusters, and business leaders - not just their delegates - including through field interviews and shadowing.
  • Act as a reliable, candid point of contact for claims stakeholders on the status and direction of AI initiatives.
  • Communicate tradeoffs and decisions clearly to both business and technical audiences, in writing and in person.
  • Work with AI governance and model risk functions to move initiatives through required review processes.

Delivery and Execution

  • Write clear user stories and acceptance criteria; participate in agile ceremonies and backlog management.
  • Partner with engineering leads to sequence work realistically and flag risk early.
  • Own outcomes past launch - monitor what shipped, identify what isn't working, and drive the fix rather than handing it off.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in the P&C insurance industry, with direct exposure to claims operations or claims systems.
  • 3+ years of product management experience, owning a roadmap and shipping software products.
  • Experience applying AI or intelligent automation to an insurance workflow - defining the use case, scoping what AI could realistically do, and working through the tradeoffs of accuracy, human review, and rollout risk. Deep technical AI/ML expertise is not required, but real experience scoping or shipping an AI-enabled feature is.
  • A track record of forming independent, well-reasoned points of view and being willing to disagree with stakeholders when the data or the user research supports it.
  • Demonstrated ability to build strong working relationships across business and technology teams, including with people several levels removed in the org chart.
  • High ownership - follows through on commitments without being chased, and treats outcomes as personal responsibility rather than someone else's job.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting to both claims operations leaders and engineering teams.
  • Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent experience.

Company Details

We provide a foundation of stability and predictability that gives employees the confidence to succeed.

Founded in 1967, W. R. Berkley Corporation has grown from a small investment management firm into one of the largest commercial lines property and casualty insurers in the United States.

Along the way, we’ve been listed on the New York Stock Exchange, become a Fortune 500 Company, joined the S&P 500, and seen our gross written premiums exceed $15 billion.

Responsibilities

This position supports the Corporate Financial Data and Analysis function by designing, maintaining, and modernizing the finance data architecture, reporting platforms, and analytical environments used by Corporate Finance, operating units, actuarial, information technology, and other enterprise stakeholders.

The role provides technical and functional support for Oracle Essbase, Oracle Analytics Server, PeopleSoft financial data, Vena, BDW, ledger-related processes, data warehouse integrations, and financial reporting data flows.

The position is responsible for supporting recurring production processes, troubleshooting data and reporting issues, maintaining and enhancing Essbase cubes and related jobs, assisting with ledger and financial close data validation, and partnering with business and technology teams to improve the reliability, scalability, and transparency of finance data.

The role will be responsible for supporting current modernization efforts to migrate and refactor finance data processes into expanded AI-enabled analytics and exception handling, strengthen data governance, and reduce manual effort across financial reporting, reconciliations, data calls, and close-related activities.

This position requires the ability to translate finance and accounting requirements into technical solutions; develop and maintain reports, databases, scripts, queries, integrations, and ETL/ELT processes; support production operations; assist with system upgrades and platform transitions; and communicate effectively with internal business users, technology partners, vendors, and operating unit stakeholders.

Key Functions/Duties of Position:  

  • Design, develop, maintain, and support finance data architecture, data warehouse structures, ETL/ELT processes, scripts, queries, reports, dashboards, cubes, and analytical environments used by Corporate Finance and operating units.
  • Participate in Databricks modernization efforts by helping identify legacy finance data processes to migrate, refactor existing data jobs, validate results between legacy and Databricks environments, support workflow orchestration, and help establish scalable data processing patterns.
  • Assist with the transition from legacy SQL Server, DataStage, SSIS, OAS, Essbase, and other existing data processes toward Databricks and modern lake house-based architecture where appropriate.
  • Support AI and automation initiatives by helping prepare trusted finance data, define business rules, identify exception-handling opportunities, improve metadata and semantic definitions, and enable self-service analytics, AI-assisted inquiry, and governed data access.
  • Provide ongoing production support for Oracle Essbase, Oracle Analytics Server, PeopleSoft warehouse data, Vena integrations, BDW reporting processes, and related financial reporting platforms.
  • Monitor recurring finance data processes, including nightly and monthly cube refreshes, data loads, job failures, close-related processing, and system-generated exception messages; investigate issues and coordinate timely resolution.
  • Maintain, troubleshoot, and enhance Essbase cubes and related reporting structures, including PeopleSoft company cubes, BDW cubes, Schedule P, Schedule F, corporate dashboard, auditing, allocation, and other financial reporting use cases.
  • Support ledger and financial close processes by assisting with hierarchy maintenance, new general ledger accounts, close error monitoring, PeopleSoft data validation, month-end close reporting, balancing, reconciliation, and downstream reporting impacts.
  • Partner with Corporate Finance, operating units, actuarial teams, and other technology teams to define requirements, resolve data issues, validate results, and implement reporting and data integration improvements.
  • Develop and maintain documentation for processes, data flows, system dependencies, controls, validations, support procedures, and modernization changes to reduce key-person risk and improve long-term supportability.
  • Provide technical analysis and support for finance data requests, including historical general ledger data, BDW validation, premium, loss, producer, expense, reinsurance, allocation, and other financial or operational datasets.
  • Assist with ServiceNow requests, security access, user support, Smart View and reporting access, data availability questions, and troubleshooting for finance reporting users.
  • Participate in system maintenance, upgrades, disaster recovery planning, server migrations, platform testing, and production deployment activities for finance data and reporting systems.
  • Apply sound development and support practices, including code review, testing, documentation, version control, issue tracking, deployment coordination, and clear communication of risks, dependencies, and downstream impacts.
  • Provide strategic and technical leadership for the Financial Data and Analysis team and business partners, establishing priorities and accountability across recurring production support, financial data architecture, reporting platforms, data quality, and modernization initiatives while ensuring reliable, scalable, and well-controlled delivery of finance data solutions.
  • Lead, coach, and develop team members by providing clear technical direction, strengthening knowledge of finance data structures and reporting environments, and promoting disciplined practices for testing, documentation, controls, issue resolution, and change management, while building the team’s capabilities in Databricks, AI-enabled analytics, automation, and modern lake house technologies.

Qualifications

Education Requirement:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent; preferably in actuarial science, math or computer science.

Qualifications: 

  • 12-15+ years of experience in finance data architecture, data engineering, business intelligence, financial reporting systems, data warehousing, analytics, or related technical support roles.
  • Strong SQL experience, preferably with Microsoft SQL Server and enterprise financial data warehouse environments.
  • Experience leading or managing a team.
  • Experience developing, maintaining, or supporting ETL/ELT processes, data integrations, data pipelines, batch jobs, and production data workflows.
  • Experience with Databricks, lake house architecture, Unity Catalog, Databricks SQL, notebooks, workflow orchestration, APIs, or cloud-based data modernization preferred.
  • Familiarity with AI-enabled analytics, semantic layers, metadata management, business definitions, exception detection, automation, and self-service finance reporting preferred.
  • Experience with Oracle Essbase, Oracle Analytics Server, Smart View, financial reporting cubes, dimensional structures, metadata, and cube refresh or maintenance processes.
  • Experience supporting finance, accounting, ledger, close, planning, budgeting, reconciliation, allocation, or statutory reporting processes.
  • Strong project management, organizational, prioritization, and planning skills, including the ability to manage competing demands, recurring production responsibilities, and modernization initiatives.
  • Working knowledge of financial data, general ledger structures, chart fields, accounting hierarchies, month-end close processes, and downstream reporting dependencies preferred.
  • Ability to understand complex finance, accounting, actuarial, and insurance reporting requirements and translate them into effective data and technology solutions.
  • Strong analytical, critical thinking, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose root causes across data, process, system, and business-rule issues.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively across Corporate Finance, operating units, actuarial, technology, data governance, vendor, and support teams.
  • Strong communication skills, including the ability to explain technical issues to business users, document support procedures, and summarize risks, dependencies, and recommended actions.
  • Demonstrated commitment to data quality, control, auditability, documentation, supportability, and customer service.
  • Multi-line property and casualty insurance experience is beneficial.
  • Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and provide leadership in ambiguous or evolving technical and business environments.
