Job.CustomJobTypeName: Safety Consultant, Risk Management / Loss Control
Job.JobDescription:
Posting Description Who We Are NFP, an Aon company, is a leading insurance broker and consultant providing property and casualty, employee benefits, wealth management and retirement solutions. We combine specialized expertise, strong carrier relationships and a people-first culture to help clients address complex risk and business challenges. NFP has been recognized by Business Insurance as a Best Place to Work in Insurance for ten consecutive years. About NFP’s Safety & Risk Consulting (SRC) NFP’s Safety & Risk Consulting (SRC) practice is a national team of safety, loss control and risk management professionals who support clients across industries and geographies. The team provides practical, client-specific consulting focused on protecting people, strengthening operations, reducing loss drivers and improving risk quality. SRC works collaboratively with clients, NFP account teams, producers, insurance carriers and other technical specialists to connect field-based risk improvement with broader insurance and business objectives. Position Summary We are seeking an experienced Construction Safety Consultant to provide hands-on safety and risk control consulting to construction clients primarily throughout the New York, New Jersey and Connecticut Tri-State area, while also supporting national clients and projects. The consultant will evaluate jobsite and operational exposures, develop practical risk improvement strategies, deliver training, and serve as a technical resource to client leadership, field teams, NFP colleagues and insurance partners. This is a full-time, field-based position with remote flexibility when not traveling. Approximately 60% travel is expected, including local jobsite travel and periodic overnight national travel. The ideal candidate will live in or near the New York City metropolitan area with convenient access to a major airport. Key Responsibilities Conduct construction jobsite safety assessments, loss control surveys and management-system reviews for general contractors, owners, developers and trade contractors. Evaluate high-hazard construction exposures and controls, including falls, scaffolds, ladders, excavation and trenching, cranes and rigging, electrical work, hot work, confined spaces, temporary structures, material handling, public protection and contractor management. Review and help strengthen corporate and project-specific safety programs, site safety plans, emergency action plans, job hazard analyses, pre-task plans, subcontractor controls and written compliance programs. Analyze loss runs, incident trends, experience modifiers and other available risk data to identify loss drivers, prioritize resources and develop measurable service plans. Perform incident and near-miss reviews, support root-cause analysis, and recommend corrective and preventive actions. This role does not replace the client’s legal, claims or regulatory counsel. Deliver practical training, executive briefings, supervisor coaching and toolbox-style education on construction safety, regulatory compliance and risk improvement topics. Prepare clear, timely reports that document observations, identify priority hazards, recommend corrective actions and communicate risk implications to both technical and nontechnical audiences. Partner with NFP producers, account teams, claims professionals and carrier risk control representatives to support client stewardship, renewal strategy, prospect evaluations and coordinated service delivery, including Owner Controlled Insurance Program (OCIP) and Contractor Controlled Insurance Program (CCIP) safety and loss-control activities. Support OCIP and CCIP program activities, including preconstruction safety reviews, contractor and subcontractor safety qualification, project-specific safety planning, orientation and training coordination, site audits, loss-trend review, corrective-action tracking, stewardship reporting and collaboration with program sponsors, administrators, carriers and claims partners. Participate in client meetings and business development activities as a construction safety subject matter resource, including service-plan development and presentation of findings to senior leadership. Maintain current knowledge of applicable federal, state and local requirements and accepted industry practices, including OSHA construction standards and relevant New York City construction and local regulations safety requirements. Manage multiple client engagements independently, document activity in designated systems and consistently meet agreed timelines and service expectations. Required Qualifications At least 5 years of progressive construction safety, loss control or construction risk consulting experience, with substantial field-based jobsite experience. Demonstrated experience supporting Owner Controlled Insurance Programs (OCIPs) and Contractor Controlled Insurance Programs (CCIPs), including project safety oversight, contractor coordination, loss-control activities and program reporting. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in occupational safety, construction management, engineering, risk management or a related subject area, or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience. OSHA 510, Occupational Safety and Health Standards for the Construction Industry. Completion of applicable New York City Department of Buildings Site Safety Training (SST) requirements and other NYC construction safety training required for the consultant’s assigned project duties. Working knowledge of OSHA 29 CFR 1926 and the ability to interpret and apply applicable federal, state and local construction safety requirements. Demonstrated ability to identify hazards, evaluate controls, analyze incidents and losses, and translate findings into practical recommendations. Strong written, presentation, facilitation and client relationship skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with executives, project managers, superintendents, safety professionals and craft employees. Valid driver’s license, an acceptable driving record consistent with company requirements, and the ability to drive to client and project locations and travel approximately 60%, including local travel and overnight national travel. Ability to perform field-based construction work while wearing required safety PPE. The position requires walking active jobsites; climbing stairs and ladders; accessing elevated, confined, uneven or unfinished work areas; standing for extended periods; bending, stooping, kneeling and reaching; and lifting or carrying up to 25 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and comfort using web-based safety, risk control and client-management platforms. Preferred Qualifications Certified Safety Professional (CSP) or Construction Health and Safety Technician (CHST). Associate Safety Professional (ASP) may be considered for candidates actively progressing toward the CSP. OSHA 500 authorized trainer status is strongly preferred for candidates who will deliver OSHA Outreach training. Experience supporting complex commercial, infrastructure, civil, high-rise, healthcare, industrial or large general-contractor construction programs. Experience within a property and casualty insurance carrier, insurance brokerage, risk consulting firm or owner-controlled/contractor-controlled insurance program environment. Familiarity with workers’ compensation, general liability, auto/fleet and builders risk loss drivers, as well as insurance-related stewardship and carrier risk control processes. Bilingual communication skills, particularly English and Spanish, are a plus. Work Environment and Travel This position is virtual when not at client or project locations. The consultant will primarily assist clients in the New York, New Jersey and Connecticut Tri-State area and will also support national clients as business needs require. Approximately 60% travel is expected. Residence in or around New York City, with convenient access to John F. Kennedy International Airport, LaGuardia Airport, Newark Liberty International Airport or another major airport serving the region, is preferred. The work includes active construction environments and requires use of appropriate PPE, ladder and stair access, regular walking and standing, and occasional lifting or carrying up to 25 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation. What We Offer We are proud to offer a competitive salary, paid time off and holidays, a 401(k) plan with company match, health and wellness programs, employee discount programs and additional benefits. Our PeopleFirst culture is focused on building meaningful relationships, supporting employee wellbeing and creating opportunities for colleagues to grow and make an impact. The base salary range for this position is $97,000 to $130,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level, scope of responsibility and geographic location. Actual base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to base salary, the position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! NFP is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. #LI-BW1 2590758

Posting Description Who We Are: NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance who has also earned the WORK180 employer endorsement. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com. Summary of the Role: As a proactive, client-focused professional, this role involves working closely with an experienced Wealth Advisor to deliver outstanding service and customized financial solutions. This role offers an outstanding opportunity to gain hands-on experience in financial planning, asset management, and personal finance advisory while learning directly from a respected industry leader. This role is ideal for a professional seeking a long-term career in financial advisory. It offers ongoing mentorship, professional development, and a clear growth path within the organization. The Associate Advisor plays a key role in enhancing the client experience while developing the skills and expertise needed for a successful advisory career. ***Candidate selected will attend the office on a full-time basis for the first six months, and then will follow a hybrid model (3x per week). *** Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Partner directly with experienced Wealth Advisors to provide outstanding financial planning and investment solutions for clients. Help create and refine comprehensive financial plans, investment proposals, and wealth strategies tailored to clients' unique goals. Participate in client meetings, gain firsthand exposure to advisory conversations, and help drive follow-up actions that support client success. Build significant client relationships by responding to inquiries and providing thoughtful support on financial planning, investment strategies, and account management. Assist with onboarding new clients and facilitating financial transactions to ensure a smooth and efficient experience. Supervise and analyze client portfolios, helping Advisors implement recommendations and maintain alignment with investment objectives. Maintain accurate client records and documentation while employing CRM tools to deliver best-in-class service. Track account openings, asset transfers, and key achievements to ensure timely execution and a positive client experience. Review account activity and maintenance reports to proactively find opportunities and address client needs. Work alongside Wealth Managers and Client Service professionals in a highly collaborative, development-focused environment. Assist with data analysis, client reporting, and operational initiatives that contribute to the success of the practice. Invest in your professional growth through ongoing mentorship, industry events, training programs, and opportunities to pursue professional certifications. Knowledge, Skills and/or Abilities: Anticipate client and team needs, proactively seeing opportunities and delivering thoughtful, timely solutions. Demonstrate strong project management and problem-solving skills, with the ability to lead multiple priorities and get results. Maintain a high level of accuracy and attention to detail while delivering exceptional work in a fast-paced environment. Stay organized and adaptable, effectively handling priorities and making sound decisions with confidence. Communicate clearly and professionally, both verbally and in writing, with clients, colleagues, and business partners. Leverage technology to drive efficiency, including Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook). Experience with CRM platforms, portfolio management tools, or financial planning software such as eMoney, Nitrogen, or Holistiplan is a plus. Bring a passion for financial planning, investing, and wealth management, along with a desire to continuously expand your knowledge and expertise. Adopt continuous learning and professional development, with a growth mindset and eagerness to advance your career in wealth management. Education and/or Experience: Four-year College Degree 2-3 years of Financial Services Experience Preferred Certificates, Licenses, Registration: Series 7 & 66 required Completed or Pursuing CFP Completed or Pursuing Life, Accident, Health Insurance License What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, when all is said and done, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $70,000-$100,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! NFP is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. #NFP 2584578

Posting Description Who We Are: Wealthspire is a leading wealth management, retirement advisory, and business management firm serving individuals, families, endowments, and institutions across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. We provide a comprehensive platform that brings together wealth management, institutional consulting, business management, family office, and retirement plan advisory services—empowering clients to navigate complexity with clarity and confidence. With over 1,200 employees across more than 40 offices, we deliver insights and solutions backed by deep research, technology, and decades of expertise. Our collective businesses create a unified ecosystem designed to meet clients wherever they are in their financial journey. Wealthspire is redefining the future of financial solutions through collaboration, scale, and a steadfast commitment to putting people first—our clients, our colleagues, and our communities. As an AVP, Advisor at Wealthspire, you will leverage deep financial expertise to craft tailored investment strategies that align with client aspirations and regulatory standards. You'll lead the execution of sophisticated financial plans, ensuring optimal outcomes while nurturing enduring client relationships. Collaborating with external experts, you'll contribute to strategic initiatives and guide the development of comprehensive wealth solutions. Embracing diversity and fostering a culture of continuous growth, Wealthspire offers a dynamic environment where your expertise can thrive. Job Responsibilities: Lead and/or support other advisors in the management of client engagements. Determine appropriate client allocations through analysis of investment objectives, risk tolerance, net worth, income, and investment experience, or other knowledge. Execute investment and planning activities (e.g. rebalancing portfolios, money movements, required minimum distributions, tax loss harvesting, charitable planning, lending evaluation, education funding, etc.). Actively service client accounts by performing and/or coordinating administrative tasks (e.g. tracking and monitoring account/asset transfers, preparing and presenting performance reports, processing transaction requests as directed, handling necessary paperwork for accounts, etc.). Initiate and field client calls on various topics and miscellaneous requests (e.g. account specific questions, general inquiries regarding portfolios, investment market discussions, planning items, money movements, etc.). Assist with the development of client financial plans using financial planning software and present results and solutions to clients. Monitor client investments, review performance, and suggest changes to client portfolios as appropriate. Prepare for and attend client meetings and manage and/or complete all meeting follow-up activities. Create proposals for prospective clients. Coordinate with clients’ attorneys, accountants, and other professionals as needed. Develop and maintain working knowledge of various financial planning concepts, such as gift, estate and income tax planning, insurance, credit solutions, education funding, charitable/philanthropic strategies, etc. Pursue professional development opportunities to include additional licenses and/or designations and actively participate in internal and external training sessions and networking events. Requirements: Minimum 5+ years of wealth management experience (other or additional experience will be considered). Proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with CRM, portfolio management and financial planning software is a plus. Bachelor’s degree or higher preferably in financial planning, business, accounting, finance, economics, law or related experience. Ability to independently manage and prioritize multiple projects. Organized, detail-oriented, and able to effectively manage task lists. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Flexible team player who is highly adaptable to change and open to new ideas. Ability to think creatively. Reliable, follows through on commitments. Personal integrity and professional initiative. Previous supervisory experience managing teams is a plus. Posting Description Who We Are: Lenox Advisors is a premier MassMutual agency supporting a network of financial professionals who provide insurance, investment, and financial planning solutions to clients nationwide. As part of NFP, an Aon company, we offer the resources of a large organization while maintaining the culture and agility of a high-performing agency. Our team is dedicated to delivering exceptional advisor support, effective supervision, and operational excellence that drive business growth and client confidence. Summary of Role: The Agency Supervisory Officer (ASO) reports to the designated supervisory leader and supports the firm’s supervisory framework with a focus on investment suitability, principal review, regulatory compliance, and risk mitigation while ensuring supervisory decisions are timely, consistent, and well documented. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Evaluate transactions, product recommendations, account features, and investment strategies for suitability and compliance with firm requirements. Provide principal review and approval for designated products, i.e. complex products. Conduct client or third-party outreach when additional validation is required to support a supervisory decision. Document review outcomes, conditions, approvals, and required follow-up. Monitor supervisory activity, transaction alerts, account exceptions, and other risk indicators to identify patterns or potential concerns. Research identified issues, coordinate corrective action, and address customer concerns or apply disciplinary standards when appropriate. Maintain required supervisory logs, reviews, approvals, and documentation in accordance with established schedules. Analyze trends and prepare recurring or targeted reports to support risk assessment and supervisory priorities. Monitor supervision arrangements that have been improved and other risk-based controls for continued efficiency. Review exception requests, gather supporting information, and coordinate decisions with the appropriate stakeholders. Serve as an escalation resource for complex supervisory matters and facilitate timely resolution. Coordinate required client, representative, and MassMutual Home Office follow-up, including corrective action and account-status changes. Maintain complete records of correspondence, decisions, and resolution steps. Job Competencies: Sound principal judgment and consistent application of policy. Strong analytical, research, documentation, and risk-identification skills. Clear written and verbal communication with clients, representatives, and business partners. Ability to manage multiple priorities and recurring deadlines with attention to detail. Proficiency with standard business, supervisory, and compliance systems. Quality, accuracy, and timeliness of supervisory reviews and decisions. Timely resolution and documentation of anomalies, blocking issues, and remedial measures. Consistency of policy application and risk-based supervision. Effectiveness of reporting, training, and communication. Responsiveness to emerging risks and regulatory or policy changes. Education, Experience, License Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, or related field (or equivalent experience). Minimum of 5 years’ experience in financial services, insurance, or agency operations, with at least 2 years in a supervisory or compliance-focused role. Active FINRA Series 7, Series 24, Series 53 (or equivalent supervisory licenses) and Series 63 required; Series 65/66 preferred. Strong knowledge of state and federal regulations governing insurance and securities activities. What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $92,300.00 – $147,800.00. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! NFP and Lenox Advisors is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. 2591274

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Customer Service Representative, Customer Service / Account Support
Job.JobDescription:
Posting Description Who We Are: NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance who has also earned the WORK180 employer endorsement. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com. Summary: This is a support role, assisting the account management teams with basic administrative and other support functions in the team's day-to-day servicing of clients. The coordinator will gather and input data into spreadsheets and client presentations, take notes at client meetings and on calls and participate in special projects and training with the team that will assist in their learning and development. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Client Support and Communication: · Assist team in answering administrative questions from clients (i.e. ID cards, claim processing, membership, general benefit information). · Assist in coordinating client mailings, communications or packets related to Open Enrollment, as directed by the Account Manager. · Assist Account Managers with implementation of new business, and group application completion and processing as directed by the Account Manager. · May assist team in scheduling meetings as their first client interaction. Data Compilation and Analysis: · Learn to compile data for the Account Manager to use in proposals and insurance plan analyses, may assist in preparing proposals and spreadsheeting results. · Assist in research of questions regarding benefits and vendor/carrier products and services. · Create and maintain a client calendar, to ensure completion of pending items and future deliverables. Document and File Management: · Create and maintain client files in accordance with office procedures. · Create and maintain files and client data; maintain client data Salesforce, as directed by Account Manager; assemble enrollment materials for clients. · Assist Account Teams in their preparation for client meetings. Will print and bind presentations prior to meetings and assist in meeting agenda preparation. May assist in reviewing presentations for grammar, formatting and verification of rates/benefits. Policy Review and Problem Resolution: · Learn to do basic policy review; will gain understanding of basic industry concepts, and carrier products and services. · Assist with problem resolution on claims, billing and eligibility issues with carriers. Administrative Support and Learning: · Assist Account Managers, Consultants, and others in the office with administrative duties. · Attend seminars and classes related to the department and prepare for L&H License. · Participate in training regarding carrier products and systems Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities: · Ability to work independently and anticipate client and team needs · Effective time management and decision-making skills · Diligent follow up skills · Ability to express ideas clearly in both written and oral communications · Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Education and/or Experience: · High School graduate or equivalent. · Preferably a bachelor's degree. What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, ultimately, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $40,000 – $55,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! NFP is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. #NFP 2586683

Job.JobTitle: Associate Broker, Commercial Insurance (Hybrid NY, CT)
Job.JobDescription:
Posting Description Who We Are: NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com. Summary: The Associate Broker will provide support to broking team members and give recommendations, problem solving, and solution development for prospects and clients. With direction from senior team members, they will develop a comprehensive understanding of prospect and client risk profiles and exposures, and act to cultivate and maximize insurance market interest leading to the development of effective risk financing and risk transfer solutions. This role focuses on tailoring required coverage, terms and conditions, and developing the appropriate program architecture and design. The Associate Broker will require supervision and direction from more senior team members. This is a full-time, hybrid position requiring three days per week in the office. Candidates may be based out of any of the following locations: Albany, Rochester (Pittsford), Williamsville (Buffalo), White Plains, NY, or Boston, MA. To support hybrid work, candidates must have access to a reliable, private workspace free from interruptions, as well as a stable high-speed internet connection. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Begin to participate in the analysis of clients’ or prospects’ existing programs and ensure requirements. Review current policies and formulate recommendations for customized risk solutions Work with senior team members to effectively negotiate with insurance carriers; drives financial and non-financial outcomes that support organic revenue development and retention. Seize upon opportunities to creatively upsell and cross-sell, leading to greater client product density and expanded account margin Learn NFP’s service model standards and timelines to ensure placements are handled accordingly Support the team in developing client/prospect diagnostics – working at the direction of the Broker or Senior Broker to complete a total program assessment, including total cost of risk, service deliverables, and opportunities for multi-faceted program improvement Assist in timely production of required documentation and follow-up, ensuring timely flow of materials Assist team members with proposal development for existing and prospective clients Respond to client queries and concerns to resolve issues promptly Review binders and policies to ensure terms and conditions are accurately reflected Attend client meetings with team; leading to refined and enhanced client communication and presentation skills Support the deployment of data and analytics to provide program insights for clients and the broking team Begin to develop productive business relationships with key insurance underwriters and local NFP account teams Execute on NFP’s broking strategies, including strategic carriers, panels, and preferred wholesaler utilization Develop and maintain a thorough knowledge of the insurance marketplace, and the various lines, products and services offered by various insurers Ensure client, broking and brokerage data files are maintained in a complete, organized and timely fashion Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities: Strong written and verbal communication skills Ability to successfully interact with a variety of people Solid negotiation skills – ability to adjust approach to effectively drive optimal outcomes depending on different personalities Proven ability to work independently and as part of a team Strong attention to detail, demonstrating reliability and accuracy Strong organizational skills with the ability to adjust to changing workload and priorities Able to coordinate resources and responsibilities Self-motivated with positive attitude Detail-oriented with strong analytical skills, both quantitative and qualitative Proven knowledge using Microsoft Office Suite Experience with Epic (agency management system) a plus Education and/or Experience: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent required Solid understanding of carrier underwriting practices and processes preferred Certificates, Licenses, Registration: P&C License required or obtained within 90 days of employment Advanced industry designation(s) (e.g. CPCU, CIC, ARM) a plus What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $75,000 – $90,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! NFP is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. #NFP 2586289

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Customer Service Representative, Customer Service / Account Support
Job.JobDescription:
Posting Description Who We Are Lenox Advisors brings together sophisticated solutions in wealth management and insurance services to high-net-worth individuals and their families. As a wholly owned subsidiary of NFP Corp., an Aon Company, we combine the culture of a boutique firm with the stability and backing of a large corporation to create an environment that's truly unique. NFP is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance. We’re a recognized Elite Agency award winner and a leading property and casualty broker, benefits consultant, wealth manager, and retirement plan advisor. NFP provides solutions enabling client success through the expertise of over 8,000 global employees, investments in innovative technologies, and enduring relationships with highly rated insurers, vendors and financial institutions. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com. Position Summary Supports the Relationship Manager by scheduling and coordinating activities and initiatives that facilitate the new policy and client service processes. The Client Services Associate must provide superior client service by identifying the client’s wants and needs, acting on, and/or delegating items and following through to completion while keeping all parties informed throughout the process. Responsibilities Pre-Sale and New Business Assembles meeting preparation documents pertaining to the client/prospect prior to sales meetings, including but not limited to, illustrations, policy and product summaries, reports, presentations, and marketing packets Performs all insurance underwriting duties, including preparation and completion of multi-life and individual disability, life, and long term care applications Schedules medical insurance exams and orders all Attending Physician Statements based on insurance underwriting guidelines Follows up with the client and Relationship Manager during the underwriting process, keeps notes on the process and conversations in MOSAIC Collaborates with the New Business Team to manage all new business arguments using MOSAIC as the system of record for status, notes, and tasks. Communicates with RM and client as necessary. Job.JobDescription:
Posting Description Who We Are: NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management, and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com. Position Summary: Are you looking for an outstanding opportunity to gain invaluable experience in a dynamic and collaborative environment? The Communications Intern position at NFP, an Aon company, offers just that! As an intern, you will be an integral part of our six-person team, responsible for crafting and maintaining our enrollment communication pieces and day-to-day materials. This role provides the chance to work on company-wide projects, interact with different teams, and contribute meaningfully to our growing business. Position Responsibilities: Essential Functions: Assist the Communications team in crafting, editing, and reviewing client communications, including Word documents, websites, and presentations. Coordinate and maintain Communications team resources and materials. Participate in company-wide projects, collaborating with various teams to ensure flawless execution. Support the team in implementing creative solutions for internal and external communications. Qualifications: The ideal candidate will possess: Attention to detail. A high level of accountability and ownership of work. Ability to work in a fast-paced team with specific deadlines. Resourcefulness and the ability to consult with others to get a job done. Strong ability to prioritize tasks and manage time effectively. A team-oriented, friendly, and collaborative attitude. Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly in Word and PowerPoint. Ability to input creativity and original ideas into projects. Familiarity with Adobe Creative Cloud applications is advantageous. Education/Experience: Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience. A degree or equivalent experience in Business Administration What We Offer: Our PeopleFirst culture emphasizes building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because our purpose is to support others. The base salary range for this position is $18 to $25 per hour. The salary offered depends on factors such as experience, credentials, education, certifications, required skill level, the position’s scope, and geographic location. Each salary offer is made individually. This position may also qualify for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! #LI-RN1 #LI-HYBRID 2588720

We provide a comprehensive platform that brings together wealth management, institutional consulting, business management, family office, and retirement plan advisory services—empowering clients to navigate complexity with clarity and confidence. With over 1,200 employees across more than 40 offices, we deliver insights and solutions backed by deep research, technology, and decades of expertise. Our collective businesses create a unified ecosystem designed to meet clients wherever they are in their financial journey. Wealthspire is redefining the future of financial solutions through collaboration, scale, and a steadfast commitment to putting people first—our clients, our colleagues, and our communities. For more information, visit www.wealthspire.com. Wealthspire Advisors LLC, Fiducient Advisors LLC, Wealthspire Retirement, LLC, dba Wealthspire Retirement Advisory, and certain other affiliates are separately registered investment advisers. Summary: Our Advisor Associates works directly with Advisors to assist with the wealth management and financial planning needs of clients. This position is responsible for providing support to Advisors including data gathering, case design, scenario building, financial plan development, financial plan application, and portfolio implementation. Responsibilities: Provide support to Advisors in all areas of financial planning. Initiate and field client calls on various items (e.g., strategy ideas, account specific questions, portfolio inquiries, etc.). Create proposals for prospective clients. Create and/or update financial plans for clients. Prepare materials for client meetings; work with other internal teams to ensure client meetings are prepared for thoroughly and accurately. Attend client meetings and manage/complete all meeting follow-up activities. Liaise with client’s attorneys and accountants as needed. Monitor portfolios and maintain portfolio target allocations. Rebalance portfolios as needed Assist with client data consolidation and maintenance as needed. Assist with special projects as required. Qualifications: 0-4 years of relevant experience. Completed or pursuing CFP®, CFA or JD. Bachelors’ degree or higher from an accredited university; major in financial planning, business, accounting, finance, economics, or law preferred Continuously exhibits personal integrity and professional initiative. Reliable, follows through on commitments, self-starter when it comes to new challenges. Must be organized, detail-oriented and able to manage and prioritize tasks. Demonstrates a commitment to accuracy by delivering high quality work. Excellent written and verbal communication. Collaborative and able to work effectively with others Series 65 – or able to successfully complete within 90 days of employment. Do you see yourself excelling in this position? Don't hesitate to apply, even if you don't meet every qualification on the list. We recognize that career journeys are as unique as individuals themselves, and valuable skills can come in various forms. We're eager to learn about your unique talents and experiences. What We Offer: Wealthspire Advisors is proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $68,000 – $80,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Customer Service Representative, Customer Service / Account Support
Job.JobDescription:
Posting Description Who We Are: NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management, and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com. Summary: The Account Manager works with Account Executives, Producers and Senior team members to provide day-to-day account management for commercial Property & Casualty clients within the Life Science & Healthcare Team. This role manages client service needs, supports the renewal and marketing process, maintains accurate account documentation, and communicates directly with clients, carriers, and other business partners. The Account Manager is expected to understand assigned clients and their insurance programs, proactively manage responsibilities through completion, and exercise independent judgement on routine account matters. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Serve as the primary contact for day-to-day client service needs, developing positive relationships with clients and carrier partners. Collaborate with internal service teams to deliver timely and accurate client service, and participate in both internal and client-facing meetings. Support the renewal and marketing process, including gathering exposure information, preparing submissions, acquiring loss runs, and updating applications. Review quotes, proposals, policies, binders, endorsements, and other insurance documents for accuracy and completeness. Process or coordinate policy changes, endorsements, certificates, evidence of property, auto ID cards, and other client deliverables. Maintain accurate policy and client information within the agency management system. Coordinate invoicing, premium finance, audits, loss control requirements, and routine accounting matters. Identify and bring up complex coverage, exposure, negotiation, or strategic issues to senior team members. Be flexible and adaptable to changing priorities, deadlines, and technology. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Practical understanding of commercial Property & Casualty insurance and account servicing. Self-confidence to make sound independent decisions. Strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and attention-to-detail skills. Ability to prioritize tasks and work independently while recognizing when a blocking issue requires attention. Excellent written and verbal communication and follow-up skills. Ability to handle situations in a calm, courteous, and professional manner. Customer-focused to establish and maintain effective relationships. Proficiency with Microsoft Office and agency management systems. Proficiency with using AI tools and maintaining appropriate security and confidentiality, or a willingness to learn. Education and Experience Associate degree or equivalent experience; BA/BS preferred. 5+ years of commercial insurance, client service, or Property & Casualty account management experience preferred. Experience with complex commercial accounts and/or wholesale/E&S placements is a plus. Licensing A Property & Casualty Insurance License is necessary. What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is 75,300.00 - 92,700.00. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! NFP is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer #LI-REMOTE 2591835

Position Summary The Production Associate supports the production and delivery of personalized enrollment communications for Individual Disability Insurance (IDI) and Long-Term Care (LTC) programs. The role works with participant data and approved communications to create accurate print and digital materials, perform quality checks, and coordinate production and distribution with internal teams and external vendors. Prepare production files and supporting materials for internal processing and external vendors. Quality Assurance & Data Validation Perform detailed quality assurance reviews throughout the production process to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and consistency of client communications. Vendor Management Coordinate with external print, mailing, fulfillment, and other production vendors to ensure jobs are executed according to specifications and deadlines. Operational & Resource Management Support onsite production and mailing activities, including printing, assembly, mailing preparation, and fulfillment. Maintain production resources, supplies, and operational trackers, and coordinate temporary staffing needs as required. Support process improvements, documentation, and additional projects based on business needs. Qualifications: Experience using Microsoft Office Suite Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and Word mail merge a plus. Strong attention to detail with the ability to accurately manage large volumes of data and personalized materials. Proficiency with Adobe PDF Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines. Analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify discrepancies and determine appropriate next steps. Effective written and verbal communication skills, including coordination with internal teams and external vendors. Flexibility and willingness to adapt to changing client requirements, timelines, and business priorities. Ability to work from the Long Island office as needed based on business and operational requirements. Education/Experience: High School Diploma or GED Required. Bachelor’s Degree preferred. Administrative, data management, communication, or project coordination skills. Experience in employee benefits, insurance, enrollment, or a related industry is a plus. Job.JobTitle: AVP, East Central Broking Leader (Hybrid, Indianapolis)
Job.JobDescription:
Posting Description Who We Are: NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com. The AVP, East Central Broking Leader will drive commercial P&C strategy and market execution across the Northeast, leading all aspects of complex placements, strengthening carrier relationships, and partnering with producers and account teams to accelerate growth and retention. Location: Hybrid - Indianapolis Key Responsibilities Strategic Leadership Lead strategy development and marketing for a book of NFP clients in the Northeast region. Partner with the account service team and client to gain strategy alignment and establishes a plan and timeline to complete the strategy. Implement national and regional broking strategies to ensure optimal outcomes for NFP’s clients Engage with producers to identify market opportunities and support new business strategies. Develop and complete strategy for at-risk accounts, ensuring retention and profitability. Identify book of business optimization opportunities Operational Process Drive placement strategy and execution – client needs assessment, program design, carrier negotiation and marketing execution to deliver customized solutions for NFP clients; ensure a go-to-market strategy is in place for each broking engagement Collaborate with account management team and client to ensure complete and timely submissions, respond to carrier queries, compile and analyze carrier quote proposals, and present clients with a clear summary of the marketing process and a proposal with recommendations Determine proper coverage given the client risk profile, business objectives (current and future) and risk appetite to ensure and mitigate risk. Develop creative solutions to effectively address difficult placement scenarios; lead the process and drive outcomes to enhance customer satisfaction around key results Proactively coordinate and handle broking around the placement cycle in accordance with NFP’s service model standards and timelines Implement NFP’s broking strategies, including strategic carriers, panels, and preferred wholesaler utilization Support team members in responding to client queries and concerns to resolve issues promptly Drive and ensure the effective deployment of data and analytics to provide meaningful program insight for clients and the broking team Lead the preparation of proposal documents for marketed accounts Prepare complex coverage and policy comparisons, diagnostics, consolidated coverage/policy analyses, letters, and reports Manage the review of binders and policies to ensure terms and conditions are accurately reflected Partner with Producers and account teams during the sales process, including prospect qualification, program review, recommendations, marketing, RFP response, BOR issuance. Support the development of sales documents, presentations, stewardship reports, and RFP responses for prospective clients Support the broking team and region in achieving KPI’s including growth and retention objectives. Drive and support prospect sales efforts, expand existing client relationships through cross-sell and up-sell initiatives, ensure distinctive client value is delivered through all placement and facets of service engagement Talent Development Ensure consistency in broking standards and client delivery across the region. Mentor and train junior talent, fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, and growth. Educate AE/AM on market dynamics and market trends and how those factors affect the client and the placement strategy. Carrier Relationships Build and maintain strategic relationships with key carrier partners to enhance placement outcomes and market access. Develop strong, productive, trustful and resilient relationships with carrier and wholesale partners and their staff and NFP local office teams Know and stay abreast of carrier appetites. Ensure the right markets are approached for the right risks. Stay current on market trends, market dynamics and terms and conditions and educates the client to help them make better informed risk transfer decisions. Operate as a steward of the broader NFP while engaging in the marketplace. Qualifications 10+ years of experience in commercial P&C broking, with a strong understanding of mid-market dynamics. Proven leadership experience in managing teams and driving pivotal initiatives. Deep carrier relationships and market knowledge across the Northeast. Strong communication, negotiation, and partner management skills. Ability to mentor and develop talent across experience levels. Experience with Epic (agency management system) a plus Proven technical proficiency and creativity demonstrating excellence in developing and delivering innovative property and casualty solutions P&C Insurance License required Travel as the need arises for client, prospect and industry events What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $125,000 to $175,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! NFP is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. 2591023

We provide a comprehensive platform that brings together wealth management, institutional consulting, business management, family office, and retirement plan advisory services - empowering clients to navigate complexity with clarity and confidence. With over 1,200 employees across more than 40 offices, we deliver insights and solutions backed by deep research, technology, and decades of expertise. Our collective businesses create a unified ecosystem designed to meet clients wherever they are in their financial journey. Wealthspire is redefining the future of financial solutions through collaboration, scale, and a steadfast commitment to putting people first - our clients, our colleagues, and our communities. For more information, visit www.wealthspire.com. Wealthspire Advisors LLC, Fiducient Advisors LLC, Wealthspire Retirement, LLC , dba Wealthspire Retirement Advisory, and certain other affiliates are separately registered investment advisers. Position Overview The Office Coordinator plays an integral role in fostering a welcoming, well-organized, and collaborative workplace while embodying our core values: “Passion for the Client,” “Own It,” and “I Have Your Back.” This position delivers essential administrative and operational support by coordinating client meetings, managing incoming calls and office supplies, and ensuring conference rooms are consistently maintained and prepared to support a professional meeting experience. Key Responsibilities Client and Team Support Coordinate client calls, meetings, reservations, and related logistics in partnership with Advisors and Client Service Associates. Maintain accurate CRM records, including meeting notes, follow-up tasks, and client and prospect information. Support client communications, login assistance, and general administrative needs. Document, Mail, and Payment Processing Track client paperwork, maintain electronic files in SharePoint, and route documents for processing. Record and coordinate the deposit of incoming checks in accordance with established procedures. Manage document preparation, filing, mail, faxes, and shipments, ensuring timely processing and delivery. Office Operations and Events Manage the RingCentral phone system, troubleshoot issues, coordinate updates, and ensure backup coverage. Oversee office supplies, equipment, shared spaces, and facilities-related needs. Support new employee onboarding and maintain a welcoming, well-prepared workplace. Coordinate office events, community initiatives, client communications, reports, cards, and gifts. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree preferred. Minimum of two years of relevant administrative or office support experience. Strong attention to detail and a high level of numerical accuracy. Ability to prioritize multiple tasks, meet deadlines, and collaborate effectively in a team environment. Professional demeanor and strong customer service orientation. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office required. Experience with Salesforce or another CRM system preferred; familiarity with portfolio management and document management software is a plus. What We Offer: Wealthspire Advisors is proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, and more. The base salary range for this position is $55,000 –$65,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. Wealthspire is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. #Wealthspire 2589057

Wealthspire Advisors LLC, Fiducient Advisors LLC, Wealthspire Retirement, LLC , dba Wealthspire Retirement Advisory, and certain other affiliates are separately registered investment advisers. Summary: Wealthspire is seeking a highly skilled Network Architect to compose, build, and operate a secure, resilient, and scalable enterprise network environment. This role is critical to supporting Wealthspire’s modern cloud-first strategy, hybrid workforce, and ongoing growth initiatives, including carve-outs and future M&A integrations. The Network Architect will act as the technical lead for connectivity, networking standards, and network security. They will collaborate closely with Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Cloud, and End User Computing teams to deliver reliable and high-performing services throughout the firm. Key Responsibilities: Network Architecture & Engineering Build and maintain enterprise network architecture, including LAN, WAN, SD-WAN, Wi-Fi, VPN, cloud connectivity (Azure), and telephony/network integrations. Establish architecture standards, documentation, and roadmaps for routing, switching, segmentation, firewalling, and zero-trust networking. Architect, implement, and support enterprise network solutions across corporate offices, data centers, and cloud environments. Support Microsoft-centric environments (Azure, M365, Intune) with secure and optimized connectivity. Operations & Reliability Coordinate network monitoring, performance tuning, high availability, and incident response. Ensure redundancy, failover, and disaster recovery capabilities are tested and maintained. Act as a point of contact for complex network issues and customer concerns. Drive configuration, change, and lifecycle management guidelines. Security & Compliance Partner with the CISO organization on IAM integration, firewall policies, endpoint connectivity, and secure remote access. Support regulatory and compliance requirements (SOC 2, ISO 27001, SEC, GDPR, NYDFS). Carve-Outs & M&A Complete network separation and integration activities aligned to carve-out timelines. Lead network-related activities for carve-outs, separations, and M&A integrations, including developing repeatable playbooks. Vendor & Collaborator Management Manage network service providers, ISPs, telecom vendors, and MSPs, including day-to-day Technology operations and vendor relationships. Drive SLA performance, cost optimization, and vendor consolidation where appropriate. Work together with Infrastructure, Service Desk, Cloud, and End User Computing teams to provide smooth employee experiences. Qualifications: 8–12+ years of experience in enterprise networking and infrastructure roles. Proven experience as a Network Architect or Senior Network Engineer in a complex environment. Deep hands-on expertise with SD-WAN, firewalls, VPNs, routing/switching, and cloud networking (Azure). Experience supporting hybrid workforces and multi-site enterprise environments. Exposure to carve-outs, integrations, or M&A activity strongly preferred. Strong documentation, communication, and collaborator engagement skills. Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience). Relevant certifications (e.g., Cisco, Palo Alto, Fortinet, Azure Networking) are a plus. What Makes This Role Unique Opportunity to build and modernize enterprise network architecture in a growing wealth management firm. High visibility role with impact across security, cloud, and end-user experience. Collaborative culture passionate about operational excellence, resilience, and innovation. Hybrid work environment with flexibility and career growth opportunities. What We Offer: Wealthspire is proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, and more. The base salary range for this position is $100,000 –$120,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. Wealthspire is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. #Wealthspire 2588725

(small market only) Understand and articulate alternative funding strategies. (large market only) Build and maintain positive relationships with carriers, companies and clients Keep clients apprised of appropriate industry trends and events, including all state and federal regulatory issues Manage relationships with carrier representatives in order to better understand available products and services in the marketplace and recommend them to clients Anticipate client needs and identify the strategies to tackle them Review request for proposals and insurance plan analyses, negotiate with carriers and recommend renewal actions. Job.JobTitle: 2027 Wealthspire IT Innovation Intern - Chicago, IL
Job.JobDescription:
Posting Description IT Innovation Intern – 2027 SUMMER PROGRAM Wealth Management Company – Private Equity Backed Carve-Out About the Company: Wealthspire is a leading wealth management, retirement advisory, and business management firm serving individuals, families, endowments, and institutions across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. We provide a comprehensive platform that brings together wealth management, institutional consulting, business management, family office, and retirement plan advisory services - empowering clients to navigate complexity with clarity and confidence. With over 1,200 employees across more than 40 offices, we deliver insights and solutions backed by deep research, technology, and decades of expertise. Our collective businesses create a unified ecosystem designed to meet clients wherever they are in their financial journey. Wealthspire is redefining the future of financial solutions through collaboration, scale, and a steadfast commitment to putting people first - our clients, our colleagues, and our communities. For more information, visit www.wealthspire.com. Internship Program Overview: Wealthspire Advisors 10-week Summer Internship Program is designed to provide students with a challenging, meaningful, and supportive experience that closely mirrors the experience of a full-time Associate. We are seeking a highly motivated and curious IT Innovation Intern to support technology, data, automation, and artificial intelligence initiatives. This role is ideal for a student interested in applying emerging technologies to improve business processes, strengthen employee and client experiences, and create measurable organizational value.The intern will work with business and technology leaders to research new capabilities, support proofs of concept, analyze data, document solutions, and contribute to initiatives involving AI, low-code development, analytics, enterprise applications, and change adoption. Key responsibilities include: Research emerging technologies, industry trends, and innovation opportunities relevant to business needs. Assist with the design, testing, and deployment of AI, automation, analytics, and digital transformation solutions. Support development of Microsoft Power Apps, Power Automate workflows, Power BI reports, and Copilot Studio agents. Help identify manual or inefficient processes that could benefit from automation, improved data, or redesigned workflows. Assist with data collection, cleansing, validation, analysis, and reporting activities. Create dashboards, visualizations, process maps, requirements, technical documentation, and user guides. Support proof-of-concept projects, pilot programs, application testing, quality assurance, and user acceptance testing. Participate in stakeholder meetings to understand business challenges, document needs, and evaluate solution options. Help develop training materials, adoption resources, and communications for new technology initiatives. Contribute to innovation workshops, demonstrations, brainstorming sessions, and continuous improvement efforts. Qualifications: Required Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Analytics, Business Analytics, Engineering, or a related field. Strong interest in technology, innovation, artificial intelligence, data, and business transformation. Excellent analytical, problem-solving, written communication, and verbal communication skills. Ability to learn new technologies quickly and work effectively across business and technical teams. Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and proficiency with Microsoft Office applications. Preferred Familiarity with Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI, or Copilot Studio. Exposure to generative AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar technologies. Basic understanding of databases, SQL, data modeling, or data visualization concepts. Experience with a programming language such as Python, JavaScript, or C#. Familiarity with Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Dataverse, Dynamics 365, or Azure. Coursework, projects, or prior experience involving analytics, automation, software development, or process improvement. Desired Attributes: Naturally curious, eager to learn, and comfortable experimenting with new ideas. Passionate about finding practical, responsible ways to solve business problems with technology. Innovative and creative while remaining attentive to quality, security, privacy, and usability. Self-motivated, dependable, collaborative, and able to manage assigned work with appropriate guidance. Learning Opportunities: Artificial intelligence and generative AI Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, and Power Platform Business process automation and enterprise applications Data analytics, reporting, governance, and data quality Agile project delivery, change management, and technology adoption What Success Looks Like: Contributes to meaningful business and technology initiatives. Develops practical skills using modern enterprise technology platforms. Builds or supports solutions that improve efficiency, insight, or the user experience. Collaborates effectively with business stakeholders and technical team members. Communicates findings, recommendations, and demonstrated results clearly. The summer internship experience provides interns with meaningful exposure to the financial planning and investment management process while building the skills needed for a successful career in financial services. Do you see yourself excelling in this position? Don't hesitate to apply, even if you don't meet every qualification on the list. We recognize that career journeys are as unique as individuals themselves, and valuable skills can come in various forms. We're eager to learn about your unique talents and experiences. The hourly range for this position is $20.00 – $22.00 per hour. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. Wealthspire is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. #Wealthspire 2592139

Handle all aspects of the placements from initial market selection through policy delivery to client. effectively closes coverage gaps or deficiencies, supports the account team in improving client product density, enhancing account profitability and margin Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities: Excellent written and verbal communication skills Excellent negotiation skills – ability to adjust approach to effectively drive optimal outcomes depending on different personalities Strong attention to detail with strong analytical skills, both quantitative and qualitative Proven technical competency and creativity demonstrating excellence in developing and delivering innovative property and casualty solutions Confident, poised and interactive - when client-facing communicates effectively, demonstrates emotional intelligence, and understands how to tailor responses in a variety of dynamic situations Experience with Epic (agency management system) a plus Education and/or Experience: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required Minimum of two to five years property & casualty insurance experience Certificates, Licenses, Registration: P&C License required or obtained within 90 days of employment Advanced industry designation(s) (e.g. CPCU, CIC, ARM) a plus What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. About the Position Join us as a Brand Intern at Wealthspire Advisors where you will have an outstanding chance to join a highly motivated team. Posting Description Who We Are: Lenox Advisors is a premier MassMutual agency supporting a network of financial professionals who provide insurance, investment, and financial planning solutions to clients nationwide. As part of NFP, an Aon company, we offer the resources of a large organization while maintaining the culture and agility of a high-performing agency. Our team is dedicated to delivering exceptional advisor support, effective supervision, and operational excellence that drive business growth and client confidence. Summary of Role: The Junior Agency Supervisory Officer is central to maintaining a strong supervisory framework, ensuring adherence to regulatory standards, and supporting the success of our registered representatives. You’ll serve as a key resource for oversight, mentorship, and resolving partner concerns across our agency. Job Accountabilities: Provide day-to-day supervision of registered representatives in accordance with FINRA, SEC, and firm policies. Review and approve communications with the public. Conduct periodic audits, inspections, and risk assessments for assigned branches. Conduct Personal Interviews with advisors and credentialed employees Monitor sales practices to ensure suitability, proper documentation, and regulatory compliance. Act as a subject-matter expert on supervisory procedures, compliance requirements, and industry guidelines for our advisor and registered staff community. Investigate and resolve escalated issues, customer complaints, and potential violations. Deliver training and coaching to representatives and managers on compliance expectations and supervisory standards. Collaborate with Compliance, Operations, and Field Leadership to strengthen supervisory controls and support business growth. Maintain accurate records and prepare reports for internal review and regulatory inquiries. Conduct email and social media reviews and partner with firm management to maintain corrective action plans. Review outgoing/incoming correspondence for compliance Take control of the Implementation for Firm Element Cont. Education Program Review and carry out 3rd Party verification Phone Calls for checks and wires Review outgoing/incoming correspondence for compliance Conduct 3rd Party verification phone calls for checks and wires Skills and Competencies: Excellent analytical, communication, and decision-making skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining accuracy and regulatory integrity. High level of integrity, discretion, and ethical judgment. Education, Experience, License Requirements: Active FINRA Series 7 and Series 63 required. Series 65/66 and Series 24 preferred. 3–5+ years of supervisory, compliance, or field leadership experience within a broker-dealer or financial services environment. Strong understanding of FINRA/SEC regulations, supervisory controls, and sales practice standards. What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $73,800.00 – $118,100.00. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! Job.JobTitle: AVP, Risk Due Diligence M&A Manager (Hybrid, US)
Job.JobDescription:
Posting Description Who We Are NFP, an Aon Company, is a multi-year Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com. NFP's Private Equity Group is seeking an Assistant Vice President, Risk Due Diligence M&A Manager to support and enhance our growing due diligence practice. This role offers the opportunity to work on sophisticated transactions, serve as a trusted advisor to private equity investors, and influence how risk and insurance considerations are evaluated throughout the deal process. The AVP will be responsible for managing complex diligence engagements, delivering high-quality client advisory services, and contributing to the continued evolution of NFP's due diligence capabilities. This position is ideal for an experienced insurance professional who enjoys solving complex transactional challenges, leading internal client teams, working directly with clients, and providing expert risk guidance in a fast-paced environment. Key Responsibilities Lead complex risk and insurance due diligence engagements for private equity transactions across a broad range of industries. Serve as a key client contact throughout the transaction lifecycle, providing consultative guidance and strategic recommendations. Contribute to enhancements to due diligence methodologies, reporting standards, and workflow efficiency to improve client outcomes and consistency of deliverables. Evaluate insurance programs, claims history, collateral arrangements, captive structures, and insurance-related financial exposures. Identify transaction-related risks and collaborate with internal and external advisors to develop effective solutions. Partner with brokers, coverage specialists, producers, client service teams, and M&A professionals to assess findings and craft risk management strategies. Deliver accurate, comprehensive, and actionable due diligence reports and executive-level presentations. Occasional travel as required Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Risk Management, Finance, Accounting, Business, Insurance, or a related field. 7+ years of experience in the insurance industry, with significant experience supporting private equity, M&A, transactional risk, or due diligence engagements. Expertise in Property & Casualty insurance and specialty lines, including Cyber, Professional Liability, Financial Lines, Environmental, and Captive programs. Understanding of financial statements, accounting concepts, insurance-related financial analysis, and transaction structures. Strong ability to manage multiple complex engagements and deliver high-quality work within tight deadlines. Client-facing presence and ability to build credibility with senior stakeholders. Outstanding written, verbal, and presentation skills. Advanced proficiency in Excel, financial analysis, and report preparation. Preferred Qualifications P&C preferred or ability to obtain within six months of hire What We Offer We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $100,000 – $135,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. NFP and You... Better Together! NFP is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. #LI-HYBRID #LI-BW1 #NFP 2588323
