Posting Description Who We Are: NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com. NFP is looking for an enthusiastic and experienced relationship management professional. This role will be focused on strategic relationship management and retention of Mid-Market core clients. Location: Chicago preferred RESPONSIBILITIES: Responsible for managing the overall relationship with assigned Mid-Market core clients including developing and engaging multiple relationships throughout and within the client organization. Establish oneself as client’s primary point of contact and communication conduit for NFP; keep client producer informed at all times. Cultivate internal and external relationships to establish effective open collaboration, client advocacy, and trust. Develop and obtain a broad knowledge of internal operations to efficiently and effectively solve the needs of the audience and the circumstances at hand. Maintain accurate records of client (or prospect) contacts and their products utilizing account management software or other technology. Developing and maintaining a robust understanding and tracking system of key client personnel and their products is essential. Drive revenue growth on existing and new clients through development of a strategic consultative sales plan in conjunction with producer including identifying and executing cross-sell opportunities when appropriate. Establish oneself as a self-starter leader with client account teams and take ownership of the success of client and colleague relationships. Contribute to client team’s holistic service strategy and establish quality standards to improve client’s experience. Demonstrate a broad understanding of insurance products and coverages, their applicability, relevant industry trends, and basic program design. The ability to understand basic insurance program structure and content is essential. Develop expertise, and remain current, in assigned client industry and/or market area, NFP’s resources and capabilities, and engage in structured continuing education Produce an annual or semi-annual stewardship report that highlights NFP’s efforts for the client over the previous twelve months. Establish, execute, and accountable for implementation of the formal NFP strategic relationship management cadence. Seeks annual client feedback/grading on NFP’s performance Travel to visit clients and engage in client development activities and entertainment. Travel approximately 25%-40%; must see clients in person at least twice annually. REQUIRED SKILLS & QUALITIES: 10+ years' experience in relationship management with face-to-face private equity (or similar) client experience. Exceptional interpersonal skills capable of interacting with private equity and C-suite clients to cultivate strong relationships through effective communication and trust. Elite project management, communication, and presentation skills. Manages time effectively through excellent organization, time-management, and multi-tasking skills. Entrepreneurial attitude with natural ability to take ownership of overall success of client relationships. Commitment to delivering exceptional customer service and results. Naturally anticipates and analyzes problems and information to proactively solve problems through critical thinking, team networking, and sound business decisions. Dedication to working in collaborative, team-oriented environment with a commitment to operating with respect and integrity. Proficient in Microsoft Office products (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint). Property & Casualty producer license and Benefits License (or ability to get licensed quickly). Bachelors’ degree from four-year college or university preferred. What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $128,000 to $184,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! NFP is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. #LI-JS3 #LI-JS3 #NFP VP000015048

Job.JobTitle: Sr. Account Executive - Private Client Broking Specialist
Job.JobDescription:
Posting Description Who We Are: NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com. Summary: The Senior Account Executive interacts with clients on a day-to-day basis while developing and maintaining relationships with both client and carrier representatives. This individual will prepare applications, specifications and marketing strategy for new business as well as the renewals of assigned clients with little to no supervision from their Supervisor on difficult lines. This role requires the employee to take on the role of lead consultant and primary point of contact for clients. The Senior Account Executive may work on large, complex accounts with large premiums and multifaceted coverages. The role may also support the marketing and placement of complex Personal Risk and Private Client accounts, partnering with carrier markets to develop tailored insurance solutions for high-net-worth individuals and families. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Negotiates terms, conditions, coverage limits and pricing with carriers and wholesalers. Sr. level facilitates requests and needs of the carriers on behalf of NFP's clients. Works with the Claims Department on relevant claims for assigned clients. Requires expertise in multi-line accounts with more sophisticated coverages including retrospective rating plans for large lines of coverages and foreign packages. Maintains a diary (follow-up system) to ensure policies, endorsements and other information is received to align with requests May supervise and advise the daily job activities of the Coordinators, Account Managers and Account Executives. Build and maintain strong relationships with carriers, and clients through regular contact and client visits. Keep clients apprised of appropriate industry trends and events, including all state and federal regulatory issues. Develop and implement marketing strategies for sophisticated Personal Risk and Private Client accounts, including high-net-worth portfolios, luxury residences, collections, excess liability, and specialty coverages. Market new and renewal business to carrier partners, evaluating coverage alternatives and placement options to secure competitive and customized solutions for clients. Collaborate with producers, account teams, and carrier underwriters to design risk management and insurance solutions that address the outstanding exposures of affluent individuals and families. Maintain positive relationships with Private Client carrier partners and stay informed of market conditions, underwriting appetite, and emerging coverage solutions to support client retention and growth. Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities: Excellent written communication skills – writes clearly; edits work for spelling and grammar; varies writing style to meet needs; presents numeric data effectively; able to read and interpret written information. Self-confident to make sound independent decisions Ability to successfully interact with a variety of people/personalities Strong leadership skills Must be able to read, analyze and reconcile financial reports Possess technical expertise plus good analytical and problem-solving skills Ability to handle situations in a calm, courteous and professional manner Education and/or Experience: BA/BS preferred Typically more than 8 years industry and product line experience Certificates, Licenses, Registration: Property & Casualty Broker's License required CIC, CPCU or other P&C designation preferred. What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $56,000 to $132,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! NFP is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. #NFP SENIO014855

Job.JobDescription:
Posting Description Who We Are: Wealthspire is a leading wealth management, retirement advisory, and business management firm serving individuals, families, endowments, and institutions across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. We provide a comprehensive platform that brings together wealth management, institutional consulting, business management, family office, and retirement plan advisory services—empowering clients to navigate complexity with clarity and confidence. With over $580B in assets under advisement, and more than 1,200 employees across 40+ offices, we deliver insights and solutions grounded in deep research, advanced technology, and decades of expertise. Our collective businesses create a unified ecosystem designed to meet clients wherever they are in their financial journey. Wealthspire is redefining the future of financial solutions through collaboration, scale, and a steadfast commitment to putting people first—our clients, our colleagues, and our communities. For more information, visit www.wealthspire.com. Wealthspire Advisors LLC, Fiducient Advisors LLC, Wealthspire Retirement, LLC, dba Wealthspire Retirement Advisory, and certain other affiliates are separately registered investment advisers. Key responsibilities include: Assist with the development and preparation of client financial plans. Support portfolio construction, analysis, and client portfolio reviews. Reconcile and review financial data to ensure accuracy and completeness. Conduct investment and market research to support client needs and firm initiatives. Assist with the review and allocation of 529 college savings plans. Research client-specific questions and issues and present findings to team members. Collaborate with colleagues across the firm to gain exposure to different areas of the business. Develop and present clear, concise analysis and recommendations. Qualifications: Pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Finance preferred, or an undergraduate/graduate degree program aligned with the CFP® certification. Demonstrated interest in financial planning and wealth management. Demonstrates integrity, professionalism, and initiative. Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Highly organized and detail-oriented. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Collaborative and able to work effectively in a team environment. Do you see yourself excelling in this position? Don't hesitate to apply, even if you don't meet every qualification on the list! We recognize that career journeys are as unique as individuals themselves, and valuable skills can come in various forms. We're eager to learn about your unique talents and experiences! The hourly range for this position is $20.00 – $22.00 per hour. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Sales Manager, Insurance Sales, Insurance Sales Representative
Job.JobDescription:
Posting Description Who We Are: NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance who has also earned the WORK180 employer endorsement. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com. Job Summary: P&C Private Client Group (PCG/affluent lines) is a division of NFP Property & Casualty. We are a retail operation for affluent and wealthy individuals and families seeking personal lines products in the United States, parts of Europe, and Canada. Our headquarters are in New York City with offices across the country - specializing in insurance ranging from homeowners and auto to specialty lines, such as aircraft and watercraft. This is a full-time role with the flexibility of a hybrid work schedule from our Bethesda, MD office. We are open to considering an exceptionally qualified remote candidate. Some travel may be required for business or client deliverables. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Builds, manages, and leads a team to handle marketing, ongoing service, and risk management. Leads sales activities with P&C complex clients and prospects. Confers with senior sales leaders on setting targets and reports actual results. Reviews sales results with members of sales team, strategizing changes and troubleshooting problems. Influences policies and may monitor sales teams within office to ensure compliance. Involved in new hire selections and internal promotions that impact the sales team. May require review with the SVP or other senior leader. Develops and initiates plans to increase sales, lower costs, and continuously improve operations. Confers with senior management on setting targets and reports actual results. Reviews sales results with subordinates, strategizing changes and troubleshooting problems. Establishes and maintains relationships with key client and prospect stakeholders and carrier representatives. Acts as subject matter authority for company products and services. Provides mentoring and coaching to team members. May be involved in setting policies and the monitoring of offices within the region to ensure compliance. May decide on all new hire selections and internal promotions. Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities: When working from home, you must maintain a private workspace to secure company equipment and correspondence; maintain high-speed internet, be present and responsive online and minimize personal interruptions during your work shift Must have Personal Lines and High Net Worth/Private Client Group (PCG) client coverage experience P&C Account/Client Management experience with a retail brokerage or independent agency Familiarity with major markets, such as AIG, Chubb/ACE, PURE, BerkleyOne and Cincinnati. This includes knowledge of their products, appetite and experience with their quoting systems Must be able to read, analyze and reconcile financial reports Highly professional and self-motivated Excellent verbal and interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate with clients, colleagues, and carriers and interact with a variety of people/personalities Proficiency in Outlook, Word, and Excel. Possess technical expertise plus solid analytical and problem-solving skills Strong writing skills include clear writing and careful editing for spelling and grammar. The candidate varies writing style to suit needs, presents numeric data effectively, and reads and interprets written information. Self-confident to make sound independent decisions and demonstrate strong leadership skills Ability to handle situations in a calm, courteous and professional manner Commanding presentation and public speaking abilities Education and/or Experience: BA/BS preferred; Master's degree in relevant subject (e.g., business, statistics, math/science, actuarial science) also desirable More than 15 years of directly related industry sales experience. In addition to familiarity with the major markets as mentioned above, a familiarity with carriers such as Travelers and Progressive as well as The National Flood Ins. Program Leadership and supervisory experience, including training or mentorship Experience with an agency management system/CRM is required. Fluency with Epic is a plus What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $200,000-275,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! Job.JobDescription:
Posting Description Who We Are Lenox Advisors is a premier MassMutual agency supporting a network of financial professionals who provide insurance, investment, and financial planning solutions to clients nationwide. As part of NFP, an Aon company, we offer the resources of a large organization while maintaining the culture and agility of a high-performing agency. Our team is dedicated to delivering exceptional advisor support, effective supervision, and operational excellence that drive business growth and client confidence. Position Summary & Overall Purpose Supports the Relationship Manager by scheduling and coordinating activities and initiatives that facilitate the new policy and client service processes. The Client Services Associate must provide superior client service by identifying the client’s wants and needs, acting on, and/or delegating items and following through to completion while keeping all parties informed throughout the process. What You’ll Be Doing Pre-Sale and New Business Assembles meeting preparation documents pertaining to the client/prospect prior to sales meetings, including but not limited to, illustrations, policy and product summaries, reports, presentations, and marketing packets Performs all insurance underwriting duties, including preparation and completion of multi-life and individual disability, life, and long-term care applications Schedules medical insurance exams and orders all Attending Physician Statements based on insurance underwriting guidelines Follows up with the client and Relationship Manager during the underwriting process, keeps notes on the process and conversations in MOSAIC Partners with the New Business Team to manage all new business reasons. Uses MOSAIC as the system of record for status, notes, and tasks. Communicates with RM and client as necessary. Participates in Relationship Manager/New Business case management calls Reviews insurance policies and prepares them for delivery; follows up on delivery requirements when needed Ensures Relationship Manager has appropriate Licensing and Appointments and works with internal contracting and licensing contact to obtain and renew licenses Partners with Advanced Sales to obtain and/or generate the appropriate illustrations/one-pagers Processes all policy changes including reinstatement of lapsed cases, smoker rating changes, addition or removal of policy riders, and face amount reductions Partners with Private Wealth Management Team to process individual asset management applications, service requests, and performance summaries Coordinates tasks and responsibilities for all joint work Client Service Processes all insurance policy service requests, including address, beneficiary/ownership changes, premium mode changes, and dividend option changes Provides superior client service by identifying client’s wants and needs, acting on, and/or delegating items and following through to completion, keeping all parties informed throughout the process Coordinates all collateral assignments, death or disability claims, and fund allocation changes with the assistance of the Relationship Manager Interacts daily with insurance carriers and vendors to ensure accurate and timely execution of client service requests Takes a proactive lead on conserving the Relationship Manager’s existing block of business by notifying clients of overdue insurance premiums and coverage in danger of lapsing, tracking all attempts and progress, and keeping the Relationship Manager informed of problematic cases Ability to follow through on a variety of requests and ability to create resolution on client and/or service related matters. Creates client correspondence as needed according to the Lenox Style Guide Business Operations Responsible for greeting clients, fielding phone calls, reviewing incoming mail, managing office supplies, ordering client gifts, and maintaining client files Manages the Relationship Manager’s calendar, scheduling and confirming client meetings, registering visitors with security, and booking conference rooms Ensures data accuracy by regularly and routinely updating information in MOSAIC and maintaining client files. This includes, but is not limited to, fact find information and notes, case management (individual and MultiLife), task management, and client and policy information Participates in occasional training and development sessions as directed by department(s) and Regional Manager Creates feeder lists as requested Partners with the Relationship Manager when participating in Lenox marketing campaigns, including MOSAIC list updates as well as updating client email addresses What We’re Looking For Required Knowledge Knowledge of office equipment operations (copier, scanner, printers) and electronic calendaring programs (Microsoft Outlook) Familiarity with business principles and practices Familiarity working with Client Database Management systems Knowledge of Customer Service fields Required Skills/Abilities Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written (email, written memos, telephone, voicemail, etc.) Ability to interact with clients diplomatically and professionally Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced sales environment Ability to work independently and also to collaborate with teams Proficient in Microsoft Outlook, Excel, Word and PowerPoint Organizational, planning and critical thinking skills Ability to multitask Required Behaviors/Attitudes Initiative Team oriented; demonstrates a service attitude Cares about delivering quality Planning & Organizing Confident / Assertive Dependable Take personal ownership for delivery of superior results; conscientious Demonstrate strong commitment to meeting the needs of internal and external clients Education & Experience High School Diploma Required College Degree Preferred 1-3 Years of Customer Service Experience What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, ultimately, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $42,945 – $68,670. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! NFP is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. #LI-NG1 #NFP 2588985

Posting Description Who We Are: NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: www.NFP.com. Summary of Role: As a New Business Coordinator, you will support the New Business team in handling life insurance underwriting requirements, reviewing medical records, and coordinating policy implementation activities. This role is responsible for tracking underwriting cases, preparing medical summaries, maintaining accurate documentation, and working with carriers, advisors, medical providers, and internal stakeholders to facilitate timely case progression and policy placement. The New Business Coordinator will also gain exposure to insurance portfolio implementation and progressively assume responsibility for handling straightforward cases and smaller portfolios independently. This position offers an opportunity to develop technical expertise in life insurance underwriting, case management, and portfolio implementation while contributing to a collaborative, service-oriented team. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Order and manage Attending Physician Statements (APS), medical records, and other underwriting requirements for active cases. Monitor outstanding underwriting requirements and coordinate follow-up activities to ensure timely case progression. Maintain accurate case notes, underwriting updates, and supporting documentation within Salesforce and other internal systems. Coordinate with medical providers, insurance carriers, examination vendors, and third-party partners to obtain required information. Assist in preparing underwriting submissions and supporting documentation for carrier review. Review and organize medical records received from physicians, hospitals, and other healthcare providers. Prepare concise medical summaries highlighting relevant diagnoses, treatments, medications, procedures, laboratory findings, and other underwriting considerations. Identify and advance significant medical findings or potential underwriting concerns to senior New Business leadership. Ensure accuracy, confidentiality, and appropriate handling of sensitive medical information. Support the New Business team throughout the insurance portfolio implementation and policy placement process. Assist with policy issuance tracking, carrier follow-up, funding requirements, policy reviews, and delivery preparation. Coordinate communication between carriers, advisors, and internal collaborators to facilitate efficient policy implementation. Participate in implementation meetings and collaborate with senior team members to develop an understanding of portfolio management. Develop working knowledge of carrier processes, underwriting practices, and insurance implementation workflows. Progressively assume responsibility for managing straightforward insurance cases, term insurance placements, and smaller portfolios. Maintain high service standards while managing assigned underwriting and implementation responsibilities. Communicate case updates, outstanding requirements, potential delays, and operational concerns proactively to management. Support departmental initiatives focused on improving workflow efficiency, operational processes, and service quality. Participate in ongoing training and professional development opportunities. Collaborate with internal teams to deliver a consistent, high-quality client and advisor experience. Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities: Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail. Ability to review, interpret, organize, and summarize complex information accurately. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities. Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Strong follow-up skills with a proactive approach to managing outstanding requirements. Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across teams. Strong sense of ownership, accountability, and professional judgment. Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, CRM systems, and related business technology. Service-oriented mentality with a commitment to delivering a positive client and advisor experience. Willingness to learn new processes, develop technical expertise, and take on additional responsibilities. Education and/or Experience: Bachelor's degree preferred or equivalent professional experience. 2–5 years of experience in insurance operations, underwriting support, case management, healthcare administration, medical records review, or a related field. Previous experience in life insurance, underwriting, or insurance case management preferred. Experience reviewing medical records or preparing medical summaries preferred. Working knowledge of life insurance underwriting concepts, carrier requirements, and policy implementation processes preferred. Experience using Salesforce or similar CRM and case management systems preferred. What We Offer We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $53,700 – $85,900. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! NFP is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. 2588668

Posting Description Wealthspire Institutional brings together a network of affiliated firms that provides institutional advisory, wealth management, institutional advisory, and business management services to individuals, families, and institutions across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Through its specialized subsidiaries and affiliates, clients can access wealth management, retirement plan consulting, nonprofit endowment and foundation advisory, business management, and family office services tailored to their evolving financial needs. Wealthspire invests in the people, technology, and resources that expand what the firm can do for clients, while preserving the personal relationships and accountability that are central to its client service approach. Inspiring Trust. Enriching Lives. For more information, visit www.wealthspire.com. The Consulting Analyst is responsible for contributing directly to a superior client experience while working closely with Investment Consultants through thoughtful and accurate analysis of the firm’s Endowment & Foundation and Defined Benefit Plan client portfolios, aligning with our mission of helping clients prosper. Responsibilities: Proactively lead portfolio evaluation/diagnostic review effort for new clients, cross-collaborating with multiple teams at the firm Evaluate and construct investment policy statements consistent with clients’ investment objectives, risk tolerance, and investment restrictions Analyze asset allocation structure of client portfolios, including modeling and portfolio optimization analysis, leveraging approved analytical and AI‑enabled tools to enhance efficiency and analytical consistency. Collaborate with Investment Research in developing solutions for client portfolios Develop fiduciary governance materials in preparation for quarterly reporting Analyze and create customized components for client reports and supplemental meeting materials, utilizing approved AI tools to assist with drafting, summarization, and quality control. Analyze and develop trade recommendations to implement investment decisions, portfolio reallocations, or rebalancing, consistent with the firm’s risk management protocol and in compliance with client investment policy guidelines and firm-established policy and procedures. Closely monitor and respond to ongoing recurrent or ad hoc cash management needs in client portfolios Collaborate with Performance Analytics and Client Services in developing optimal reporting solutions for clients Issue and evaluate vendor RFIs and RFPs, using AI‑enabled tools to support data extraction, comparison, and synthesis while exercising independent judgment in all conclusions. Respond to periodic audit requests for investment-related data and analysis Conduct special ad-hoc analyses and projects as needed to support Investment Consultants Interact with and proactively communicate with Investment Consultants on all client matters and related projects Apply AI tools to support drafting, summarization, reconciliation, and quality‑control of analytical outputs (e.g., IPS drafts, trade rationales, governance materials), ensuring all final deliverables are reviewed and validated by the analyst. Attend and present at client meetings in a supporting role on occasion Respond to all meeting follow-up and action items in a timely and effective manner Maintain accurate client account and investment records in the CRM Respond to client and vendor requests in a timely and effective manner Required Education, Professional & Technical Experience Bachelor’s degree required with a preferred concentration in Economics or Finance Two (2) to five (5) years of investment consulting or investment-related work experience Experience with servicing Institutional clients in a Discretionary Outsourced CIO (“OCIO”) servicing framework is a plus Proficiency in Microsoft Suite Previous experience with CRM, custody portals, and asset allocation modeling software is a plus Familiarity with AI‑enabled productivity or analytical tools (e.g., Copilot, large language model–based assistants, automation tools, or analytical copilots) to support research, drafting, reconciliation, summarization, or quality control of analytical outputs. Ability to critically review, validate, and refine AI‑assisted outputs, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and alignment with fiduciary and firm standards. CFA candidate is a plus Knowledge of capital markets, including domestic and foreign equity, fixed income, and alternative investments Intellectual curiosity about investments, asset allocation, and portfolio structure Fundamental knowledge of retirement plans (Defined Benefit and Defined Contribution) and nonprofit client marketplaces Essential Traits Thoughtful ability to establish rapport and build relationships. Demonstrates the ability to thoughtfully adopt firm‑approved analytical tools (including AI‑enabled solutions) to improve efficiency, accuracy, and service scalability while maintaining strong judgment and attention to detail. Exceptional communication in a public setting with notable writing and presentation skills. Adaptability when priorities shift and able to work independently. Sound judgment and problem-solving skills. Innovative, curious, and enthusiastic. Detail-oriented with a high level of accuracy and organization. Ability to cultivate and develop inclusive and collaborative working relationships to support a sense of belonging. Passionate about working in an organization that values and promotes inclusion and belonging. Work Environment & Travel Requirements This role may travel up to 10% of the time for training and or business/events. This role offers a hybrid work model with three days in one of our professional office environments and two days remotely. Physical Job Expectations The physical expectations described here are representative of those that must be met by an associate to successfully perform the essential functions of this job: Must be able to remain in a stationary position for up to 8 hours. Constantly operate a computer and other office productivity machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine, and computer printer. The ability to communicate information and ideas so others will understand. The individual should be able to exchange accurate information. The person in this position may at times need to move throughout the building to access different areas. Ability to move equipment weighing up to 25 pounds. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform their primary responsibilities. What We Offer (Summary Highlights) A workplace that welcomes authenticity and practices acceptance for what makes each of us different. We are committed to educating our team, growing as a firm, and taking intentional actions related to inclusion and belonging. We strive to be active participants of change in and outside our industry. The base salary range for this position is $65,000-$87,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. Paid Time Off Generous PTO with optional rollover Personal/Sick Time 10 Holidays with additional half days off for specific holidays throughout the year Summer Perks Bereavement Time –inclusive time off for a loved one, unborn child, or pet. Employer Paid Parental, Personal and Family leaves. Professional Development Day for eligible exams Work Life Convenience Benefits Exclusive Wellness Benefit Programs from VirginPulse, Care.com, Torchlight, Real Appeal, Peloton and more KindBody – Family & Fertility Assistance Wellness Reimbursement Program Professional Development Designation reimbursement Employee Referral Program Employee Resource Groups, Mentorship Program & New Hire Cohort 401K Plan with company match Cell Phone Reimbursement Program Wealthspire is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. #Wealthspire 2589059

Constantly operate a computer and other office productivity machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine, and computer printer. The ability to communicate information and ideas so others will understand. The individual should be able to exchange accurate information. The person in this position may at times need to move throughout the building to access different areas. Ability to move equipment weighing up to 25 pounds. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform their primary responsibilities. What We Offer (Summary Highlights) A workplace that welcomes authenticity and practices acceptance for what makes each of us different. We are committed to educating our team, growing as a firm, and taking intentional actions related to inclusion and belonging. Posting Description Who We Are: NFP, an Aon Company, is a multi-year Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance who has also earned the 5-Star Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) award from Insurance Business magazine and the WORK180 employer endorsement. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com. Summary of Role: Join our dynamic Employee Benefits team in a pivotal support role that combines analytical prowess with client-focused service. As a key member of the team, you will engage in daily data analysis and reporting, tailored to meet the unique needs of our clients. Your responsibilities will include managing and meticulously reviewing vendor reports to ensure accuracy, creating comprehensive client-specific reports that provide valuable insights, and participating in meetings to discuss findings and strategies. This role is ideal for detail-oriented professionals passionate about data-driven decision-making and exceptional client service. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Build new financial models to improve financial analysis reporting and/or renewal process Collaborate with Unit Leader to build, develop and implement processes and procedure for maximum value and efficiency Quality review/proof exhibits prepared by analysts for mathematical, formulaic, spelling, grammatical and branding errors and ensure the exhibits are client ready Lead financial analysis and develop high-level, multi-year financial strategies for clients Make recommendations to clients regarding financial issues including appropriate renewal rating, cost drivers, plan design changes and funding methods Prepare and lead clients discussions around weekly, monthly, and quarterly financial reports that are inclusive of claims, budget/premium, payroll contributions, membership, high claimants and network utilization Develop and present to clients renewal projections for medical, dental and vision Complete renewal analysis and support the carrier negotiation process Prepare renewal financial summary Perform financial modeling of plan designs, employee contributions, specific stop loss, incurred claims and the financial impact of potential mergers, acquisitions and divestitures Perform IBNR reserve analysis Prepare and present stop loss sensitivity analysis for self‐insured clients Facilitate special projects as requested of the Data Analytics and Reporting Unit Support the sales process through financial analysis and present to clients upon request Attend seminars, sales meetings or educational activities to stay up‐to‐date on the latest developments, trends and regulations in the market place Build and maintain solid relationships with clients as well as carrier sales representatives and consultants Knowledge, Skills and/or Abilities: Strong Analytical Skills Ability to correspond on all financial issues in a clear, concise and persuasive manner Ability to effectively establish rapport, present information and respond to questions from consultants, clients and coworkers Dedicated work ethic with a commitment to client service excellence Well organized with the ability to handle several projects/clients simultaneously Strong knowledge of the group insurance marketplace including alternative funding methods and industry trends Working knowledge of carriers and products Strong knowledge of Microsoft Excel Proficiency with Power BI and Visual Basic Travel required as needed Education and/or Experience: Four-year college or university degree. Finance/Statistics/Mathematics, Risk Management, Actuarial Science, or related studies is highly preferred. 3+ years of experience in an Analytics or Financial role preferred What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $70,000 – $90,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! NFP is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. #LI-JS3 #LI-JS3 #NFP ACCOU014669

Posting Description Who We Are: NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance who has also earned the WORK180 employer endorsement. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com. Summary of Role: The Market Leader is responsible for the employee benefits consulting practice in a geographic market, supervising all aspects of the business segment with ultimate responsibility for its performance. The Market Leader develops the team, the business operations and the client experience to drive top line revenue growth and achieve financial outcomes. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Manages the business to achieve performance outcomes – strong client retention and top line revenue growth. Monitors market trends and reviews services to keep pace with market expectations. Applies NFP resources and subject matter experts to support the client’s scope of services. Acts as escalation point for challenging client situations and serves as executive sponsor, leading house account relationships. Partners with Growth and Sales Leaders for business planning and metrics, including cross sell and upsell opportunities. Looks for opportunities for NFP to participate in local marketing & networking events and participates as senior leader. Participates in new client acquisition and other business activities to drive growth. Oversees Managing Consultants providing mentorship, overall guidance and adherence to NFP policies, procedures and service scopes. Leads by example and promotes a culture of collaboration, trust and transparency. Develops team member growth, development and career advancement opportunities. Participates in compensation and employee bonus allocation. Participates in local internal cultural initiatives and external community service. Recruits top talent and assists in hiring decisions. Communicates regularly and optimally with team members and with senior leadership, sharing meaningful updates and addressing problems in a timely manner. Collaborates with shared services team on client deliverables, timelines and innovation. Collaborates with regional and national benefits leadership to share ideas, present opportunities and promote procedures. Collaborates with business line leaders to drive and support key regional and national initiatives; holds team accountable. Leads in the utilization of NFP standards and shares local advancements across the region and nationally. Works with other regional practice leaders to create and promote consistent business practices and processes. Provides feedback on team performance and staffing needs. Monitors new business pipeline to assist with team assignments and other prospecting efforts. Assists in closing new business as needed. Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities: Knowledge of benefits administration, HealthCare Reform, industry trends, carrier products and services Ability to work independently and anticipate client and team needs Effective time management and decision making skills Diligent follow up skills Ability to express ideas clearly in both written and oral communications Strong Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills Commanding presentation and public speaking abilities Education and/or Experience: BA/BS preferred Typically more than 10 years industry and product line experience. 8+ years of health and welfare consulting experience required. Certificates, Licenses, Registration: Life, Accident and Health Insurance License required GBA or CEBS Certification a plus What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $154,800 – $300,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! NFP is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. 2588279

Posting Description Who We Are: NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance who has also earned the WORK180 employer endorsement. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: NFP. Summary of Role: As a Consultant in our dynamic team, you will be the cornerstone of client interactions, fostering and deepening relationships with both clients and carrier representatives daily. You'll be the key contact for clients, handling and enhancing our relationships, diving into researching and advising on various benefit plans, and taking a leading role as an advisor. This is more than a job; it's a chance to make a significant impact – both in our clients' lives and within our team. If you're ready to take this leap and become a pivotal part of our client's journey, we're excited to welcome you aboard. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Serve as a strategic advisor and subject matter expert on Health & Welfare benefits, developing strong relationships with clients, carriers, and vendor partners. Anticipate client needs, recommend solutions, communicate industry trends and regulatory updates, and provide guidance on benefits compliance topics including COBRA, HIPAA, ERISA, Section 125, and Health Care Reform. Lead the renewal and marketing process by reviewing RFPs, analyzing plan designs, negotiating terms, coverage, and pricing with carriers, recommending renewal strategies, overseeing new business implementations, and articulating alternative funding approaches. Maintain strong carrier relationships to stay informed of market offerings and recommend appropriate solutions to clients. Partner with leadership to develop and execute client strategy plans, manage project timelines and deliverables, coordinate open enrollment activities, review employee communications and presentations, conduct annual compliance audits, and ensure client data is accurately maintained in Salesforce. Demonstrate a strong understanding of client financials, funding strategies, and benefit plan administration, including interpreting plan documents and SPDs to ensure compliance and accurate plan management. Provide leadership within the service team by delegating work, overseeing deliverables, reviewing Account Manager work product, and offering informal coaching and mentorship to support team development and service excellence. Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities: Knowledge of benefits administration, HealthCare Reform, industry trends, carrier products and services Ability to work independently and anticipate client and team needs Effective time management and decision making skills Diligent follow-up skills Ability to express ideas clearly in both written and oral communications Strong Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills Commanding presentation and public speaking abilities Education and/or Experience: BA/BS preferred Typically more than 5 years industry and product line experience. 4+ years of health and welfare consulting experience required. Certificates, Licenses, Registration: Life, Accident and Health Insurance License required. GBA or CEBS Certification a plus. What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $84,295 – $134,895. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! NFP is an inclusive Equal Employment Opportunity employer. #NFP 2584131

We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com. Summary: The Account Manager is responsible for servicing an assigned book of habitational commercial insurance accounts in partnership with Advisors/Client Executives and Account Executives. Clients may include apartment and multifamily property owners, condominium associations, homeowners associations, and property managers. This role manages day-to-day client needs, renewals, marketing and remarketing, carrier communications, and the preparation of proposals, coverage comparisons, and client presentations. The Account Manager builds strong relationships with clients and carrier partners, works with significant independent discretion, and collaborates with senior team members on account strategy, complex coverage matters, and placement decisions. We offer the flexibility of either a hybrid or a fully remote arrangement available to candidates located in any U.S. city. The required work schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (PST), regardless of residential time zone. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Works proactively to develop relationships with carrier and client contacts; may take active role in meetings Prepare and send the request for proposals to applicable insurance carriers and spreadsheets results as they come in. First draft of renewal presentation Takes the lead on reviewing proposals and carrier source documents for accuracy in collaboration with the Account Executive or Advisor/Client Executive. Begins to communicate directly with clients and carriers, with approval from the Account Executive or Advisor/Client Executive Creates and maintains client files in accordance with office procedures. May be responsible for keeping client policy records in the agency management system First line of answering billing questions from clients and insurance company personnel with assistance from Accounting Dept. when necessary Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities: Highly organized with excellent verbal and written communication skills Self-confident to make sound independent decisions Ability to successfully interact with a variety of people and function well both in a team environment and autonomously Ability to handle situations in a calm, courteous and professional manner Customer focused to establish and maintain effective relationships Intermediate level of experience in Microsoft Office products, specifically Word, Excel and Outlook Ability to prioritize multiple tasks to meet deadlines Possess strong analytical and problem solving skills Sharp attention to detail, decision making skills, and problem resolution Flexibility and adaptability to changing priorities, deadlines and technology When working from home, you must maintain a private workspace to secure company equipment and correspondence; maintain high-speed internet, be present and responsive online and minimize personal interruptions during your work shift Education and/or Experience: Associates degree (or equivalent), and BA/BS preferred More than 3 years’ client service and/or industry and product line experience Certificates, Licenses, Registration: California P&C Insurance License required What We Offer: We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $70,800 – $90,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives. NFP and You... Better Together! Who We Are

For over 70 years, Glatfelter Insurance Group has believed in doing the right thing for our clients, agents, communities and associates. This founding principle has enabled Glatfelter to grow from the kitchen-table, one-man-operation as it began, to one of the largest managing general agencies in the U.S. with nearly 500 associates across the country, a distribution network of over 4,500 independent brokers and more than 30,000 clients. It is what drives us to innovate—the desire to deliver the best for our clients. Founded as The Glatfelter Agency, which is still in operation, the program basis of Glatfelter Insurance Group, Volunteer Firemen’s Insurance Services (VFIS), was founded in 1969. Throughout the years, Glatfelter has expanded to include specialized program business inclusive of public entities, educational institutions, healthcare facilities, and religious organizations. Glatfelter provides their insureds with comprehensive insurance solutions including property, casualty, life insurance, and more. In 2018, Glatfelter joined American International Group (AIG) and is now part of the AIG family.

About the Position

Glatfelter Insurance Group is seeking a Claims Examiner for our Glatfelter Claims Management team. This customer facing claims adjuster position's primary responsibilities include the direct investigation, evaluation, and handling of high complexity and/or large exposure claims within the handler's designated line(s) of business, specialty, and financial authority under limited supervision. The position includes handling of management liability and professional heath care liability claims.

This position is required to be onsite at our Leader Heights, York, PA office.

Key Responsibilities

  • Proactive handling of assigned claims in compliance with applicable state regulatory requirements, departmental standards, and designated financial authority.
  • Upholding the highest standards of customer satisfaction and service to insureds, agents, regional directors, and other interested parties while fulfilling obligations to protect the insured’s interests and the company’s assets. 
  • Communicating investigation and handling status and final determinations to insureds and claimants in compliance with regulatory requirements and departmental standards. This includes verbal communications, written correspondence, internal reports, and issuance of formal denial, disclaimer, and reservation of rights letters. 
  • Representing GIG through continuous countrywide contact with insureds, claimants, brokers, insurance carriers, and vendors. May include field work, trial attendance, mediation, or other travel. 
  • Maintaining claim file integrity to document activity, preserve evidence in an organized fashion, capture accurate claims data, and provide an appropriate basis for all claims handling decisions. 
  • All specialized tasks and duties necessary for the prompt and efficient handling of assigned claims within the handler’s designated specialty/line(s) of business. May include litigation management, subject matter expertise development or other advanced technical training or industry education.
  • All other duties as assigned. May include training, mentoring or other staff development or supervisory support functions.

What We’re Looking For

  • Secondary school diploma or equivalent, college degree, and Associate in Claims designation preferred.
  • Ten (10) or more years of experience in appropriate specialty insurance claims handling or appropriate transferable experience in a related field required. 

Technical Qualifications:

  • Effective verbal and written communication skills. 
  • Efficient time management skills.
  • Extensive knowledge of insurance policy forms, pertinent coverages, and claims handling processes and procedures. 
  • Superior understanding of technical subject matter appropriate to assigned specialty/line(s) of business.
  • Must be proficient with the use of computer applications (standard Microsoft products), keyboard/typing, and telecommunication tools and technology. 
  • Quality focus and attention to detail. 
  • Ability to perform calculations, prepare reports, and maintain files.
  • Effective interpersonal skills and ability to work as part of a team. 

Upon employment the associate is required to:

  • Develop a working knowledge and understanding of GCM processes and procedures as well as GIG culture, products, and services within an appropriate period of time. 
  • Develop functional proficiency in the use of GIG/GCM computer systems and applications.
  • Complete required training as assigned to enhance knowledge, expand technical understanding, and develop skills. 
  • Obtain required adjuster licenses within an aggressive timeframe and maintain licensure renewals by obtaining required continuing education credits.
  • Demonstrate ability to take ownership of assigned tasks and complete tasks timely/accurately.

Why Choose Glatfelter?

Glatfelter is honored to have been named a Best Place to Work in PA since 2005. We are proud to offer a range of employee benefits and resources that help you protect what matters most - your health care, savings, financial protection and wellbeing. In addition to 17 paid holidays, (which includes a personal holiday and mental health and wellness day) we provide a variety of leaves for personal, health, family, and volunteer needs. 

We believe in fostering our associates' development and offer a range of learning opportunities for associates to hone their professional skills to position themselves for the next steps of their careers. We have a tuition reimbursement program for eligible associates to enhance their education, skills, and knowledge in areas that relate to their current position or future positions to which they may transfer or progress.

Equal Opportunity Employer

It has been and will continue to be the policy of Glatfelter Insurance Group to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We provide equal opportunity to all qualified individuals regardless of race, color, religion, age, gender, gender expression, national origin, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected categories. At Glatfelter, we believe that diversity and inclusion are critical to our future and our mission – creating a foundation for a creative workplace that leads to innovation, growth, and profitability. Glatfelter is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to job applicants and employees with physical or mental disabilities. If you believe you need a reasonable accommodation in order to search for a job opening or to complete any part of the application or hiring process, please contact Human Resources. Reasonable accommodations will be determined on a case-by-case basis.

In 2018, Glatfelter joined American International Group (AIG) and is now part of the AIG family.

About the Position

Glatfelter Insurance Group is seeking an Assistant Underwriter to join our Glatfelter Healthcare Underwriting team. Our new associate will provide assistance to the Underwriter in the evaluation of new business and renewal exposures and recommend acceptance, modification, or rejection. Screens new business submissions and endorsement requests based on underwriting guidelines. May assist the Underwriter in the pre-renewal process by referring questionable risks to the Underwriter. Maintains sound customer relationships with producers through demonstration of professional communication skills.

This position is required to be onsite at our Leader Heights, York, PA office.

Key Responsibilities 

  • Receives and reviews new business submissions for completeness and acceptability. 
  • Identifies, classifies, and analyzes exposures. Provides pricing information for each line of business using published guidelines as a starting point. 
  • Responds to inquiries from brokers and sales associates regarding pricing and coverage issues. 
  • Provides instructions to Underwriting Assistants for rating and processing based on company guidelines and operating procedures. 
  • Authorizes instructions for insurance proposals. 
  • Accepts, rejects or requests additional information from customers on new business, renewals, and endorsements based on underwriting guidelines. 
  • Reviews renewals in accordance with guidelines and recommends pricing and coverage changes. 
  • Monitors loss control and claims activities. 
  • Determines appropriate loss control recommendations and insurance to value requirements for conditional acceptability.

  • Proactive handling of assigned claims in compliance with applicable state regulatory requirements, departmental standards, and designated financial authority.
  • Upholding the highest standards of customer satisfaction and service to insureds, agents, regional directors, and other interested parties while fulfilling obligations to protect our insured’s interests and the company’s assets. 
  • Communicating investigation and handling status and final determinations to insureds and claimants in compliance with regulatory requirements and departmental standards. This includes verbal communications, written correspondence, internal reports, and issuance of formal denial, disclaimer, and reservation of rights letters. 
  • Representing GIG through continuous countrywide contact with insureds, claimants, brokers, insurance carriers, and vendors. May include field work, trial attendance, mediation, or other travel. 
  • Maintaining claim file integrity to document activity, preserve evidence in an organized fashion, capture accurate claims data, and provide an appropriate basis for all claims handling decisions. 
  • All specialized tasks and duties necessary for the prompt and efficient handling of assigned claims within the handler’s designated specialty/line(s) of business. May include litigation management, subject matter expertise development or other advanced technical training or industry education.
  • All other duties as assigned. May include training, mentoring or other staff development or supervisory support functions.

What We’re Looking For

  • Secondary school diploma or equivalent, college degree, and Associate in Claims designation preferred.
  • Three to six (3-6) years of experience in first-party property insurance claims or appropriate transferable experience in a related field required. 

Technical Qualifications:

  • Effective verbal and written communication skills. 
  • Efficient time management skills.
  • Proficient knowledge of insurance policy forms, pertinent coverages, and claims handling processes and procedures. 
  • Proficient understanding of technical subject matter appropriate to assigned specialty/line(s) of business.
  • Must be proficient with the use of computer applications (standard Microsoft products), keyboard/typing, and telecommunication tools and technology. 
  • Quality focus and attention to detail. 
  • Ability to perform calculations, prepare reports, and maintain files.
  • Effective interpersonal skills and ability to work as part of a team.  

Upon employment the Associate is required to:

  • Develop a working knowledge and understanding of GCM processes and procedures as well as GIG culture, products, and services within an appropriate period of time. 
  • Develop functional proficiency in the use of GIG/GCM computer systems and applications.
  • Complete required training as assigned to enhance knowledge, expand technical understanding, and develop skills. 
  • Obtain required adjuster licenses within an aggressive timeframe and maintain licensure renewals by obtaining required continuing education credits.
  • Demonstrate ability to take ownership of assigned tasks and complete tasks timely/accurately.

This position is required to be onsite at our Leader Heights, York, PA office.

Job.JobTitle: Sr. Property & Casualty Underwriter - Glatfelter Healthcare
Job.JobDescription:
Who We Are

For over 70 years, Glatfelter Insurance Group has believed in doing the right thing for our clients, agents, communities and associates. This founding principle has enabled Glatfelter to grow from the kitchen-table, one-man-operation as it began, to one of the largest managing general agencies in the U.S. with nearly 500 associates across the country, a distribution network of over 4,500 independent brokers and more than 30,000 clients. It is what drives us to innovate—the desire to deliver the best for our clients. Founded as The Glatfelter Agency, which is still in operation, the program basis of Glatfelter Insurance Group, Volunteer Firemen’s Insurance Services (VFIS), was founded in 1969. Throughout the years, Glatfelter has expanded to include specialized program business inclusive of public entities, educational institutions, healthcare facilities, and religious organizations. Glatfelter provides their insureds with comprehensive insurance solutions including property, casualty, life insurance, and more. In 2018, Glatfelter joined American International Group (AIG) and is now part of the AIG family. 

About the Position

Glatfelter Insurance Group is seeking a Sr. Property & Casualty Underwriter to join the Glatfelter Healthcare (GH) team who will independently qualify and price new and renewal business consistent with program underwriting guidelines and pricing directives. This position will also be responsible for servicing accounts in accordance with service standards. 

This position is required to be onsite at either our Berwyn, PA or Leader Heights, York, PA office. 

Key Responsibilities

  • Completes underwriting qualification and pricing of new business and renewal submissions, using discretion and independent judgment to accept, reject or modify submission proposal.
  • Requests additional information when needed to qualify submission and communicates acceptance or declination to producer.
  • The Senior Underwriter is responsible for producers and/or account relationship building and is the primary point of contact for producers in his/or her assigned region.
  • Analyzes and reviews underwriting information including applications, MVR's, loss notifications, loss runs, inspections, financial reports, websites, supplemental applications, budgets, and audits
  • Participates in large account reviews and prepares underwriting approach to large renewals and new business.
  • Handles all business in a proficient, timely manner, and fully adheres to underwriting authority as delegated by GUS management
  • Demonstrates superior working knowledge of program forms and endorsements, including various manuscript forms required on more complex accounts and program rating methodology.
  • Follows and meets Glatfelter Underwriting service standards
  • Assists management in the development of new/existing products and programs
  • Responsible for accuracy of final policy product and complies with all quality control and state filing requirements
  • Acts as leader in the development and success of GUS team
  • Assists in staff training and as a mentor to less experienced team members.
  • Seeks to enhance skills, knowledge and work abilities of other employees
  • Depending on GUS program, manages and evaluates the performance of Underwriting Assistants on assigned team and conducts semi-annual and annual performance reviews.
  • Provides instructions to Underwriting Assistants to rate risk according to company guidelines and current market conditions.
  • Requests any additional underwriting information required including risk control surveys, insurance to value, driver information and compliance with outstanding recommendations.
  • Monitors risk control and claims activities.
  • Reviews and takes appropriate action on any transactions which exceed the written underwriting authority of the Underwriting Assistants.
  • Refers and suggests action on any unusual exposures to Underwriting Supervisor for approval.
  • Refers all accounts exceeding designated authority level to higher level for approval.
  • Provides support to sales staff. Attends agent meetings, conventions, trade shows, and visits agents as requested.
  • Maintains OnBase files consistent with standard file procedures
  • Evaluates and compares competitor's forms and coverages.
  • Performs other duties and special projects as assigned by management. 

What We’re Looking For

  • BA degree in insurance, business or related field preferred. Must attain or be working toward AU, CPCU, ARM designation or comparable higher insurance education.
  • Must have a minimum of five (5) years of experience as a Property & Casualty Underwriter. Preferred experience underwriting public entities or educational institutions.
  • Must have or attain within three (3) months and maintain a current property-casualty license for state of residence and other licenses as required.
  • Has a proven and consistent level of high performance as an underwriter with the ability to underwrite large accounts, including thorough knowledge of all commercial insurance.
  • Analytical ability is required to exercise underwriting judgment and make decisions.
  • Organizational skills and ability to handle tasks on a priority basis required to maintain consistent high quality and quantity of work.
  • Effective negotiation skills
  • Ability to work independently
  • Effective oral and written communication skills including formal and informal presentation skills
  • Ability to cope with stressful situations.
  • Good research skills and detail oriented
  • Proficient in IT tools, and software applications. 

Why Choose Glatfelter?

Glatfelter is honored to have been named a Best Place to Work in PA since 2005. We are proud to offer a range of employee benefits and resources that help you protect what matters most - your health care, savings, financial protection and wellbeing. In addition to 17 paid holidays, (which includes a personal holiday and mental health and wellness day) we provide a variety of leaves for personal, health, family, and volunteer needs.  

We believe in fostering our associates' development and offer a range of learning opportunities for associates to hone their professional skills to position themselves for the next steps of their careers. We have a tuition reimbursement program for eligible associates to enhance their education, skills, and knowledge in areas that relate to their current position or future positions to which they may transfer or progress.

We provide equal opportunity to all qualified individuals regardless of race, color, religion, age, gender, gender expression, national origin, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected categories. At Glatfelter, we believe that diversity and inclusion are critical to our future and our mission – creating a foundation for a creative workplace that leads to innovation, growth, and profitability.  Glatfelter is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to job applicants and employees with physical or mental disabilities. Job.CustomJobTypeName: Loss Control Consultant, Risk Management / Loss Control
Job.JobDescription:
Insurance Loss Control Field Representative

Job Description
At Alexander & Schmidt, an Insurance Loss Control Field Representative performs on-site property, general liability and incidental auto inspections and prepares reports for insurance underwriting purposes. Insurance companies use the reports to properly insure commercial or residential buildings or properties for a new policy or renewal of a current policy.
Required Skills
  • MUST HAVE 3 – 5 years’ experience with a commercial carrier or working as an independent contractor providing commercial insurance loss control services.
  • Understanding of commercial property and casualty lines including property, general liability, auto and workers compensation.
  • Solid communication skills—including exceptional writing ability, organizational skills, and computer skills
  • Excellent time management skills
  • Travel within a reasonable territory, 60 mile radius
  • Professional certifications CSP, OHST, ALCM and/or ARM are preferred, but not required.
  • Uploading completed reports, photos and diagrams through a special website or complete reports on web based systems
High-quality, accurate loss control surveys guide the underwriter in the selection of profitable business, and assist the insured in controlling losses through the demonstrated value of the loss control services provided.
